notices.description:
MINISTRY OF GENDER, CULTURE AND CHILDREN SERVICES

STATE DEPARTMENT FOR CHILDREN SERVICES

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES - INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT SELECTION-IC)

Country

Kenya

Name of Project

Second Kenya Social and Economic Inclusion Project (KSEIP- 2)

Credit No

IDA-78450-KE

Project ID No

P504218

 

S/No

Reference No

Assignment Title

  1.  

KE-SDCS-561184-CS-INDV

Individual Consultant to enhance NICHE MIS and Develop ADoP MIS.

2.

KE-SDCS-574722-CS-INDV

Individual Consultant to Develop NICHE Communication Strategy

3.

KE-SDCS-572314-CS-INDV

Individual Consultant to Develop NICHE Programme Website

  1. The Government of Kenya (GoK) has received funding from the World Bank towards the cost of Second Kenya Social and Economic Inclusion Project (KSEIP -2), and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under the contract for consulting services. The Program has three key result areas;
  1. Building human capital of children and adolescents
  2. Building Climate and Economic Resilience of Adults
  3. Advancing Systems and Strengthening Adaptive Social Protection

2. The Consulting Services (“Services”) main objective of the assignments is to enhance the Nutrition Improvement Through Cash and Health Education (NICHE) MIS and develop adolescent MIS, develop NICHE communication strategy and the programme website.

3.The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR’S) for the assignments can be found on The Public Procurement Information Portal https://tenders.go.ke and the State Department for Children Services Website https://www.childrenservices.go.ke

4.The State Department for Children Services invites eligible individual consultants to indicate their interest by providing information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services. Interested Individuals MUST provide information indicating that they are qualified to perform the services (attach Curriculum Vitae (CV’s), copies of documentary evidence of academic qualifications, professional qualifications).

The shortlisting Criteria is as follows;

  1. KE-SDCS-561184-CS-INDV -    Individual Consultant to enhance NICHE MIS and Develop                                                 ADoP MIS.
  • A minimum of a Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Software Engineering, Information Systems, or a closely related field. A Master's degree will be an added advantage.
  • At least five (5) years of relevant professional experience in analysis, design, development, enhancement, or support of management information systems or related enterprise applications.
  • Demonstrated experience in developing or enhancing operational systems that support business processes such as registration, enrolment, payments, grievance/case management, monitoring and reporting, preferably in social protection, health, education, or public sector programmes.

2. KE-SDCS-574722-CS-INDV -    Individual Consultant to Develop NICHE               Communication Strategy

  • A University Degree in Communications, Journalism or equivalent from a recognized university. Previous employment experience (minimum 3 years) in communication, journalism, print media, research documentation and report writing.
  • Experience in Child Protection, Social Protection or health communication
  • Demonstrated expertise in developing and implementing communication guidelines, strategies or plans.

3.  KE-SDCS-572314-CS-INDV -    Individual Consultant to Develop NICHE Programme Website

  • Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a closely related discipline; professional certifications in programming, cloud architecture, or DevOps are a strong advantage. A Master's degree will be an added advantage.
  • Proven experience in developing interactive websites for government, UN, or donor-funded programmes.
  • Portfolio of previous designed products in health, nutrition, social protection, or child protection sectors
  • Expertise in UX/UI design, responsive web development, and CMS platforms.

5.The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs,3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” Procurement Regulations of September 2023, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

6. An Individual consultant will be selected in accordance with the procedures set out in the World Bank’s Guidelines: Selection and Employment of Consultants [under IBRD Loans and IDA Credits & Grants] by World Bank Borrowers.

7. Interested Individual Consultants may obtain further information at the address below from 0900 to 1700 hours East African Time (EAT) from Monday to Friday excluding lunch hour (1300 to 1400hours EAT) and public holidays.

8. Interested Individual Consultants should submit their expression of interest, which MUST be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person or by e-mail) by Wednesday 16th December, 2026 at 11:00 Hours EAT and deposited in the Tender Box clearly marked State Department for Children Services located at NSSF Building “Annex” 7th Floor Bishops Road Nairobi or send by email to scm@childrenservices.go.ke and quote the Assignment Title and respective Reference No.

The Principal Secretary,

Ministry of Gender, Culture and Children Services

State Department for Children Services

P. O. Box 4036 - 00100

Nairobi

Attention: HEAD SUPPLY CHAIN MANAGEMENT SERVICES

Email: scm@childrenservices.go.ke

9.         The Expression of Interest shall be delivered using one of the following modalities; Deposit          in the Tender Box located on 7th floor, NSSF Building, “Annex” along Bishops Road Kenya     0r Send via email to; scm@childrenservices.go.ke

notices.description:
MINISTERE DE L’EDUCATION NATIONALE

------------------

SECRETARIAT GENERAL

--------------

UNITE DE FACILITATION DE PROJET

---------------

PROJET MADAGASCAR YOUTH SKILLS FOR ECONOMIC TRANSFORMATION AND JOBS (MYSET)

-----------
Crédit IDA n° 80210-MG

 

 

 

 SOLLICITATION DE MANIFESTATION D’INTERÊT

N°01-26/AMI/UFP/MYSET-Ni

Pays : Madagascar

Financement : Crédit IDA n° 78760-MG / Don GPE n° TFOC8850

AMI N° : N°01-26/AMI/UFP/MYSET-Ni

Date : 24 novembre 2026

Objet : RECRUTEMENT D’UN (01) RESPONSABLE ADMINISTRATIF ET FINANCIER (RAF) ET DE DEUX (02) COMPTABLES POUR LE PROJET MYSET

 

Le Gouvernement de la République de Madagascar a reçu un financement de l’Association Internationale de Développement (IDA) pour couvrir le coût du Projet Madagascar Youth Skills for Economic Transformation and Jobs (MYSET), mis en œuvre par l’Unité de Facilitation de Projets (UFP), et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie du montant de ce financement pour effectuer les paiements au titre des contrats de consultants pour les postes de Responsable Administratif et Financier (RAF) et de Comptables.

Dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre du Projet MYSET, l’Unité de Facilitation de Projets (UFP) envisage de recruter un (01) Responsable Administratif et Financier (RAF) et deux (02) Comptables afin d’assurer la bonne gestion administrative, financière et comptable du Projet, conformément à l’Accord de financement, au Manuel de procédures et aux textes réglementaires applicables.

Les termes de référence détaillés de chaque poste sont disponibles dans les liens ci après :

  • Lien RAF : https://tinyurl.com/raf-myset
  • Lien comptable : https://tinyurl.com/compta-myset

L’Unité de Facilitation de Projets (UFP) invite les consultants individuels intéressés à manifester leur intérêt en présentant leurs qualifications et expériences démontrant leur capacité à réaliser les missions.

 

  1. Poste de Responsable Administratif et Financier (RAF) – Un (01) poste

Le Responsable Administratif et Financier assurera la coordination de la gestion administrative, financière et comptable du Projet. Il veillera notamment à l’éligibilité des dépenses, à la disponibilité des fonds, à la fiabilité des informations financières et comptables, au respect des procédures applicables, ainsi qu’à la production des états financiers et rapports dans les délais requis.

Les candidats doivent être titulaires d’un Diplôme de Master 2 en Finances et Comptabilité, délivré par une université ou un établissement d’enseignement supérieur parmi la liste des diplômes habilités par l’OECFM, et justifier au minimum :

  • Sept (07) années d’expériences professionnelles réussies, au cours des dix (10) dernières années, dans la gestion administrative et financière de projets financés par des bailleurs de fonds, dont le financement moyen annuel géré s’élève à au moins dix millions (10 000 000) USD, ou dans une entité ayant un chiffre d’affaires moyen annuel d’au moins un million (1 000 000) USD ;
  • La maîtrise des logiciels courants de comptabilité et de l’outil informatique et bureautique ;
  • Une grande capacité d’analyse de données, de synthèse et de rédaction ;
  • Une capacité à travailler de manière autonome et en équipe ;
  • Être méthodique, rigoureux(se) et intègre ;
  • La maîtrise de la langue française et une bonne connaissance de l’anglais ;
  • Être disponible et apte à effectuer des déplacements dans les zones d’intervention du Projet.

 

Atouts :

  • Expérience dans la gestion administrative, financière et comptable de projets financés par la Banque mondiale ou d’autres bailleurs de fonds ;
  • Expérience en supervision d’équipe et coordination des activités administratives et financières ;
  • Bonne connaissance des procédures de gestion financière applicables aux projets financés par les bailleurs de fonds.

 

2. Poste de Comptable – Deux (02) postes

 

Les Comptables seront chargés d’assurer la gestion quotidienne et la traçabilité des opérations comptables et financières du Projet. Ils contribueront notamment à la saisie et à la tenue de la comptabilité, à la préparation des dossiers de dépenses et de paiement, au suivi des opérations de caisse et de banque, ainsi qu’au classement et à l’archivage des pièces justificatives.

Les candidats doivent être titulaires d’un diplôme de niveau Master en comptabilité, finance, gestion ou discipline équivalente, et justifier au minimum :

  • Trois (03) années d’expérience professionnelle pertinente dans un poste similaire (comptable), au cours des cinq (05) dernières années ;
  • Une bonne connaissance des principes comptables, de la gestion des pièces justificatives et des opérations de caisse et de banque ;
  • La maîtrise des logiciels comptables ainsi que des outils bureautiques, notamment les tableurs ;
  • La rigueur, l’intégrité, l’organisation, la discrétion et la capacité à travailler dans le respect des délais ;
  • Une bonne maîtrise du français écrit et oral ;
  • Être disponible pour des déplacements ponctuels dans les zones d’intervention du Projet, si nécessaire.

Atouts :

  • Expérience au sein d’un projet financé par des partenaires techniques et financiers internationaux ;
  • Connaissance de l’anglais.

 

  1. Dossiers de candidature

 

Les dossiers de candidature doivent comprendre :

  • Une lettre de motivation précisant le poste sollicité ;
  • Un Curriculum Vitae détaillé faisant ressortir les expériences pertinentes et les références professionnelles ;
  • Une copie du diplôme requis pour le poste sollicité ;
  • Des attestations, certificats de travail ou tout autre document justifiant les expériences professionnelles pertinentes.
  •  

Les candidats intéressés peuvent manifester leur intérêt pour l’un des postes ou pour plusieurs postes, en précisant clairement leur choix dans leur lettre de motivation.

Les critères seront évalués sur consultation des dossiers, à travers un test écrit et/ou par entretien.

L’attention des Consultants intéressés est attirée sur la Section III, paragraphes 3.14, 3.16 et 3.17 du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement FPI », publié par la Banque mondiale – version septembre 2025, énonçant la politique de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflits d’intérêts.

Les consultants seront sélectionnés conformément à la méthode de Sélection de Consultant Individuel énoncée dans le Règlement de Passation des Marchés.

Les candidatures doivent être déposées, au plus tard le 4 décembre 2026 à 16h00, à l’adresse ci-après :

Bureau de l’UFP, 1er étage, Lot 18 Bis, Rue Rainitovo, Antsahavola – 101 Antananarivo, à l’attention de Monsieur le Coordonnateur de l’UFP, avec la mention :

« RECRUTEMENT (poste à mentionner) – PROJET MYSET », en précisant le ou les postes sollicités.

Seules les candidatures présélectionnées sur la base des critères définis dans le présent Appel à Manifestation d’Intérêt seront contactées pour l’étape suivante.

Le Coordonnateur

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST      

THE REPUBLIC OF UZBEKISTAN

Uzbekistan Digital Inclusion Project

Credit No: 7425-UZ

Assignment title: Consulting Services for Technical Supervision of the Construction of the ITES Centre Building in Syrdarya Region

Reference No.: UZ-DIP-583966-CS-CQS

The Republic of Uzbekistan (hereinafter referred to as the “Borrower”) has applied for financing from the International Development Association (IDA) (hereinafter referred to as the “Bank”) in the form of a “credit” (hereinafter referred to as the “credit”) to cover the costs of the Uzbekistan Digital Inclusion Project. “Administration of Technology Park of Software and I” LLC as the Implementing Agency, intends to use part of the funds to pay for consulting services for technical supervision of the construction of the ITES Centre building in Gulistan City, Syrdarya Region.

The assignment covers the construction of the office building of two blocks, designed to accommodate IT companies, start-ups, training centres and the IT Park regional office. The construction works contract is expected to be signed in December 2026, with a construction period of 426 days.

The purpose of this consultancy is to provide independent technical supervision and contract administration of the construction. The Consultant will act as the Engineer under the construction works contract and as the Client’s technical supervisor under the legislation of the Republic of Uzbekistan, and will ensure that the works comply with the approved design, the national building codes and standards and the World Bank Environmental and Social Standards.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include, but are not limited to:

  1. Construction supervision and quality control, including acceptance of hidden works and load-bearing structures, seismic detailing, approval and testing of materials;
  2. Contract administration and cost control: measurement of completed works, verification of the acts of completed works and payment certificates, assessment of variations, claims and extensions of time;
  3. Supervision of the Contractor’s compliance with environmental, social, health and safety requirements;
  4. Testing, commissioning and taking-over, including life and fire safety systems, and supervision during the 12-month Defects Liability Period.

The consulting services are expected to last approximately 27 months, including construction supervision, testing and taking-over, and the 12-month DLP. The contract will be time-based.

To obtain the Terms of Reference for the assignment, please send your request to the following
e-mail address: udip@it-park.uz.

“Administration of Technology Park of Software and I” LLC now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to express their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants must provide information confirming they have the necessary qualifications and relevant experience to provide the Services.

The expressions of interest will be evaluated against the following criteria:

1. Legal registration in the Republic of Uzbekistan and the right to provide technical supervision services under the legislation of the Republic of Uzbekistan. (Evidence: state registration certificate and documents confirming the right to perform technical supervision.)

2. At least 5 years of experience in technical supervision of new construction or major renovation of buildings. (Evidence: list of contracts with verifiable client contact details, including contract scope, construction value and period of execution.)

3. At least 2 completed technical supervision contracts in the last 7 years for new construction or major renovation of public, office or commercial buildings of 3 or more floors, each with a construction value of at least USD 2 million equivalent, in seismic zones of intensity 7 or higher; at least one of them a public-access building. (Evidence: contract copies, completion certificates or client reference letters confirming the building type, number of floors, construction value and location.)

For a joint venture (if applicable): each partner shall meet criteria 1. The combined experience of the partners may be considered for criteria 3, provided that the Lead Partner meets criterion 2 in full and has at least one of the contracts required under criterion 3.

Failure to provide supporting documentation for any of the above criteria may result in the expression of interest not being considered.

Experience of sub-consultants and Key experts will not be evaluated at this stage.

The attention of interested consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, 5th Edition, September 2023 (the “Procurement Regulations”), which sets forth the World Bank’s conflict of interest policy.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their expertise, but must clearly state whether the association is a form of joint venture and/or sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all partners in the joint venture are jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if one is chosen.

The Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Consultant’s Qualification-based Selection (CQS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations. The firm with the best qualifications and relevant experience will be invited to submit a combined technical and financial proposal and to negotiate the contract.

As part of the expression of interest, the Consultant must include the following information:

notices.title: Ghana Market Access and Connectivity Project
notices.description:
REPUBLIC OF GHANA

MINISTRY OF ROADS AND HIGHWAYS

DEPARTMENT OF FEEDER ROADS

 

GENERAL PROCUREMENT NOTICE

 

 

Country

Ghana

Name of Project

Ghana Market Access and Connectivity Project (GMACP)

Credit No

IDA-80450-GH

Project ID Number

P513708

 

 

  1. The Government of the Republic of Ghana has received financing in the amount of US$ 500 million from the World Bank towards the cost of the Ghana Market Access and Connectivity Project (GMACP), and it intends to apply part of the proceeds to payments for goods, works, non-consulting services and consulting services to be procured under this project. This project will be jointly financed with counterpart funding of US$ 23 million from the Government of Ghana for maintenance of the rehabilitated Feeder Roads.

 

The Project Development Objective (PDO) of the GMACP is to improve and sustain all-season farm-to-market connectivity in selected districts of Ghana.

 

2. The project will include the following components:

Component 1: Feeder Road Rehabilitation.

This component finances the rehabilitation of approximately 1,050 kilometres of feeder roads to improve all-season access between agricultural production areas and markets. It includes the design and construction of climate-resilient feeder roads, integration of road safety features, universal accessibility measures, promotion of women’s participation in the road construction sector, supervision of civil works, and implementation of Resettlement Action Plans where required. This component will be implemented by the Department of Feeder Roads (DFR) under the Ministry of Roads and Highways (MRH).

 

Component 2: Road Maintenance and support to the Road Maintenance Trust Fund.

This component adopts a co-financing approach with counterparts funding from Government of Ghana to ensure road maintenance over the life of the project through performance-based contracts (PBCs), thereby enhancing sustainability. This component will maintain the rehabilitated feeder roads and ensure the sustainability of the road investment through technical assistance to the Road Maintenance Trust Fund (Act 1147, 2025), which is operational and enhancement of the road asset management systems through traffic data and road inventory development. Implementation will be undertaken by MRH and DFR.

Component 3: Project Management, Monitoring and Evaluation.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

COUNTRY: Botswana

Name of Project BOTSWANA: Botswana Health Emergency Preparedness, Response, and Resilience Project (HEPRR)

Project ID: P510190

Loan No: 98750

Assignment Title: Survey Coordinator for MICS

Reference No.: BW-MOH-577376-CS-INDV

 

The Government of the Republic of Botswana, through the Ministry of Health, is implementing the Botswana Health Emergency Preparedness, Response and Resilience Project with World Bank support under the regional Multiphase Programmatic Approach for Eastern and Southern Africa. The Project Development Objective is to strengthen health-system resilience and multisectoral preparedness and response to health emergencies. The project is structured around four components. Component 1 strengthens preparedness and resilience through improved governance and multisectoral coordination, access to quality health commodities, and health system digitalization. Component 2 improves detection and response capabilities. Component 3 supports project management, fiduciary oversight, and monitoring and evaluation. Component 4 is a Contingent Emergency Response Component (CERC) enabling rapid reallocation of funds in response to an eligible emergency. The survey forms part of the investments under Component 1, Sub-Component 1.3, which aims to strengthen the quality and utilization of data. Specifically, it falls under Sub-Activity 1.3.11.3.2 of the Project, which focuses on strengthening health information systems, improving data quality and promoting the use of evidence for planning and decision-making.

The MoH is seeking an individual Survey Coordinator to support the preparation, implementation, and completion of the Botswana MICS. The coordinator will provide technical advice and coordination support to the MoH and the survey implementing institution, including its sampling and data processing experts, throughout survey planning, questionnaire design, sampling, training, fieldwork, data processing, analysis, reporting, dissemination, and archiving, ensuring adherence to MICS protocols and recommendations.

A full ToRs is available at website www.bomra.co.bw

The consultant should demonstrate to meet the following Qualifications and Competencies

  • A master’s degree in Demography, Statistics, Social Sciences, Epidemiology, or any other related technical field is required.
  • Proven minimum of 7 years of experience in the coordination and/or management of quantitative household surveys, preferably MICS or Demographic and Health Survey
  • Demonstrated experience in questionnaire customization, ethical review, listing and mapping, training and field supervision visits, CAPI data collection, data processing and validation, analysis, and dissemination.
  • Strong computer skills and strong expertise in statistical analyses (familiarity with data processing and data analysis software, particularly SPSS),
  • Experience engaging/coordinating with National Statistics Organizations, Ministries of Health, and development partners.
  • Proven ability to manage work plans, budgets, risks, technical reviews, and follow-up actions,
  • Prior experience working with UNICEF MICS protocols and regional or global technical review processes would be highly desirable. .

 

Key competencies

  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills,
  • Excellent oral and written communication in language(s) required,
  • Familiarity and previous experience of working in the country and/or in the region are highly desirable,
  • Demonstrated ability to work in a multicultural environment and to establish harmonious and effective relationships both within and outside the organisation,
  • Demonstrated leadership, managerial and supervisory ability,
  • Ability and willingness to travel in-country extensively and to attend regional workshops.

 

Candidates who meet the required qualifications will be assessed based on the following evaluation criteria. The first ranked candidate will be invited for contract negotiations.

The consultancy will therefore be for an initial period of 12 months, commencing February 2027, with the possibility of extension where necessary to support completion of the MICS process.

The contract model would be a time-based contract and linked with a defined result agreement.

Ukraine has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of the Housing Repair for People’s Empowerment Project (HOPE) (the “Project”) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services under Component 3 “Project Management and Capacity Strengthening”.

The consulting services (the “Services”) comprise implementation, analytical support and technical support for the State Register of Damaged and Destroyed Property (RDDP or the “Register”). The assignment aims to support the continuous functioning and effective use of the Register and the services implemented on its basis, and to strengthen the Client’s institutional capacity.

The Services cover five principal service areas:

  1. First-line support and service request analysis: receive, register, classify and analyse user requests; resolve routine issues; escalate matters requiring the Registry Administrator (L2) or the Client (L3); track requests through resolution; and identify recurring issues and best practices.
  2. Implementation support: support the roll-out and use of RDDP services and new or updated functionality, update user instructions and collect feedback on implementation.
  3. Knowledge Base: maintain, populate, structure and update the RDDP Knowledge Base, including guidance, frequently asked questions and documented resolution practices.
  4. User training and methodological support: deliver regular training, webinars and consultations; prepare learning materials; and transfer practical knowledge to users and designated MRIT representatives.
  5. Data analytics and dashboards: configure, maintain and develop Power BI dashboards and analytical reports; support data integration, ETL processes and data quality; and transfer dashboards, documentation and configurations to the Client.

Duration and contract arrangements

The Services are expected to commence upon the contract’s entry into force, and continue until November 30, 2027. The contract duration may be extended by mutual agreement of the parties in the event of an extension of the Project implementation timelines.

The Services shall be provided under a Time-Based contract, with payment based on actual person-hours worked, supported by approved monthly timesheets and Consolidated Reports. Approval is subject to the applicable service levels and reporting requirements specified in the Terms of Reference (ToR). The estimated level of effort is up to 45,360 person-hours. This estimate is indicative and non-binding; the Client has no obligation to utilise the full estimated number of hours.

The Consultant shall use Jira Service Management or an equivalent service request management system and other software necessary for the assignment. Microsoft Power BI licences shall be procured and administered by the Consultant as reimbursable costs, subject to the Client’s prior approval and evidence of price reasonableness, in accordance with the ToR and the Contract.

L1 ticket receipt, logging, handling and resolution shall be provided from 08:00 to 20:00 on Business Days (12×5), with escalation and continued monitoring of Critical Tickets as specified in the SLA. Weekly operational reports and monthly consolidated and time and effort reports shall be submitted in accordance with the ToR.

Detailed information on the scope, deliverables, reporting, staffing and Service Level Agreement (SLA) is provided in the attached Terms of Reference.

D. Gestion administrative

Le RAF assure :

  • la gestion du patrimoine ;
  • la supervision de la logistique ;

E. Rapports financiers

Il prépare :

Le RAF veille à :

Le RAF :

  • coordonne les missions des auditeurs ;
  • assure la mise en œuvre des recommandations d'audit ;
  • suit les plans d'actions convenus avec la Banque mondiale.

H. Coordination

Le RAF travaille en étroite collaboration avec :

  • le Coordonnateur Principal ;

notices.description:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(INDIVIDUAL CONSULTING SERVICES)

Syrian Arab Republic

Syria Public Financial Management Capacity Strengthening Project (P512516)

Grant No.: E6410-SY

Assignment Title: SIFMIS Program Manager (Syria Integrated Financial Management Information System)

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): SY-MOF-583041-CS-INDV

The Ministry of Finance of the Syrian Arab Republic (the “Employer”) has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of the Syria Public Financial Management Capacity Strengthening Project (P512516) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include the services of a SIFMIS Program Manager, who will provide the Government of Syria with experienced, full-time program management leadership and functional advisory for the implementation of the Syria Integrated Financial Management Information System (SIFMIS), ensuring effective planning, coordination, quality assurance, risk management, vendor governance, and change management throughout the system's design, procurement, configuration, testing, rollout, and stabilization phases.

The SIFMIS Program Manager combines program management leadership with business analysis and functional expertise, reflecting the need for a single accountable leader who can govern the vendor relationship at both the program level and the functional process level, and who can effectively represent the Ministry of Finance's interests in reviewing and approving all functional deliverables produced by the implementation vendor. The SIFMIS Program Manager will lead program planning and management across the full SIFMIS lifecycle - requirements validation, design, configuration and development, data migration, integration, testing, training, rollout, and post-go-live support; review and recommend acceptance or rejection of the vendor's IT infrastructure assessment, technical architecture, network and security architecture, and data center readiness; lead the government-side functional engagement across all SIFMIS modules; support the RFP finalization, bid evaluation and contract negotiation; oversee data migration, User Acceptance Testing, change management and training; maintain the program risk register; and oversee the post-go-live stabilization and the capacity building of the Ministry of Finance's SIFMIS Reform Implementation Team (RIT). The assignment is expected to span approximately thirty-six (36) months, covering the diagnostic and design, procurement support, and implementation oversight and capacity building phases.

The SIFMIS Program Manager will report to the Project Coordinator and will work within the Public Financial Management Reform Coordinating Unit (PFMRCU) of the Ministry of Finance, coordinating with the Ministry of Administrative Development (MoAD), line ministries, the Central Bank of Syria, the Supreme Audit Institution, the National Authority for IT Services (NAITS) and development partners, and reporting to the PFM Reform Oversight Steering Committee (PFM-ROSC) on overall program progress.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment are included below.

The Ministry of Finance (through the Public Financial Management Reform Coordinating Unit - PFMRCU) now invites eligible individuals (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services (attach curriculum vitae with description of experience in similar assignments, similar conditions, etc.). Firms' staff may express interest through the employing firm for the assignment and, under such situation, only the experience and qualifications of individuals shall be considered in the selection process.

The criteria for selecting the Consultant are:

  1. an advanced degree (Master's level or equivalent) in Public Financial Management, Information Systems, Finance, or a related field, and a minimum of fifteen (15) years of professional experience in government IFMIS programs, with a career trajectory that includes hands-on functional or business analysis roles in earlier years and senior program management responsibility in later years;
  2. demonstrated experience as a functional lead or business analyst on at least two (2) IFMIS implementations - covering module design, business process validation, User Acceptance Testing (UAT) and training - before progressing to program management;
  3. demonstrated experience managing at least two (2) IFMIS implementation programs in developing or post-conflict country contexts at senior level;
  4. deep knowledge of PFM processes across budget, treasury, payroll, procurement and accounting functions, with the ability to independently challenge and validate vendor functional designs, and knowledge of international PFM standards including GFS 2014, IPSAS cash basis and the PEFA assessment frameworks;
  5. experience in developing or reviewing technical specifications and RFPs for government IFMIS procurement; familiarity with the World Bank's Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, with experience managing procurement under World Bank-financed projects being a strong advantage; demonstrated experience in capacity building, training oversight and change management for government staff; professional certification (PMP, PRINCE2 or equivalent) and prior experience in fragile or conflict-affected environments are highly desirable; and
  6. proficiency in English is required; Arabic language proficiency is a strong advantage given the need to work directly with Syrian government counterparts.

 

The attention of interested Consultants (including firms) is drawn to paragraph 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank's Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers [insert correct title and date of applicable Regulations edition as per the financing agreement] (“the Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank's policy on conflict of interest.

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the following email address: syriapfmprocurement@gmail.com  by 5PM on 11 December 2026 Damascus time.

 

Attn: Project Coordinator

Ministry of Finance

Syria Public Financial Management Capacity Strengthening Project

Joul Jammal Street, P.O. Box 13136

Damascus, Syrian Arab Republic

E-mail: syriapfmprocurement@gmail.com

 

===================================================

 

Terms of Reference

SIFMIS Program Manager

Syria Integrated Financial Management Information System (SIFMIS)

1. Background and Context

The Government of the Syrian Arab Republic (GoS) is committed to rebuilding and modernizing its Public Financial Management (PFM) system as part of broader post-conflict reconstruction and institutional reform efforts. The Ministry of Finance (MoF) recognizes that a well-functioning Syria Integrated Financial Management Information System (SIFMIS) is essential to achieving transparent, accountable, and efficient management of public resources.

Strong government ownership, robust program management, and a pragmatic approach to implementation are critical success factors. The Syria Public Financial Management Capacity Strengthening Project (P512516) will finance the purchase, installation, integration, testing, user training, and commissioning of the SIFMIS, associated end-user devices, hardware, network infrastructure, and related support services. The envisaged Commercial Off-the-Shelf (COTS) SIFMIS will support procedural and control systems to ensure the legality, accuracy, and timeliness of fiscal information across core PFM functions including: budget preparation, budget execution, human resource and payroll management with biometric registration, expenditure control, cash management, purchasing, revenue management, fixed asset registration, inventory management, accounting, reporting, audit trails, and financial reporting and analytics.

The SIFMIS will include a seamlessly integrated centralized payroll module with biometric registration functionalities to enforce system-based entry/exit controls, position controls, grade/scale, location, and allowances. The payroll module will enhance the efficiency of human resource management (HRM) transactions under the control of the Ministry of Administrative Development (MoAD), enable the creation of a consolidated and up-to-date database of public sector employees, and facilitate reconciliation of personnel and payroll records.

The project will also finance the upgrade of the current Data Center at the MoF to meet data center functionality, capacity, uptime, and cybersecurity standards. SIFMIS connectivity will be through the Government Secure Network (GSN) managed by the National Authority for IT Services (NAITS).

Eight of the fifteen Governorate Finance Offices — Ministry of Finance (Central Department), Damascus, Damascus Rural, Aleppo, Tartous, Lattakia, Homs, and Hama — will be prioritized for the initial SIFMIS rollout, accounting for approximately eighty percent of average payment values. A rollout strategy will be developed to achieve full governorate coverage in the medium-term.

The State and Peace-Building Fund (SPF) has provided technical assistance to advance the Budget Classification and Chart of Accounts (BC-CoA) reform and develop functional requirements for the SIFMIS. These outputs provide the foundation for this assignment.

2. Objectives of the Assignment

The SIFMIS Program Manager combines program management leadership with business analysis and functional expertise, reflecting the need for a single accountable leader who can govern the vendor relationship at both the program level and the functional process level, and who can effectively represent MoF's interests in reviewing and approving all functional deliverables produced by the implementation vendor.

3. Scope of Work

The SIFMIS Program Manager will report to the Project Coordinator and will be responsible for the following:

3.1 Program Planning and Management

The SIFMIS Program Manager will develop and maintain a detailed program implementation plan covering all phases of the SIFMIS lifecycle — requirements validation, design, configuration and development, data migration, integration, testing, training, rollout, and post-go-live support. The Program Manager will track progress against agreed milestones, deliverables, and the overall project budget, escalating deviations and proposing corrective actions as needed.

notices.title: The selection of Siraj Product Manager
notices.description:
Ministry of Education and Human Resources Development

Modernizing Education, Skills, and Administrative Reforms (MASAR) Program

Terms of reference for Siraj Product Manager

Reference No.: JO-MOE-581318-CS-INDV

Program Background:

The Modernizing Education, Skills, and Administrative Reforms (MASAR) Program for Results (PforR) is a transformative, system-wide reform initiative anchored in Jordan’s Economic Modernization Vision (EMV). The MASAR Operation is designed to support the Ministry of Education and Human Resources Development in addressing foundational bottlenecks in access, quality, and relevance of education, with a dual emphasis on equity and efficiency. The operation aims to strengthen institutional capacity while enabling measurable improvements in learning outcomes and employability, particularly through early childhood education and labor market-aligned technical and vocational education and training (TVET), and digital transformation in education.

The program became effective in 2024, with a total financing envelope of USD 400 million, supported by the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD). It comprises two core components:

  • Program-for-Results (PforR): the principal financing instrument that disburses against verified achievement of results tied to government reform priorities.
  • Investment Project Financing (IPF): a complementary technical assistance (TA) component aimed at supporting the implementation of system-strengthening activities and accelerating the achievement of Disbursement Linked Indicators (DLIs).

MASAR is structured around four interlinked Results Areas (RAs) that are strategically aligned with key education-sector transition points and cross-cutting governance reforms:  

  • RA1: Home to School – Expanding Access to Foundational Learning. This includes (i) increasing equitable access to KG2, particularly in under-served districts and refugee-hosting communities; (ii) enhancing the quality of early childhood education through a revised KG1-KG2 curriculum and quality assurance mechanisms; and (iii) improving foundational literacy skills for Grades 1–3 through targeted pedagogical interventions and a comprehensive implementation plan.
  • RA2: School to Work – Increasing Access to Labor Market-Relevant TVET. MASAR seeks to improve the alignment of TVET with private sector needs by institutionalizing public-private partnerships, scaling apprenticeships, and expanding career guidance and employment pathways. This is complemented by the operationalization of an equivalency system that supports the portability and recognition of TVET qualifications, and enhanced use of learner trajectory data to inform student support services.
  • RA3: Strengthening Sector Governance and Efficiency. The program supports the operationalization of a restructured governance model for the education sector and introduces reforms to human resource management, with a particular focus on teacher recruitment, deployment, and professional development policies.
  • RA4: Digital Transformation in Education, to be introduced through the MASAR Additional Financing (AF), supporting digital and AI-enabled learning for students in Grades 4-12 and strengthening the institutional infrastructure needed for national-scale technology integration in education.

In addition to its core education objectives, MASAR embeds environmental and social sustainability principles across its implementation.

Ultimately, MASAR is designed to deliver measurable, inclusive, and sustainable improvements in Jordan’s education system. It expands access to early learning, strengthens foundational skills, improves graduate employability, strengthens digital skills, technology-enabled learning, and future-ready competencies, and reinforces institutional coherence through evidence-based policymaking. By supporting inclusive education and strengthening school-to-work transitions, the program directly contributes to Jordan’s long-term economic resilience and human capital development agenda.

Objectives of the Assignment:

Siraj is a curriculum-aligned AI learning platform supporting Jordanian classrooms. Siraj Product Manager is accountable for the end-to-end product vision and roadmap, ensuring Siraj delivers measurable learning value, operates with strong safeguarding appropriate for minors, and scales responsibly in partnership with the Ministry of Education. This role requires a combination of education expertise (learning science, learning experience design, curriculum, assessment) and AI product leadership (LLM behavior, evaluation, safety, and iteration at scale).

Roles and Responsibilities

  • Vision & Roadmap
  • Own Siraj’s multi-quarter roadmap aligned with MoE priorities and classroom realities.
  • Set prioritization principles that balance learning impact, learner engagement, usability, safeguarding, feasibility, and cost.
  • Learning Experience & Curriculum Integrity
  • Define the quality standard for Siraj’s learning support across grades/subjects (e.g., scaffolding, misconception handling, formative guidance, age-appropriate responses).
  • Map and optimize the end-to-end learner journey, ensuring the interface and AI interactions minimize extraneous cognitive load.
  • Maintain curriculum alignment and clear boundaries for what the platform should and should not do.
  • AI Quality, Evaluation, and Release Discipline
  • Establish measurable quality criteria for AI behavior (helpfulness, grounding, appropriateness, consistency, and pedagogical alignment).
  • Implement an evaluation approach that combines automated checks with structured human review, and use it to prevent regressions and guide iteration.
  • Safeguarding, Monitoring, and Incident Response
  • Own safeguarding for a minor-facing AI product, including boundaries, refusal behaviors, and safe redirection.
  • Operate monitoring and escalation processes: flagged conversation categories, severity levels, review workflows, response SLAs, and remediation.
  • Run human-in-the-loop sampling and rubric-based reviews; translate findings into corrective actions and continuous improvement.
  • Lead AI incident management (triage, mitigation, post-mortems) and embed prevention into release processes.
  • Stakeholder Leadership & Delivery Execution
  • Partner with MoE stakeholders, school leaders, and educators to align priorities, communicate tradeoffs, and maintain trust.
  • Drive cross-functional execution with engineering and design partners, ensuring consistent delivery and high-quality releases.
  • Enablement & Change Management
  • Define the enablement approach that drives effective adoption (guidance, playbooks, onboarding, and usage standards).
  • Advise on and help design teacher training where needed, using classroom feedback and usage data to target what matters (safe use, best practices, and instructional integration).
  • Measurement & Evidence-Based Decisions
  • Define success metrics for learning value, teacher value, trust/safety, active student engagement, and adoption.
  • Use data and feedback to make deliberate roadmap decisions and to continuously improve product performance.

Expected Deliverables

  • A clear product strategy and prioritized roadmap aligned with MoE goals and measurable KPIs.
  • A defined learning-quality standard operationalized through evaluation and release gates.
  • A functioning safeguarding operating model (monitoring, sampling, escalation, remediation loop).
  • Tangible improvements shipped that move adoption, trust, and learning-quality indicators.

Eligibility and Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Education, Learning Sciences, Instructional Design, Educational Technology, Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, or a closely related field.
  • 7+ years of experience working at the intersection of education, EdTech, digital learning, or AIenabled products, including in senior product, program, or learningexperience leadership roles.
  • Strong grounding in education theory, curriculum design, and assessment literacy (K–12).
  • Proven experience owning product strategy and roadmaps in complex, multi-stakeholder environments.
  • Strong AI product fluency (LLM behavior, retrieval/grounding concepts, evaluation methods, safety considerations).
  • Ability to translate ambiguity into standards, measurable outcomes, and execution plans.
  • Arabic fluency and Arabic-first product sensitivity strongly preferred.

Duration and location of the Assignment

Contract duration is 1 year with possible extension based on performance and availability of funding. Full-time presence is required. The hired individual will be based at the Ministry of Education and Human Resources Development, Amman, Jordan.

Submission

Interested candidates are invited to submit their résumé, cover letter, and any relevant certifications to the Tender Coordinator at the Ministry, in accordance with the submission deadline (date and time) specified on the Ministry’s website: https://moehrd.gov.jo/ar/international-tenders . Shortlisted candidates will be contacted for an interview

Through its regular and shock-responsive cash transfer windows, Baxnaano has reached hundreds of thousands of poor and vulnerable households throughout Somalia. The programme has also strengthened key social protection delivery systems, including participant targeting, payment delivery, grievance redress mechanisms, and the unified social registry (USR).

Building on these achievements, Baxnaano is now in a new phase supported by the World Bank-financed Building Opportunities and Outcomes in Social Protection and Youth Employment in Somalia (BOOST-YOU) Project (P507433), which deepens coverage, expands the program to four windows, and accelerates the transition to full government ownership and management. In its current phase, to be implemented between 2026 and 2029, Baxnaano operates through four programmatic windows: the Regular Window, the Shock-Response Window, the Early Response Human Capital Window, and the Economic Inclusion (EI) Window.

The EI Window builds on an initial pilot aimed at improving employment outcomes, income generation, and productive livelihoods among poor and vulnerable youth. It supports participants in increasing their productive capacity, improving income-earning opportunities, and strengthening long-term resilience. Baxnaano’s EI Window applies a structured and sequenced package of support along two economic inclusion tracks: 1. Wage employment and labour market integration; and 2. Self-employment and entrepreneurship. For each track, an overview of the support package is listed in Table 1.

Objective of the Assignment:

 The overall objective of this consultancy is to provide MoLSA, the World Bank, and other relevant stakeholders with timely, accurate, and independent assurance on programme implementation, output quality, emerging outcomes, the functioning of program processes and systems, and participant experiences. The TPM function will support improved programme oversight, strengthen accountability, identify implementation challenges and risks, and generate actionable recommendations to enhance the effectiveness, efficiency, and impact of the BOOST-YOU Project.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found in Annex I.

The Ministry of Labor Social Affairs now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. The Consultant shall provide the work performed, name, country and contact address of the Client (office and e-mail address and telephone number), date(s) of execution, name (s) of lead and associate firms, contract amount and financing sources.

Country                   Republic of Iraq

Assignment Title    Consultancy Services of Management Agent CAPEX

The Republic of Iraq has applied for financing from The World Bank toward the cost of the Iraq Railways Extension and Modernization Project (P507282 and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward Consulting Services. 
The consulting services (“the Services”) include management support to IRR to carry out the Project, including: 
    •    Establish effective Project management and control procedures by establishing the cost and schedule baseline and the reporting pro-form as for all components under the IREM Project.
    •    Review and comment with dedicated project teams and submit to IRR management for approval of projects’ documentation at every stage in each project delivery value chain—procurement, construction, and commissioning.
    •    Collect progress-related data and report projects’ progress to IRR Management.
    •    Develop, monitor, and manage IRR’s overall risk profile arising from the implementation of concurrent projects under the IREM Project.
    •    Coordinate management of concurrent projects and resolve any resourcing conflict between different project teams.
    •    Understand and interpret projects’ status and implications to determine whether the IRR Board requires authorization for any deviations from the agreed-upon project targets.
    •    Support for the reviewing the outputs of component 2 of IREM Project (studies, transaction advisory for mobilizing private sector resources) and manage E&S risks in all phases of their implementation (elaboration of ToRs, procurement procedures, contracting, evaluation of interim and final reports of the various consultants, etc.).
    •    Develop a training and development program for the IRR Projects’ staff in management of CAPEX projects. 
    •    It is foreseen that the duration of the overall service will last for 5 years.

The expected date for starting the assignment is May 2027. 

The Terms of Reference (TOR) for the primary procurement stage for the assignment are attached to this request for expressions of interest.

1.    General qualifications: Details of the company’s organization, core business, and years in business, relevant experience in railway infrastructure development, management of CAPEX projects, and technical and managerial capability of the firm to deliver the assignment.

1.1 Railway sector in Iraq

The performance of Iraq’s transport sector is essential for the efficient movement of goods and people. However, faced with almost four decades of conflict, neglect, and underinvestment, the sector is unable to provide valuable services to the industry and the residents of Iraq.
Even though the transport sector contributes 9% to Iraq's GDP, the sector suffers from inadequate maintenance and the government's inability to fund and operate aging infrastructure, leading to widespread deterioration. This has negatively impacted national and regional connectivity, economic growth, and traffic safety, while limiting private financing opportunities. Inefficiencies in public sector governance and SOE performance, as well as SOE indebtedness, have led to a weak transport and logistics performance, high private sector costs, and barriers to entry. In addition, weak sector governance and chronic underfunding impede the sector's growth and improvement. The Government of Iraq is fully committed to enhancing the efficiency of the railway transport sector and to increasing the transport market share of railways.
In May 2023, Iraq launched the Iraq Development Road Initiative, which aims to leverage its strategic geographical location for regional trade connectivity. This road and rail corridor is an integral part of Iraq’s development strategy, and it will connect Al Faw Grand Port on the Gulf to Europe via Iraq and Türkiye. GoI plans to develop the initiative in two stages: the first stage involves extending and modernizing the existing railway network and creating new connections from Al-Faw Seaport to the Türkiye border. The second stage will develop a 1,200 km greenfield railway link from Al-Faw Grand Port to the Türkiye border at an estimated cost of US$ 17 billion.

notices.title: Independent Technical QA Consultant – Architect
notices.description:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST
(Consultant Services – Individual Consultant)

Country: Republic of Kosovo
Project Name: Kosovo Comprehensive Approach to Health System Strengthening (KOMPAS)
Loan No.: IDA 75410
Assignment Title: Independent Technical QA Consultant – Architect
Reference No.: TBD
Issued on: 20 November 2026

Background

The Government of Kosovo has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Kosovo Comprehensive Approach to Health System Strengthening Project (KOMPAS), including its Additional Financing (AF) from the Pandemic Fund, and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The primary objective of this assignment is to provide independent technical quality assurance and professional advice to the Ministry of Health (MoH or “the Client”) on architectural designs and project plans for health infrastructure investments financed under KOMPAS, including the targeted refurbishment of laboratory spaces and other relevant facilities supported by the Project. The Consultant will review relevant technical documentation, assess conformity with applicable requirements, observe relevant pre-construction activities, and provide findings and recommendations to support the Client's decision-making on the designs’ completeness, technical consistency, functionality and compliance with applicable requirements. The role is advisory and does not include responsibility for design preparation, design approval, construction supervision, or contract administration.

The Consultant will be engaged on an intermittent basis for six (6) months from contract signature, with an estimated maximum input of sixty (60) person-days. Inputs will be requested and agreed with the PCU based on the needs and timing of KOMPAS-financed design and pre-construction activities.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment are attached to this Request for Expressions of Interest.

The Ministry of Health now invites eligible individual consultants (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested candidates should submit:

  • A Letter of Expression of Interest
  • A detailed Curriculum Vitae (CV)
  • Copies of diplomas and relevant certifications
  • References for similar assignments (if available)

Selection Method

The Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultants (IC) method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers.

Qualifications and Experience Requirements

The Consultant shall meet the following minimum qualifications:

  • A valid professional license as an architect (Category [A/B]), issued by the Chamber of Architects of the Republic of Kosovo (OARK) under Law No. 08/L-012 on the Chambers of Architects and Engineers in the Field of Construction, or a license issued outside Kosovo and recognized by the Chamber;
  • Continued validity of the license, and membership in good standing of the Chamber, for the full duration of the contract.
  • Master's degree in Architecture, or equivalent, from an accredited institution.
  • At least ten (10) years of professional experience in architectural design, technical review of architectural drawings and specifications, and quality assurance of building projects;
  • At least three (3) assignments involving independent technical review of architectural designs;
  • Experience in the design or technical review of at least three (3) healthcare facility projects (e.g., hospitals, primary healthcare centers);
  • Experience in the design or technical review of healthcare waste management and/or laboratory facilities is desirable.
  • Proficiency in CAD and architectural design software (e.g., AutoCAD, ArchiCAD, Revit or equivalent);
  • Thorough knowledge of Kosovo construction legislation, building regulations and technical standards;
  • Knowledge of international standards and guidelines for healthcare facility design is desirable;
  • Knowledge of applicable environmental, health and safety requirements relevant to healthcare infrastructure is desirable.
  • Fluency in Albanian and English, written and spoken;
  • Working knowledge of Serbian is desirable.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours 09:00 to 16:00.

Expressions of Interest must be delivered electronically (by e-mail) to the address below no later than 04 December 2026 at 16:00 local time. Expressions of Interest received after the deadline will not be considered.

Ministry of Health

Project Coordination Unit Kosovo Comprehensive Approach to Health System Strengthening (KOMPAS)
Pristina, Kosovo

Attn: Fanol Duli, Project Coordinator

Email: fanol.duli@rks-gov.net

CC: Blerim Çerkini, Procurement Specialist

Email: blerim.cerkini@rks-gov.net

 

 

TERMS OF REFERENCE

Country: Kosovo                            

World Bank Loan/Credit Name: Kosovo Comprehensive Approach to Health System Strengthening- KOMPAS

Project ID: P179831

Ref. No.: TBD

Assignment name:  Independent Technical QA Consultant – Architect

 

  1. Background

Referring to the Financing Agreement between the Republic of Kosovo and the International Development Association for the Kosovo Comprehensive Approach to Health System Strengthening Project (KOMPAS), the KOMPAS Project (P179831) was approved on 07 May, 2024. The Project Development Objective (PDO) is to strengthen institutional capacity and governance for quality of care in the Kosovo health system.

The following are the components of the project:

Component 1: Strengthening key health system building blocks for Quality of Care (QoC)

The objective of this component is to support aspects of public health/Pandemic Preparedness and Response (PPR), service delivery, and health financing (strategic purchasing), that will help unblock the bottlenecks in the structural and process of care. This component will include three sub-components, outlined below:

Subcomponent 1.1 Improving service delivery. This subcomponent is aligned with the strategic objectives of the forthcoming Health Sector Strategy for 2023-2030 and builds on the recommendations of the recent World Bank’s report highlighting the quality aspect of noncommunicable diseases (NCD) management in Kosovo.

Subcomponent 1.2: Developing and implementing strategic purchasing for quality. This subcomponent will support the development and implementation of key strategic purchasing elements which are not in place in Kosovo but are critical for both structural and process aspects of quality care.

Subcomponent 1.3 Strengthening public health and PPR. This subcomponent will build on activities carried out under the Kosovo Emergency COVID-19 Response Project (P173819) in the areas of PPR. It will support key areas of the Action Plan of the National Program on Communicable Diseases (2022) and the Action Plan for HCWM (2023).

Additional Financing (AF) resources support: (i) scaling up AMR surveillance and analytics; (ii) procurement of laboratory equipment and consumables based on national capacity assessments; (iii) strengthening biosafety and biosecurity through risk assessments, equipment, and standard operating procedures; and (iv) targeted refurbishment of laboratory spaces to improve workflows and accreditation readiness. The AF also funds expansion of HCWM infrastructure and practices, including equipment and operational systems, alongside workforce training for laboratory staff, frontline health workers, and epidemiological surge capacity (including training, simulation exercises, and emergency response preparedness)

Component 2: Developing an Integrated Health Information System (IHIS): The objective of this component is to support the design, development, and implementation of an integrated digital health ecosystem that is critical for the functioning of the entire health system. The foundational and key strategic IHIS building blocks will set the digitized health data environment to support health service delivery and decision-making.

This component will include three sub-components, outlined below:

Subcomponent 2.1: Establishing foundational building blocks of IHIS. This subcomponent will support the establishment of critical elements of foundational environment (Enterprise Architecture) for digital health systems implementation, including: (i) the legal and regulatory framework for transformed health services delivery through digital systems utilization; (ii) the assessment and design of Master Data Management standards and systems, such as foundational registries and common coding and classification systems; (iii) design and implementation of the Health Information Exchange services; and (iv) upgrade of hardware platforms on central locations and in health facilities.

Subcomponent 2.2: Digital health support for improvement in QoC. Implementation of Component 1 will require finalization of the implementation and upgrade of the basic health information system (BHIS). Currently, the BHIS is not fully implemented in all Primary Health Care (PHC) facilities and with full functionality. This subcomponent will support: (i) rolling out the BHIS to all PHC facilities (including finalization of patient empanelment and zoning); (ii) upgrading the BHIS functions (automatic update of codes from key registries and allowing dashboard and smart reporting on facility level); and (iii) upgrading the integration with e-Referrals system and introduction of e-Appointments.

Subcomponent 2.3: Implementation of IHIS strategic systems. The eHealth Feasibility Study envisages full digitalization of the health sector in Kosovo to improve the effectiveness and efficiency of service delivery, clinical decision support, health financing, pandemic preparedness and public health functions, supply chain for pharmaceuticals and nutraceuticals, health workforce management, and health system management and policy making.

AF financing under Component 2 strengthens and operationalizes digital foundations critical for real-time surveillance and data-driven response. The AF supports development and rollout of an integrated LIMS, enhanced disease surveillance and early warning systems, and improved interoperability between surveillance platforms, laboratory systems, and analytics tools under a One Health approach. Resources finance software development and adaptation, targeted IT hardware, and technical assistance to ensure alignment with the modular and interoperable IHIS architecture defined under KOMPAS. By embedding these systems within the broader health information exchange ecosystem, the AF enables timely data sharing, performance monitoring, and cross-border information exchange, amplifying the preparedness imp

1. The Government of Mozambique (GoM), through the Ministry of Finance (MF) and has received funding from the World Bank toward the cost of the Mozambique: Access to Finance & Economic Opportunities Project (Mais Oportunidades) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

 

2. The Consulting Services (“the Services”) include to produce a comprehensive, evidence-based Condition Assessment and an integrated Conservation and Presentation Design for both Manyikeni and Chibuene, providing the technical foundation for subsequent civil works, site management planning, and tourism infrastructure investments under MozTourisms. The Specific objectives are to:

  • Document the current physical and conservation condition of all heritage structures, archaeological deposits, and landscape elements at both sites.
  • Identify and prioritize threats — structural, environmental, biological, and anthropogenic — and assess their urgency.
  • Propose graded, phased conservation and stabilization interventions consistent with international standards (ICOMOS, UNESCO) and Mozambican heritage legislation.
  • Develop an architectural and landscape design concept for site presentation, interpretation infrastructure, and visitor management.
  • Produce technical specifications and cost estimates sufficient to proceed to procurement of civil works.
  • Provide recommendations for long-term integrated management

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be provided on request to the following e-mail: procurement.pled@gmail.com.

 

3. The Ministry of Finance (MF) now invites eligible Consultants to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services (brochures, description of similar assignments, experience in similar conditions, etc.). The firm or Consortium selected must be legally registered institutions with the qualifications and experience below.

The shortlisting criteria are:

 

a)Eligibility and legal status

  • Legally registered consulting firm (or joint venture) whose core business includes heritage conservation, archaeology, architecture or engineering applied to heritage sites, or cultural heritage consulting. A copy of the certificate of registration shall be submitted.
  • Eligible in accordance with the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, and not subject to debarment or sanctions by the World Bank Group.
  • Free of any conflict of interest. The selected firm, and any of its affiliates, shall be ineligible to provide goods, works or non-consulting services, including the civil works, resulting from or directly related to this assignment.

 

b) General experience

  • At least 10 years of operation in heritage conservation, archaeology or cultural heritage consulting.

 

c) Specific experience (assignments completed within the last 10 years)

  • At least 3 conservation or condition-assessment assignments at archaeological or historic sites, of which at least 1 at a UNESCO World Heritage or Tentative List site;
  • At least 2 assignments on dry-stone or masonry heritage structures; experience with Zimbabwe Tradition or comparable stonework is an advantage;
  • At least 1 coastal erosion assessment or mitigation design in a heritage or coastal setting, preferably in East Africa or the Indian Ocean;
  • At least 1 assignment producing heritage interpretation or site presentation designs;
  • At least 2 assignments in sub-Saharan Africa; experience in a Portuguese-speaking country, particularly Mozambique, is an advantage;
  • At least 1 assignment producing Bills of Quantities, cost estimates and technical specifications for civil works;
  • Experience in assignments financed by the World Bank or other multilateral or bilateral development partners is an advantage.

 

d) Technical and managerial capacity

  • Adequate organizational structure and permanent professional staff in the relevant disciplines (heritage architecture, archaeology, structural and coastal engineering, interpretation design).
  • Access, owned or subcontracted, to the equipment and software required for the assignment, including GNSS/GPS, photogrammetry/SfM, GIS and CAD and, where applicable, geophysical survey equipment.
  • Capacity to work and to produce all deliverables in both Portuguese and English.

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

 

4. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

 

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

 

5. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost Based Selection method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations.
