  3. El Ministerio de Obras Públicas y de Transporte invita a los proveedores cotizar los Bienes descritos en el Anexo 1: Requisitos del Comprador adjunto a esta SdC.

Fraude y Corrupción

  1. El Banco requiere el cumplimiento de sus Directrices Contra el Fraude y la Corrupción y de sus políticas y procedimientos de sanciones vigentes incluidos en el Marco de Sanciones del Grupo del Banco Mundial, conforme se describe en el apéndice de las Condiciones Contractuales (Apéndice A).
  2. En virtud de esta política, los Proveedores deberán permitir al Banco —y requerir que lo permitan sus agentes (hayan sido declarados o no), subcontratistas, subconsultores, prestadores de servicios, proveedores y personal— inspeccionar todas las cuentas, registros y otros documentos relativos a esta contratación directa y la ejecución de contratos (en el caso de adjudicación), y disponer que sean auditados por auditores designados por el Banco.

Elegibilidad de los Servicios (y los servicios Conexos, si corresponde)

  1. Todos los Bienes que hayan de contratarse de conformidad con la Orden de Compra y que sean financiados por el Banco podrán tener su origen en cualquier país sujeto al Párrafo 10.

Proveedores Elegibles

  1. En caso de que el Proveedor sea una Joint Venture (JV), todos los miembros serán responsables conjunta y solidariamente de la ejecución de todo el contrato de conformidad con los términos del contrato. La JV designará a un representante que tendrá la autoridad para realizar todos los negocios para y en nombre de todos y cada uno de los miembros de la JV durante el proceso de Solicitud de Cotización y, en caso de que la JV se adjudique el contrato, durante la ejecución del contrato.
  2. Un Proveedor puede tener la nacionalidad de cualquier país, sujeto a las restricciones de conformidad con los párrafos 9 y 10 en adelante. Se considerará que un Proveedor tiene la nacionalidad de un país si el Proveedor está constituido, incorporado o registrado y opera de conformidad con las disposiciones de las leyes de ese país, como lo demuestran sus términos de incorporación (o documentos equivalentes de constitución o asociación) y sus documentos registrales, según sea el caso. Este criterio también se aplicará a la determinación de la nacionalidad de los subcontratistas o subconsultores propuestos para cualquier parte de la orden de compra, incluidos los Servicios Relacionados.
  3. Las empresas y las personas pueden no ser elegibles si así se indica en el párrafo 10 a continuación y:
    1. como cuestión de ley o reglamentación oficial, el país del Prestatario prohíbe las relaciones comerciales con ese país, siempre que el Banco esté convencido de que dicha exclusión no impide la competencia efectiva para el suministro de Bienes o la contratación de las obras o servicios requeridos; o
    2. mediante un acto de cumplimiento de una decisión del Consejo de Seguridad de las Naciones Unidas adoptada en virtud del Capítulo VII de la Carta de las Naciones Unidas, el país del Prestatario prohíbe cualquier importación de Bienes o contratación de obras o servicios de ese país, o cualquier pago a cualquier país, persona o entidad de ese país.
  4. En referencia a los párrafos 6 y 9, para información de los proveedores, en la actualidad se excluyen de este proceso de contratación las empresas, bienes y servicios de los siguientes países:
    1. de conformidad con los párrafos 6 y 9 (a): ninguno.
    2. de conformidad con los párrafos 6 y 9 (b): ninguno.
  5. Un Proveedor que ha sido sancionado por el Banco, de conformidad con las Directrices de Anticorrupción del Banco, de acuerdo con sus políticas y procedimientos de sanciones vigentes según lo establecido en el Marco de Sanciones del GBM, como se describe en el anexo a las Condiciones de la orden de compra (Anexo A) párrafo 2.2 d., no será elegible para presentar una oferta o ser adjudicado o beneficiarse de otro modo de un contrato financiado por el Banco, financieramente o de otro modo, durante el período de tiempo que el Banco haya determinado. Una lista de empresas y personas excluidas está disponible en el sitio web externo del Banco: http://www.worldbank.org/debarr.
  6. Los Proveedores que sean empresas o instituciones de propiedad estatal en el país del Comprador pueden ser elegibles para competir y recibir un Contrato (s) solo si pueden establecer, de una manera aceptable para el Banco, que:
  1. son legal y financieramente autónomos;
  2. operan bajo la ley comercial; y
  3. no están bajo la supervisión del Comprador.
  1. Un Proveedor no deberá tener un conflicto de intereses. Cualquier Proveedor que tenga un conflicto de intereses será descalificado. Se puede considerar que un Proveedor tiene un conflicto de intereses a los efectos de este proceso de Solicitud de Cotizaciones, si el Proveedor:
    1. controla directa o indirectamente, está controlado por o está bajo control común con otro Proveedor que presentó una Cotización;
    2. recibe o ha recibido algún subsidio directo o indirecto de otro Proveedor que presentó una Cotización;
    3. tiene el mismo representante legal que otro Proveedor que presentó una Cotización;
    4. tiene una relación con otro Proveedor que presentó una Cotización, directamente o a través de terceros comunes, que lo coloca en una posición para influir en la Cotización de otro Proveedor, o influir en las decisiones del Comprador con respecto a este proceso de Solicitud de Cotizaciones;
    5. o alguna de sus afiliadas participó como consultor en la preparación del diseño o especificaciones técnicas de los Bienes, o Servicios Relacionados, que son objeto del proceso de Solicitud de Cotizaciones;
    6. o cualquiera de sus afiliadas ha sido contratada (o se propone contratarla) por el Comprador o Prestatario para implementar el Contrato;
    7. estaría proporcionando Bienes, obras o servicios distintos a los de consultoría que resulten de, o estén directamente relacionados con los servicios de consultoría para la preparación o implementación del proyecto especificado en esta Solicitud de Cotizaciones, que proporcionó o fueron provistos por cualquier afiliado que directamente o controla indirectamente, está controlado por, o está bajo control común con esa empresa;
    8. tiene una relación comercial o familiar cercana con un personal profesional del Prestatario (o de la agencia de ejecución del proyecto, o de un receptor de una parte del préstamo) que: (i) están directa o indirectamente involucrados en la preparación de la Solicitud de Cotizaciones o especificaciones y / o la evaluación de Cotizaciones, del Contrato sujeto; o (ii) estaría involucrado en la implementación o supervisión de dicho Contrato a menos que el conflicto derivado de dicha relación se haya resuelto de una manera aceptable para el Banco durante el proceso de Solicitud de Cotizaciones y la ejecución del Contrato Garantía de Cumplimiento.
  2. El proveedor adjudicado deberá presentar una garantía de Cumplimiento de Orden de Compra, por el valor del 10 % de la Orden de Compra, el cual podrá ser a través de un pagaré (ver anexo No. 4), este deberá otorgarse por el proveedor a favor del Estado y Gobierno de El Salvador en el ramo de Obras Públicas y de Transporte, para asegurar que cumplirá con todas lo establecido en la Orden de Compra y cuyo bienes y servicios serán entregados y recibidos a entera satisfacción.

Esta garantía deberá ser presentada en la Unidad de Compras Públicas, ocho (8) días hábiles posteriores a la orden de inicio, la vigencia de la garantía será por el plazo establecido en el contrato, más NOVENTA (90) DÍAS CALENDARIOS adicionales y estará vigente a partir de la suscripción del mismo.

Purchaser: Ministry of Environmental Protection and Agriculture of Georgia (MEPA)

Project: Georgia Resilient Agriculture, Irrigation and Land Project (GRAIL)

Contract title: Design, Development, Integration, Migration, Testing, Deployment, and Support of the Preferential Agro-Credit Project System (PACPS)

Country: Georgia

Loan No: 9504-GE

RFP No.: GRAIL/G/RFP/03

Issued on: October 02, 2026

1.        Georgia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Georgia Resilient Agriculture, Irrigation and Land Project (GRAIL), and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under the contract for the Design, Development, Integration, Migration, Testing, Deployment, and Support of the Preferential Agro-Credit Project System (PACPS).

2.        The Ministry of Environmental Protection and Agriculture of Georgia (MEPA) now invites sealed Proposals from eligible Proposers for the design, development, integration, migration, testing, deployment, and support of the Rural Development Agency's Preferential Agro-Credit Project System (RDA-PACPS). The Rural Development Agency (RDA) is a state agency under the Ministry of Environmental Protection and Agriculture of Georgia (MEPA), which is responsible for the administration of the “Preferential Agro-Credit Project.” The Project provides access to loans and leasing products by subsidizing the interest rates. The proposed PACPS will support RDA and MEPA in administering the Preferential Agro-Credit Project on a fully digital, centrally governed, and auditable basis. The system will comprise a Core Case Management System, a Transactional and Financial Reconciliation Module, an API and Integration Layer, and a Financial Institutions Portal, and will enable structured, API-based and portal-based interoperability with participating financial institutions (banks and leasing companies) and relevant state registers.

The installation, configuration, and full operational acceptance of the system shall be completed within twelve (12) months from the Effective Date of Contract, followed by an eleven (11)- month warranty.

The Project implementation will take place in Tbilisi, Georgia, primarily at MEPA’s and RDA’s central offices, with remote access and integration points across participating agencies.

3.        The procurement process will be conducted through international competitive procurement using Request for Proposals (RFP) as specified in the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers”, September  2025, (“Procurement Regulations”), and is open to all eligible Proposers as defined in the Procurement Regulations.

notices.description:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – SELECTION OF INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANTS)

 

Republic of Uzbekistan

Uzbekistan Digital Inclusion Project

Credit No.: 7425-UZ

 

Assignment Title: AI and Technology Ecosystem Adviser – International Individual Consultant

Reference No.: UZ-DIP-582910-CS-INDV

 

The Republic of Uzbekistan has received financing from the International Development Association toward the cost of the Uzbekistan Digital Inclusion Project. “Administration of Technology Park of Software and IT” LLC (IT Park), as the Implementing Agency, intends to apply part of the proceeds to engage an individual consultant as AI and Technology Ecosystem Adviser to the CEO of IT Park Uzbekistan, under Subcomponent 1.1 of the Project.

Under Subcomponent 1.1, the Project supports IT Park Uzbekistan’s AI and technology ecosystem agenda, including the implementation of AI strategy, priority AI initiatives, international technology partnerships and the commercialization of innovations, in line with Uzbekistan’s Strategy for the Development of Artificial Intelligence Technologies until 2030.

The Adviser will support the CEO of IT Park in prioritising, designing and delivering
AI ecosystem initiatives, partnerships and programmes, and in strengthening IT Park’s internal capacity to manage its AI agenda. Results are expected to contribute to the Project Development Objective through the creation of digital jobs, growth of AI-enabled IT services exports and inclusion of women, youth, persons with disabilities and the regions.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include, but are not limited to:

  • assessment of existing AI initiatives, capabilities and AI-readiness, and recommendation of priorities for a 12-month AI ecosystem work plan;
  • advice on strategic AI-related decisions, including decision papers on proposed AI programmes, centres, partnerships and investment initiatives;
  • identification and engagement of international technology partners, and support for cooperation proposals and authorised negotiations;
  • support for applied AI initiatives and the commercialisation of innovations developed by local startups and IT Park residents;
  • advice on mechanisms to attract AI talent and strengthen IT Park’s institutional capacity, including working sessions for IT Park staff;
  • support to the CEO across IT Park’s strategic directions (startups and venture investment; export and international positioning; Uzbekistan as a regional technology hub; support to IT Park residents and their AI adaptation; and R&D, data and robotics).

The assignment is proposed for a period of 12 months. The Adviser will work in a hybrid format, under a time-based contract.

To obtain the Terms of Reference for the assignment, please send your request to the following e-mail address: udip@it-park.uz.

“Administration of Technology Park of Software and IT” LLC now invites eligible individuals (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services: a curriculum vitae in the English language, and contact details of references.

The evaluation criteria are:

1) General Qualifications

  • University degree in technology, engineering, economics, management or a related field;
  • Fluent professional English;
  • Availability to work in person in Tashkent, Uzbekistan for at least 5 working days per month throughout the assignment.

2) Professional Experience

  • At least 8 years of experience in technology businesses, innovation, digital transformation or technology ecosystem development, including at least 5 years in leadership or strategic roles;
  • At least 3 years of substantive experience in managing AI projects or programmes, and at least one completed AI initiative with verifiable results and a clearly identified personal contribution;
  • Demonstrated experience in advising senior decision-makers, developing programmes involving companies, startups, universities, investors and public institutions, and supporting technologies through pilots, deployment, licensing, investment or entry into overseas markets;
  • Experience in international technology projects, negotiations with organisational leaders and cooperation with government bodies or development institutions;
  • Active professional relationships with AI companies, technology centres, customers and investors, supported by examples of collaboration.

3) Advantages

  • Russian or Uzbek proficiency;
  • Experience with recognised technology clusters or AI centres;
  • Experience working on MDB-financed projects (e.g., World Bank, ADB);
  • Experience in developing or transition economies, preferably in Central Asia/CIS, including AI ecosystem or policy development;
  • Knowledge of responsible AI and data governance frameworks.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers”, Fifth Edition, September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest, and to paragraph 3.21 on eligibility.

notices.description:
Request for Expressions of Interest for Consulting Service

Country: The Republic of the Gambia

Project Title: The Gambia Public Administration Modernization for Citizen Centric Service Delivery (PAMP) Project

Grant Number: IDA-E3820

Project ID NO:  P176924

 

Assignment Title: Technical Assistance to support identity verification of all civil servants and pensioners, including gender statistics

Procurement Method: Consultant Qualification Selection (CQS)    

Reference No.   GM-CPCU - MOFEA-514455-CS-CQS

  1. Background:

The Government of The Gambia, through the Ministry of Public Service (MoPS), is undertaking a civil service transformation initiative aimed at enhancing integrity, efficiency, and transparency across the human resource, payroll, and pension systems. This will involve a comprehensive identity verification exercise for all civil servants and pensioners, digitization of personnel records, and the establishment of a robust data and analytics platform, including gender-disaggregated statistics.

 

The initiative is part of broader public service reforms that seeks to eliminate ghost workers, introduce biometric verification, establish a centralized data warehouse, and modernize HR data management for informed decision-making.

To operationalize this vision, the Government requires the services of a qualified consulting firm with expertise in biometric systems, digital records management, data warehousing and data analytics.

  1. Objective of The Assignment:

The main objectives of this consultancy are to:

  • To support the verification of all civil servants and pensioners by developing and deploying a digital platform for data collection and analysis.
  • To prepare a cleaned-up establishment registry for all civil servants and pensioners.
  • Digitize personnel files to support efficient human resource management.
  • Use the establishment registry to update the payroll system and the Manpower Budget Framework.
  • Build institutional capacity for data governance, HR analytics, and sustainable system operation.
  • Establish a scalable data warehouse architecture and enable advanced workforce analytics for decision making.
  1. Scope of Work:

The consulting firm will be responsible for delivering the following:

3.1 Identity Verification and Census

  • develop and deploy an application for data collection and analysis.
  • Design establishment registry for civil servants and pensioners.
  • Support and monitor the verification exercise.
  • Conduct training on the designed data collection and analysis tools.
    • Develop user manuals, technical documentation, and standard operating procedures (SOPs).
  • Digitalize the personal files of civil servants to facilitate the verification and validation of the data collected.
    • Design and implement an automated document digitization system using OCR and AI.
    • Digitalize key HR records (e.g., application forms, appointment letters, birth certificates etc).
    • Store and index documents for easy retrieval and lifecycle management
  • Develop a scalable data warehouse architecture and enable advanced workforce analytics for decision making.
    • Develop an enterprise-grade data warehouse with ETL/ELT capabilities to ingest, transform, and store data from payroll, pension, HR, and flat files.
    • Build analytics-ready datasets and enable KPI dashboards for workforce and gender statistics.
    • Ensure on-premise data storage in line with national data protection and cybersecurity regulations.

Develop a framework to facilitate the updating of the payroll system and the Manpower Budget.

  1. Firm Qualification and Experience

The consulting firm must have:

  • Minimum of 10 years’ experience in developing digital platform for data collection and analysis, designing Human Resource establishment registry and conducting large scale data collection and verification exercise.
  • Proven track record in delivering at least three similar projects for governments, international agencies, or large public institutions.
  • Designed and implemented a document digitization system using OCR and AI to digitalize HR records.
  • Evidence of developing a data warehouse for an institution.
  • Experience of working with public sector institutions in West Africa, preferably The Gambia.
  • Collaboration with a Gambian firm with expertise in OCR, data warehousing or advanced business intelligence analytics will be an advantage

Full TOR Availability Notice

The full Terms of Reference (TOR) will be made available upon request. Please send your request via email to the address provided below. Contract duration is Seven (7) months.

notices.description:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REOI)

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

 

Country: Republic of Türkiye

Project: Türkiye Flood and Drought Management Project (P179313)

Loan No./Credit No./Grant No.: 9707-TR

Assignment Title: Flood Forecasting and Early Warning System in 6 River Basins (Marmara, Yeilrmak, Sakarya, Bat Akdeniz, Akarçay and Burdur)

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): TR-DGWM-573893-CS-QCBS

Market Approach: Open International Competition

Contract Type: Lump Sum

Contract Duration: 600 calendar days from the commencement date

 

1. The Government of the Republic of Türkiye has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Türkiye Flood and Drought Management Project (P179313), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

2. The consulting services (“the Services”) include the expansion, enhancement, integration and operationalization of the National Flood Forecasting and Early Warning System (TATUS) in six river basins (Marmara, Yeilrmak, Sakarya, Bat Akdeniz, Akarçay and Burdur). The Services comprise, among others: integration of the six targeted river basins into the existing TATUS platform and integration with five previously established basins to establish a unified national-scale forecasting network; development, calibration, validation and operationalization of hydrological forecasting models, including modelling of regulated/reservoir-controlled basins; integration and consolidation of meteorological, hydrological, satellite and third-party data, including real-time data acquisition and API interfaces; enhancement of alarm, warning and notification mechanisms; enhancement of the web-based user interface, visualization, reporting, role-based access and interoperability with relevant external systems; system architecture, database and software integration, cybersecurity, data protection, testing and quality assurance; and training, user documentation and support. The assignment also includes a six-month system operation phase during which the Consultant will operate the integrated system and resolve operational issues. The assignment is expected to be implemented mainly from Ankara, with activities in the six river basins identified above. The total contract duration is 600 calendar days from the commencement date.

3. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website: https://www.tarimorman.gov.tr/SYGM/Sayfalar/Detay.aspx?SayfaId=186 .

4. The Directorate General of Water Management (DGWM) of the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

5. A consulting firm is allowed to submit the expression of interest alone if it considers itself to be fully qualified on its own for the assignment, as it is not mandatory for consultants to associate with any other firm(s), whether foreign or local. Alternatively, if consultants themselves choose to associate to enhance their qualifications and capability for the assignment, then such associations may either be as a Joint Venture (i.e. all members of the joint venture shall be jointly and severally responsible) and/or Sub-consultants (i.e. the Consultant will be responsible, including for the services of the sub-consultant). In case of an association, the Consultants must explain in the EOI submission (a) the rationale for forming the association and (b) the anticipated role and relevant qualifications of each member of the Joint Venture and/or of each sub-consultant for carrying out the assignment, to justify the proposed inclusion of the JV members and/or sub-consultants in the association. Failure to provide the above explanation in the Expression of Interest may risk the association not being shortlisted for the assignment. Please note that in the evaluation of EOIs of associations for shortlisting purposes, only the qualifications of the JV members will be taken into account whereas the qualifications of proposed sub-consultants will not be considered.

6. The shortlisting criteria are as follows, in which specific experience of the Consultant relevant to the assignment will be considered of paramount importance:

i. General Experience of the Consultant (as a firm):

The Consultant (as a firm) should have been in the general consulting services sector for at least 10 year sprior to the deadline for submission of the expression of interest.

ii. Specific Experience of the Consultant (as a firm) relevant to the assignment in providing similar services under contracts of comparable size:

The Consultants (as a firm) should have specific experience providing similar consulting services under contracts completed within the last 10 years prior to deadline for submission of EOIs in the development of flood risk management plans (including for regulated river basins or those with dams), flood forecasting and early warning systems, hydrological units, real-time data comparison, web-based systems, and related information technologies.

Note: Key experts will not be considered during the shortlisting process.

7. To demonstrate their qualifications and experience in meeting the above shortlisting criteria, Consultants are requested to submit, at a minimum, the supporting documentation listed below. A consultant firm can only use its own qualifications and experience and not those of its parent, sister or subsidiary companies or its employees.

(i)      The firm's incorporation/trade/registration documents issued by the concerned government authority of the country of the firm.

(ii)     The firm’s company brochures including the core areas of business; and

(iii)    Completed Form-1 (attached to this Request for Expression of Interest) to provide information on similar contracts. This should include the name and reference number of the contract, a brief description of the scope of work, contract amount, period of the contract, name of the client and country of assignment, and role of the Consultant in the contract. Copies of completion certificates/references of clients of completed contracts are not required to be submitted with the EOI. In the subsequent stage, at the time of submission of proposals, the Client may request the shortlisted Consultants to submit such supporting completion certificates.

8. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraphs 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers: Procurement in Investment Project Financing (Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services) (September 2023), setting forth the World Bank's policy on conflict of interest.

9. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

10. Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours, from 10:00 to 16:00 (Turkish time).

11. Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, by mail or by e-mail) by 16:00 (Turkish time) on 25/12/2026

GENERAL PROCUREMENT NOTICE

Country: TURKMENISTAN
Project: TURKMENISTAN ONE HEALTH FOR PANDEMIC PREVENTION, FOOD SYSTEMS RESILIENCE, AND ECOSYSTEM HEALTH PROJECT
Sector: Agriculture, Health, and Environmental Protection
Pandemic PPR Grant No.: TF-C9689
Project ID No.: P512354

Turkmenistan has received financing in the amount of US$1.79 million from the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development, acting as administrator of the Pandemic Prevention, Preparedness and Response Trust Fund, toward the cost of the Turkmenistan One Health for Pandemic Prevention, Food Systems Resilience, and Ecosystem Health Project, and intends to apply part of the proceeds to payments for goods, non-consulting services, and consulting services to be procured under the Project.

The Project Development Objective is to strengthen Turkmenistan’s capacity to prevent, detect, and respond to priority zoonotic diseases, antimicrobial resistance, and food safety issues through the One Health approach.

The Project comprises three components.

Component 1. Strengthening One Health Governance

Preparation of the National One Health Action Plan, establishment of a national One Health digital platform, multisectoral coordination and training, and review of veterinary legislation and regulations.

Component 2. Improving One Health Prevention, Early Detection and Response Systems

Strengthening veterinary, environmental, and public health surveillance and laboratory capacity through equipment, reagents, supplies, technical assistance, training, and laboratory accreditation.

Component 3. Project Management, Monitoring and Evaluation, and Learning

Support to the Project Implementation Unit for project management, procurement, financial management, environmental and social requirements, monitoring and evaluation, and learning.

The goods and consulting services expected to be procured through open international competitive procurement include the following.

Goods

  1. Veterinary tools, a vehicle with built-in disinfection equipment, and chemical protective equipment for the Ministry of Environmental Protection and the State Veterinary Service.

  2. Laboratory equipment, reagents, and supplies for the State Veterinary Service.

  3. Specialized laboratory equipment, reagents, and supplies for the Ministry of Environmental Protection.

  4. Field, wildlife monitoring, and related equipment for the Ministry of Environmental Protection.

  5. IT equipment for the Ministry of Health and Medical Industry and the Ministry of Environmental Protection under a single procurement package.

  6. Testing equipment and reagents for the Ministry of Health and Medical Industry.

  7. IT and office equipment, including furniture, for the Project Implementation Unit under a separate procurement package.

Consulting Services

  1. Preparation of the National One Health Action Plan and coordination of One Health activities with development partners.

  2. Establishment of a national One Health digital platform.

  3. Cross-sectoral training and monitoring of the implementation of agreed project work plans.

  4. External audit of the Project.

  5. Assessment of the legal framework for infectious animal diseases, review and updating of legislation on priority zoonotic diseases, and review of veterinary regulations and standard operating procedures, regulations related to antimicrobial resistance, and food safety guidelines.

  6. Development of a veterinary surveillance system and professional training for veterinarians and other stakeholders.

Procurement of contracts financed by the World Bank will be conducted through the procedures specified in the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, dated September 2025 (Procurement Regulations), and is open to all eligible firms and individuals as defined in the Procurement Regulations. Specific procurement notices for contracts subject to open international competitive procurement, including requests for expressions of interest for consulting services, will be published, as they become available, on the World Bank’s external website and on the official One Health Project page of the Ministry of Finance and Economy of Turkmenistan at https://fineconomic.gov.tm/one-health.

MINISTRY OF GREEN ECONOMY AND ENVIRONMENT

 

                               REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST

                               INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT SELECTION

                                                       OPEN-NATIONAL

 

The Government of the Republic of Zambia (GRZ), through the Ministry of Green Economy and Environment (MGEE), developed the Eastern Province Jurisdictional Sustainable Landscape Program (EP-JSLP). The EP-JSLP seeks to generate payments for measured, reported, and verified Emission Reductions (ERs) from reduced deforestation, forest degradation, enhancement of forest carbon stocks (REDD+), agriculture, and other land use (AFOLU) sectors, and distribute the payments according to an agreed Benefit Sharing Plan. By curbing rapid agricultural expansion and increasing the benefits derived from forestry and agriculture, the program aims to reduce emissions by approximately 29 million tons and increase communities' resilience to climate change. 

 

The Ministry seeks to recruit suitably qualified and experienced individuals under the Eastern Province Jurisdictional Sustainable Landscape Programme Implementation Unit in Chipata for the following positions on  two year renewable contracts;

 

  1. JOB TITLE; MONITORING, REPORTING AND VERIFICATION TECHNICAL OFFICER

 

1.1   JOB PURPOSE

 

The Monitoring, Reporting and Verification Technical Officer’s primary responsibility is to ensure the project produces the results specified in the project document, to the required quality standard and within the specified time and cost.

1.2 RESPONSIBILITIES

 

  1. Lead the delivery of technical activities for the project with an emphasis on producing the monitoring reports required to receive payments from the World Bank;
  2.  Working with sector-lead institution officers (Energy, Agriculture and Forestry) to deliver high-quality data and calculations required as input for producing the monitoring reports and associated documents;
  3. Oversee and coordinate the responses to the findings of the Independent Validation and Verification Body and any changes needed to the monitoring reports and the associated documents;
  4. Lead the formulation of annual/multi-year work plan for MRV-related activities in consultation with sector lead institution and other relevant stakeholders;
  5. Work closely with sector leads, traditional leaders, community leaders, and private sector partners in developing and maintaining the MRV systems, including standard operating procedures and sampling frameworks required to produce the data and calculations for receiving the payments for emission reductions;
  6.  Coordinate data collection at the district and chiefdom level for Agriculture, Energy and Forestry;
  7. Coordinate the data collection needed for the implementation of the Benefit Sharing Plan and determine the share of the different beneficiaries based on performance in the delivery of ERs
  8. Provide project-related MRV inputs to the national MRV system and other national development planning processes as necessary;
  9. Design and organize refresher capacity-building and knowledge-sharing activities on MRV, mobilize appropriate resource persons, and serve as trainer/resource person as necessary;
  10. Review technical aspects of AFOLU carbon project activities and guide project implementing partners regarding project typology, methodological requirements, and mechanics of carbon measuring, reporting, and verification;

 

1.3 QUALIFICATIONS

 

  1. Degree in applied natural sciences such as forestry, ecology, natural resources, biogeochemistry, GIS or remote sensing, Development Economics/Planning, Land Use Planning, Environmental Management, Agriculture and related qualifications. Coursework in GIS analysis, remote sensing, and tropical forest systems may also be considered
  2. A Master’s Degree in applied natural sciences such as forestry, ecology, natural resources, biogeochemistry, GIS or remote sensing, Development Economics/Planning, Land Use Planning, Environmental Management, Agriculture and related qualifications will be an added advantage;

 

    1. COMPETENCIES

 

  1. Organized, detail- and results-oriented;
  2. Should be a good team player and self-starter with the ability to work under minimum supervision;
  3. Able to work collaboratively in a multi-sectoral team yet self-manage deliverables;
  4. Able to work under physically challenging circumstances during field visits;
  5. Able to train, motivate, and manage field crews with different degrees of experience and education;
  6. Excellent oral and written communication skills in English. Spoken technical environmental Chichewa/Nyanja will be an added advantage; and
  7. Exceptionally computer literate, including complete mastery of Microsoft Excel, Word, and PowerPoint.

 

    1. WORK EXPERIENCE
  2. Minimum of 5 years of experience with carbon projects, including an affinity with accreditation programs and standards for both the compliance and voluntary markets;
  3. Experience with biomass inventories in forest systems;
  4. Familiar with basic biogeochemistry in forest and agricultural ecosystems, including understanding of terrestrial carbon quantification;
  5. Practical understanding of mathematical and statistical concepts.
  6. Minimum of 5 years post-qualification experience with at least 3 years in a management role;
  7. Work experience with any other donor-funded projects, including the World Bank, would be an added advantage;
  8. Experience in technical report writing and presentation;
  9. Experience in MRV implementation;
  10. Experience in project implementation of community-based activities in the AFOLU sectors;
  11. In-depth knowledge of all AFOLU market standards, guidelines, and protocols. Knowledge of the Initiative for Sustainable Forest Landscape (ISFL) requirements is an added advantage;
  12. Direct experience in carbon development work and methodologies for AFOLU projects;
  13. Experience in livelihood and community-driven development work;
  14. Proven track record in the management of national, rural, community development, and/or sustainable development projects/programs;
  15. Experience working in an inter-disciplinary environment with multiple stakeholders;
  16. Relevant work experience in Eastern Province would be an added advantage.\

 

2.0 JOB TITLE: ASSISTANT ACCOUNTANT

 

2.1 JOB PURPOSE

The Assistant Accountant shall report to the Program Accountant and shall assist the Program Accountant in providing financial and accounting services to the project and supporting the management team in ensuring program resources are used with due attention to economy, efficiency, and effectiveness.

2.2 RESPONSIBILITIES

 

  1. To prepare and process accounting documents for payments to staff, suppliers, contractors, consultants and other service providers;
  2. To run bank errands and manage day-to-day transactions;
  3. To ensure timely conduct and finalization of audits of Project financial records, statements, and reports on a regular basis and provide information to the Accountant;
  4. To process and record project financial transactions in the financial management system and keep all ledgers and cashbooks up to date;
  5. To carry out reconciliations of accounting records/books such as bank reconciliations, fixed assets, stores/inventories, imprest, etc
  6. To sensitize staff on the adherence to financial regulations in handling project finances and ensure adherence to the Public Finance Management Act, 2018 or as may be revised;
  7. To assist the Program Accountant in monitoring the various bank accounts opened in the district and in reviewing expenditure returns;
  8. Reviewing District financial reports for accuracy and meticulously tracing errors back to their source; and
  9. To undertake any other duties as may be assigned by the Program Accountant.

notices.title: Recruitment of a Procurement Specialist to Support the Liberia Urban Resilience Project (LURP)
notices.description:
Republic of Liberia

Ministry of Public Works

South Lynch Street

Monrovia, Liberia

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REOI)

INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT SELECTION

COUNTRY: Republic of Liberia NAME OF PROJECT: Liberia Urban Resilience Project (LURP) PROJECT ID: P169718 CREDIT/GRANT NO.: IDA-7122-LR / IDA E-041-LR ASSIGNMENT: Recruitment of a Procurement Specialist for the Liberia Urban Resilience Project (LURP) REFERENCE NO.: LR-MPW-581045-CS-INDV

1. Background

The Government of the Republic of Liberia, through the Ministry of Public Works (MPW), is implementing the Liberia Urban Resilience Project (LURP), with financing from the International Development Association (IDA) of the World Bank and co-financing from the French Development Agency (AFD).

The Project Development Objective (PDO) is to increase flood resilience and access to urban infrastructure in underserved neighborhoods in Greater Monrovia and to improve urban infrastructure planning and management in Liberia.

The Project comprises four components:

  • Component 1: Climate-Resilient Infrastructure and Urban Upgrading. Supports resilient infrastructure for climate risk management, neighborhood upgrading, and market improvements.
  • Component 2: Strengthening Integrated Resilient Urban Development Capacity. Supports improvements in laws, regulations, building codes, permitting processes, climate-resilient spatial development planning, revenue mobilization, financial sustainability, and infrastructure operations and maintenance.
  • Component 3: Contingency Emergency Response Component (CERC). Provides a mechanism for the rapid reallocation of undisbursed project funds to respond to eligible emergencies or crises.
  • Component 4: Project Management. Supports project coordination, procurement, financial management, environmental and social safeguards, monitoring and evaluation, and other operational activities.

The Project is implemented through a Project Management Unit (PMU) domiciled at the Ministry of Public Works. The PMU is responsible for coordinating and overseeing the implementation of project activities in accordance with the applicable financing agreements, project implementation arrangements, and development partner requirements.

In view of the growing procurement requirements of the Project, the Ministry of Public Works, through the Liberia Urban Resilience Project, seeks to recruit an experienced and qualified Procurement Specialist to provide technical and operational support to the Project Management Unit (PMU) in the implementation of procurement activities under the Project. The Procurement Specialist shall work under the direct supervision of the Senior Procurement Specialist and the overall management oversight of the Project Coordinator (PC), while maintaining effective coordination with relevant PMU staff, technical departments and other stakeholders to ensure that procurement activities are undertaken efficiently, transparently and in accordance with the applicable World Bank Procurement Regulations, Financing Agreements, approved procurement plans and relevant national procurement requirements.

2. Objective of the Assignment

The objective of the assignment is to support the PMU in the efficient, transparent and timely implementation of procurement activities under LURP in accordance with the applicable World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, Financing Agreement, approved PPSD and Procurement Plan, Project Implementation Manual, and applicable national requirements. The Procurement Specialist shall provide technical and operational support to the Senior Procurement Specialist in ensuring that procurement arrangements contribute to Value for Money, timely project implementation and achievement of the Project Development Objective. All assigned responsibilities shall be undertaken under the direct supervision of the Senior Procurement Specialist and the overall management oversight of the Project Coordinator.

 

3.  Roles and Responsibilities

Under the direct supervision of the Senior Procurement Specialist and the overall management oversight of the Project Coordinator, the Procurement Specialist shall provide technical and operational support in the planning, processing, implementation, monitoring, and documentation of procurement activities under the Liberia Urban Resilience Project (LURP), in accordance with the applicable procurement policies, procedures, guidelines, and project requirements.

In carrying out these functions, the Procurement Specialist shall perform the following duties and responsibilities as outlined in this Terms of Reference (TOR) in coordination with the Senior Procurement Specialist and other relevant PMU personnel, as appropriate:

 

  • Support the Senior Procurement Specialist in the preparation and periodic updating of the Project Procurement Strategy for Development (PPSD), including appropriate market research and market analysis, procurement approaches, packaging strategies and assessment of procurement risks, consistent with the applicable World Bank Procurement Regulations
  • Support the Senior Procurement Specialist in preparing, updating and monitoring the Procurement Plan through STEP, ensuring that procurement activities, procurement methods, review arrangements, estimated costs and implementation timelines are accurately reflected and periodically updated. Monitor procurement milestones against approved STEP timelines and promptly identify delays and proposed corrective actions.
  • Support the Senior Procurement Specialist in ensuring that procurement plans and process comply with the applicable World Bank’s requirements/ guidelines and the arrangements defined in the financing agreements
  • Assist in preparing and facilitating the publication of procurement notices, invitations for bids, requests for expressions of interest and other solicitation documents, under the guidance of the Senior Procurement Specialist;
  • Provide technical and procedural procurement support to PMU staff and project stakeholders on applicable national and development partner procurement policies and requirements, in coordination with the Senior Procurement Specialist;
  • Support the preparation and review of evaluation criteria, evaluation methodologies and minimum qualification requirements for inclusion in bidding documents and requests for proposals, subject to review by the Senior Procurement Specialist.
  •  Assist in preparing and reviewing invitations for bids, bidding documents, requests for expressions of interest and requests for proposals for procurement packages under the Project, in accordance with applicable procurement requirements;
  • Facilitate bid/proposal evaluation processes in accordance with the applicable procurement procedures, including supporting the constitution and orientation of evaluation committees, providing procedural guidance, serving as secretary where assigned, and supporting preparation of evaluation reports, while ensuring that evaluation judgments and recommendations remain the responsibility of the duly constituted Evaluation Committee;
  • Review procurement-related aspects of draft contracts, amendments, extensions and other contractual instruments and submit observations, advice and recommendations to the Senior Procurement Specialist for review and onward consideration by the Project Coordinator, as appropriate;
  • Support the Senior Procurement Specialist in establishing and maintaining a procurement monitoring system, including appropriate Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), to track procurement progress, processing timelines, contract awards, procurement values, delays, outstanding approvals and corrective actions, and prepare periodic updates to facilitate management decision-making;
  • Support procurement-related aspects of contract management, including monitoring contract award and effectiveness, securities, contractual milestones, amendments, extensions, complaints and procurement records, while coordinating with designated contract managers, engineers and technical specialists responsible for technical contract administration;
  • Maintain an organized procurement filing and archiving system, ensuring that procurement documents, correspondence, approvals, evaluation reports and contract records are properly documented and readily available for audits, reviews and donor supervision missions;
  • Assist the Senior Procurement Specialist in monitoring the progress of procurement activities relating to goods, works, non-consulting services and consulting services against the approved Procurement Plan and implementation schedules;
  • Prepare procurement inputs and updates for project progress reports and other management reports and submit them to the Senior Procurement Specialist for review and onward submission through the established PMU reporting arrangements;
  • The Consultant shall maintain the confidentiality of procurement, commercial and other non-public project information obtained during the assignment and shall promptly disclose any actual, potential or perceived conflict of interest in accordance with the applicable World Bank Procurement Regulations.
  • Support the Senior Procurement Specialist in providing procurement-related orientation, knowledge sharing and capacity-building support to PMU staff and other relevant project stakeholders, as required;
  • Regularly update procurement information and contract management records in STEP, under the guidance and supervision of the Senior Procurement Specialist, ensuring consistency between the system and the official procurement records;
  • Perform other procurement-related duties and responsibilities assigned by the Senior Procurement Specialist, consistent with the objectives and scope of this TOR, under the overall management oversight of the Project Coordinator.

 

4. Minimum Qualifications and Experience:

The suitable candidate for this position should have the following minimum qualifications and experience:

  • At least a bachelor’s degree in Procurement and Supply Chain Management, Economics, Management, Engineering, Social Sciences, Business Administration, Public Administration, Law or another relevant discipline. A master’s degree or relevant professional procurement qualification or training, particularly in World Bank-financed procurement, shall be an advantage.
  • Professional Experience: At least five (5) years of relevant professional experience in public procurement, including at least two (2) years of experience supporting procurement activities under projects financed by the World Bank or other international development partners. Experience in infrastructure or urban development projects shall be an advantage.
  • Procurement Categories: Demonstrated practical experience in procurement involving goods, works, non-consulting services and consulting services, including preparation of solicitation documents, procurement processing, evaluation process support, contract award documentation and procurement monitoring.

notices.description:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRM SELECTION)

 

Country:                                             Independent State of Samoa

Name of Project:                              Samoa Finance Sector Resilience and Development Project (SFSRDP) 2025 – 2029 (World Bank Financed Project P181456)

Loan No./Credit No./Grant No.:      IDA – E3780

Assignment Title:                              Diagnostic assessment for a National Retail Payment Switch

Reference No.:                                   CBS/CS/004

 

1. Introduction:

The Government of Samoa has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the SFSRDP P181456 and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The Central Bank of Samoa invites eligible consulting firms ("Consultants") to express their interest in providing consulting services to conduct a diagnostic assessment for a national retail payment switch.

The objective of this assignment is to undertake a diagnostic assessment of Samoa's retail payments ecosystem and evaluate the need, feasibility, and potential design options for establishing a National Retail Payment Switch.

Interested consulting firms should provide information demonstrating that they possess the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services.

This REOI is being issued for the purpose of establishing a shortlist of qualified consulting firms who will subsequently be invited to submit detailed technical and financial proposals under the Quality and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method.

 

2. Background:

The Central Bank of Samoa (CBS) is the monetary authority responsible for maintaining financial stability, managing currency issuance, and overseeing the payment systems in Samoa.

Under the Samoa Finance Sector Resilience and Development project supported by the World Bank, the CBS is pursuing initiatives to strengthen the national payments ecosystem, increase digital financial inclusion, improve payment efficiency, and support the country's broader digital transformation agenda. As electronic payment channels continue to expand across banks, mobile money operators, government agencies, merchants, and consumers, the need for more efficient interoperability arrangements has become increasingly important.

Currently, retail payment transactions may be processed through bilateral arrangements, proprietary networks, or international payment schemes, resulting in potential inefficiencies, higher transaction costs, limited interoperability, and constraints on innovation. A National Retail Payment Switch could provide a shared infrastructure enabling seamless, secure, and real-time interoperability among payment service providers.

Before making investment and policy decisions, CBS seeks the services of a consultancy firm to conduct a comprehensive diagnostic assessment to determine whether a National Retail Payment Switch is necessary, feasible, and economically viable, and if so, to identify the most appropriate implementation model for Samoa

 

3. Objective of the Assignment:

The objectives of the assignment include:

  1. Assess the current state of retail payment systems and interoperability arrangements.
  2. Identify gaps, inefficiencies, and constraints within the existing payment ecosystem.
  3. Evaluate current and future demand for interoperable retail payment services.
  4. Assess the business, technical, operational, regulatory, and financial viability of a National Retail Payment Switch.
  5. Examine alternative interoperability models and determine whether a national switch is the most appropriate solution.
  6. Provide recommendations and an implementation roadmap, if deemed necessary.

 

4. Scope of Services:

The Consultant will be expected to undertake activities including, but not limited to:

Task 1: Inception Phase and stakeholder consultation

Task 2: Assessment of the current payment ecosystem

Task 3: Gap Analysis

Task 4: Assessment of the Need for a National Retail Payment Switch

Task 5: Evaluation of Alternative Models

Task 6: Design Considerations (If a Switch is Recommended)

Task 7: Implementation Roadmap

 

5. The detailed Terms of Reference for the Assignment is provided in the Annex of this document.

 

6. The Central Bank of Samoa now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

 

7. A consulting firm is allowed to submit the expression of interest alone if it considers itself to be fully qualified on its own for the assignment, as it is not mandatory for consultants to associate with any other firm(s), whether foreign or local. Alternatively, if consultants themselves choose to associate to enhance their qualifications and capability for the assignment, then such associations may either be as a Joint Venture (i.e. all members of the joint venture shall be jointly and severally responsible) and/or Sub-consultants (i.e. the Consultant will be responsible, including for the services of the sub-consultant). In case of an association, the Consultants must explain in the EOI submission

(a) the rationale for forming the association and

(b) the anticipated role and relevant qualifications of each member of the Joint Venture and/or of each subconsultant for carrying out the assignment, to justify the proposed inclusion of the JV members and/or sub-consultants in the association.

Failure to provide the above explanation in the Expression of Interest may risk the association not being shortlisted for the assignment. Please note that in the evaluation of EOIs of associations for shortlisting purposes, only the qualifications of the JV members will be taken into account whereas the qualifications of proposed sub-consultants will not be considered.

 

 

8. The shortlisting criteria are as follows, in which specific experience of the Consultant relevant to the assignment will be considered of paramount importance:

    1. Demonstrated experience in assignments of comparable scope, specifically in conducting diagnostics and advisory services for national or regional payment systems, with a focus on retail payment switch design, implementation, or assessment within the last 10 years.
    2. Proven track record in supporting the modernization of payment systems to enhance efficiency, security, and interoperability of digital financial services, including experience with regulatory and supervisory frameworks for payment systems in developing country contexts.
    3. Experience advising central banks, financial sector regulators, or payment system operators on the development, evaluation, or integration of payment infrastructure, including interoperability standards (e.g., API, QR) and digital financial services ecosystems.
    4. Familiarity with financial inclusion strategies and demonstrated capacity to assess payment system use cases that promote access to formal financial services and reduce remittance costs
    5. Documented organizational systems and methodologies for conducting diagnostics, stakeholder consultations, and technical assessments in the context of payment system modernization.
    6. Capacity to address data protection, cybersecurity, and business continuity considerations relevant to payment system infrastructure, as required for robust and resilient digital financial services.
    7. Ability to coordinate with the Central Bank of Samoa and other relevant stakeholders, reflecting experience in multi-institutional environments and government-led financial sector reforms.
    8. Sufficient organizational resources to field a multidisciplinary team with expertise in payment systems, digital finance, regulatory analysis, and IT systems, appropriate to the assignment’s scope and complexity
    9. Compliance with the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (Fifth Edition, September 2023) and absence of conflict of interest or debarment
    10. If joint ventures or subconsultants are proposed, the lead firm must be clearly identified, and the proposal must specify how relevant experience will be aggregated to meet the above requirements.

The Consultants should demonstrate availability of and/or access to the key experts for the performance of the services described in the TOR (e.g., by providing a list of key experts they are working with). The Consultants should demonstrate sound administrative and financial capacity. Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

 

9. Eligibility and Shortlisting Criteria:

Interested consulting firms must:

  • Be legally registered entities.
  • Have been in operation for at least 15 years.
  • Have no conflict of interest related to this assignment.
  • Not be subject to suspension, debarment, or ineligibility by any applicable authority, development partner, or international financing institution.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include route selection and survey, feasibility study, detailed engineering design, Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) and preparation of tender documents for Lot I:  Feasibility study & detail design of Key kokab - Gelkem- Kelt Rural Access Roads (30 Km) in Maji Woreda &  Duku-Tulgit-Haro Rural Access Roads (20 Km) in Surma Woreda  Lot II: Feasibility study & detail design of Nada-Kumba-Bunanta- Meshgebezh-Shallo Rural Access Roads (50 Km) in Goba Woreda & Shasha-Kira- Aduba Rural Access Roads (35 Km) in Meanit Shasha Woreda.  Lot III:  Feasibility study & detail design of Turga River Medium span bridge (16m) Goba woreda & Kibish River Large span bridge (70m) in Anjo Kebele, Surma Woreda.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

LOWLANDS LIVELIHOOD RESILIENCE PROJECT – PHASE II (LLRP-II)

Credit No.: 7519-ET

Assignment Title: Consultancy Services for Hydrogeological and Geophysical Investigation for Groundwater Development at Nine (9) Drilling Locations in Dunyar, Shilabo (two sites), Dambel, Guradhamole, Lagahida, Mayamuluko, Harawo and Hadhagala Woredas, Somali Regional State

Reference No.: ET-SOM-RPCU-570299-CS-QCBS

The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia has received financing from the International Development Association (IDA) of the World Bank and the International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD) for the Lowlands Livelihood Resilience Project – Phase II (LLRP-II) and intends to use part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include hydrogeological and geophysical investigations to identify, assess and recommend technically feasible, sustainable, climate-resilient, environmentally sound and socially acceptable groundwater drilling sites for water supply (domestic and livestock) and, where applicable, irrigation development at nine (9) drilling locations in eight (8) woredas of Somali Regional State, namely: Dunyar Woreda, Siti Zone (Asli kebele); Shilabo Woreda, Korahey Zone (Qudha’shir and Miyir Kaynan kebeles – two sites); Dambel Woreda, Siti Zone (Dalamane kebele); Guradhamole Woreda, Liban Zone (Dektah kebele); Lagahida Woreda, Erer Zone (Busa kebele); Mayamuluko Woreda, Erer Zone (Magaalacad kebele); Harawo Woreda, Siti Zone (Darcade kebele); and Hadhagala Woreda, Siti Zone (Geedwayn kebele). The Client may adjust the final locations and number of sites during implementation depending on field conditions and project priorities.

The Services comprise: review of existing information and preparation of an Inception Report (including a data gap register, stakeholder engagement plan and security management plan); reconnaissance survey and baseline assessment, including mapping of seasonal livestock migration routes, grazing areas, existing water points and customary water rights; stakeholder consultation, conducted in the Somali language, with pastoral and agro-pastoral communities, customary institutions, women, youth and vulnerable groups; hydrogeological mapping, including assessment of transboundary aquifers; estimation of groundwater potential, recharge and likely yields using empirical and analogue methods; geophysical surveys (a minimum of three Vertical Electrical Soundings per site, i.e. at least twenty-seven (27) VES) and their interpretation, with a primary and at least one alternative drilling point for each site; sampling of existing water points and laboratory analysis for drinking, livestock and irrigation suitability; environmental and social impact assessment in accordance with the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) and IFAD requirements, including preparation of Environmental and Social Management Plans (ESMPs); uncertainty, data gap and risk management, including site confidence classification, site risk registers and a decision matrix presented at a validation workshop; groundwater development planning; establishment of a GIS database and maps; capacity building of Client staff; estimation of the drilling contract period; and preparation of preliminary engineering recommendations, draft bidding documents based on the World Bank Standard Procurement Documents (technical specifications, drawings and bills of quantities, including drilling-risk provisions) and the Engineer’s cost estimate for the subsequent borehole drilling and test pumping works.

The assignment is a pre-drilling investigation based on desk study, field reconnaissance, hydrogeological mapping, geophysical surveys, sampling of existing water points and empirical estimation. It does not include test well (exploratory borehole) drilling, borehole construction or pumping tests, which will be procured under a separate works contract.

The implementation period is three (3) calendar months from the date of commencement, and the assignment is expected to start in December 2026.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained at the address given below.

Somali Regional State, Office of the President, Lowlands Livelihood Resilience Project (LLRP-II) Regional Project Coordination Unit now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

(a)  Core business and years in business: the firm’s core business shall be in groundwater/hydrogeological investigation and water resources consultancy services. Provide the company profile, certificate of registration, and number of years in business.

(b)  General experience: experience in consultancy services for water supply, irrigation and/or water resources development during the last ten (10) years.

(c)  Specific experience: experience in assignments of similar nature and complexity, i.e. hydrogeological and geophysical investigations for groundwater development, borehole siting, groundwater quality assessment and preparation of drilling recommendations, bills of quantities and bidding documents, preferably in arid, semi-arid or pastoral/agro-pastoral areas with sedimentary, karstic or basement aquifer settings (such as the Ogaden basin and other lowland areas of Ethiopia), and under projects financed by the World Bank or other international development partners, including application of environmental and social (ESF/safeguard) requirements and in remote or security-constrained areas. For each assignment, indicate the client, location, contract value, duration, scope of services, and the firm’s role, supported by contract or completion certificates. Where available, indicate the drilling outcome (success rate) of boreholes drilled on sites recommended by the firm.

(d) Technical and managerial capability of the firm: organizational structure, geophysical survey equipment (e.g. resistivity meters for VES/ERT), GPS and field logistics, hydrogeological and GIS software, access to accredited water quality laboratories, quality assurance systems, and capacity to mobilize multidisciplinary field teams, including Somali-speaking staff, to remote and geographically dispersed areas of Somali Region, and to manage field security, health and safety risks.

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality- and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours, 8:00 A.M. to 5:30 P.M. local time, on working days.

MINISTRY OF GREEN ECONOMY AND ENVIRONMENT

 

                               REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST

                               INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT SELECTION

                                                       OPEN-NATIONAL

 

The Government of the Republic of Zambia (GRZ), through the Ministry of Green Economy and Environment (MGEE), developed the Eastern Province Jurisdictional Sustainable Landscape Program (EP-JSLP). The EP-JSLP seeks to generate payments for measured, reported, and verified Emission Reductions (ERs) from reduced deforestation, forest degradation, enhancement of forest carbon stocks (REDD+), agriculture, and other land use (AFOLU) sectors, and distribute the payments according to an agreed Benefit Sharing Plan. By curbing rapid agricultural expansion and increasing the benefits derived from forestry and agriculture, the program aims to reduce emissions by approximately 29 million tons and increase communities' resilience to climate change. 

 

The Ministry seeks to recruit suitably qualified and experienced individuals under the Eastern Province Jurisdictional Sustainable Landscape Programme Implementation Unit in Chipata for the following positions on  two year renewable contracts;

 

  1. JOB TITLE; MONITORING, REPORTING AND VERIFICATION TECHNICAL OFFICER

 

1.1   JOB PURPOSE

 

The Monitoring, Reporting and Verification Technical Officer’s primary responsibility is to ensure the project produces the results specified in the project document, to the required quality standard and within the specified time and cost.

1.2 RESPONSIBILITIES

 

  1. Lead the delivery of technical activities for the project with an emphasis on producing the monitoring reports required to receive payments from the World Bank;
  2.  Working with sector-lead institution officers (Energy, Agriculture and Forestry) to deliver high-quality data and calculations required as input for producing the monitoring reports and associated documents;
  3. Oversee and coordinate the responses to the findings of the Independent Validation and Verification Body and any changes needed to the monitoring reports and the associated documents;
  4. Lead the formulation of annual/multi-year work plan for MRV-related activities in consultation with sector lead institution and other relevant stakeholders;
  5. Work closely with sector leads, traditional leaders, community leaders, and private sector partners in developing and maintaining the MRV systems, including standard operating procedures and sampling frameworks required to produce the data and calculations for receiving the payments for emission reductions;
  6.  Coordinate data collection at the district and chiefdom level for Agriculture, Energy and Forestry;
  7. Coordinate the data collection needed for the implementation of the Benefit Sharing Plan and determine the share of the different beneficiaries based on performance in the delivery of ERs
  8. Provide project-related MRV inputs to the national MRV system and other national development planning processes as necessary;
  9. Design and organize refresher capacity-building and knowledge-sharing activities on MRV, mobilize appropriate resource persons, and serve as trainer/resource person as necessary;
  10. Review technical aspects of AFOLU carbon project activities and guide project implementing partners regarding project typology, methodological requirements, and mechanics of carbon measuring, reporting, and verification;

 

1.3 QUALIFICATIONS

 

  1. Degree in applied natural sciences such as forestry, ecology, natural resources, biogeochemistry, GIS or remote sensing, Development Economics/Planning, Land Use Planning, Environmental Management, Agriculture and related qualifications. Coursework in GIS analysis, remote sensing, and tropical forest systems may also be considered
  2. A Master’s Degree in applied natural sciences such as forestry, ecology, natural resources, biogeochemistry, GIS or remote sensing, Development Economics/Planning, Land Use Planning, Environmental Management, Agriculture and related qualifications will be an added advantage;

 

    1. COMPETENCIES

 

  1. Organized, detail- and results-oriented;
  2. Should be a good team player and self-starter with the ability to work under minimum supervision;
  3. Able to work collaboratively in a multi-sectoral team yet self-manage deliverables;
  4. Able to work under physically challenging circumstances during field visits;
  5. Able to train, motivate, and manage field crews with different degrees of experience and education;
  6. Excellent oral and written communication skills in English. Spoken technical environmental Chichewa/Nyanja will be an added advantage; and
  7. Exceptionally computer literate, including complete mastery of Microsoft Excel, Word, and PowerPoint.

 

    1. WORK EXPERIENCE
  2. Minimum of 5 years of experience with carbon projects, including an affinity with accreditation programs and standards for both the compliance and voluntary markets;
  3. Experience with biomass inventories in forest systems;
  4. Familiar with basic biogeochemistry in forest and agricultural ecosystems, including understanding of terrestrial carbon quantification;
  5. Practical understanding of mathematical and statistical concepts.
  6. Minimum of 5 years post-qualification experience with at least 3 years in a management role;
  7. Work experience with any other donor-funded projects, including the World Bank, would be an added advantage;
  8. Experience in technical report writing and presentation;
  9. Experience in MRV implementation;
  10. Experience in project implementation of community-based activities in the AFOLU sectors;
  11. In-depth knowledge of all AFOLU market standards, guidelines, and protocols. Knowledge of the Initiative for Sustainable Forest Landscape (ISFL) requirements is an added advantage;
  12. Direct experience in carbon development work and methodologies for AFOLU projects;
  13. Experience in livelihood and community-driven development work;
  14. Proven track record in the management of national, rural, community development, and/or sustainable development projects/programs;
  15. Experience working in an inter-disciplinary environment with multiple stakeholders;
  16. Relevant work experience in Eastern Province would be an added advantage.\

The Assistant Accountant shall report to the Program Accountant and shall assist the Program Accountant in providing financial and accounting services to the project and supporting the management team in ensuring program resources are used with due attention to economy, efficiency, and effectiveness.
