REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(LEARN-2.6--4-R – Cross-Functional Strategy and Alignment Expert (Budget Planning)

 

UKRAINE

Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program

GPE TF0D0613

 

Assignment Title: Cross-Functional Strategy and Alignment Expert (Budget Planning)

No. LEARN-2.6--4-R

Ukraine with the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association (hereinafter referred to as the World Bank) have signed the agreements for the Program “Lifting Education Access and Resilience in times of Need in Ukraine” (hereinafter referred to as the LEARN or Operation).

LEARN was developed to address critical challenges and provide essential support to the education sector, aligning with the Ministry of Education and Science’s (MoES) Strategic Action Plan. The objectives of the Operation are to (i) improve teaching and learning conditions; and (ii) strengthen management capacity of the education system.

The objective of this assignment is to support the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine (MoES) in aligning budget planning and public financial management processes with the strategic priorities of the education sector and the implementation of flagship national programmes and reforms. In particular, the assignment will contribute to the effective planning, prioritisation, financing, and coordination of key initiatives. The Consultant will support the development of effective planning and resource allocation approaches aimed at improving the efficiency, effectiveness, and transparency of public expenditure, strengthening evidence-based decision-making, and ensuring better alignment between strategic objectives, reform implementation, and available financial resources.

The Consultant will be contracted through competitive selection in line with the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”). 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the Procurement Regulations, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

MOES now invites qualified interested persons to submit their expression of interest in Ukrainian and English as provided in the Terms of reference.  

The detailed Terms of Reference and submission modalities for the assignment are attached to this Request for Expression of Interest. The deadline for submission of applications is 14:00 am Kyiv time December 01, 2026.

 

TERMS OF REFERENCE

for Consulting Services (Individual Consultant)

Cross-Functional Strategy and Alignment Expert (Budget Planning)

Contract No. LEARN-2.6-CC-4-R

Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Project

GPE TF0D0613

I. Background

Ukraine with the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association (hereinafter referred to as the World Bank) have signed the agreements for the Program “Lifting Education Access and Resilience in times of Need in Ukraine” (hereinafter referred to as the LEARN or Operation).

LEARN was designed to address critical issues and provide the necessary support to the education sector in accordance with the Strategic Action Plan of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine until 2027, approved by the Order of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine dated 07.03.2024 No. 276 (hereinafter referred to as the Strategic Plan).

The Operation focuses on supporting the priorities “1. Early Childhood and Preschool Education” and “2. Reform of the “New Ukrainian School” stipulated in the Strategic Plan.

The LEARN objectives are: (i) to improve teaching and learning conditions; and (ii) to strengthen the management capacity of the education system. The total LEARN financing amounts to US$737 mln  provides a combination of the World Bank financing instruments: Program for Results (PforR) – US$675.9 mln and Investment Project Financing (IPF) – US$61.1 mln.

The Program-for-Results (PforR) is implemented through a US$235 million loan provided by Bank resources, supported by loan enhancement from the Advancing Needed Credit Enhancement for Ukraine (ADVANCE Ukraine) Trust Fund, which is backed by the Government of Japan. This is formalized under the Loan Agreement between Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development for the Program (LOAN No 9721-UA). An additional US$150 million is provided under the Special Program for Ukraine and Moldova Recovery (SPUR) of the International Development Association (IDA) Crisis Facility, as outlined in the Financing Agreement between Ukraine and the International Development Association for the Program (CREDIT No 7626-UA). On July 1, 2025, the Financing Agreement (Additional Financing: Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program) between Ukraine and the International Development Association (CREDIT No 7905-UA) was signed in the amount of US$4.9 million. On June 9, 2026, a Loan Agreement (Third Additional Financing for Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program) was signed between Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (Loan No. K019-UA) in the amount of $286 million.

Furthermore, US$30 million in Investment Project Financing (IPF) is secured under the Grant Agreement between Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association, acting as the administrator of the Ukraine Relief, Recovery, Reconstruction, and Reform Multi-Donor Trust Fund (URTF GRANT No TF0C5794). On December 19, 2025, the Grant Agreement (Additional Financing for Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Project) between UKRAINE and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association jointly acting as a Supervising Entity for the Global Partnership for Education Fund and as administrator of the Ukraine Relief, Recovery, Reconstruction and Reform Multi-Donor Trust Fund (GPE GRANT No TF0D0613, URTF GRANT No TF0D0612) was signed in the amount of US$31.1 million.

More detailed information about the LEARN program is provided at  https://projects.worldbank.org/en/projects-operations/project-detail/P504171

The latest additional grant agreement provides for expanded support for reforms in the education sector, in particular by:

• financing activities for the development of preschool education;

• providing grant support of the Global Partnership for Education (GPE) aimed at strengthening the institutional capacity of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine to implement educational reforms.

In accordance with the provisions of the agreements concluded, the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine is responsible for the overall implementation, coordination, monitoring and reporting on the Project activities, in particular those aimed at strengthening the institutional management capacity of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine. Such activities include the provision of technical assistance, the development and implementation of information systems, conducting training activities in the field of vocational (technical) education, as well as the implementation of initiatives in cross-sectoral areas, in particular inclusive education, European integration, education infrastructure management and strategic planning.

II. Objective

The objective of this assignment is to support the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine (MoES) in aligning budget planning and public financial management processes with the strategic priorities of the education sector and the implementation of flagship national programmes and reforms. In particular, the assignment will contribute to the effective planning, prioritisation, financing, and coordination of key initiatives. The Consultant will support the development of effective planning and resource allocation approaches aimed at improving the efficiency, effectiveness, and transparency of public expenditure, strengthening evidence-based decision-making, and ensuring better alignment between strategic objectives, reform implementation, and available financial resources.

III. Scope of services

The Consultant shall provide the following services, including but not limited to:

  • Analyze the current system of budgetary and strategic planning within the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine (MoES), including the application of the program-based budgeting approach;
  • Analyze the alignment of budget programs with strategic objectives and national policy priorities in the education and science sector;
  • Develop recommendations for aligning strategic documents (strategies, operational plans) with MoES budget programs;
  • Ensure integration of strategic objectives and priorities into the budget process (including preparation of budget requests, budget program passports, and reporting);
  • Contribute to the improvement of the structure of budget programs, performance indicators, and effectiveness metrics;
  • Support medium-term budget planning in line with strategic documents;
  • Provide methodological support on the application of the program-based budgeting approach within MoES;
  • Coordinate with the Ministry of Finance of Ukraine on budget planning and alignment of budget programs;
  • Provide methodological and analytical support for public expenditure reviews in relevant MoES sectors;
  • Develop proposals for implementing recommendations from expenditure reviews and ensure their incorporation into future budget planning cycles;
  • Support the implementation of results-based management approaches in the budget process;
  • Assess the effectiveness of MoES budget programs;
  • Prepare analytical materials on the efficiency of public expenditure and achievement of results.

Expected Deliverables:

  • Regular reports on the progress of aligning budgetary and strategic planning;
  • Analytical notes on the effectiveness of budget programs and their alignment with strategic objectives;
  • Proposals for improving the MoES budget process:

consulting and practical support to the Ministry of Education and Science in implementing results-oriented management approaches;

conducting analysis and assessment of the efficiency and effectiveness of budget programs of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine;

  • Analyze the implementation of previously provided recommendations and their impact on MoES budget indicators in the medium term, including collection and systematization of recommendations provided by the Accounting Chamber, the State Audit Service, and expenditure reviews conducted during the previous three years, as well as assessment of their implementation status.

 

IV. Reporting

The Consultant shall report to the Project Coordinator/Project Co-Coordinator and work in coordination with the Deputy Ministers of Education and Science of Ukraine, relevant MoES directorates, and project managers involved in the implementation of Project activities. REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

Georgia

Project Name: The Relief and Recovery for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs)

Project No: P173975

Loan No. 9239-GE

Assignment Title: Procurement Manager

Reference No. GE-GEDC-CS-IC-48

 

Introduction

JSC Georgian Economic Development Corporation (GEDC), within the Relief and Recovery for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) Project supported by the World Bank (WB) intends to apply part of the loan proceeds for consulting services of Procurement Manager (National Consultant).

The Project Development Objective for the Relief and Recovery for MSME operation is to provide relief to MSMEs and support their recovery, including by strengthening the enabling environment for access to finance.

 

Project Description

The Project is being implemented nationwide and consist of four components:

Component 1 – Financial relief and recovery for MSMEs

Component 2 – Digital payments & financial infrastructure upgrading

Component 3 – Project management and monitoring

Component 4 – Contingent Emergency Response Component

A substantial portion of the Project activities fall under Component 1. The component will support the expansion of the following financial instruments implemented by GEDC: (a) grants for MSMEs through GEDC’s Micro and Small Entrepreneurship Support Program, (b) co-financing of interest payments through GEDC’s Produce in Georgia Program, and (c) partial credit guarantees (PCGs). The component will also provide non-financial support in the form of training and technical assistance to help firms adjust to new conditions, improve their business skills, and increase their resilience.

  • Sub-component 1.1 provide micro-grants to finance working capital and fixed assets for micro and small firms.
  • Sub-component 1.2 co-finance interest payments on loans underwritten by participating financial institutions (PFIs).
  • Sub-component 1.3 provide partial credit guarantees for loans issued by PFIs.
  • Sub-component 1.4 provide technical assistance for COVID-proofing and digitalization of MSMEs.

Scope of Work

Procurement Manager / Individual Consultant shall assist the GEDC in all procurement activities related to implementation of WB financed MSMEs Project in accordance with the New Procurement Framework  - Policy, Regulations, Guidance issued for the projects After July 1, 2016 according to the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers - PROCUREMENT IN INVESTMENT PROJECT FINANCING -  Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services, July 2016 and revised in September 2025.

This includes not only procurement activities where GEDC is the beneficiary of the loan proceeds, but also the activities where GEDC is acting as a procuring agency for other agencies, which are final beneficiaries (GEDC’s fiduciary responsibilities are defined in the Loan Agreement).

Anticipated Procurement Activities

The remaining procurement activities under the Project may include, but are not limited to:

  • Event Organization Services: Procurement of services related to the organization and technical support of business events and other similar activities under the Project.
  • Consulting Services: Procurement of consulting services for feasibility studies, assessments, and other analytical activities supporting the Project's objectives.

The scope and selection methods of these activities will be determined based on the Project's needs and the approved Procurement Plan, in accordance with the World Bank Procurement Regulations.

Key Responsibilities

In order to achieve the objective of this contract, the Procurement Manager / Individual Consultant shall:

  • Lead the process of preparation of Project Procurement Plan, its update on a regular basis in close partnership with the GEDC in alignment with the WB rules and regulations;
  • Administer the entire process for the procurement cycle, ensuring compliance with the WB regulations:  selection of the appropriate procurement methods, preparation of the Terms of References, cost estimates, Requests for Expression of Interest, Requests for Quotations/Bids/Proposals, evaluation reports, participation in contracts’ negotiations and awards, as well as in contracts’ execution, getting the WB approvals, as appropriate.
  • Lead contract administration, including framework agreements and managing call-off contracts in each framework agreement.  
  • Keep all relevant procurement documentation on file in an orderly manner and make it available for the authorized national inspecting agencies, auditors, and the WB upon request;
  • Enter all up-to-date procurement related information, both post and prior review, in STEP;
  • Prepare quarterly and annual procurement reports including contract monitoring and management;
  • Cooperate with the GEDC for regular preparation of Project Management/Financial Reports, as part of the WB project and financial reporting requirements;
  • Participate in contract management, monitoring and supervision, including but not limited to ensuring timely submission of all deliverables specified under the contract.
  • Perform other procurement related tasks as required.

 

Qualification and experience

  • University-level degree in business administration, finance, law, or related discipline;
  • 5 (Five) years of practical experience as a procurement or contract specialist;
  • At least 3 (three) years of working experience in procurement and contract management of projects funded by the WB and/or other International Financial Institutions (IFIs);
  • Knowledge of the World Bank procurement regulations, local taxation, banking and other pertinent regulations affecting national and international procurement;
  • Experience with World Bank Systematic Tracking of Exchanges in Procurement (STEP) portal;
  • Proven teamwork skills;
  • Superior verbal and writing communication skills in Georgian;
  • Strong verbal, reading and writing skills in English;
  • Good negotiating skills;
  • Proficiency in various software under OS Windows (MS Office, Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint, Access, Adobe).

Reporting

The Individual Consultant shall directly report to the Project Manager.

Facilities and Services to be provided by the Client

The Client shall provide office area and facilities, office equipment and communication necessary to carry out the services. The Client shall also provide all necessary information and documents for that purposes.

Duration

The assignment will be time-based, continuing until the Project’s closing date of June 30, 2027.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraph 3.14 “Conflict of Interest” of the World Bank’s Guidelines: New Procurement Framework  - Policy, Regulations, Guidance issued for the projects After July 1, 2016 according to the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers - PROCUREMENT IN INVESTMENT PROJECT FINANCING -  Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services, July 2016 and revised in September 2025, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.  In addition, please refer to the following specific information on conflict of interest related to this assignment: The Consultant shall not receive any remuneration in connection with the assignment except as provided in the contract. The consultant and its affiliates shall not engage in consulting or other activities that conflict with the interest of the client under the contract. The contract shall include provisions limiting future engagement of the consultant for other services resulting from or directly related to the firm’s consulting services in accordance with the requirements of paragraphs 3.16, 3.17 and 3.18 of the Guidelines.

An individual consultant will be selected in accordance with the procedures set out in World Bank’s Guidelines: New Procurement Framework  - Policy, Regulations, Guidance issued for the projects After July 1, 2016 according to the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers - PROCUREMENT IN INVESTMENT PROJECT FINANCING -  Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services, July 2016 and revised in September 2025. “Selection of Individual Consultants”.

Interested consultants may obtain further information by email: hr@gedc.ge

CVs of candidates in English language must be submitted electronically to the address below not later than 23 November, 2026

E-mail To: hr@gedc.ge

Please include the title of the announced position in subject line of the email.

Avis Spécifique d’Appel d’Offres (AA0)

Appel d’Offres pour Fournitures

(Processus à Une Enveloppe)

Appel d’Offres N° : BI-PAFEN-PIU-1.1.3.11-GO-RFB

Projet : Projet d’Appui aux Fondations de l’Economie Numérique (PAFEN)

Acheteur : PAFEN

Pays : Burundi

Intitulé du Marché : Fourniture et l’installation des équipements, applications, hardware et logiciels pour le CERT national afin de permettre des capacités de renseignement sur les menaces, de prévention, d'atténuation, de défense et de réponse

Don No : E0930-BI

Emis le : 6 Novembre 2026

1. Le Gouvernement de la République du Burundi a reçu un don de 92 millions de dollar USD de la Banque mondiale pour financer le coût du Projet d’Appui aux Fondations de l’Economie Numérique dont l’objectif de développement est d’accroitre l’accès à l’internet haut débit en particulier pour les communautés mal desservies et d’améliorer la capacité du gouvernement à gérer les ressources plus efficacement et fournir les services publics par voie numérique.

Le Ministère des Finances, du Budget et de l’Economie Numérique de la République du Burundi, à travers le Projet d’Appui aux Fondations de l’Economie Numérique (PAFEN), financé par la Banque mondiale, a prévu de mettre en place le CERT/SOC en le dotant des équipements, applications, hardware et logiciels national afin de permettre des capacités de renseignement sur les menaces, de prévention, d'atténuation, de défense et de réponse.

2. L’Unité de Gestion du Projet d’Appui aux Fondations de l’Economie Numérique (PAFEN) sollicite des offres fermées de la part de soumissionnaires éligibles et répondant aux qualifications requises pour la fourniture et l’installation des équipements, applications, hardware et logiciels pour le CERT national afin de permettre des capacités de renseignement sur les menaces, de prévention, d'atténuation, de défense et de réponse (en 3 lots), tels que décrits dans la Section VII de ce Dossier d’Appel d’Offres:

  • Lots 1 : Fourniture, livraison et installation des infrastructures et équipements technologiques, Prestations de services et accompagnement à l’opérationnalisation
  • Lot 2 : Fourniture des équipements bureautiques
  • Lot 3 : Réaménagement des infrastructures et renforcement du système électrique

3. Les fournitures, installations et services connexes doivent être livrées, dans un délai ne dépassant pas :

  • Lot 1 : trois (3) mois calendriers pour le Volet 1 (Fourniture, livraison et installation des infrastructures et équipements technologiques) et 5 ans pour le Volet 2 (Déploiement des plateformes SOC/CERT, opérationnalisation et transfert de compétences)
  • Lot 2 : 3 mois calendriers
  • Lot 3 : 3 mois calendriers

4. Les exigences en matière de qualification sont :

  1. Pour tous les Lots : Capacité financière : Le Soumissionnaire doit soumettre des états financiers vérifiés ou, si la loi du pays du Soumissionnaire ne l’exige pas, d’autres états financiers acceptables pour l’Acheteur, pour les cinq (5) dernières années avant la date limite de remise des Offres, démontrant la solidité actuelle de la situation financière du Soumissionnaire. Dans le cas d’un GE, cette exigence doit être respectée par chaque membre.
  2. Le soumissionnaire doit démontrer qu’il dispose d’avoir liquides ou a accès à des actifs non grevés ou des lignes de crédit, etc. autres que l’avance de démarrage éventuelle, à des montants suffisants pour subvenir aux besoins de trésorerie nécessaires à l’exécution du marché objet du présent Appel d’Offres à hauteur d’un montant au moins égal à quatre cent mille (400 000) dollar US. ou l’équivalent en Francs Burundais (BIF) ou dans une autre monnaie librement convertible pour le Lot 1,  Cent Mille (100 000) de Dollars Américains pour le Lot 2 et Cent Cinquante Mille (150 000) de Dollars Américains pour le Lot 3. La justification est établie par des déclarations appropriées des banques ou organismes financiers habilités.
  3. Avoir, au cours des cinq (05) dernières années, un chiffre d’affaires annuel moyen d’au moins un (01) million cinq cent mille (1 500 000) de dollars US, ou l’équivalent en Francs Burundais (BIF) ou dans une autre monnaie librement convertible pour Lot 1, Quatre Cent Mille (400 000) de Dollars Américains pour le Lot 2 et  un Six cent Mille (600 000) de Dollars Américains pour le Lot 3.
  4. Expérience spécifique :

Lot 1 :

  • Le soumissionnaire doit démontrer une expérience avérée dans la mise en œuvre d’environnements de centre des opérations de sécurité (SOC), intégrant des outils de sécurité tels que des pares-feux, des solutions de détection et de réponse étendues (XDR), des systèmes de détection d’intrusion (IDS) ainsi que des solutions de gestion des vulnérabilités.
  • Le soumissionnaire doit démontrer la réalisation d’au moins deux (2) projets de mise en œuvre de SOC au cours des cinq (5) dernières années, incluant des solutions SIEM avec collecte et corrélation de logs issus de sources multiples, des plateformes de Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI), ainsi que des solutions SOAR permettant l’automatisation de la détection et de la réponse aux incidents.
  • Le soumissionnaire doit démontrer l’intégration opérationnelle de solutions SIEM et CTI avec des plateformes SOAR et ITSM/SIRP, incluant la gestion automatisée des tickets, l’orchestration des workflows, la gestion des alertes et le reporting de sécurité.
  • Le prestataire devra justifier d’une maîtrise avérée des normes et référentiels internationaux, notamment ISO/IEC 27001, ISO/IEC 27002, le NIST Cybersecurity Framework et ITIL.
  • Une expérience dans des pays en développement, notamment en Afrique, constituera un atout.

Lot 2 :

Le Soumissionnaire doit démontrer qu’il a conclu avec succès au moins deux (2) marchés similaires au cours des cinq dernières années avant la date limite de remise des Offres, chacun d’une valeur d’au moins Trois Cent Mille (300 000) Dollars Américains qui ont été conclues avec succès et substantiellement et qui sont de nature et de complexité similaires aux Fournitures et Services Connexes faisant l’objet du Marché. Dans le cas d’un GE, cette exigence peut être respectée par tous les membres réunis.

Lot 3 :

Le Soumissionnaire doit démontrer qu’il a conclu avec succès au moins un (1) marché similaire au cours des cinq dernières années avant la date limite de remise des Offres, chacun d’une valeur d’au moins Six Cent Mille (600 000) Dollars Américains qui ont été conclues avec succès et substantiellement et qui sont de nature et de complexité similaires aux Fournitures et Services Connexes faisant l’objet du Marché. Dans le cas d’un GE, cette exigence peut être respectée par tous les membres réunis.

Personnel-Clé pour le Lot 1 : voir les DPAO pour informations complémentaires

NB : Les pièces administratives et autres critères d’attribution du marché sont contenus dans les données particulières de l’appel d’offres (DPAO). Voir les DPAO pour informations complémentaires

5. La passation du Marché sera conduite par Mise en Concurrence nationale (AON) tel que défini dans le « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement » de la Banque mondiale Edition de juillet 2016, révisé en novembre 2017, août 2018 et novembre 2020, et ouvert à tous les soumissionnaires de pays éligibles tels que définis dans ledit Règlement.

6. Les soumissionnaires éligibles et intéressés peuvent obtenir des informations auprès de du PAFEN, sis à Kinindo, Quartier Zeimet, Jonction Rues Kiremba et Kinyinya No14, Mail : info@pafen.gov.bi avec copies obligatoires à procurement@pafen.gov.bi et mvukiyekeges.archive@gmail.com et prendre connaissance des documents d’Appel d’offres à l’adresse mentionnée ci-dessus de 8 heures à 12 heures 30 min et de 14 heures à 17 heures tous les jours ouvrables de lundi à jeudi et de 8 heures à 14 heures les vendredis à l’adresse mentionnée ci-dessous.

6. Les Soumissionnaires intéressés et éligibles peuvent obtenir un dossier d’appel d’offres complet en Français à l’adresse mentionnée ci-dessous et contre un paiement d’un montant non remboursable de Cent Dollars Américains (US$ 100.00) ou l’équivalent dans une autre devise librement convertible.

notices.title: Research assistant on international good practice in the financing of tertiary education (TVET and Higher education)
notices.buyer: Ministry of Economy and Finance of the Republic of Uzbekistan
notices.description:
TERMS OF REFERENCE

 For research assistant on international good practice in the financing of tertiary education (TVET and Higher education)

Grant Facility for Project Preparation (GFPP) – Uzbekistan Student Loan Program:

I. Background

The Government of the Republic of Uzbekistan is implementing comprehensive reforms aimed at expanding equitable access to higher education and strengthening the effectiveness, sustainability, and inclusiveness of student financing mechanisms. As higher education participation continues to increase, ensuring adequate, equitable, and effective financing has become a key priority to support equal educational opportunities and long-term sector development.

To support these reforms, the Grant Facility for Project Preparation (GFPP) represents a strategic investment of US$2 million, financed by the World Bank, to support the preparation and implementation readiness of the Student Loan Program in Uzbekistan. The GFPP finances analytical studies, institutional capacity building, implementation support, and policy development to establish a sustainable and efficient student financing system. The facility supports comprehensive analytical work to assess the current student financing landscape, conduct stakeholder consultations, evaluate international good practices, and develop evidence-based policy recommendations. It also strengthens implementation capacity through the recruitment of specialized Project Implementation Unit (PIU) staff and fiduciary experts, while supporting national and international training programs for representatives of the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF), the Ministry of Education and Science (MoES), and other relevant stakeholders.

These reforms take place in a context of rapid expansion. Gross enrolment in higher education rose from 9 percent to 21 percent between 2016 and 2022, the number of HEIs grew from 70 to 194, and the Government aims to reach 50 percent enrolment by 2030. Admission is still largely managed through centrally set quotas of places, which are increased every year.2 Public spending on tertiary education has risen more than fivefold in five years to about 0.89 percent of GDP, close to the OECD average. However, the financing model continues to rely heavily on households: around 68 percent of public higher education institutions’ (HEIs’) revenues come from tuition fees; free (state-funded) places, held by about 17 percent of students, are allocated on admission test scores and benefit mostly students from middle- and higher-income families; and government funding to HEIs is based on enrolment alone, so it does not reward labour market outcomes, curricular innovation or industry links.1 The regional “dual-track” model of budget-funded and fee-paying places, combined with centralised quotas that may not correspond to demand for specific programmes, has been found to create an incentive for institutions to retain fee-paying students at the expense of academic standards.2 World Bank analysis has pointed to a package of system-level financing reforms, including a transparent funding formula that combines enrolment with performance on strategic indicators, competitive grants, diversification of institutional revenues and reform of student financial aid. These reforms depend on greater institutional financial and academic autonomy and on reliable data on graduate outcomes.1

The Government recognizes the importance of evidence-based analysis to inform future reforms of the financing of tertiary education, covering both technical and vocational education and training (TVET) and higher education (HE). It also places high value on learning from good practice in relevant and comparable international cases, so that design choices for Uzbekistan are informed by what other systems have done, what results they achieved, and under which conditions.

II. The assignment

To inform these reforms, the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF) and the PIU have engaged an international consultant to carry out research on international good practice in the financing of tertiary education (TVET and HE). The research covers the general design of TVET and HE financing systems in a selection of relevant and comparable countries, including their institutional and legal frameworks, the incentives they create and their impact on the sector; and countries’ experiences in phasing out admission quotas for students entering TVET and HE, including the finance-related aspects of this transition. It will assess how far these arrangements fit, or would need to be adapted to, the Uzbek context. The work runs from October to December 2026. It starts with an initial review of how TVET and HE are currently financed in Uzbekistan and exploratory desk research on international experience, through which the analytical framework will be refined. It then includes a selection of country cases with national counterparts, in-depth interviews with stakeholders in the selected countries and, subject to confirmation, a mission to Tashkent in mid-November 2026.

III. Objective

The objective of this assignment is to provide research support to the international consultant throughout the study, by collecting, organising, analysing and synthesising evidence and data on the financing of TVET and HE in Uzbekistan and in the selected countries, and by supporting interviews, the mission to Tashkent and the preparation of the report.

IV. Scope of Work and Deliverables

Under the guidance and supervision of the international consultant, who defines the overall methodology of the research, the research assistant will carry out the following tasks:

  1. Review of the current system in Uzbekistan. Collect and organise documents and data on the current financing of TVET and HE in Uzbekistan (e.g., laws and regulations, budget and enrolment data, admission quota decisions, available studies), in coordination with the PIU, and prepare summary tables and notes as requested by the consultant.
  2. Exploratory and in-depth desk research. Identify, collect and review relevant documents on the financing of TVET and HE and on admission quotas in other countries (laws and regulations, policy documents, funding rules, evaluations, academic and grey literature), first to help identify countries for the long-list and then in more depth for the selected cases.
  3. Data collection and analysis. Where necessary, extract data from available national and international databases (e.g., UNESCO UIS, OECD, Eurostat, World Bank and national statistics) and run specific analyses as requested by the consultant, such as comparisons of funding levels, enrolment and outcomes across countries.
  4. Case profiles. Draft short country profiles using common templates developed by the consultant, which will be refined as the research progresses.
  5. Evidence management. Set up and maintain a library of sources and references and an evidence matrix that brings together the information collected across countries, flagging gaps and inconsistencies to be checked in interviews.
  6. Support to interviews. Support the consultant, who will lead the interviews, by helping to prepare interview guides; identify and contact potential interviewees and schedule interviews; take notes and prepare written summaries of interviews.
  7. Support to the mission to Tashkent. Subject to confirmation, travel to Uzbekistan on the same dates as the consultant; support the preparation of meetings in coordination with the PIU; collect documents and data shared by national counterparts; take notes and prepare summary notes of meetings and consultations.
  8. Support to reporting. Prepare tables, figures and annexes; check facts and references; and proofread and format drafts of the inception note and report.

Deliverables: (1) Collection of documents and data on the current financing system in Uzbekistan, with summary tables; library of sources; and first draft case profiles of long-listed countries; (2) Summary notes of meetings held during the mission to Tashkent (if it takes place); (3) Interview notes, completed case profiles for the selected countries, evidence matrix, and datasets and outputs of the data analyses carried out; (4) Tables, annexes and reference list for the final report.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

Bosnia and Herzegovina
Just Transition in Select Coal Regions of Bosnia and Herzegovina Project
Loan No.: IBRD-98010
Assignment Title: LTU Liaison Officer/Legal Officer – Zenica Coal Mine (HR Department)
Reference No.: BA-FBIH-JCT-CS-ICS-26-4.2.3.A

 

The Federal Ministry of Energy, Mining and Industry (FMERI) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Just Transition in Select Coal Regions of Bosnia and Herzegovina Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include providing daily operational support to the Workforce Transition Unit (LTU) within the Human Resources Department of the Zenica Coal Mine (RMU Zenica). The LTU Liaison Officer will act as the single point of contact and case manager for mine workers affected by the mine closure. The primary objective is to deliver high-quality, individual, and personalized career transition support—ranging from initial profiling and psychosocial guidance to job matching, training referrals, and coordination with employment bureaus—with a strong focus on older workers and individuals with disabilities.

The assignment expects continuous physical presence at the HR Department of RMU Zenica. The initial contract period is twelve (12) months, with the possibility of extension subject to satisfactory performance and project implementation schedules.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website: https://fmeri.gov.ba/project-implementation-unit/

The Federal Ministry of Energy, Mining and Industry (FMERI) now invites eligible individual consultants (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide a Curriculum Vitae (CV) and supporting documentation demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (dated September 2023) (“the Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

An Individual Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Open Competitive Selection of Individual Consultants method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Shortlisting and Evaluation Criteria:

  • Core Qualifications (Educational Background): University degree in Sociology, Economics, Law, Human Resources, Psychology, or a related field [20%].
  • Relevant Work Experience: Proven experience in career counseling, employment services, case management, or human resources, ideally working directly with job seekers or redundant workers (experience with the mining or industrial workforce is an asset) [50%].
  • Knowledge of Local Systems: Strong familiarity with employment services, active labor market measures, and welfare/insurance frameworks within the Zenica-Doboj Canton [20%].
  • Interpersonal and Language Skills: Strong communication skills suited for sensitive worker engagement, and fluency in the official languages of the Zenica-Doboj Canton (working knowledge of English is an asset) [10%].


Interested candidates must submit the following application documents:

TEACHERS SERVICE COMMISSION

 

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

Kenya

SELECTION METHOD

Consultant’s Qualifications-based Selection (CQS))

THE MOST QUALIFIED CONSULTING FIRM SHALL BE REQUESTED TO SUBMIT TECHNICAL AND FINANCIAL PROPOSALS

The Teachers Service Commission has received funding from the World Bank toward the cost of the Kenya Primary Education Equity in Learning (KPEEL) project. The Commission intends to apply part of the proceeds to implement the Mid-term Assessment of Teacher Proficiency for Kenya Primary Education Equity in Learning (KPEEL).

The service includes  Assessment of Teacher Proficiency for Kenya Primary Education Equity in Learning (KPEEL). The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment is attached for your review and response. 

The Teachers Service Commission now invites eligible and qualified consulting firms under Consultant’s Qualifications-based Selection (CQS) to express their interest in undertaking the Services of Mid-term Assessment of Teacher Proficiency for Kenya Primary Education Equity in Learning (KPEEL).

Interested and qualified consulting firms should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria and the detailed Terms of Reference are available are attached herein.

Consultants shall be required to submit only the documents demonstrating their qualifications to perform the assignment stated under the mandatory and technical requirements. Consultants are advised NOT to submit the Technical Proposal.

The attention of interested Consulting Firms is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September, 2025 setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. Consulting Firms or Individual Consultants involved in Banks Procurements should not participate.

A Consultant shall not submit more than one Proposal, either individually or as a joint venture partner in another Proposal. If a Consultant, including a joint venture partner, submits or participates in more than one Proposal, all such Proposals shall be disqualified. However, this does not preclude a firm’s participation as a sub-consultant, or an individual’s participation as a team member, in more than one Proposal when circumstances justify and if permitted by the request for proposals document

Consulting firms may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should clearly indicate whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Consultant’s Qualifications-based Selection (CQS) Method set out in the Procurement Regulations. Further information can be obtained at the Procurement Office, Teachers Service Commission Podium Wing Second Floor during working hours between 8.00 a.m. to 5.00 p.m.

Expressions of interest must be submitted/delivered and placed in the tender box located at Teachers Service Commission Podium Wing Ground Floor in a plain sealed envelope clearly marked Consultancy for Technical Assistance for End-Line  Assessment of Teacher Proficiency for Kenya Primary Education Equity in Learning (KPEEL) - TSC/KPEEL/EOI/001/2026-2027on or before Monday,19 October, 2026,  9.00 a.m. Bulky tenders can be delivered to the Teachers Service Commission Procurement office located at Second Floor Podium Wing. Electronic Tenders will not be permitted.

Physical Address:      Teachers Service Commission Upper, Hill Kilimanjaro Road

Postal Address:    P. O Box Private Bag Nairobi.

Expressions of Interest will be opened immediately on before Monday,19 October, 2026 at 9.00 a.m. at the Teachers Service Commission Ground Floor Podium wing in the presence of the Tenderers' designated representatives who choose to attend at the address below:

Address for Opening of Tenders.

Teachers Service Commission

Upper Hill, Kilimanjaro Road,

TSC Building-Podium Wing, Ground Floor

 

TERMS OF REFERENCE (ToRs)

  1. BACKGROUND.

The Teacher Service Commission (TSC) is implementing the Kenya Primary Education Equity in Learning (KPEEL) Program. The program is designed to reduce regional disparities in learning outcomes, improving the retention of girls in upper primary education, and strengthen systems for delivering equitable education outcomes. The program is envisaged to realize three core results; -

  1. Result Area 1: Equalize Learning Opportunities:
  2. Result Area 2: Improve Girl’s Participation in Schooling Including in Refugee Hosting Counties
  3. Result Area 3: Strengthen Reforms Implementation Capacity

The Commission is expected to intervene in the Result Area one on equalizing learning opportunities by addressing the highest teacher shortages in public primary schools in both refugee host and non-host communities.

The program funding is through Program for Result (PforR) which uses the existing government system to implement program activities and secure reimbursement on achievement of the Disbursed Linked Indicator which is “number of new teachers deployed to primary schools with the highest teacher shortage”. By the end of the program in 2026, the Commission is expected to have recruited and deployed 5,000 new teachers to primary schools with highest teacher shortages. Out of which refugee host communities (Garissa and Turkana) will receive 640 newly recruited and deployed teachers while refugee non-host communities will receive 4,360.

The Commission has committed to utilize the funds to implement robust teacher management systems which are: (a) strengthening Teacher Performance Appraisal and Development (TPAD), (b) enhancing the capacity of teachers to integrate Information, Communication and Technology (ICT) in teaching and learning, (c) utilize Live Streaming of Lesson and Remote Learning Methodologies (RLM) as alternative mode of curriculum delivery, and (d) through Teacher Induction, Mentorship and Coaching (TIMEC). The goal for these interventions is to improve teacher proficiency so that they can provide dynamic learning experiences and improve learning outcomes. 

Teacher Performance Appraisal and Development (TPAD): Since the inception of the program, the Commission has been training five thousand (5000) teachers per year on TPAD implementation. In addition, the TPAD technical team and the field officers have been monitoring TPAD and offering teachers professional support. In relation to these milestones, the number of TSC teachers on TPAD has risen from 334,810 in term 1, 2022 to 425,215 in term 2, 2025.

Integration of Information, Communication and Technology (ICT) in teaching and learning: In line with Curriculum Based Establishment (CBE), Digital Literacy is a core competence that both teachers and learners require to integrate in teaching and learning. Under the program, teachers have been trained on digital skills such as use of digital platforms such as Microsoft and use of online gamification as a form of administering assessment to learners.

Live Streaming of Lesson and Remote Learning Methodologies (RLM) as alternative mode of curriculum delivery: Under the program, the Commission rolled out livestreaming of lessons in thirty target primary schools. The experience with livestreaming lessons demonstrated that this innovation is a transformative model for delivering equitable, high-quality education nationwide. By addressing teacher shortages, enhancing access, promoting equity, strengthening capacity, and equipping teachers and learners with digital skills, livestreaming directly supports Kenya’s aspirations under SDG 4 (Quality Education) and the Kenya Vision 2030 education pillar.

 Teacher Induction, Mentorship and Coaching (TIMEC): The TIMEC Programme is a key initiative by the Commission aimed at addressing and reducing cases of teacher indiscipline. This programme is aligned with Strategic Objective No. 3 of the Commission’s Strategic Plan (2019–2023) and has been carried forward into the 2023–2027 Strategic Plan.

Titre du posteResponsable de suivi et évaluation pour l'UGP-MSPPCompagnieMSPP / Unite de Gestion du Projet PEPFAR
DomaineManagement/Gestion, Finance, Comptabilité et CommerceSpécialitéGestion de Projets
Date publication4 Nov 2026Date limite17 Nov 2026
PaysHaitiVillePort-au-Prince
ZoneBureau de l’UGP MSPP, Delmas 81 – Haiti.DuréeDéterminée : deux (2) mois renouvelable
Introduction

L’Unité de Gestion des Projets (UGP) a été créée en 2005 pour gérer les subventions ou dons de bailleurs internationaux de fonds pour le MSPP. Elle fournit une assistance technique à tous les sous-bénéficiaires pour atteindre les buts, objectifs et cibles fixées dans le contexte des programmes appuyés. Dans ce cadre, l’UGP travaille en forte collaboration avec les autres directions et unités du MSPP pour optimiser le financement fourni afin d’atteindre les résultats prévus, tout en assurant la conformité avec les règles, procédures, et dispositions standard liées à l’utilisation des fonds alloués par les bailleurs respectifs. Le personnel de l’UGP est responsable avec le MSPP sur toutes les questions qui touchent directement ou indirectement l’exécution des programmes mis en œuvre et l’utilisation des fonds alloués. Pour jouer ce rôle, l’UGP sert de liaison entre le Ministère (MSPP) et les bailleurs, et fournit au Ministère tous les éléments nécessaires à leurs interactions régulières avec ces bailleurs.

Fonctions

RESUME DU POSTE

Le Responsable de Suivi et d’Évaluation intervient pour l’UGP/MSPP dans les domaines relatifs au Suivi et Évaluation des projets qui sont mis en œuvre. Il/Elle s'assure que la collecte, le conditionnement et la transmission des informations sont opportuns, supervise le processus et crée les conditions optimales pour la production de données fiables, réalise des examens à mi-parcours et capitalise sur les enseignements tirés des expériences pour le futur.
Il/Elle assure la coordination technique entre les unités centrales du MSPP qui ont la responsabilité principale de collecte et reportage de données inclus dans les cadres de résultats des projets mis en œuvre par l’UGP, de veille et de point focal technique pour les partenaires techniques et financiers de l’UGP/ MSPP.
Il/Elle assiste techniquement les activités liées au monitoring et à l'évaluation d’indicateurs de Projet.

RESPONSABILITES PARTICULIERES

Sous l’autorité immédiate du Directeur Technique et en collaboration avec les Directions et les Unités du MSPP bénéficiaires des projets gérés par l’UGP MSPP, les partenaires techniques et financiers de l’UGP MSPP et les différentes composantes de l’UGP MSPP telles que les Directions Administrative, financière, entre autres, il/elle assume les responsabilités suivantes :

1) Support et outils d’informations

Il/elle est responsable de la bonne exécution des activités des projets dans son domaine d’intervention notamment :
a. Analyser les stratégies et apprécient les critères de mesures de la performance.
b. Participer à la mise à jour des outils de collecte et des formulaires de rapport d’activités.
c. Procéder chaque fois que nécessaire à l’inventaire des besoins des institutions en outils et équipements du système d’information.
d. S’assurer de leur approvisionnement continu en outils de collecte et autres instruments de travail pour éviter toute rupture de stock.

2) Formation et encadrement pour assurer la collecte et reportage de données qui répondent aux besoins des cadres de résultats des projets mis en œuvre par l’UGP

a. Etablir les besoins en encadrement et / ou formation du personnel.
b. Participer à l’élaboration et à l'opérationnalisation du plan de formation.
c. Maintenir à jour la base de données des formations réalisées
d. Participer activement à l'élaboration du plan de travail et des calendriers périodiques suivi & évaluation.
e. Participer à la formation du personnel impliqué dans la collecte des données au niveau central, départemental, et institutionnel, incluant les sites et des directions sanitaires départementales supportés par les projets du MSPP/UGP.

3) Supervision

a. Effectuer des visites de supervision des sites dans les départements concernés couverts, selon le calendrier prévu afin de s’assurer de l'utilisation correcte des dossiers et des autres outils de collecte des données, du respect des procédures de collecte, de la qualité des données produites et d'identifier les besoins des sites.
b. Préparer les rapports des visites de supervision dans un délai ne dépassant pas une semaine.

4) Statistiques et surveillance épidémiologique

a. En collaboration avec les unités centrales responsables, procéder à la validation des rapports départementaux.
b. Participer à l'élaboration ou révision de manuel et tout instrument destiné à la formation du personnel des sites et aux responsables impliqués dans la collecte de données institutionnels et programmatiques
c. Participer à la réalisation des réunions de coordination de la cellule de gestion du projet à l'UGP.
d. Tenir le cadre des résultats de projet et du manuel opérationnel à jour, incluant, au minimum, un reportage bi annuel

5) Suivi et Evaluation

a. Participer à la conception des plans de suivi et évaluation pour chaque projet de concert avec les Programmes et les autres directions du MSPP.
b. Contribuer à l’élaboration des cibles programmatiques.
c. Travailler avec les managers des contractants et des partenaires de mise en œuvre dans le domaine du suivi et de l’évaluation.
d. Diffuser les outils de collecte de données auprès des contractants et partenaires d’implémentation (PI) et veiller à leur bonne utilisation.
e. Développer les outils nécessaires à la collecte des données, pour les indicateurs de projet gérés par l’UGP.
f. Assurer le contrôle de qualité des données collectées et transmisses par les unités centrales et départementales respectives
g. Assurer la bonne application des outils nécessaires à la collecte des données
h. Contribuer activement à l’élaboration des cadres logiques des différents projets.
i. Préparer et/ou mettre à jour le Plan de Monitoring et de Performance des différents projets de la plateforme
j. Analyser les données afférentes au programme pour les informer sur une base régulière.
k. Préparer les éléments du rapport trimestriel d’activités particulièrement les aspects quantitatifs et qualitatifs pour les rapports programmatiques et ceux destinés aux bailleurs.
l. S’assurer de l’exécution du suivi résultant des contrôles et supervisions.

Le Responsable de Suivi et d’Évaluation partage la co-responsabilité de l’atteinte des objectifs et de la mise en œuvre des activités avec les entités du MSPP concernées.

Qualifications Requises

Education/formation et expériences

• Disposer d'au moins dix ans d'expérience de travail dans le cadre suivi et de l'évaluation de programme.
• Disposer d’une formation de niveau universitaire en statistique et épidémiologie et en suivi et évaluation.
• Expérience dans la coordination de projets et de financements soutenus par des partenaires techniques et financiers comme le Fonds Mondial et la Banque Mondiale serait un atout ;
• Avoir une bonne connaissance de l’environnement de travail avec les directions sanitaires départementales.
• Maitriser les logiciels de base en informatique et expérience dans l'utilisation des logiciels d'analyse des données et de gestion de projets : SAS, SPSS, Epi Info, MAP info, MS Project.
• Être disposé à effectuer au besoin des missions sur le terrain à travers les départements.
• Expérience de travail dans le système national de santé, du MSPP, du système national de gestion d’information, des processus de collecte de données au niveau central et départemental ;

Connaissances, compétences et aptitudes

• Proactivité dans l’anticipation et la résolution de problème de mise en œuvre de projet
• Maitrise et pratique des différentes phases de la gestion du cycle de projet
• Aptitudes de communication, coordination, et de travail en équipe et multidisciplinaire
• Sens de la priorisation dans la coordination des différentes activités
• Compétences de facilitation et de recherche de consensus
• Capacités d’analyse et de synthèse
• Autonomie, rigueur et approche solution et résultats.
• Connaissance des pratiques de financement du développement est un atout.
• Français, créole. Une connaissance de l’anglais est un atout mais non essentielle
• Bonne maitrise des outils informatiques et de communications courants (MS Office, etc.)

Conditions particulières

La durée du contrat est de deux (2) mois. Le renouvellement est conditionné par une évaluation satisfaisante de la performance globale du contractant dans l’exécution des responsabilités assignées suivant le processus standard de l’UGP.

Conditions de travail

Le Responsable de Suivi et d’Évaluation est supervisé par le/la Directeur (trice) Technique de l'UGP-MSPP

The consulting services are expected to last approximately 7 months.

e-mail address: udip@it-park.uz.

Note: This Request for Expression of Interest is being uploaded retrospectively solely for the purpose of completing the procurement records in the World Bank’s Systematic Tracking of Exchanges in Procurement (STEP). The procurement procedure has already been finalized. This publication does not constitute a new invitation or the reopening of the procurement process.

The Central Bank of Kosovo (CBK) has applied for financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Financial Sector Development Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for the following consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include project management, technical advisory, supervision, quality assurance, and stakeholder coordination to support the Central Bank of the Republic of Kosovo (CBK) in the implementation of the Fast Payments System Project under the World Bank–financed Financial Sector Development Project. The assignment covers deployment of the domestic Instant Payments System (TIPS Clone), including system integration, testing, onboarding of participating institutions, and Go-Live readiness. The Consultant will also provide regulatory and strategic advisory services to ensure alignment with EU payment legislation and SEPA standards and prepare Terms of Reference for future procurement of overlay services. The services will extend through Go-Live and project closure, including knowledge transfer and capacity building.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment will be made available to interested consulting firms upon written request sent to the following email address: prokurimi@bqk-kos.org.  

The Central Bank of Kosovo (CBK) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraph 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (Seventh Edition, September 2025) (“the Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

The best qualified firm to carry out the services will be selected in accordance with the Consultant’s Qualifications Based Selection (CQS) method set out in the Regulations and based on the following criteria:

The qualification criteria are:

  1. General Qualification and Competences of the consultant (firm)
  • Capacity, competences and organizational structure, of the Consultant firm (Company)

The consulting firm must be a legally registered entity:

 ---------------------------------------------------------------------------(Max 40 points on this criteria).

  1. Qualification of the consultant (firm) relevant to the assignment:
  • Experience in minimum 1 (one) project in the design, development, and implementation of payment systems.
  • The firm shall demonstrate a proven track record in knowledge transfer and institutional capacity building within financial sector or payment system projects.
  • Demonstrated expertise related to SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst) is required. This requirement may be satisfied through the experience of the firm and/or its proposed key experts.
  • The firm must demonstrate a solid understanding of centralized and distributed payment infrastructures, including requirements related to system resilience, cybersecurity, scalability, and high availability. Prior experience in the Western Balkans region and/or Kosovo is considered an advantage.
  • The firm shall demonstrate strong knowledge of European payment market infrastructures, clearing and settlement arrangements, and payment schemes.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------(Max 60 points on this criteria).

 

As evidence of relevant experience, the consulting firm shall submit a table summarizing comparable assignments, including: assignment title, client name, scope of work, year of implementation, country/region, contract value, and reference contact details.

The Consultant firm may also submit other documents and which are not listed above in order to justify general qualifications and qualifications relevant to the assignment it considers relevant, such us indicative list of the key staff/key personnel that is generally available for this kind of work.

Qualifications and experience of Key Experts shall not be included.

Government of the People’s Republic of Bangladesh

Ministry of Social Welfare

Department of Social Services

Strengthening Social Protection for Improved Resilience,

Inclusion, and Targeting (SSPIRIT) Project

21/1 & 21/2 Bir Uttam A.N.M. Nuruzzaman Sarak,

Shyamoli Square (9th Floor), Shyamoli, Dhaka-1207.

   Memo No.41.01.0000.126.07.024.2026-414                                                   Date: 03 November, 2026

 

Request for Expression of Interest (REOI)

 

The World Bank is supporting the Government of the People’s Republic of Bangladesh to better serve the poorest and most vulnerable populations by expanding coverage and strengthening delivery of the national social protection system for the poor through an IDA Credit of USD 200 million for the “Strengthening Social Protection for Improved Resilience, Inclusion and Targeting (SSPIRIT)” project. Key features of the initiative include, i) establishment and roll out of a Dynamic Social Registry (DSR), which will act as a central platform to improve the accuracy and efficiency of identifying and supporting beneficiaries; ii) strengthening Institutional Capacity for service delivery; iii) enhancing benefits adequacy of allowance programs; iv) strengthening skills development and complementary services; and v) providing tailored livelihood support to vulnerable group.

 

DSS intends to utilize a part of this credit to hire a MIS Specialist as an individual national consultant to ensure effective management of the Project.   

 

  • MIS Specialist (Package No. SD-04): 1 Position

 

Qualifications & Experience

  1. Master's Degree in ICT/ CSE / CS/ MBA in MIS or equivalent;
  2. At least Fifteen (10) Years of overall experience;
  3. Hands on Experience in comprehensive software development.
  4. Experience in Programming languages such as Python, Java and PHP.
  5. Expertise in CI/CD implementation
  6. Must have minimum Five (05) years' experience as MIS Expert/Specialist in any International Development Partner funded programs/project;
  7. Demonstrated successful experience in technical projects with large scale MIS specially in social protection/ Services domain;
  8. Excellent communication skills in English and preferably working experience with foreign agencies/firms/stakeholders.

 

  • SSPIRIT, DSS now invites eligible applicant(s) to indicate their interest in providing the services mentioned above. The Applicants are invited for providing information in detail including their qualifications to perform the service (complete CV along with a description of the similar assignment, experience in similar position and conditions, general qualification etc.)

 

  • A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Selection of Individual Consultants (SIC) method set out in the Procurement Regulations. The Procurement Regulations can be viewed at the World Bank’s external website: https://thedocs.worldbank.org/en/doc/178331533065871195-0290022020/original/Procurement Regulations.pdf

 

  • The attention of interested Consultants is drawn in particular to:
    • Section III, paragraphs, 3.15, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, Sixth Edition, February 2025setting forth the World Bank’s policy on Conflict of Interest, and (ii) Section III, paragraphs, 3.20-3.25 of the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, Sixth Edition, February 2025 setting forth the World Bank’s policy on Eligibility, including the specific pre-requisite conditions to be met for the eligibility, on exceptional basis of Government officials and civil servants of the Borrower’s country under consulting contracts in the Borrower’s country.

 

  • Individuals who are currently working as MIS Specialist/consultants on another World Bank-financed project may also compete in this selection process, but if they are selected they will be required before signing the proposed contract to provide documentary evidence of having satisfactorily complied with their existing contract’s requirements with respect to early termination of the contract by the consultant, including advance notice period, to avoid disruption in implementation of that project.

 

  • Expression of Interest shall have to be submitted to the address mention below (in person, by mail or through email: procurement.sspirit.dss@gmail.com) by 30 November, 2026 by 4:00 pm and be clearly marked as "Expressions of Interest for the position of (………….……………………..………)” in the email’s subject line or on top of the envelope.

 

  • The client reserves the right to accept or reject any/all Expressions of Interest (EOI) or cancel the EOI process at any stage without assigning any reason whatsoever and without incurring any liability to the affected applicant(s).

 

  • TOR can be found at the following website: http://www.dss.gov.bd/; further information in this regard could be obtained from the undersigned during office hours (9:00 AM to 4:00 PM BST).

  1. Background and Rationale

The Government of the Republic of Moldova is implementing the Strengthening Moldova's Disaster Risk Management and Resilience Project (SMORE), financed by the World Bank. The Project aims to strengthen national preparedness and resilience to natural hazards and climate-related shocks, including through improved policy, regulatory and technical instruments for disaster risk reduction.

This assignment is part of Subcomponent 3.1 - which includes technical assistance for the development of methodologies, regulatory documents, data systems and supporting tools aimed at reducing seismic risk in the Republic of Moldova. Within this framework, the methodology for the elaboration of the Interactive Map on Seismic Risk is required as a core technical product linking seismic hazard, exposure and vulnerability information into a coherent and usable risk assessment framework.

The Republic of Moldova is exposed to significant seismic hazard, primarily generated by the Vrancea intermediate-depth seismic source (Romania), which has historically affected the entire territory of the country. The 1940 (M 7.4) and 1977 (M 7.2) earthquakes underlined the vulnerability of the existing building stock and the importance of integrated risk assessment for prioritization of public investment, retrofit planning and emergency preparedness. In this context, an interactive seismic risk map — built on an explicit and reproducible methodology — is a foundational instrument for evidence-based seismic risk management.

    1. Conceptual scope of the interactive seismic risk map

Object of the risk assessment. This Terms of Reference addresses the seismic risk of buildings. The primary risk objects of the methodology and of the interactive map are buildings — residential, public and other categories agreed with the Client — consistent with the PAD, with the RVS methodology under GD 334/2025 (Activity 1b) and with the retrofit feasibility studies under Activity 1d. Critical facilities and infrastructure may be represented as contextual/ancillary layers for interpretation and prioritization (e.g. location of hospitals, schools, emergency services), but the full seismic risk modelling of infrastructure networks (utilities, transport, lifelines) is outside the scope of this assignment, because it requires component-specific fragility models and network data that are not available in the Republic of Moldova and are not covered by the Subcomponent 3.1 data chain

The interactive seismic risk map is not, by design, a mere visualization product. It is the visible output of a structured technical process that must define: the data architecture, the calculation logic, the risk indicators and their thresholds, the treatment of uncertainties, the scenarios to be assessed, and the rules for presenting results in a transparent, auditable and reproducible manner. The map shall enable public authorities, technical experts and decision makers to identify where seismic risk is concentrated, which factors drive that risk, and how alternative assumptions or scenarios affect the outcome.

The assignment is closely coupled with the other outputs of Subcomponent 3.1, in particular: (i) the methodology for seismic hazard zoning developed under Activity 1a, which provides the hazard input layer; (ii) the Rapid Visual Screening (RVS) methodology operationalized through Activity 1b, which provides the building-level exposure and vulnerability data; (iii) the future regulatory NCM package harmonized with Eurocode 8; and (iv) the seismic risk reduction recommendations to be developed under subsequent project activities. Os serviços de consultoria de Contratação de um(a) Gestor(a) da Equipa Técnica de Infraestruturas para a realização das actividades no âmbito do PAT II incluem: a) Liderar, organizar e coordenar a equipa multidisciplinar de infraestruturas, definindo prioridades, responsabilidades, produtos e prazos e acompanhando sistematicamente o cumprimento dos planos de trabalho; b) Assegurar o planeamento integrado da carteira de obras, articulando o progresso físico, os cronogramas de execução, os custos, os processos de contratação e os requisitos técnicos, ambientais e sociais; e c) Monitorizar sistematicamente o progresso das obras e dos contratos, identificando riscos, atrasos, dependências e constrangimentos, e assegurando a definição e o acompanhamento de medidas correctivas.

 

O Projecto de Empoderamento da Rapariga e Aprendizagem Para Todos convida por este meio, os consultores individuais ("Consultores") elegíveis a manifestarem o seu interesse em prestar os Serviços. Os consultores interessados deverão fornecer informações que demonstrem que possuem as qualificações requeridas e experiência relevante para executar os serviços. A qualificação e experiências mínimas para execução dos serviços são as seguintes:

 

1) Grau de Licenciatura ou superior em Engenharia Civil ou Arquitectura. Formação pós-graduada ou certificação em Gestão de Projectos será considerada uma vantagem; 2) Experiência profissional comprovada de, pelo menos, 10 anos em projectos de engenharia, arquitetura ou construção, incluindo planeamento, elaboração ou revisão de projectos, execução ou fiscalização de obras. Experiência em infraestruturas sociais, preferencialmente escolares, será considerada uma vantagem; 3) Experiência comprovada de, pelo menos, 5 anos na liderança e gestão de equipas técnicas multidisciplinares, incluindo planeamento e distribuição do trabalho, definição de responsabilidades e prazos, coordenação de entregas, orientação dos membros da equipa e acompanhamento do seu desempenho; 4) Experiência comprovada na gestão de projectos ou programas complexos de infraestruturas, envolvendo múltiplas obras, contratos e/ou localizações, incluindo planeamento integrado, gestão de prioridades, cronogramas, dependências, riscos e acompanhamento de marcos e resultados; 5) Experiência comprovada na gestão e acompanhamento de contratos de obras e serviços de engenharia, incluindo acompanhamento de obrigações contratuais, medições, alterações, não conformidades, reclamações, prazos contratuais e articulação com empresas de construção e fiscalização; 6) Experiência técnica comprovada na análise e resolução de problemas de engenharia ou arquitectura, incluindo capacidade para orientar equipas na análise de soluções e apoiar a revisão de projectos, desenhos, especificações técnicas, mapas de quantidades e outros produtos técnicos; 7) Experiência na utilização de ferramentas de planeamento, gestão e monitorização, incluindo cronogramas Excel avançado, dashboards e/ou softwares de gestão de projectos, para acompanhamento de progresso, prazos, custos, riscos e indicadores; 8) Experiência  na integração de requisitos ambientais, sociais e de segurança e saúde no trabalho, em projectos de infraestruturas, em articulação com as respectivas áreas especializadas e 9) Excelente capacidade de comunicação oral e escrita na língua Portuguesa e conhecimento funcional da língua Inglesa.

 

Importante atentar que não é permitida a contratação, a qualquer título, de servidores activos da Administração Pública de qualquer nível do Governo, bem como de empregados de suas subsidiárias e controladas, no âmbito dos projectos financiados pelo Banco Mundial. REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

Country: Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia

Project: Lowlands Livelihood Resilience Project Phase Two (LLRP-II)

Assignment Title: Consultancy service for Detail Design for Adigafelema irrigation scheme from groundwater sources [40 Ha]

Credit No.: IDA- 7519-ET

Procurement Reference No.: ET-DR-RPCU-571065-CS-QCBS

  1. The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia has received financing from the World Bank (IDA) and IFAD toward the cost of the Lowlands Livelihood Resilience Project Phase Two (LLRP-II), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services for the detailed design of the Adigafelema irrigation scheme from groundwater sources [40 Ha] in Aseliso Woreda.
  2. The consulting services (“the Services”) include the following:

The objective of the assignment is to prepare a bankable, climate-resilient, environmentally sustainable, socially inclusive, and implementation-ready irrigation scheme in accordance with national standards, the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) and IFAD SECAP. Specifically, the Consultant shall:

  • Verify existing groundwater investigations (hydrogeology, boreholes, pumping tests, water quality) and assess long-term sustainability of abstraction; no new production well design is envisaged unless instructed;
  • Undertake baseline, socioeconomic, gender and social inclusion, soil and land suitability, agronomic and agricultural economics studies, and a climate-risk assessment;
  • Carry out topographic and geotechnical surveys and the feasibility study, including technical, economic and financial analysis of alternatives;
  • Prepare the ESIA and applicable ESF instruments (ESMP, SEP, LMP, IPMP, GBV/SEA/SH risk assessment);
  • Prepare detailed designs of the solar-pumped, pipe-supported surface irrigation system and drainage, drawings, technical specifications, Bills of Quantities, cost estimates, tender documents and construction readiness package; and
  • Develop the operation and maintenance framework and Water Users Association arrangements, and build the capacity of stakeholders.

The Consultant shall carry out all investigations, surveys, analyses, assessments, stakeholder consultations, designs, cost estimates and tender document preparation to achieve the objectives above, in accordance with generally accepted professional standards, whether or not a specific activity is cited in the Terms of Reference. The estimated level of effort is 25.25 key-expert staff-months. The assignment duration is three (3) calendar months (twelve weeks) from the contract commencement date, and the assignment is expected to start on February 25th, 2027.

The Dire Dawa Administration Agriculture, Water, Mines and Energy Bureau, LLRP-II Regional Project Coordination Unit now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and services.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained from the address given below.

3. The shortlisting criteria are:

  • Core business and years in business: the firm’s core business shall be in irrigation and water resources engineering consultancy services; provide the company profile, registration certificate, and number of years in business;
  • Relevant experience: proven experience during the last ten (10) years in feasibility studies, detailed design and ESIA of irrigation and drainage schemes (preferably groundwater-based and/or solar-powered schemes) and preparation of tender documents; experience on World Bank- or IFAD-financed projects is an advantage. For each assignment, indicate the client, location, irrigated area, contract value, duration and the firm’s role, supported by contract or completion certificates;
  • Technical and managerial capability of the firm: managerial and organizational structure, survey and field equipment, design software (e.g. for hydraulic and pipe network design), quality assurance systems and capacity to mobilize field teams. Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

In addition, please refer to the following specific information on conflict of interest related to this assignment: the selected Consultant will prepare the detailed design, technical specifications, bills of quantities, cost estimates, and tender documents for the construction of the irrigation scheme. Accordingly, the Consultant and any of its affiliates, joint venture partners and sub-consultants shall be disqualified from providing goods, works or non-consulting services resulting from or directly related to this assignment, including the construction works and the supply and installation of the solar pumping system. REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST

(Consulting Services – Individual Selection)

Country
