Assignment Title

Senior Personal Data Protection Compliance & Audit Advisor

Reference No.

ET-NIDP-573615-CS-INDV

Required No.

1 (one)

Organization

Ethiopian Communications Authority (ECA)

Duty Station

Ethiopian Communications Authority (ECA), Addis Ababa, Ethiopia

Employment Type

Contract

Duration

12 months, with possibility of extension subject to satisfactory performance and availability of budget

The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia, Ministry of Finance (MoF), has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Ethiopia Digital ID for Inclusion and Services Project. The National ID Program (NIDP), the ultimate project implementer, intends to apply part of the proceeds for selecting an individual consultant.

The National ID Program is seeking a Senior Personal Data Protection Compliance & Audit Advisor to support the Ethiopian Communications Authority (ECA) in strengthening ECA’s personal data protection compliance, audit, inspection, risk assessment, and regulatory supervision functions under Personal Data Protection Proclamation No. 1321/2024 and applicable subsidiary legislation, directives, standards, and guidelines.

1. Background

The Government of Ethiopia has established a comprehensive legal framework for the protection of personal data through Personal Data Protection Proclamation No. 1321/2024. The Proclamation designates the Ethiopian Communications Authority (ECA) as the national authority responsible for regulating and enforcing personal data protection.

ECA’s mandate includes, among others, registration and supervision of data controllers and processors, compliance monitoring, investigation of violations and complaints, development of regulatory instruments, and enforcement of personal data protection requirements. The Proclamation establishes obligations concerning lawful and fair processing, purpose limitation, storage limitation, security and confidentiality, data-subject rights, registration of controllers and processors, Data Protection Officers, technical and organizational measures, breach notification, Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIAs), and privacy by design.

The implementation of these requirements requires ECA to develop a risk-based, systematic and evidence-based compliance and audit capability capable of assessing whether public and private sector organizations are effectively complying with the Proclamation and applicable subsidiary legislation, directives, standards and guidelines. This is further reinforced by Digital Ethiopia 2030, which assigns ECA an expanded role in implementing personal data protection and exercising proactive oversight of digital platforms and data markets.

2. Objective of the Assignment

The overall purpose of the assignment is to provide senior-level professional expertise to strengthen ECA’s personal data protection compliance, audit, inspection and supervisory functions. The Advisor will support ECA in developing and implementing a risk-based compliance and audit framework for data controllers and processors; conducting compliance assessments and audits; identifying systemic and sector-specific privacy risks; assessing technical and organizational measures; supporting DPIA and high-risk processing assessments; developing audit tools and methodologies; monitoring corrective actions; and providing evidence-based recommendations for regulatory intervention and enforcement.

The Advisor shall also support ECA in translating the personal data protection objectives of Digital Ethiopia 2030 into practical supervisory mechanisms for digital platforms, data-driven businesses, emerging technologies and data markets.

3. Scope of Services / Key Responsibilities

The Advisor will:

  • Establish risk-based frameworks, indicators, maturity models, and annual plans for supervisory inspections, audits, desk reviews, and regulatory follow-ups.
  • Plan and lead audits to assess compliance with Proclamation No. 1321/2024 and other applicable laws and directives, evaluating entities’ governance structures, DPO arrangements, policy enforcement, registration accuracy, and data-subject rights implementation.
  • Evaluate the adequacy of technical controls, including access management, encryption, logging, backup, physical security, data localization, cloud arrangements, and cross-border transfer safeguards.
  • Review Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIAs) and assess risks linked to high-risk processing, digital platforms, data monetization, and emerging technologies, including AI, biometrics, digital ID, cloud, IoT and fintech.
  • Assess breach preparedness, investigate root causes and control failures in reported incidents, review notification compliance, and oversee remedial action plans.
  • Provide technical evidence, risk ratings, and recommendations to support ECA’s regulatory inquiries, enforcement actions, corrective orders, and administrative sanctions.
  • Formulate standardized supervisory toolkits, including audit manuals, inspection checklists, sector guidelines, DPIA/breach assessment templates, and compliance dashboards.
  • Deliver technical training, develop audit materials, mentor ECA inspection teams, and facilitate awareness workshops with controllers, processors, and peer data protection authorities.
  • Execute any additional assignments directed by ECA leadership to support ECA’s mandate.

4. Minimum Qualifications and Professional Experience

The candidate should have:

  • A minimum of a Master’s degree in Information Technology; Computer Science; Cybersecurity; Information Security; Information Systems; Data Science/Data Engineering; Computer Engineering; Telecommunications Engineering; Digital Transformation; Privacy/Data Protection; Risk Management; or another closely related discipline.
  • At least ten (10) years of progressively responsible professional experience in personal data protection, privacy compliance, information security, technology risk, IT audit, cybersecurity, data governance, regulatory compliance, or related fields.
  • Of which at least five (5) years shall involve substantial experience in personal data protection/privacy compliance, IT audit, information-security auditing, regulatory supervision, or data-governance assessment.
  • Demonstrated experience conducting compliance audits, IT audits, privacy assessments, security assessments or regulatory inspections.
  • Demonstrated experience developing compliance frameworks, audit methodologies, risk assessment tools and supervisory mechanisms.
  • Experience assessing cloud environments, data centers, digital platforms, data-sharing arrangements and third-party processors.
  • Experience in data breach assessment and incident-response compliance.
  • Experience working in a multi-stakeholder regulatory environment.
  • Good communication skills in both English and Amharic.

5. Duration and Location

The consultant will be engaged on a full-time basis for an initial period of twelve (12) months, with the possibility of extension subject to satisfactory performance and availability of budget. The position will be based in Addis Ababa, Ethiopian Communications Authority (ECA).

The Advisor shall report to the Deputy Director General responsible for Personal Data Protection at ECA, or another designated ECA supervisor, and shall work in close coordination with the Personal Data Protection Directorate and other relevant ECA departments.

6. Selection Method

The selection method is based on paragraphs 7.36 and 7.37 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations. The attention of interested individuals is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers,” July 2016, as revised November 2017, August 2018, and February 2025, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

An individual will be selected in accordance with the Selection of Individual Consultant (Section V) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

7. Submission of Expression of Interest

The National ID Program, Digital ID for Inclusion and Services Project, now invites eligible individual consultants to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The Expression of Interest should include CV, formal application/cover letter; and Documentary evidence supporting the stated qualifications and experience, including descriptions of relevant assignments and experience in similar conditions.

CVs, formal application letters and all supporting documents must be delivered in written form to the address below in person, or by mail, preferably by e-mail, on or before November 16, 2026.

Further information may be obtained by e-mail during office hours from 8:30 AM to 5:30 PM Addis Ababa time.

CONSULTING SERVICES OF THE FIRM

to

(MLVT-CS-20-A)

 

Cambodia

Procurement Tittle:   Consultancy Firm to Support the Upgrading of the Job Matching Portal (Digital) of the National Employment Agency and Developing the Labour Market Information System (LMIS)

Procurement No.:     MLVT-CS-20-A

 

  1. The Royal Government of Cambodia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Skills for Better Jobs Project (SBJ) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

 

  1. The consulting services (“the Services”) is to address these challenges, MLVT intends to strengthen two key components of the LMIS ecosystem:

(i) the development of an integrated LMIS website to disseminate structured labour market information to jobseekers, employers, policymakers, and training providers. It must include the following:

  1. Job-matching portal;
  2. Counseling Service portal (the Developed Digital Self-Assessment Tool, Graduate survey, Tracer study, Migration data); and
  3. Labour Market Intelligence portal.

(ii) the enhancement of the NEA Job Matching Portal to improve the quality and transparency of job matching services. These two components will operate as complementary systems that share common taxonomies, datasets, and API services.

For in depth understanding of the required services under this assignment, please referred to the ToR of this consultancy for your reference.

 

  1. The SBJ Project is now invites eligible Consulting firm’ “consultants” to support the Upgrading of the Job Matching Portal (Digital) of the National Employment Agency and Developing the Labour Market Information System (LMIS). The specific objectives of the consultancy are to strengthen selected components of Cambodia’s LMIS by:

(1) Providing the technical upgrade of the Job Matching Portal, LMIS website, and supporting infrastructure;

(2) Strengthening data and taxonomy governance for consistent classification and interoperability;

(3) Enhancing institutional capacity to support effective management and maintenance;

The assignment aims to create an integrated digital ecosystem in which it embeds relevant labour market information and insights (e.g., occupational demand trends, skills gap alerts) into the job-matching portal interface to guide informed decisions by jobseekers and employers.

The shortlisting criteria are:

 

The consulting firm must demonstrate substantial institutional experience, technical capability, and a proven record of delivering sustainable digital systems in the employment, labour market, or public-sector domain. Firm must have international experience particularly in system architecture, taxonomy, job matching. The firm must show that it can successfully execute the project within the required timeline and governance environment.

 

Minimum qualifications include:

  • Minimum 10 years of experience in designing, developing, or job matching systems, MIS solutions, or other large-scale government digital systems involving structured datasets and multi-stakeholder workflows.
  • Experience implementing a job portal or a web-based platform for a Public Employment Service (PES) in a country with a population of at least 5 million is an advantage. (please provide reference)
  • Completion of at least three contracts involving:
  • Development and implementation of bidirectional job matching technology for Public Employment Services Agency is an advantage;
  • Implementation of user-facing dashboards and data-driven search or filter features with API-based integration or modular system development for future scalability; knowledge of system interoperability; and
  • Implementation of structured gap analysis or career pathway module.

 

  • Demonstrated at least 3 projects or contracts in developing explainable, rule based, weighted, and bi directional matching algorithms, including transparency features, scoring breakdowns, and fairness considerations and Capability in database restructuring, performance optimisation, data quality assurance, identity resolution, and long-term data governance across bilingual datasets.
  • Demonstrated at least 3 projects or contracts in LMIS or similar labour market analytics solutions, including labour market indicators, Labour Market Taxonomy, dashboards, and data pipelines integrating multiple data sources.
  • Demonstrated at least 3 projects or contracts in CMS implementation for government or private sector or donor-funded content workflows, structured metadata, and accessibility compliance is highly desirable.

 

  1. Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

 

  1. The   detailed   Terms   of   Reference (ToR) for   the   assignment   can   be   found   at   the   link: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1kKkN11mtxpGJleYKvYZxknn14CxtOUGc/view?usp=sharing

notices.title: Personal Data Protection Existing and Emerging Technologies Technical Advisor for ECA
notices.buyer: Prime Minster Office, National ID Program
notices.description:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST

(Consulting Services – Individual Selection)

Senior Personal Data Protection Existing and Emerging Technologies – Technical Advisor

Country

Ethiopia

Project

Ethiopia Digital ID for Inclusion and Services Project

Project ID

P179040

Assignment Title

Senior Personal Data Protection Existing and Emerging Technologies – Technical Advisor

Reference No.

ET-NIDP-573612-CS-INDV

The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia, Ministry of Finance (MoF), has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Ethiopia Digital ID for Inclusion and Services Project. The National ID Program (NIDP), the ultimate project implementer, intends to apply part of the proceeds to select an individual consultant.

The National ID Program is looking for a Senior Personal Data Protection Existing and Emerging Technologies – Technical Advisor located at the Ethiopian Communications Authority (ECA) to support the implementation of the Ethiopia Digital ID for Inclusion and Services Project with respect to providing high-level technical expertise in translating the requirements of the Personal Data Protection Proclamation into practical and technically implementable standards, safeguards, and supervisory mechanisms, among others.

The primary objective of the assignment is to provide high-level technical expertise to support ECA in translating the requirements of the Personal Data Protection Proclamation into practical and technically implementable standards, safeguards, and supervisory mechanisms. The Advisor will bridge technology, cybersecurity, data governance and privacy, enabling ECA to assess risks associated with existing and emerging technologies, strengthen technical compliance audits and DPIA assessments, develop appropriate standards and assessment tools, advise on data localization and cross-border data transfers, support breach-response mechanisms, and enhance the Authority’s oversight of digital platforms and data markets.

Scope of Service and specific tasks

     Scope of Services

The Technical Advisor shall provide specialized technical advisory, assessment, regulatory development, capacity-building, and supervisory support to the Authority in the implementation and enforcement of the Personal Data Protection Proclamation No. 1321/2024 and other applicable legal and regulatory instruments.

The scope of services shall include, but not be limited to, the following:

  • Technology Foresight and Advisory: Advise ECA on the privacy, cybersecurity, and regulatory implications of existing and emerging technologies.
  • Technical Standards Development: Develop technical standards, guidelines, and security baselines for secure personal data processing, storage, and transfer.
  • Technical Risk Assessments: Conduct system reviews, security assessments, and DPIAs for high-risk personal data processing activities.
  • Technical Compliance and Supervision: Develop audit tools and support ECA's inspections and technical compliance assessments of data controllers and processors.
  • Breach and Incident Response: Develop incident-response procedures and support technical investigations, root-cause analysis, and remediation monitoring.
  • Capacity Building and Stakeholder Engagement: Develop training materials and deliver technical training and workshops for ECA staff and relevant stakeholders.
  • Technical Coordination and Other Duties: Collaborate with relevant ECA departments and stakeholders and undertake related assignments directed by ECA leadership within the scope of the assignment.

   Specific Tasks

Based on the above Scope of Service, the Technical Advisor shall perform the following specific tasks:

  • Technology Foresight and Strategic Technical Advisory
  • Development of Technical Standards and Security Baselines
  • Technical Assessments, System Reviews, and DPIAs
  • Technical Compliance Audits and Supervisory Support
  • Personal Data Breach and Security Incident Management
  • Technical Capacity Building and Stakeholder Engagement
  • Reporting, Knowledge Management, and Additional Assignments

Minimum Qualifications and Experience

The candidate is required to have the following minimum Qualifications and Experience:

  • A Master's degree or equivalent in Computer Science, Information Technology, Information Systems, Cybersecurity, Data Science, Telecommunications/Communications Engineering or a related field;
  • At least seven (7) years of relevant professional experience in cyber security, technology strategy, digital transformation, data architecture, emerging technologies, technology governance or a related field;
  • Strong knowledge and demonstrated practical understanding of AI, biometrics, digital identity, cloud computing, privacy-enhancing technologies, data technologies and other emerging technologies;
  • Good understanding of personal data protection, privacy by design and by default, and technology-related regulatory requirements;
  • Experience working with digital public infrastructure, telecommunications, financial services or other complex technology environments is an advantage;
  • Experience or knowledge in RegTech and technology-enabled regulatory solutions is desirable;
  • Strong analytical, research, communication and report-writing skills, including the ability to explain complex technical issues to legal, policy and regulatory audiences;
  • Relevant professional certifications in data protection, privacy, cybersecurity, information technology or related fields are an advantage; and
  • Excellent command of written and spoken English and Amharic.

Duration and Location

The consultant will be engaged on a full-time basis for an initial period of twelve (12) months, with the possibility of extension subject to satisfactory performance and availability of budget. The position will be based in Addis Ababa, Ethiopian Communication Authority (ECA)

The Technical Advisor shall report to the Director General or the designated Deputy Director General/Director responsible for personal data protection, or another designated ECA supervisor. The Advisor shall work in close coordination with the Personal Data Protection Directorate and other relevant ECA departments.

The Advisor shall submit deliverables in editable electronic format, together with supporting technical documentation, assessment tools, and presentation materials where applicable. Reports containing sensitive information shall be handled in accordance with ECA's applicable confidentiality, information-security, and records-management requirements.

Selection Method

The selection method is based on paragraphs 7.36 and 7.37 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations. The attention of interested individuals is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers,” July 2016, as revised, including February 2025, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

An individual will be selected in accordance with the Selection of Individual Consultant (Section V) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Submission of Expression of Interest

National ID Program, Digital ID for Inclusion and Services Project now invites eligible Individual Consultants to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The Expression of Interest should include a CV, formal application/cover letter, and documentary evidence supporting the stated qualifications and experience, including descriptions of relevant assignments and experience in similar conditions.

Expressions of interest must be submitted by e-mail on or before November 16, 2026.

Further information may be obtained by e-mail during office hours from 8:30 AM to 5:30 PM Addis Ababa time.

RÉPUBLIQUE DU BURUNDI

MINISTERE DES FINANCES, DU BUDGET ET DE L’ECONOMIE NUMERIQUE

PROJET D’APPUI AUX FONDATIONS DE L’ECONOMIE NUMERIQUE AU BURUNDI « PAFEN »

Pays : Burundi

N° du projet : P176396/P180987

Don N° : E2820-BI

Références : BI-PAFEN-PIU-2.4.1.13b

AVIS A MANIFESTATION D’INTERET

(SERVICES DE CONSULTANTS)

SÉLECTION DE FIRMES/CABINETS

Recrutement d’un cabinet pour assurer la formation et la certification des techniciens de la DSI, SETIC et de l'OBR sur l'Audit Système d'information (CISA).

  1. Le Gouvernement du Burundi a reçu un financement de la Banque Mondiale pour la mise en place du Projet d’Appui aux Fondations de l’Economie Numérique du Burundi (PAFEN) en sigle « le Projet », et financer ses activités. Il est prévu qu'une partie des ressources de ce financement soit utilisée pour financer les prestations d’un cabinet chargé du « Renforcement des capacités en matière de gouvernance, d’utilisation et de gestion des technologies de l'information » pour le compte du Ministère des Finances, du Budget et de l’Economie Numérique, le Secrétariat Exécutif des Technologies de l’Information (SETIC) et l’Office Burundais des Recettes (OBR)».
  2. Dans ce cadre, le projet prévoit le financement des prestations « d’un cabinet pour assurer la formation et la certification des techniciens de la DSI, SETIC et de l'OBR sur l'Audit Système d'information (CISA).
  3. L'objectif global de la mission est de recruter un cabinet de formation spécialisé et accrédité pour dispenser une formation certifiante en Audit des Systèmes d'Information (CISA) au profit du personnel de la Direction Générale de l'Économie Numérique (DGEN) du Ministère des Finances, du Budget et de l'Économie Numérique (MFBEN), du Secrétariat Exécutif des Technologies de l’Information (SETIC) ainsi que du personnel de la Direction des Technologies de l'Information (DTI). Le cabinet devra être accrédité par l'ISACA ou autorisé par un organisme reconnu par celle-ci à dispenser la formation et à préparer les candidats à la certification CISA, garantissant ainsi la conformité du programme aux standards internationaux. Cette mission vise à renforcer les compétences des participants en matière d'audit, de gouvernance, de contrôle et de gestion des risques des systèmes d'information. Elle leur permettra d'acquérir les connaissances et les compétences nécessaires pour planifier et conduire des missions d'audit, évaluer l'efficacité des contrôles internes, apprécier la conformité des systèmes d'information aux bonnes pratiques et référentiels internationaux, notamment COBIT et les cadres de gouvernance de l'ISACA, afin d'améliorer la sécurité, la fiabilité et la performance des systèmes d'information du MFBEN, du SETIC et de l'OBR.
  4. Spécifiquement, la formation vise à :
  • Comprendre les principes de gouvernance et de management des systèmes d’information, incluant les rôles et responsabilités des différentes parties prenantes.
  • Maîtriser les méthodologies et techniques d’audit des systèmes d’information, y compris la planification, l’évaluation des risques et la conduite des missions d’audit.
  • Identifier, collecter et analyser les informations nécessaires pour évaluer l’efficacité des contrôles internes, la sécurité des systèmes et la conformité aux normes.
  • Évaluer les processus d’acquisition, de développement et de maintenance des systèmes d’information afin de garantir leur alignement avec les objectifs stratégiques de l’organisation.
  • Analyser les contrôles de protection des actifs informationnels et recommander des mesures correctives ou préventives adaptées.
  • Produire des rapports d’audit clairs et exploitables, destinés aux décideurs, managers et parties prenantes techniques.
  • Appliquer des méthodes d’analyse structurée et de gestion des risques pour identifier les vulnérabilités et améliorer la performance et la sécurité des systèmes.
  • Définir et formaliser des processus organisationnels d’audit et de contrôle pour intégrer les bonnes pratiques et assurer la pérennité des systèmes d’information.
  • Organiser le passage des examens officiels CISA;

5. La durée globale de la mission sera négociée entre le fournisseur et le bénéficiaire mais devra s’étendre sur une période ne dépassant pas 8 semaines, à compter de la date de mise en œuvre du contrat.

6. Les Termes de référence peuvent être téléchargés sur le site du PAFEN : https://pafen.gov.bi/appels-doffres/  ou obtenus aux adresses mentionnées ci-dessous.

7. L’Unité de Gestion du PAFEN invite les cabinets (firmes), spécialisés dans le domaine objet desdites prestations intéressés par la présente mission à fournir des informations démontrant qu'ils disposent des qualifications requises et de l'expérience pertinente pour l’exécution des services.

8. Profil du Cabinet : 

La mission sera exécutée par un cabinet de formation agréé et reconnu, spécialisé dans les domaines de la gouvernance des systèmes d’information, de l’audit informatique et de la cybersécurité.

Le cabinet devra répondre aux exigences suivantes :

 1) Justifier d’au moins dix (10) ans d’expérience dans la conduite          de formations certifiantes en audit des systèmes d’information et           en sécurité informatique ;

2) Présenter au moins cinq (5) références pertinentes attestant de la réalisation de missions similaires dans la formation ou l’accompagnement en audit informatique, conformité et gestion des risques IT au cours des trois (3) dernières années ;

3) Fournir des preuves d’accréditation officielles (contrats, certificats, lettres de partenariat, etc.) émises par ISACA ou tout autre organisme reconnu, attestant que le cabinet est habilité à dispenser la formation et à faire passer la certification CISA (Certified Information Systems Auditor) 

4) Fournir un lien vers son site Internet officiel, permettant de vérifier ses activités, ses références et son statut institutionnel.

9. L’attention des Consultants intéressés est attirée sur la Section III, paragraphes 3.14, 3.16 et 3.17 du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement des Projets d’Investissement (FPI) de la Banque mondiale, édition de septembre 2023 (« Règlement de Passation des Marchés relatifs aux règles de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflit d’intérêt).

En outre, veuillez-vous référer aux informations spécifiques sur les conflits d’intérêts liées à cette mission comme énoncés au paragraphe 3.17 du Règlement de Passation des Marchés.

10. Les consultants peuvent s’associer à d’autres firmes pour renforcer leurs compétences, mais ils doivent indiquer clairement si l’association prend la forme d’un groupement solidaire (joint-venture) et / ou d’un accord de sous-traitant. Dans le cas d'un groupement solidaire (joint-venture), tous les partenaires du groupement solidaire (joint-venture) seront conjointement et solidairement responsables de la totalité du contrat, s’ils sont sélectionnés.

11. « Le Consultant » sera sélectionné selon la méthode de Sélection fondée sur les Qualifications du Consultant (SQC), conformément au Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le financement de Projets d’Investissement (FPI) de la Banque mondiale, édition de Septembre 2023 et conformément aux critères exigés au regard des présents termes de référence ».

12. De plus amples informations peuvent être obtenues à l’adresse ci-dessous pendant les heures de bureau : de 8H :00 à 12H :00 et de 13H: 00 à 17H : 30 heure locale de lundi à vendredi (heure de Bujumbura : GMT+2)

13. Les manifestations d'intérêt écrites doivent être remises par écrit à l'adresse ci-dessous par courrier ordinaire ou par e-mail au plus tard le 20/11/2026 à 17 heures 00 (heure de Bujumbura, GMT+2) avec la mention :

« REPONSE A L’AVIS DE SOLLICITATION DE MANIFESTATIONS D'INTERET N° BI-PAFEN-PIU- 2.4.1.13b -CS- SQC PORTANT RECRUTEMENT D’UN CABINET POUR ASSURER LA FORMATION ET LA CERTIFICATION DES TECHNICIENS DE LA DSI, SETIC ET DE L'OBR SUR L'AUDIT SYSTEME D'INFORMATION (CISA).

14. L’adresse à laquelle il est fait référence ci-dessus est :

A l’Attention de Bienvenu IRAKOZE, Coordonnateur du PAFEN

REPUBLIC OF LIBERIA

MINISTRY OF GENDER, CHILDREN, AND SOCIAL PROTECTION

Ministerial Complex, Congo Town 1000 Monrovia 10, Liberia, West Africa

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REOI)

 

COUNTRY:                 

Republic of Liberia  

NAME OF PROJECT: 

Liberia Women Empowerment Project  

PROJECT ID:              

P173677                        

CREDIT/GRANT No.: 

IDA-7168-LR and E0910-LR             

ASSIGNMENT:

 

 

Consulting Services for the Development, Deployment, Rollout and Post-Deployment Support for a Gender-Based Management Information System (GB MIS)

REFERENCE No.:     LR-MOGCSP-546313-CS-CQS

The Government of the Republic of Liberia through the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Liberia Women Empowerment Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for the Consulting Services for the Development, Deployment, Rollout and Post-Deployment Support of a Gender-Based Management Information System (GB MIS) at the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection (MGCSP)

 

Objective of the Assignment  

The objective of the consultancy is to develop and operationalize an integrated Gender-Based Management Information System (GB MIS) for the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection (MGCSP) that will enhance the Ministry’s institutional capacity to systematically collect, capture, store, manage, analyze, visualize, and report gender-related data and information. The consultancy will cover the design, development, testing, deployment, rollout, user training, documentation, and post-deployment support of the GB MIS, ensuring that the system is scalable, secure, interoperable, user-friendly, and aligned with the Ministry’s gender data and information management requirements.

The system is expected to improve the availability, quality, accessibility, timeliness, and use of sex- and gender-disaggregated data to support evidence-based policy and program planning, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, coordination, and decision-making at national and sub-national levels

The Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection (“the Client”) now invites eligible Consultants to submit an Expression of Interest (EOI) in providing the Services. Interested firms must provide their detailed profile demonstrating that they meet the following shortlisting criteria:

  • Core business of the firm/JV/Consortium that is relevant to the assignment  
  • At least 7 years of general experience in design, development, deployment, and support of Management Information Systems (MIS), digital platforms, or integrated ICT systems.
  • At least 5 years of specific experience implementing MIS or digital systems for government institutions, donor-funded projects, or development partner-supported programs. 
  • Have a proven record of successful completion of at least 3 similar MIS or digital system assignments within the last 5–7 years, of comparable scope and complexity.
  • Have experience implementing at least 2 assignments for government institutions, donor-funded, or development partner-financed programs, preferably in the social, gender, GBV, or related sectors. Experience in West Africa is an advantage.
  • Demonstrated experience in delivering end-to-end digital solutions, including system design, development, integration, deployment, training, documentation, and postdeployment support.
  • Demonstrated experience in system integration, interoperability, data management, and scalable solutions for decentralized or multi-location operations.
  • Evidence of capacity for knowledge transfer, user training, technical support, and preparation of system and operational documentation.
  • Evidence of technical and managerial capability to complete the assignment (Provide only the structure of the firm, general qualifications, and number of key staff. Do not provide CVs of staff as Key experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.)  

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to the fact that the selection of Firm/Consortium will be done in accordance with the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (“Procurement Regulations”) dated July 2016, revised in November 2017 and August 2018, and updated in November 2020, September 2023, February 2025, and September 2025

Consultants may associate with other firms in the form of a joint venture or a sub consultancy to enhance their qualifications.

A Firm/Consortium of firms will be selected in accordance with the Consultant Qualification Selection (CQS) method set out in the IPF Procurement Regulations.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours 0900 to 1700 hours from Monday to Friday, excluding lunch hour (1300 to 1400 hours) and public holidays. A Copy of the Detailed Terms of Reference for this assignment with scope of assignment and specific tasks, qualifications and experience, and other requirements, can be access on the Ministry’s website:https://mogcsp.gov.lr/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/MGCSP-GBMIS-TOR-2026.pdf  

The completed expression of interest documents in writing, three (3) copies, must be delivered to the Procurement Unit or by email to the address below to be received on or before November 23, 2026, at 1500 hours GMT. Le Gouvernement de la République du Cameroun a obtenu de la Banque Mondiale le financement IDA 6770 - CM pour l’exécution du Projet d’Aménagement et de Valorisation des Investissements de la Vallée de la Bénoué (VIVA-BENOUE) et se propose d’utiliser une partie de ce financement pour effectuer des paiements autorisés au titre du Contrat objet de la présente demande de cotation.

Le Projet d’Aménagement et de Valorisation des Investissements de la Vallée de la Bénoué (VIVA-BENOUE) sollicite des offres fermées de la part de soumissionnaires éligibles et répondant aux qualifications requises pour l’exécution des travaux de construction d’une salle de conférence à l’Ecole Technique d’Agriculture de Garoua.

Le financement relatif à ce Marché est assuré par le Crédit IDA N° 6770 - CM de l’Association Internationale de Développement (IDA).

La passation du marché sera conduite par mise en concurrence en recourant à une Demande de Cotations Ouvertes (DCO) tel que définie dans le « Règlement de Passation des Marchés de la Banque mondiale pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le financement des projets d’investissement (FPI) pour les Fournitures, Travaux, Services Autres que des Services de Consultants, révisée en septembre 2025 » et ouvert à tous les soumissionnaires de pays éligibles tels que définis dans le Règlement susvisé.

Le Dossier de demande de cotation, rédigé en langue française, est disponible gratuitement :

  • sur la plateforme COLEPS : www.marchespublics.cm et www.publiccontracts.cm ;
  • sur le site de l’ARMP : www.armp.cm ;

Chaque offre est rédigée en français ou en anglais et devra être transmise par le soumissionnaire via la plateforme COLEPS au plus tard le 02 Novembre 2026 à 10 heures précises. Une copie de sauvegarde de l’offre enregistrée sur clé USB ou CD/DVD devra être transmise sous pli scellé portant clairement la mention « copie de sauvegarde – Demande de Cotation Ouvert N° 005_/DCO/ MINEPAT/ MEADEN /VIVA-BENOUE/UGP/CSPM/RAF/SPM/2026 du 05 octobre 2026 pour l’exécution des travaux de construction d’une salle de conférence à l’Ecole Technique d’Agriculture de Garoua. » « A N’OUVRIR QU’EN SÉANCE DE DÉPOUILLEMENT ».

Format PDF pour les documents textuels ;

NB : l’absence de l’offre témoin entraîne l’irrecevabilité de l’offre du candidat concerné, dès l’ouverture des plis par la Commission de Passation des Marchés.

Chaque soumissionnaire doit joindre à ses pièces administratives un cautionnement de soumission, acquitté à la main, délivré par un organisme ou une institution financière agréée par le Ministre chargé des Finances pour émettre des cautions dans le domaine des marchés publics don’t la liste figure en annexe de la présente Demande de cotations accompagné d’unn récépissé de consignation délivré par la Caisse de Dépôt et Consignation (CDEC).

Ces deux pièces sont obligatoires et éliminatoires. Le montant de la caution s’élève à Cinq cent mille (500 000) Francs CFA. Néanmoins, la présentation de ces pièces conformes, signées et datées sera une condition d’attribution du marché.

La période de validité des offres est de quatre-vingt-dix (90) jours à compter de la date d’ouverture des plis.

The Government of the Republic of Moldova has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Strengthening Moldova’s Disaster Risk Management and Resilience Project, and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

 

The consulting services (“the Services”) include the consultancy services for the Preparation of Functional and Technical Requirements and Procurement-Ready Technical Specification for the RVS Mobile Application and Data Collection Workflow.

 

The Terms of Reference (TOR) for the primary procurement stage for the assignment are attached to this request for expressions of interest.

The Ministry of Infrastructure and Regional Development (MIRD) and the P.I. “Office for External Assistance Programs Management” (OEAPM) Project Implementation Unit (PIU) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria is:

At least 5 (five) years of experience in combining seismic/RVS methodology knowledge, building screening and vulnerability assessment, GIS/spatial data modelling, data quality control and QA/UAT design , together with IT business analysis for digital data-collection systems.

Background and Rationale

The Government of the Republic of Moldova is implementing the Strengthening Moldova's Disaster Risk Management and Resilience Project (SMORE), financed by the World Bank. The Project aims to strengthen the country's preparedness and resilience to natural hazards and climate-related shocks, including through improved policy, regulatory and technical instruments for disaster risk reduction.

This assignment is part of Subcomponent 3.1 – Policy, Regulatory, and Feasibility Study Support to Reduce Seismic Risk. Within this Subcomponent, the Rapid Visual Screening (RVS) of buildings represents one of the foundational mechanisms for collecting standardized exposure and vulnerability information at building level. RVS data feed directly into the seismic risk assessment chain — combined with the seismic hazard outputs developed under Activity 1a and with the seismic risk map methodology developed under Activity 1c — and constitute a primary input for prioritization of risk reduction interventions, retrofit feasibility studies, public-investment planning and emergency preparedness.

The Republic of Moldova is exposed to significant seismic hazard, primarily generated by the Vrancea intermediate-depth seismic source (Romania), which has historically affected the entire territory of the country. The 1940 (M 7.4) and 1977 (M 7.2) earthquakes demonstrated the vulnerability of the existing building stock and underlined the need for a systematic, standardized and traceable building inventory and screening process. In this context, RVS is recognized internationally — through methodologies such as FEMA P-154/P-155, EMS-98 vulnerability classification and EU national approaches — as a cost-effective first-tier tool for building-level screening prior to detailed engineering assessment.

Role and scope of the RVS mobile application

The RVS mobile application is, by design, an operational tool for standardized field data collection, executed in accordance with the RVS methodology described in Government Decision No. 334 of 05.06.2025 and with the quality-assurance requirements applicable under the Project. Together with the web-based administration and data-management portal defined in Section 3.4, it forms a single digital data-collection solution operating on one controlled backend database. The application shall ensure that building-level exposure and vulnerability information is collected in a uniform, controlled and traceable manner, so that the resulting dataset is fit-for-purpose for seismic risk assessment, GIS integration, prioritization and future regulatory or investment decisions.

The mobile application shall not, however, be treated as the primary technical substance of this assignment. The critical quality risk under Activity 1b is not the coding of a mobile application as such, but the correct translation of seismic risk principles, RVS methodology, building typology, vulnerability indicators, field screening logic, scoring rules, data validation and GIS/export requirements into a clear, complete, testable and procurement-ready functional and technical specification. The future software solution is expected to implement standard mobile data-collection functions — structured forms, role-based access, mandatory fields, photo and GPS capture, offline operation, synchronization, review/validation status, export and audit trail — and is not expected to perform complex seismic modelling or scientific hazard calculations within the application itself.

Justification and need

The Republic of Moldova currently lacks a unified, digital building inventory aligned with modern RVS practice and with the requirements of GD 334/2025. Existing building data are fragmented across cadastral, statistical and sectoral sources, are not structured around vulnerability/exposure indicators, do not follow a controlled data dictionary, and are not directly usable as input for seismic risk analysis. A procurement-ready specification for an RVS mobile application and the underlying data-collection workflow is therefore a precondition for:

  • the practical operationalization of the RVS methodology established by GD 334/2025;
  • the production of a building-level dataset compatible with the seismic risk map methodology developed under Activity

The Government of Malawi (GoM), through Blantyre Water Board (BWB) and Blantyre City Council (BCC) has secured financial support from the International Development Agency (IDA) of the World Bank (WB) towards the cost of the Malawi Water and Sanitation Project-1 (MWSP-1) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

Blantyre Water Board (BWB), which is the main implementing agency, intends to apply part of these proceeds from the grant to recruit an individual consultant to take up assignment of Contract Management Specialist to be positioned in the Project Implementation Unit (PIU) for the Malawi Water and Sanitation Project (MWSP-1) in adherence to the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers.

  1. Scope of the Services

The Contract Management Specialist shall assist and be answerable to the PIU Manager and will play a crucial role to support the project on contract compliance and risk management by spearheading the planning, design /review implementation, monitoring and management (supervision) of all contracts under the Project according to the World Bank Procurement regulations and work according to principles of good practice in contract management, and bear responsibility for performance management and cost effectiveness of contracts. The specialist will be expected to work very closely with the other members of the PIU and technical officers from the implementing agencies such as BWB, BCC, Ministry responsible for water development, and Ministry responsible for sanitation and hygiene, in the management and supervision of all contracts under the project. Specifically, the Contract Management Specialist will perform the following duties:

  1. Work hand in hand with the procurement team to prepare contract documents covering specifically guarantee requirements, price-adjustment provisions and indices, commencement and effectiveness conditions, sectional and substantial completion arrangements, and other potential claims risks.
  2. Provide support on contract administration and management with focus on proper contract compliance and performance oversight management for example appropriate determination of time and cost entitlements, variations to ensure technical necessity, accuracy as well as consistent value-for-money pricing; IPC reviews, contract price adjustment calculations, contingency utilization assessments and contract performance assessments;
  3. Undertake regular contract progress reports reviews and preparation of a synthesis report of key findings and recommended actions;
  4. Undertake proper project closure by ensuring preparation and issuance of completion certificates, management of the defects liability period, including decommissioning, final inspections, supervision requirements, outstanding payment obligations, completion documentation etc.,
  5. Manage works supervision contracts (both lumpsum and time-based consultancy contracts) by tracking deliverables, timesheets and associated payments;
  6. Maintain contract management tracking for all the contracts under implementation and coordinate any variation required, well in time as per contract.
  7. Monitoring and analyzing contracts performance under the projects against agreed benchmarks and advise Contract Managers in monitoring agreed contract-management key performance indicators, identifying potential bottlenecks and recommended remedial actions (close-out, extension or renewal of contracts) according to the FIDIC Conditions of Contract;
  8. Assist in resolving any unforeseen technical difficulties, complaints and other problems that may arise in the process of implementation
  9. Communicate regularly with the management on the status of various contracts, and ensure proper guidance and approvals are acquired before any contract amendments or cancellation / termination as per contract provisions.
  10. Assist the project in preparing realistic work plans and budgets for execution of contracts and tracking progress including undertaking period updating of contract management module in STEP.
  11. In liaison with the Contracts Managers (Engineers and implementing team), conduct progress review meetings and field supervisory visits to project sites to assess technical, administrative, and financial processes and implementation progress of the contracts.
  12. Ensure all formal and informal meetings and discussions with the service providers and implementing sectors are documented and records adequately filed.
  13. Review financial data submitted by the contractor and service providers in support of the Finance Unit and ensure timely payment of certificates and invoices.
  14. Address all matters associated with delivery of goods/services e.g. taxation, duties, clearance etc. in consultation with the Financial Management specialist.
  15. Contribute to the formulation of any contract amendments and any changes in accordance with the Bank Procedures i.e. ensuring that prior review documents are sent to the Bank for relevant approvals.
  16. Support the preparation quarterly, semi-annual, and annual progress reports for the project including completion reports for subprojects
  17. Document learnings and best practices from the implementation of the contract under the project, and preparation of performance assessment reports for completed contracts.
  18. Attend and participate in World Bank Missions including monthly progress review meetings and support the preparation of appropriate technical briefs as required.

 

2. Professional Qualifications and Experience

The candidate should meet the following minimum qualifications:

  1. Post-graduate Degree in Management Discipline such as Contract Management, Project Management, Procurement, Civil Engineering or Construction Management from a recognized institution and those with procurement qualifications such as CIPS, or FIDIC training in contract management or adjudication, will have added advantage;
  2. At least 8 years of post-qualification experience in contract management or procurement under projects financed by International Financing Institutions including practical engineering experience in design, field supervision, or both, for high-value infrastructure Water Supply and Sanitation works.
  3. Demonstrated experience (at least 3 years) applying standard international conditions of contract, particularly the FIDIC Red Book and thorough understanding of contract management tools and project fiduciary procedures including Interim Financial Reports (IFR) and World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers;
  4. Demonstrated proficiency with project management software /tracking tools and project fiduciary procedures;
  5. Demonstrated experience managing contracts works and services, and experience in the public sector will be considered an asset;
  6. Demonstrated experience in the development and use of contract management and tracking tools and/or platforms
  7. Willingness to work under pressure and with minimum supervision; and
  8. Good computer skills and proficient in the use of Microsoft Office (Excel, Word and PowerPoint, etc.);
  9. Highly motivated with excellent planning, analytical, communications and   interpersonal skills as well as a high level of diplomacy; and
  10. Upholding of anti-corruption and anti-bribery ethics.

3.  Duration of the Assignment

The Contract Management Specialist shall be recruited for a period of two (2) years, but the contract shall be renewable annually subject to satisfactory performance, need and availability of funding.

4. Facilities to be provided by the Client

The following shall be provided by the client: office space, furniture, and office equipment, communication, and internet facilities. For all field related assignments, the Project shall provide transport and costs and other expenses (per Diems etc.) related to the field work.

5. Location of Employment and Obligations of the Consultant

The Contract Management Specialist will be based at the Chileka PIU Offices in Blantyre but would be required to travel regularly to various locations within the Blantyre City and surrounding areas, where BWB/BCC shall be implementing the project activities.

notices.description:
REPUBLIQUE DU NIGER

Fraternité – Travail – Progrès

            __________

MINISTERE DE l’ENVIRONNEMENT, DE l’HYDRAULIQUE ET DE L’ASSAINISSEMENT

__________

PROJET DE PLATEFORME INTEGREE POUR LA SECURITE DE L’EAU AU NIGER (PISEN)

__________

UNITE DE GESTION DU PROJET

 

AVIS A MANIFESTATION D'INTERET N°004/MEHA/PISEN/2026 RELATIF AU RECRUTEMENT DE DEUX SPECIALISTES EN DEVELOPPEMENT RURAL POUR L’UNITE DE COORDINATION REGIONALE D’AGADEZ ET TAHOUA.

 

N° de Crédit IDA/Portion A : 6990-NE

N° de Crédit IDA/Portion B : 6991-NE

N° de référence : NE-PISEN-559922-CS-INDV

                              NE-PISEN-559898-CS-INDV

 

  1. Le Gouvernement de la République du Niger a obtenu un financement de l'Association Internationale de Développement (IDA) pour financer le coût du Projet Plateforme Intégrée pour la Sécurité de l’Eau au Niger (PISEN). Il est prévu qu'une partie du montant de ce financement soit utilisée pour effectuer les paiements au titre du contrat relatif au recrutement de deux Spécialistes en Développement Rural pour les Unités des Coordinations Régionales d’Agadez et Tahoua.

 

  1. Les services du spécialiste en développement rural (« les Services ») consistent à :

 

  • Mettre en cohérence les activités d’infrastructures hydrauliques à vocation productive et d’aménagement rural avec les textes législatifs, réglementaires, organisationnels et stratégiques en vigueur au Niger ;
  • Veiller à l’alignement des activités de mobilisation et d’utilisation productive des ressources en eau sur les critères-cadres, les documents de référence et les objectifs du projet
  • Contribuer à l’organisation du processus d’engagement citoyen relatif à la maîtrise de l’eau, à la mise en œuvre de la Stratégie de la Petite Irrigation au Niger (SPIN), à la gestion durable des ressources naturelles, à l’élevage et aux ouvrages pastoraux, en coordination avec les spécialistes environnementaux et sociaux ;
  • Participer à l’élaboration et à l’exécution des Plans de Travail et Budgets Annuels (PTBA) ;
  • Contrôler la conformité des plans d’action et des activités proposées avec les objectifs, les critères d’éligibilité et les résultats attendus du projet ;
  • Fournir un appui technique et organisationnel aux services déconcentrés, collectivités territoriales, organisations communautaires et autres acteurs impliqués dans la mise en œuvre des activités planifiées ;
  • Coordonner la revue technique et le processus de validation des études, avant-projets, dossiers techniques et livrables relatifs aux investissements de développement rural ;
  • Assurer le suivi technique des activités de développement rural du sous-bassin concerné, analyser les contraintes de mise en œuvre et proposer les mesures correctives nécessaires, tout en harmonisant les interventions avec celles des autres régions ;
  • Participer à la coordination et à la supervision des interventions de développement rural financées par le PISEN, y compris les missions de terrain, les réceptions techniques et le suivi de la qualité des ouvrages ;
  • Coordonner, dans son domaine de compétence, le suivi de l’exécution des marchés d’infrastructures rurales et d’aménagement de l’espace rural, vérifier l’avancement physique, la conformité technique et la qualité des prestations, et signaler sans délai les écarts et risques ;
  • Coordonner l’assistance technique aux administrations communales et régionales dans son domaine de compétence ;
  • Contribuer, en coordination avec le Spécialiste en passation des marchés, à la préparation et à la mise à jour des plans de passation des marchés, des termes de référence, des spécifications techniques et des dossiers d’appel d’offres relevant de son domaine ;
  • Suivre régulièrement les progrès vers l’atteinte des indicateurs et résultats du PISEN dans son domaine d’intervention, renseigner les outils de suivi et contribuer aux rapports périodiques et aux missions d’appui à la mise en œuvre ;
  • Exécuter toute autre tâche en lien direct avec ses compétences et les objectifs du poste, à la demande du Coordonnateur régional.

 

 

(Voir les TDRs ci-joints pour les détails via le lien :

https://drive.google.com/file/d/1qi_3NUZfepDtqIX-XlShwGchWep6HWMy/view?usp=drive_link

https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_K96pb-LAA0GIeXC2ULY6pTxhnfBboxt/view?usp=drive_link

L’Unité de Gestion du projet Plateforme Intégrée pour la Sécurité de l’Eau au Niger (PISEN) invite les candidats admissibles à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les services décrits ci-dessus. Les candidats intéressés doivent fournir les informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications requises et une expérience pertinente pour l’exécution des Services.

 

Il est rappelé aux candidats intéressés, qu’ils doivent fournir :

 

  • Une demande manuscrite adressée à l’Unité de Gestion du Projet PISEN ;
  • Une lettre de motivation ;
  • Un CV détaillé, daté et signé mettant en évidence les aptitudes du candidat, expérience et indiquant les contacts de trois personnes de référence professionnelle ;
  • Les copies légalisées du ou des diplômes et attestations de formations obtenues.

 

 

Le Candidat devra notamment :

  • Être titulaire d’un diplôme de niveau Bac + 5 au minimum, ou équivalent, en génie rural, hydraulique agricole, irrigation, gestion des ressources naturelles, génie agricole ou dans une discipline étroitement apparentée ;
  • Justifier d’au moins dix (10) années d’expérience professionnelle générale dans le domaine du développement rural, des infrastructures rurales, de l’hydraulique agricole ou de la gestion des ressources naturelles ;
  • Justifier d’au moins trois (3) expériences spécifiques pertinentes, réalisées à un niveau de responsabilité comparable, dans la préparation d’études, le contrôle ou la supervision de travaux de développement rural, notamment en petite irrigation, aménagements hydro-agricoles, mobilisation des eaux, restauration des terres, ouvrages pastoraux ou infrastructures rurales ;
  • Une expérience dans des projets financés par la Banque mondiale ou par d’autres institutions internationales de développement constitue un atout ;
  • Une expérience avérée dans la préparation ou la revue d’études techniques et de dossiers d’appel d’offres, ainsi que dans la supervision d’infrastructures rurales et de travaux hydro-agricoles, est requise ;

Une expérience en gestion et suivi de contrats de consultants ou d’entreprises, en mobilisation communautaire et en coordination avec les collectivités territoriales est requise ;

Une connaissance pratique de la gestion des risques environnementaux et sociaux applicables aux infrastructures rurales est requise ;

Une expérience professionnelle dans un contexte sahélien, fragile ou affecté par l’insécurité constitue un atout.

  • Avoir une bonne connaissance des stratégies, politiques, normes techniques et cadres institutionnels en vigueur au Niger dans les secteurs du développement rural, de l’eau, de l’agriculture et de la gestion des ressources naturelles ;
  • Maîtriser les logiciels bureautiques courants (Word, Excel et PowerPoint). La maîtrise d’outils de conception, de dessin technique, de cartographie ou de suivi des infrastructures adaptés aux missions du poste constitue un avantage ;
  • Démontrer de solides capacités d’organisation, de coopération, de coordination multisectorielle, de rédaction et de synthèse, ainsi qu’une aptitude à travailler de manière autonome avec les partenaires institutionnels, les collectivités et les communautés ;
  • Être disponible à la date prévue de prise de fonction et apte à effectuer des missions fréquentes sur le terrain, y compris dans des zones présentant des contraintes sécuritaires, conformément aux procédures du projet.

 

 

  1. Le recrutement sera conduit conformément aux procédures applicables au projet pour la sélection de consultants individuels. L’évaluation comprendra :

 

  1. La vérification des critères minimaux d’éligibilité ;
  2. La notation comparative des qualifications et expériences pertinentes ; et
  3. Le cas échéant, un entretien technique avec les candidats les mieux classés.

 

Les critères minimaux d’éligibilité comprennent le diplôme requis, les dix (10) années d’expérience générale et les trois (3) expériences spécifiques pertinentes. Les candidatures satisfaisant à ces exigences seront évaluées selon la grille indicative suivante : qualifications académiques, 15 points ; expérience professionnelle générale, 15 points ; expériences spécifiques similaires, 35 points ; expérience en études, dossiers d’appel d’offres, supervision et gestion contractuelle, 15 points ; expérience en mobilisation communautaire, collectivités territoriales et gestion environnementale et sociale, 10 points ; expérience de projets financés par des institutions internationales et en contexte sah&ea

Assignment Title: Consulting Services for the Development of the Methodology on the Zoning of Design Spectral Acceleration of the Territory of the Republic of Moldova

 

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): MD-OEAPM-578952-CS-CQS

 

The Government of the Republic of Moldova has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Strengthening Moldova’s Disaster Risk Management and Resilience Project, and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

 

The consulting services (“the Services”) include the consultancy services for the Development of the Methodology on the Zoning of Design Spectral Acceleration of the Territory of the Republic of Moldova.

 

The Terms of Reference (TOR) for the primary procurement stage for the assignment are attached to this request for expressions of interest.

The Ministry of Infrastructure and Regional Development (MIRD) and the P.I. “Office for External Assistance Programs Management” (OEAPM) Project Implementation Unit (PIU) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria is:

At least 5 (five) years of experience in experience in seismic design, engineering seismology and/or probabilistic seismic hazard assessment, geotechnical/engineering geology assessment, seismic hazard-related methodologies and GIS-based mapping.

Only the firm’s relevant experience and qualifications will be assessed at the shortlisting stage. Key Experts are not required to be proposed and will not be evaluated at this stage.

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

 

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

 

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the „Consultant’s Qualification-based Selection” described in the Procurement Regulations and to be specifically set out in the Request for Proposals.

 

The Expression of Interest shall clearly state the name of the Consultant (individual Firm, Joint Venture or sub-consultancy). The Consultant shall provide relevant references (assignment name, Client, time frame, the role of the firm (main Consultant/Partner in JV/sub-consultant, contract amount, tasks performed etc.) to confirm its experience and qualifications.

 

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours 08:30 to 17:30 hours.

 

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (by e-mail) by 17:30 local time, November 16, 2026.

Background and Rationale

The Government of the Republic of Moldova is implementing the Strengthening Moldova’s Disaster Risk Management and Resilience Project (SMORE), financed by the World Bank. The Project aims to strengthen the country’s preparedness and resilience to natural hazards and climate-related shocks, including through improved policy, regulatory and technical instruments for disaster risk reduction.

 

This assignment is part of Subcomponent 3.1 – Policy, Regulatory, and Feasibility Study Support to Reduce Seismic Risk, which includes technical assistance for the development of methodologies, regulatory documents and supporting tools aimed at reducing seismic risk in the Republic of Moldova. Within this framework, the development of a methodology for seismic hazard design parameters for ultimate and serviceability limit states at the finest administrative unit level is required as a key technical input for seismic design, seismic hazard assessment and future seismic risk mapping.

 

The methodology will support the modernization and harmonization of the national construction regulatory framework with relevant European standards, in particular Eurocode 8 and the corresponding Moldovan construction norms (NCM). It will also provide the technical basis for the preparation of seismic zoning maps and associated GIS datasets, to be used by public authorities, designers, engineers and other relevant stakeholders.

 

The zoning of design acceleration is a fundamental element for both:

i) the seismic design and verification of buildings and structures according to applicable technical regulations; and

ii) the development of seismic risk assessment tools, including seismic risk maps, where hazard information must be combined with exposure and vulnerability data. Subcomponent 3.1 treats this deliverable as a core technical product that must be scientifically justified, traceable, reproducible and compatible with GIS-based risk analysis.

 

Therefore, the purpose of this assignment is to ensure that the Republic of Moldova has a clear, technically sound and nationally applicable methodology for zoning seismic hazard design parameters for ultimate and serviceability limit states at the finest administrative unit level, supported by documented assumptions, validated input data, transparent calculations, maps, GIS files, metadata and quality assurance records. The resulting methodology will contribute to strengthening seismic safety, improving the consistency of future NCM provisions and supporting evidence-based seismic risk reduction decisions.

 

Currently, the Republic of Moldova does not have an updated national seismic hazard methodology and zoning map fully harmonized with European practice (Eurocode 8). The existing regulatory framework relies on legacy provisions that no longer reflect the state of the art in probabilistic seismic hazard analysis (PSHA), updated seismicity catalogues, modern ground-motion prediction equations (GMPE), or the harmonization requirements with the Romanian seismic zoning (essential for coherent values in border areas).

The development of a robust, traceable, and reproducible methodology for seismic hazard zoning is a precondition for:

  • the elaboration of the NCM "Seismic design of buildings" harmonized with Eurocode 8;
  • the elaboration of the national Interactive Seismic Risk Map;
  • the application of the Rapid Visual Screening (RVS) methodology under GD 334/2025;
  • the prioritization of public-building retrofit and feasibility-study activities;
  • the alignment with EU practice and with neighbouring countries (in particular Romania), ensuring coherent hazard values in border areas.

Objective of the Assignment

The general objective of the assignment is to develop a clear, technically sound and nationally applicable methodology for the zoning seismic hazard design parameters for both the ultimate limit state (ULS) and the serviceability limit state (SLS), at the finest administrative-territorial unit level (level I administrative-territorial units — communes, towns/cities and municipalities), on the territory of the Republic of Moldova. The methodology shall provide the technical basis for defining seismic design parameters to be used in construction design, assessment and future regulatory updates, while ensuring compatibility with the national construction framework, relevant Moldovan Construction Norms and the principles of Eurocode 8. notices.title: Digital Transformation Expert
notices.description:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

Georgia

Project Name: The Relief and Recovery for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs)

Project No: P173975

Loan No. 9239-GE

Assignment Title: Digital Transformation Expert

Reference No. GE-GEDC-CS-IC-45

Introduction

JSC Georgian Economic Development Corporation (GEDC), within the Relief and Recovery for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) Project supported by the World Bank (WB) intends to apply part of the loan proceeds for consulting services of a Digital Transformation Expert, who will operate under the World Bank MSMEs Project structure, while being functionally integrated with GEDC’s Growth Hubs network.

The Project Development Objective for the Relief and Recovery for MSME operation is to provide relief to MSMEs and support their recovery, including by strengthening the enabling environment for access to finance.

Project Description

The Project is implemented nationwide and consist of four components:

Component 1 – Financial relief and recovery for MSMEs

Component 2 – Digital payments & financial infrastructure upgrading

Component 3 – Project management and Monitoring

Component 4 – Contingent Emergency Response Component

A substantial portion of the Project activities fall under Component 1. Component 1 is implemented by GEDC. It comprises of the following sub-components:

  • Sub-component 1.1 - micro-grants to finance working capital and fixed assets for micro and small firms.
  • Sub-component 1.2 - co-financing interest payments on loans underwritten by participating financial institutions (PFIs).
  • Sub-component 1.3 - partial credit guarantees for loans issued by PFIs.
  • Sub-component 1.4 - technical assistance for COVID-proofing and digitalization of MSMEs.

Objectives of the assignment

Subcomponent 1.4 of the Relief and Recovery for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) Project aims to support both the design and the provision of technical assistance to firms to adjust to the post Covid environment through the adoption of relevant managerial, digital, and other relevant practices and supporting the creation of a market for such services. The objective is to supplement the financial support under other subcomponents with technical assistance to address outstanding firm needs in key sectors, informed by stakeholder outreach.

This subcomponent will also aim to gauge the feasibility of establishing and eventually scaling the most relevant of managerial capability and digitization programs in the context of Georgia. It will also pilot activities aimed at creation of a local market for firm consultancy services.

In order to effectively provide support services mentioned above and ensure coverage and accessibility in all regions, GEDC will be developing Growth Hubs in all regional centres.

Scope of Work of the Digital Transformation Expert

The Expert will support the implementation of Subcomponent 1.4's digitalization component, ensuring alignment with GEDC’s strategic digital transformation agenda and Growth Hub service portfolio.

The Digital Transformation Expert will report to the Head of Business Services Development Division and coordinate closely with the Strategic Development Unit within GEDC’s M&E Department, as necessary, particularly on monitoring, reporting, and knowledge-sharing related to digitalization activities at the Central Office of GEDC. The Expert will play a pivotal role in enabling digital transformation among MSMEs supported through the Growth Hub network. This includes conducting digital diagnostics, recommending tailored digital solutions, supporting implementation, and contributing to knowledge development across regions and sectors.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Conduct digital maturity assessments to MSMEs identified through the Growth Hub’s diagnostics, analyze their existing digital maturity level, their business processes, assess the existing technological infrastructure, and identify opportunities and draft a tailored digitalization plan to recommend how to digitally transform their business operations based on their outstanding needs;
  • Provide technical support to MSMEs during the rollout of selected digital tools and solutions, as defined by their digitalization plans;
  • Contribute to building the capacity of Growth Hub staff and partner consultants to apply digital diagnostic tools and support MSMEs’ digitalization efforts;
  • Identify and maintain a roster of credible technology vendors and digital service providers, in coordination with GEDC procurement and technical teams;
  • Recommend appropriate technology platforms for individual MSMEs, considering their size, industry, and operational capacity;
  • Develop and implement, and periodically update/improve methodologies for assessing digital maturity of businesses and contribute to the creation of sector-specific digital transformation roadmaps;
  • Create and maintain a structured catalog of digital tools, platforms, and their providers available on the Georgian market;
  • Collaborate effectively with project partners, internal teams, and external contractors to align on shared goals and work streams;
  • Actively participate in the planning and delivery of educational and awareness-raising activities to promote digital literacy and transformation among current and potential beneficiaries;
  • Engage proactively with MSMEs, responding to inquiries and providing follow-up guidance throughout the digitalization process;
  • Monitor the adoption and effectiveness of digital solutions after implementation, and issue recommendations to ensure sustained impact;
  • Participate in the development of content and input for project progress reports related to digitalization;
  • Perform other related tasks within the scope of the assignment, as required to support the successful implementation of digital transformation initiatives within the project, and as assigned by management;
  • Provide data and inputs on digitalization activities, indicators, and results to the Strategic Development Unit for inclusion in MSME Project monitoring and evaluation reports.

Reporting and Deliverables

The Digital Transformation Expert shall perform the above responsibilities continuously throughout the duration of the assignment, under the direction of the Head of Business Services Development Division. The specific deliverables include:

  • Monthly contribution to project progress reports, including a summary of digital assessments conducted, tools recommended or implemented, and overall MSME engagement;
  • Quarterly summary of digitalization results, including number of MSMEs assessed, number of digitalization plans developed, and key outcomes achieved, to feed into Subcomponent 1.4 reporting;
  • Maintain and quarterly update a catalog of vetted digital tools and solution providers relevant for MSMEs;
  • Documentation of digital maturity assessments and sector-specific roadmaps developed or updated during the reporting period;
  • Reports on post-implementation monitoring, outlining the effectiveness and outcomes of deployed solutions;
  • Individual Digitalization plans produced for each MSME undergoing digital maturity assessments;
  • Other deliverables or briefings as requested by the Head of Business Services Development Division, related to the digitalization pillar of the Growth Hub project.
  • Document and share case studies or success stories of MSME digital transformation to inform Growth Hub learning and communication efforts

Facilities and Services to be provided by the Client:

The Client shall provide office area and facilities, office equipment and communication necessary to carry out the assignment. The Client shall also provide all necessary information and documents for that purposes.

Qualification and Experience:

  • Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Business Administration, or a related field;
  • At least 5 years of work experience in a position related to the described responsibilities;
  • Practical experience in implementing modern and up-to-date technologies;
  • Experience preparing analytical and performance reports related to digital adoption or SME support
  • Familiarity with enterprise diagnostics, digitalization frameworks, or SME capacity-building programs.
  • Experience in the digitalization of small and medium-sized enterprises;
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with teams involved in or connected to the project;
  • Fluency in Georgian and a strong command of English is preferred.

Facilities and Services to be provided by the Client:

The Client shall provide office area and facilities, office equipment and communication necessary to carry out the services. The Client shall also provide all necessary information and documents for that purposes.

Duration

Consultant will be hired under the full-time employment contract.

Interested consultants may obtain further information by email: hr@gedc.ge

CVs of candidates in English language must be submitted electronically to the address below not later than 15th November.

E-mail To: hr@gedc.ge

Please include the title of the announced position in subject line of the email.
