REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES - FIRMS SELECTION)

 

Digital West Bank & Gaza Project (P174355)

Grant number: (TF0B5236)

Assignment Title: Capacity Building for TRA

Reference No.: GZ-MTIT-548204-CS-CQS

 

The Palestinian Liberation Organization has received a grant from the International Development Association (IDA) for USD 20 million for the benefit of the Palestinian Authority (PA) to finance the Digital West Bank & Gaza Project (the Project). The Project will seek to produce concrete and tangible results for the Palestinians by enhancing access to high-speed broadband services and increasing access to selected e-services for citizens and businesses. The Project will focus on key points to unleash digital transformation in the Palestinian territories, addressing some of the bilateral challenges that prevent digital transformation from achieving its full potential. It will strengthen the Palestinian territories' digital resilience and the PA's ability to respond to shocks such as COVID-19.

The Project is implemented and overseen by the Ministry of Telecommunications and Digital Economy (MTDE), formerly the Ministry of Telecom and Information Technology (MTIT), to support digital transformation and resilience in the West Bank and Gaza.

The project has the following four components:

  1. Enabling legal and regulatory environment for Digital Economy, mainly institutional development including the development of section Palestinian Telecommunications Regulatory Authority and Trust Service Supervisory Body; legal and regulatory framework; a Quality-of-Service platform; and capacity building.

  2. Implementing Digital Infrastructure Solutions for Emergency Response, Recovery and Resilience which includes the development of an emergency response center.

  3. Fostering User Centered E-Service Delivery, which includes the establishment of a whole government digital transformation strategy, data infrastructure, support for a digital public platform and prioritization, simplification and digitization of services, the launch of e-services, and implementation of an e-Government Procurement (e-GP) System; and

  4. Project Management, which will support the establishment of a Project management unit in MTDE.

     

The Telecommunications Regulatory Authority (TRA) was established as an independent regulatory body under Decree-Law No. (37) of 2021 Concerning Telecommunications and Information Technology. Its mandate includes overseeing and developing the Palestinian telecommunications market and implementing policies designed by MTDE. The Project supports the establishment and operationalization of TRA, including capacity building to strengthen its effectiveness, credibility and independence.

 

MTDE seeks a qualified consulting or specialized training firm to design and deliver a targeted capacity-building program for TRA staff. The program will strengthen core regulatory skills, institutional processes and evidence-based decision-making, drawing on ITU guidance, ITU Global Symposium for Regulators best practices, and regional and international regulatory experience.

 

The assignment covers the following five training topics, with course content and modalities as detailed in the TOR:

  1. Telecom Licensing, Regulatory Compliance and Enforcement (15 trainees): licensing procedures and conditions; compliance monitoring; risk-based inspections; evidence and case management; proportionate enforcement, sanctions and due process. Expert-led applied workshop with practical exercises.

  2. Telecom Market Analysis and Competition Regulation (7 trainees): market definition and analysis; significant market power; competition remedies; infrastructure sharing, network access and interconnection; and regulatory case studies. Blended training with practical market analysis exercises.

  3. Regulation and Measurement of Telecommunications Quality of Service (QoS) and Quality of Experience (QoE) (7 trainees): regulatory frameworks and standards; network performance indicators; drive testing; measurement, monitoring, data analysis and reporting; and compliance assessment. Specialized training with remote follow-up sessions.

  4. Protection of Telecommunications Consumers and Users' Rights (5 trainees): consumer protection frameworks; provider obligations; complaints and dispute resolution; contracts, pricing and billing transparency; investigations, remedies and consumer protection indicators. Practical workshops.

  5. National Emergency Telecommunications Planning and Telecom Sector Resilience (15 trainees): emergency governance; critical infrastructure risks; business continuity and disaster recovery; incident coordination and reporting; priority communications and service restoration; supply-chain resilience; and tabletop emergency and cyber scenarios. Multi-stakeholder workshop with practical scenarios.

 

Assignment deliverables include training delivery; printed/electronic training materials for each trainee, PMU and TRA; course completion certificates for successful participants; and an evaluation report for each course summarizing outcomes and comparing pre- and post-training test results. Detailed training plans and course outlines will be requested at the subsequent proposal stage and are not required with the expression of interest.

 

Training shall be conducted physically at MTDE labs or the firm's labs, with the course-specific follow-up modalities indicated in the TOR. Arabic is preferred but is not mandatory. Where relevant, professional certification examinations, vouchers, registration and related services may be proposed as optional components with a separate itemized financial offer; TRA may procure all, some or none of these components.

 

Download Full Tor from Here: TRA-Capacity Building ToR.pdf

 

The Ministry of Telecommunications and Digital Economy (MTDE) now invites eligible consulting firms and specialized training centers ("Consultants") to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating the required qualifications and relevant experience.

 

The shortlisting criteria are the firm's core business and years in business, relevant experience, and technical and managerial capability, demonstrated through the following:

  • Specialization in telecommunications regulatory training and capacity building, with demonstrated expertise relevant to the five training topics specified in the TOR.

  • A successful record of similar telecommunications/ICT regulatory training assignments, including completion of at least two training programs on similar topics within the last three (3) years.

  • Experience providing training to telecom/ICT regulatory authorities, ministries or comparable public-sector institutions, preferably in the MENA region.

  • Technical and managerial capacity to organize and deliver the program, and a clear understanding of the assignment and approach to its execution.

     

Expressions of interest should include a firm profile; details of relevant completed assignments, including dates, clients, scope and supporting evidence; and a initial list of proposed trainers and Key Experts, indicating their intended training topics or roles. Trainers and Key Experts will not be evaluated or assigned scores at this stage. No training plan or course outline is required at the expression-of-interest stage.

 

Interested firms must also answer the following questions in their expressions of interest:

  1. What training delivery modality does the firm offer for this assignment: face-to-face, online, or blended? Please specify the proposed modality for each training topic.

  2. Is the firm a local or international company? Please state its country of registration and whether it has a local presence in Palestine.

  3. In which language(s) can the firm deliver the training: Arabic, English, or both? Please specify the available language(s) for each training topic.

     

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank's "Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers" dated September 2025 ("Procurement Regulations"), setting forth the World Bank's policy on conflict of interest.

 

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

 

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Consultant's Qualifications-based Selection (CQS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours: Sunday – Thursday (09:00 AM – 01:00 PM) (Local Time GMT +2)

 

Ahmad Khatib - Procurement Specialist

e-mail: akhatib@mtde.gov.ps

notices.title: Recrutement d’un consultant individuel Responsable des THIMO (RTHIMO)
notices.description:
SOLLICITATION DE MANIFESTATIONS D’INTERET

NOM DU PAYS : BURUNDI

NOM DU PROJET : PROJET D’APPUI AUX FILETS SOCIAUX PRODUCTIFS ET EMPLOIS-MERANKABANDI II

INTITULE DE LA MISSION: RECRUTEMENT DU PERSONNEL DE L’UNITE DE GESTION DU PROJET (UGP) AU PROJET D’APPUI AUX FILETS SOCIAUX PRODUCTIFS ET EMPLOIS-CASH FOR JOBS “MERANKABANDI ”

Don IDA_BI 9440

Emis : 28 Octobre 2026

 

Le Gouvernement de la République du Burundi a reçu un don de l’Association Internationale de Développement (IDA) pour financer le Projet d’Appui aux Filets Sociaux Productifs et Emplois « MERANKABANDI II », et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie de ce don pour effectuer des paiements au titre des contrats de prestations de services du Personnel de l’Unité de Gestion du Projet (UGP) pour les postes ci-après:

  • Responsable des Travaux à Haute Intensité de Main d’Œuvre (RTHIMO);
  • Chargé des Travaux à Haute Intensité de Main d’Œuvre (CTHIMO) ;
  • Assistant au Responsable des Travaux à Haute Intensité de Main d’Œuvre (ARTHIMO);

Les services (taches) de ces consultants (« Services ») sont bien détaillées dans les termes de référence qui sont disponibles à l’adresse ci-bas indiquée dans le présent appel à manifestation d’intérêt ainsi que sur le site web: www.merankabandi2.bi, celui de l’agence NETPRESS, www.lerenouveau.bi et le site Web d’Intercontact.

Le Consultant fournira les Services sur la durée du Projet incluant une période d’essai de six mois et une évaluation annuelle des performances qui peut conduire à la résiliation du contrat si elle n’est pas satisfaisante.

 

Le Projet d’Appui aux Filets Sociaux Productifs et Emplois-Cash for Jobs « MERANKABANDI» invite les consultants (« Consultants ») admissibles à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les services décrits dans les termes de référence. Les Consultants intéressées doivent fournir les informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications requises et une expérience pertinente pour l’exécution des Services à savoir :

  • Une lettre de motivation ;
  • Un curriculum vitae détaillé et signé ;
  • Une copie certifiée conforme du diplôme ou attestation tenant lieu de diplôme certifié ;
  • Une (des) attestation(s) de services rendus ou certificat de travail ;
  • Toute autre document de référence justifiant l’expérience concernant l’exécution des prestations analogues, etc.

Les candidats recherchés doivent satisfaire aux critères ci-après:

  1. Pour le Responsable des Travaux à Haute Intensité de Main d’Œuvre (RTHIMO):
  • Avoir au moins un niveau universitaire (Bac+5) dans les domaines des travaux publics, de l’aménagement, du génie civil ou rural ou équivalent ;
  • Avoir au moins une expérience de 5 ans dans les THIMO (pistes et routes, aménagement des bassins versant et des marais) ;
  • Avoir une expérience avérée dans la gestion de travaux comprenant un nombre important d’ouvriers (au moins 5 chantiers avec un minimum de 250 ouvriers chacun) ;
  • Avoir une expérience en organisation et gestion simultanées des chantiers disséminés dans différentes localités ;
  • Avoir une expérience dans des projets financés par les bailleurs internationaux, de préférence la Banque mondiale serait un atout ;
  • Avoir une connaissance des méthodes d’entretien, de préférence à partir des techniques HIMO ; 
  • Être apte à travailler dans une équipe multidisciplinaire ;
  • Etre prêt à gérer des situations stressantes ;
  • Posséder une très bonne maîtrise du français ;
  • Être capable de communiquer en Kirundi et en Swahili ;
  • La connaissance de l’anglais est un atout ;
  • Maitriser les logiciels informatiques de base (avec certificat à l’appui) : Word, Excel, Power Point.

 

  1. Pour le Chargé des Travaux à Haute Intensité de Main d’Œuvre (CTHIMO) 
  • Avoir au moins un Diplôme de niveau universitaire (Bac+5) dans les domaines des travaux publics, de l’aménagement, du génie civil ou rural ou équivalent ;
  • Avoir une expérience de 3 ans dans les THIMO (pistes et routes, aménagement des bassins versant et des marais) ;
  • Avoir une expérience avérée dans la gestion de travaux comprenant un nombre important d’ouvriers (au moins 2 chantiers avec un minimum de 250 ouvriers chacun) ;
  • Avoir une expérience en organisation et gestion simultanées des chantiers disséminés dans différentes localités.

Les qualifications et aptitudes suivantes sont un atout :

  • Avoir une expérience des projets financés par les bailleurs internationaux, de préférence la Banque mondiale ;
  • Avoir une connaissance des méthodes d’entretien routier, de préférence à partir des techniques HIMO ; 
  • Être apte à travailler dans une équipe multidisciplinaire ;
  • Etre prêt à gérer des situations stressantes ;
  • Posséder une très bonne maîtrise du français ;
  • Être capable de communiquer en Kirundi et en Swahili ;
  • Maitriser les logiciels informatiques de base (avec certificat à l’appui): Word, Excel, Power Point.

 

 

  1. Pour l’Assistant au Responsable des Travaux à Haute Intensité de Main d’Œuvre (ARTHIMO)
  • Avoir au moins un Diplôme de niveau universitaire (Bac+5) dans les domaines des travaux publics, de l’aménagement, du génie civil ou rural ou équivalent ;
  • Avoir une expérience de 3 ans dans les THIMO (pistes et routes, aménagement des bassins versant et des marais) ;
  • Avoir une expérience avérée dans la gestion de travaux comprenant un nombre important d’ouvriers (au moins 2 chantiers avec un minimum de 250 ouvriers chacun) ;
  • Avoir une expérience en organisation et gestion simultanées des chantiers disséminés dans différentes localités ;
  • Avoir une expérience des projets financés par les bailleurs internationaux, de préférence la Banque mondiale ;
  • Avoir une connaissance des méthodes d’entretien routier, de préférence réalisé par le biais de techniques HIMO ; 
  • Être apte à travailler dans une équipe multidisciplinaire ;
  • Etre prêt à gérer des situations stressantes ;
  • Posséder une très bonne maîtrise du français ;
  • Être capable de communiquer en Kirundi et en Swahili ;
  • La connaissance de l’anglais est un atout ;
  • Maitriser les logiciels informatiques de base (avec certificat à l’appui) : Word, Excel, Power Point ;
  • Avoir une très forte motivation pour une mission compliquée et être très dynamique.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT SELECTION)

 

Country:  Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia

Employer: Ministry of Revenues (MOR)

Project: Governance Modernization for Efficient Service Delivery Project

Credit No.: 7619 ET

Assignment Title: Selection of Technical Lead / Chief Architect for the Integrated Tax Administration System (ITAS)

Reference No.: ET-MOR-577821-CS-INDV

Issued on: October 24, 2026

 

The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Governance Modernization for Efficient Service Delivery Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

 

The consulting services (“the Services”) aim to engage a highly qualified Technical Lead / Chief Architect to provide independent technical leadership for the Integrated Tax Administration System (ITAS). The role will focus on strengthening enterprise architecture, governing system design, ensuring compliance with approved standards, and overseeing vendor performance in alignment with program objectives and governance frameworks.

 

The Ministry of Revenues requires two (2) individual consultants for the role of Technical Lead/ Chief Architect for ITAS. This notice is for Reference No.: ET-MOR-577821-CS-INDV. A similar notice has been published for the second position under Reference No.: ET-MOR-578032-CS-INDV. Interested candidates are required to submit a separate Expression of Interest for each specific reference number they wish to be considered for.

 

The Ministry of Revenue invites qualified professionals to apply for the role of Technical Lead / Chief Architect for the ITAS initiative. The selected candidate will be responsible for reviewing and updating enterprise architecture, defining and maintaining solution architecture, establishing governance standards, and ensuring integration across ITAS, DW/BI, e-Invoicing, and other Ministry systems. The role also includes oversight of vendor activities, management of technical risks, and ensuring compliance with security, scalability, and performance requirements. Given the scale, complexity, and national importance of this program, the Ministry seeks an experienced Chief Architect with a proven track record in large-scale IT system implementations within multi-stakeholder environments.

 

The Ministry of Revenue invites qualified individual consultants to apply for the role of Technical Lead / Chief Architect for the ITAS initiative. Applicants must hold a Master’s or Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field, with a minimum of 12 years’ experience (10 years with a Master’s). Required expertise includes mission-critical system integration, distributed systems, multi-vendor environments, architecture governance, and advisory roles. Strong competencies in enterprise IT system design, data and security architecture, infrastructure, API-based integration, and high-availability systems are essential; experience with containerized architectures (e.g., Kubernetes) is an advantage. Prior work in public sector or large government systems is required, with preference for tax administration or revenue/financial systems. Interested consultants should submit CVs and documentation demonstrating qualifications and relevant experience.

                    

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraph 3.13 and 3.14 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulation for IPF Borrowers, Seventh Edition, September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

 

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant Selection method set out in the World Bank’s Procurement Regulation for IPF Borrowers, Seventh Edition, September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”).

notices.title: Change Management Specialist
notices.buyer: Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources
notices.description:
Vanuatu Affordable and Resilient Settlements Project (VARS)

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REOI)

Selection of Individual Consultant or Individual Consultant Selection (INDV).

Assignment Title:

Change Management Specialist

Duty Station:

PMU, Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources,

Port Vila, Vanuatu

Date of Publication:

27th October 2026

Deadline for submission:

10th November 2026 at 2:00 p.m. Vanuatu Time.

Reference Number:

VU-MLNR-573544-CS-INDV

1. BACKGROUND OF THE PROJECT:

The Government of Vanuatu, through the Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources (MLNR), is implementing a comprehensive programme of land-sector reform and institutional strengthening guided by the Ministry’s Reform Masterplan, Corporate Plan and associated business-planning and performance-management arrangements. These reforms seek to improve service delivery, strengthen organisational performance, modernize administrative and land-management systems, and enhance accountability, responsiveness, and public confidence.

Under the Vanuatu Affordable and Resilient Settlements Project (VARS), supported by the World Bank, the Ministry is progressing major institutional and systems initiatives, including operationalization of the Land Management Information System (LMIS), improved records and revenue management, electronic workflows and forms, digital service delivery, and development of a new integrated Ministry headquarters in Port Vila.

The new headquarters is intended to be more than a replacement office building. Consultation during the Concept Design phase identified opportunities to improve organisational integration, public service delivery, leadership visibility, staff collaboration, records and information management, use of digital technologies, shared facilities, operational resilience, and workplace culture. Successful occupation will therefore depend not only on completion of the physical facility, but also on the Ministry’s readiness to transition its people, systems, processes, governance arrangements, workplace practices and organisational culture into a new operating environment.

At the same time, staff within the Department of Lands and Corporate Services Unit currently work across a mixed environment of paper files, scanned records, email, shared drives, emerging digital platforms and established administrative procedures. Inconsistent work practices limited digital confidence, unclear filing and follow-up arrangements, and weak individual work organisation can reduce productivity, create duplication, delay decisions, weaken records integrity and limit the benefits expected from institutional investment.

The Ministry therefore seeks to engage a Change Management Specialist to provide structured organisational change support and practical, person-centred coaching to selected staff in the Department of Lands (including the Valuer General’s Office), the Corporate Services Unit, and the Geology and Mines Unit. The Specialist will help staff and managers adopt improved administrative practices, transition from paper-based to digital ways of working, prepare for new systems and workflows, and progressively become ready to occupy and operate from the new headquarters. The Department of Water is undertaking its own internal reform programme and will therefore participate only in Ministry-wide initiatives under this assignment; the assignment will not provide routine one-to-one coaching or unit-specific reform support to Department of Water staff.

The assignment is administrative, organisational, and behavioural in nature. It will not replace technical specialists or supervisors responsible for land administration, surveying, valuation, legal services, finance, human resources, ICT, records management, facilities management or building delivery. The Specialist will work closely with these parties to ensure that staff adoption, workplace practices and change activities are aligned with technical, legal, policy, ICT, design, and operational requirements.

Strategic alignment and implementation sequencing. The Ministry’s DG-approved Briefing Note 233 establishes a progressive digital-first information-management model, supported by electronic records, workflows and cloud-based systems while preserving physical records when required for statutory, operational, or historical purposes. Briefing Note 202 establishes complementary physical storage and archive accommodation requirements for the new Headquarters. Core Department of Lands lease-creation, registration and subsequent-transaction processes remain substantially manual and require further specification and digital-system development under LMIS beyond current DTS, TIS and M-Files functionality. The Specialist shall support organisational readiness and adoption in step with approved technical releases; the assignment does not imply these processes are already digitised.

2. PURPOSE OF THE ASSIGNMENT:

The objective of this assignment is to improve the organisational effectiveness, administrative capability, digital work practices and change readiness of selected staff within the Department of Lands (including the Valuer General’s Office), the Corporate Services Unit, and the Geology and Mines Unit, while supporting Ministry-wide change initiatives and preparing MoLNR to successfully transition into the new headquarters. Department of Water participation will be limited to relevant Ministry-wide initiatives, recognising that the Department is undertaking its own internal reform programme and is not intended to receive routine one-to-one coaching or unit-specific reform support under this assignment.

The assignment will seek measurable improvements in:

•  consistent task organisation, prioritisation, follow-up, and completion within approved administrative workflows.

•  administrative accuracy, consistency, timeliness, and quality control.

•  electronic filing, email management, document handling and records discipline.

•  adoption and effective use of approved digital tools, electronic workflows, forms, and productivity applications.

•  staff confidence, adaptability and readiness for new systems, workplace protocols and shared facilities.

•  leadership visibility, staff engagement, collaboration, and organizational cohesion.

•  operational readiness, business continuity and staff preparedness for occupation of the new headquarters; and

•  management capacity to monitor process effectiveness, identify training needs and sustain organisational improvements.

3. REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE:

3.1 Education

•  Degree in Change Management, Organizational Development, Public Administration, Human Resource Management, Business Administration, Organizational Psychology, Information Management, Workplace Strategy, Project Management, or a related field.

•  Relevant professional certification in change management, project management, business-process improvement, coaching, digital transformation, operational readiness or training and development would be an advantage.

3.2 Experience

•  Minimum 10 years of relevant professional experience in organizational change, institutional strengthening, workforce capability development, public-sector reform, digital workplace transformation or operational readiness.

•  Demonstrated experience providing practical on-the-job coaching and process-improvement and practical workplace coaching support to staff and managers.

•  Demonstrated experience in stakeholder engagement, organizational readiness assessment, change communication, staff training and monitoring of change initiatives.

•  Experience in digital adoption, electronic document and records management, email and productivity practices, business-process improvement and development of practical SOPs and work aids.

•  Experience supporting workplace transition, operational readiness, occupation of new facilities, integration of multiple business units or implementation of new ways of working.

•  Experience working on complex public-sector infrastructure or institutional-development projects involving multiple stakeholders and competing operational requirements.

•  Experience in developing countries is essential; previous experience in Pacific Island Countries or Small Island Developing States is highly desirable.

•  Experience on World Bank or other donor-funded projects would be an advantage.

3.3 Skills

•  Strong coaching, facilitation, mentoring, communication, and interpersonal skills.

•  Ability to build trust and work respectfully with staff at different levels of seniority, education, experience, and digital confidence.

•  Ability to translate reform objectives into practical changes in daily work behavior.

•  Strong analytical, diagnostic, organizational and problem-solving capability.

•  Ability to develop simple, usable, and culturally appropriate procedures, tools, training, and communication materials.

•  Sound understanding of organization change-management approaches and ability to adapt them pragmatically to the Vanuatu public-sector context.

•  Understanding of the relationship between workplace design, operational processe

NATIONAL INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY AUTHORITY – UGANDA (NITA-U)

 

 REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION

UGANDA DIGITAL ACCELERATION PROJECT – GOVERNMENT NETWORK (UDAP-GOVNET)

PROJECT ID: P171305

LOAN NUMBER: IDA-68980

 

REFERENCE NUMBER: NITA-UDAP/CONS/26-27/00027

 

ASSIGNMENT TITLE: CONSULTANCY SERVICES FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE NATIONAL DIGITAL SKILLS TRAINING PROGRAMME (NDSTP)

 

The Government of Uganda, represented by the National Information Technology Authority – Uganda (NITA-U), has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of the Uganda Digital Acceleration Project – Government Network (UDAP-GOVNET) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for Consultancy services for the implementation of the National Digital Skills Training Programme (NDSTP)

 

The consultant will have the overall responsibility of implementation of the National Digital Skills Training Programme (NDSTP) programme across Uganda. The assignment will equip at least 6,000 beneficiaries drawn from public servants, teachers and tutors, out-of-school youth, refugees and refugee-host communities, and persons with disabilities with the digital knowledge and practical competencies needed to access services safely and productively, pursue education and livelihood opportunities, and participate as informed digital citizens.

The duration of the assignment will be five (5) months from the date of contract signing.

The detailed Terms of Reference (ToR) for the assignment can be accessed at https://www.nita.go.ug

The National Information Technology Authority - Uganda now invites eligible consulting firms to indicate their interest in providing the services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria for the firm’s capability and experience is:

 

The shortlisting criteria for the firm’s capacity and experience are:

  1. A minimum of eight (8) years of core business experience in ICT digital skills training, capacity building and skills development consultancy.
  2. Demonstrated successful completion of at least five (5) assignments in atleast two or more assignments involving: digital-skills training, digital literacy upskilling, ICT competency development, education technology, or large-scale capacity-building programmes within the past seven (7) years.  Evidence should indicate the client, scope, duration, and status/completion of each assignment.
  3. Presence of appropriate skills among staff in the areas of; Coordinator/team leader, Trainer-of-trainers, digital skills trainers, Curriculum development specialist, assessment and certification specialist, cybersecurity/digital safety specialist, gender and disability inclusion officer, research/data science officer, and monitoring and evaluation. Please do not submit CVs or biodata of individual experts at this stage.

 

The attention of interested consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.15 and 3.16, of the World Bank’s ‘Procurement in Investment Project Financing Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services, Seventh Edition September 2025 (Procurement in investment Project Financing; Goods, Works, Non- Consulting and Consulting Services), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications.

A consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations “Procurement in Investment Project Financing Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services, Seventh Edition September 2025”.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours at the address below 08:00 to 17:00 hours from Monday to Friday at the address given below.

Expressions of Interest (One original plus two copies) must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person or by e-mail) on or before Wednesday, 18th November, 2026 at 11:00am.

The packages must be clearly marked: “Expression of Interest for Consultancy Services for the Implementation of the National Digital Skills Training Programme (NDSTP).”

 

Address for submission

National Information Technology Authority – Uganda (NITA-U)

Palm Courts, Plot 7A Rotary Avenue, 1st Floor

Kampala, Uganda

Email: jacqueline.musimenta@nita.go.ug

 

Any form of canvassing or lobbying for the tender shall lead to automatic disqualification

 

EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR

Country: Republic of Indonesia

Reference Number: ID-DGLT-572449-GO-RFP

RFP No.: PL.103/1/1/X/RFP-ITS 2026

Issued on: 28 October 2026

1. The Republic of Indonesia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Indonesia Mass Transit Project (MASTRAN) and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under the contract for the Intelligent Transport System (ITS) for Mass Public Transport in the Metropolitan Areas of Medan and Bandung.

The Project will be implemented across two metropolitan Implementation Areas in Indonesia:

a) Medan Metropolitan Area, comprising Medan, Binjai, and Deli Serdang, hereinafter referred to as “MEBIDANG”; and

b) Bandung Metropolitan Area, corresponding to the Bandung Basin Metropolitan Area, hereinafter referred to as “BBMA”.

For the purposes of this document, MEBIDANG and BBMA are the defined terms used to refer to the respective Implementation Areas.

2. The Ministry of Transportation of the Republic of Indonesia, acting through the Commitment Making Officer for the MASTRAN Intelligent Transport System (ITS) Development, Directorate General of Land Transportation, Ministry of Transportation of the Republic of Indonesia (“the Purchaser”), now invites eligible Proposers to submit sealed Proposals for the design, supply, installation, integration, testing, commissioning, operational and maintenance support of an integrated Intelligent Transport System (ITS) for Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) operations in the Medan, Binjai, and Deli Serdang Metropolitan Area (Mebidang) and the Bandung Basin Metropolitan Area (BBMA).

3. The ITS comprises operational ITS subsystems: Fleet Management System (FMS), Automatic Fare Collection System (AFCS), Passenger Information System (PIS), Security System (SS), Area Traffic Control System/Transit Signal Priority (ATCS/TSP), and Communication and Network System (CNS). These subsystems will be integrated through a shared BRT Integrated Control and Management System (ICMS) and supported by a BRT Operations Control Center (BOCC) in each Implementation Area. The System will also provide the required data integration, analytics, reporting, cybersecurity, and interfaces with relevant existing and external systems.

4. The detailed scope of supply, functional, architectural, technical and performance requirements, implementation schedule, system inventory, integration and interface requirements, testing and commissioning requirements, training, Warranty, Maintenance, and support requirements are specified in Request for Proposals (RFP) Part 2, Purchaser’s Requirements, including Section VII, Requirements of the Information System, and its contractual Annexes.

5. Procurement will be conducted through international competitive procurement using a single-stage, two-envelope Request for Proposals (RFP) procedure, with the Technical Part and Financial Part submitted concurrently in separate sealed envelopes, in accordance with the applicable World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, and is open to all eligible Proposers as defined in the Procurement Regulations.

6. Proposals will be evaluated in accordance with the evaluation process set out in the RFP. The following weightings shall apply in the combined evaluation: eighty percent (80%) for Rated Criteria, including technical and non-price factors, and twenty percent (20%) for Proposal cost.

7. Interested eligible Proposers may obtain further information from the procurement contact indicated below and inspect the Request for Proposals during normal office hours at the address stated in paragraph 12.

8. The Request for Proposals document in English may be obtained by interested eligible Proposers upon submission of a written application to the address below. notices.title: Monitoring and Evaluation Expert
notices.description:
Request for Expression of Interest 

Country: Kosovo 

Project IDs: P507659 and P507881 

Reference Nr.:  TTFP-CS-IC-3.026 

Project Names: Western Balkans Trade and Transport Facilitation 2.0 (WBTTFP) and Kosovo Financial Sector Development (FinDev) 

  

Position: Monitoring and Evaluation Specialist 

Background 

The Government of Kosovo (GoK), with support from World Bank financing, has established the Central Support Division for Implementing Development Projects (CSD) within the Ministry of Finance (MF). The CSD will serve as a centralized Project Implementation Unit (PIU) for selected development projects where the GoK or independent public institutions are direct beneficiaries.  

The CSD and its PIU will support the implementation of two World Bank-financed projects: the Western Balkans Trade and Transport Facilitation 2.0 Project (P507659) and the Kosovo Financial Sector Development Project (P507881). 

The Western Balkans Trade and Transport Facilitation 2.0 Project is supported through a combination of EUR 12 million grant financing and EUR 34.7 million loan financing. Its objective is to increase trade and transport efficiency and strengthen quality infrastructure in Kosovo and the Western Balkans region. The project will finance improvements at key Border Crossing Points, modernization of customs and border services infrastructure, procurement of equipment, and digitalization of trade-related procedures through systems such as the National Single Window (NSW), the New Computerized Transit System (NCTS), and upgrades to ASYCUDA. It will also support investments to improve market competitiveness, including laboratory equipment for quality testing, an e-tolling system, 5G corridor infrastructure, road safety improvements, and rail safety upgrades at selected railway level crossings. 

The Kosovo Financial Sector Development Project is supported through an EUR 49.3 million loan and aims to improve financial stability and inclusion in Kosovo. The project will support the strengthening of the Deposit Insurance Fund of Kosovo, by providing the capital needed to increase the deposit insurance coverage limit and reduce the payout period for insured depositors following an insured event. It will also expand access to finance for underserved firms through Partial Credit Guarantees via the Kosovo Credit Guarantee Fund, support the development of a National Development Bank, and finance the development of a modern and interoperable Fast Payment System to promote faster and more efficient digital payments. 

Both projects include activities aimed at strengthening project management and implementation capacity, including capacity building for the CSD, PIU staff, and relevant public institutions involved in project implementation. The PIU will be responsible for the day-to-day coordination and implementation of project activities, including fiduciary, technical, monitoring, reporting, and coordination functions, in cooperation with the relevant beneficiary institutions and World Bank task teams. 

Responsibilities of the Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) Specialist 

The objective of this consultancy is to establish, operationalize, and maintain a robust, integrated Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) system for TTFP 2.0 and FinDev in Kosovo. The M&E Specialist will ensure systematic tracking, validation, analysis, and reporting of all Project Development Objectives (PDO) indicators, Intermediate Results Indicators (IRIs), Environmental and Social Commitment Plan (ESCP) metrics, and citizen engagement/gender indicators in strict alignment with the Project Results Framework, Project Operations Manual (POM), and World Bank reporting guidelines. 

The M&E Specialist will ensure that project activities for both projects are systematically monitored, evaluated, and reported in alignment with World Bank standards and the project’s results framework. The role will also contribute to strengthening institutional capacity for M&E within the Project Implementation Unit (PIU) and beneficiary agencies, with a particular focus on stakeholder engagement and gender-responsive monitoring. 

Minimum (Mandatory) Qualifications: 

Education: 

  • Master's degree in economics, Public Policy, Statistics, Social Sciences, Business Administration, or related fields. 

Professional Experience: 

  • General Experience: Minimum 8 years of professional experience in monitoring and evaluation of public sector or donor-funded development projects. 

  • Specific M&E Experience: Minimum 8 years of professional experience in monitoring and evaluation of public sector or donor-funded development projects, with experience with projects financed by international financial institutions (ex: World Bank, EBRD, KfW, EIB, etc.) or development agencies (UN, GIZ, etc.) considered as an advantage.  

  • Cross-Cutting Tracking: Proven track record in tracking Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) metrics, Grievance Redress Mechanisms (GM), gender targets, and citizen engagement indicators. 

 

Additional (Desired) qualifications: 

  • Methodological Expertise: Technical knowledge of Time Release Studies (TRS), WCO Data Models, Global Quality Infrastructure Index (GQII) methodologies, or transport sector performance metrics is an advantage. 

  • Fiduciary Systems: Familiarity with World Bank IPF reporting is an advantage. 

  • Advanced proficiency in statistical and data management software (e.g., SPSS, Stata, Power BI, Excel, or R). 

Languages & Technical Skills: 

  • Fluency in Albanian and English is required; English proficiency will be assessed against proof of certificates received (TOEFL, IELTS, etc), and/or documented work experience in an international or English-speaking setting and/or reference to English language proficiency in a reference letter. 

Duration of the Assignment 

Initial 12-month full- time contract, with the possibility of extension for the full projects' duration (3–5 years) subject to satisfactory annual performance evaluation and project requirements. The engagement is expected to continue until the closing dates of the FinDev Project in June 2030 and the WBTTFP Project in December 2031, including any extensions approved by the World Bank. The contract shall include a six-month probationary period. Continuation and renewal shall be subject to satisfactory performance, based on a written evaluation prepared by the Head of PIU and endorsed by the Director of the Department of Financing. 

Application Procedure 

All interested applicants shall submit the following documents: 

  • Curriculum Vitae (CV); 

  • Letter of interest (500 words maximum) 

  • Copies of relevant certificates and diplomas; 

  • At least one (1) and up to three (3) reference letters from previous employers or clients, including official contact details (email and telephone number), or other documentary evidence demonstrating the required experience, such as contract award letters, certificates of completion, employer confirmations, service certificates, or similar references.   

Selection Process 

Experienced and qualified individuals shall be selected in accordance with the provisions of the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, dated September 2023, through an open competitive selection process. 

Evaluation Criteria: 

  • General Experience                     (60 Points)  

  • Specific M&E Experience           (40 Points)

Assignment Title: Selection of Technical Lead / Chief Architect for the Integrated Tax Administration System (ITAS)

Issued on: October 24, 2026

 

The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Governance Modernization for Efficient Service Delivery Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

 

The consulting services (“the Services”) aim to engage a highly qualified Technical Lead / Chief Architect to provide independent technical leadership for the Integrated Tax Administration System (ITAS). The role will focus on strengthening enterprise architecture, governing system design, ensuring compliance with approved standards, and overseeing vendor performance in alignment with program objectives and governance frameworks.

 

The Ministry of Revenues requires two (2) individual consultants for the role of Technical Lead/ Chief Architect for ITAS. This notice is for Reference No.: ET-MOR-578032-CS-INDV. A similar notice has been published for the second position under Reference No.: ET-MOR-577821-CS-INDV. Interested candidates are required to submit a separate Expression of Interest for each specific reference number they wish to be considered for.

 

The Ministry of Revenue invites qualified professionals to apply for the role of Technical Lead / Chief Architect for the ITAS initiative. The selected candidate will be responsible for reviewing and updating enterprise architecture, defining and maintaining solution architecture, establishing governance standards, and ensuring integration across ITAS, DW/BI, e-Invoicing, and other Ministry systems. The role also includes oversight of vendor activities, management of technical risks, and ensuring compliance with security, scalability, and performance requirements. Given the scale, complexity, and national importance of this program, the Ministry seeks an experienced Chief Architect with a proven track record in large-scale IT system implementations within multi-stakeholder environments.

 

The Ministry of Revenue invites qualified individual consultants to apply for the role of Technical Lead / Chief Architect for the ITAS initiative. Applicants must hold a Master’s or Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field, with a minimum of 12 years’ experience (10 years with a Master’s). Required expertise includes mission-critical system integration, distributed systems, multi-vendor environments, architecture governance, and advisory roles. Strong competencies in enterprise IT system design, data and security architecture, infrastructure, API-based integration, and high-availability systems are essential; experience with containerized architectures (e.g., Kubernetes) is an advantage. Prior work in public sector or large government systems is required, with preference for tax administration or revenue/financial systems. REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

Country: KENYA

Name of Project: NATIONAL YOUTH OPPORTUNITIES TOWARDS ADVANCEMENT (NYOTA)

Credit No. IDA-7355-KE/ GRANT NO: E210-KE

Assignment Title: Consultancy Services For the Provision for Delivery of Socio-Emotional Skills Development, On-The-Job Experience and Support RPL Implementation to Refugee Youth Selected To Participate in NYOTA Component 1

 

 

The Government of Kenya, with financing from the World Bank, invites eligible consulting firms to submit Expressions of Interest (EOI) for the assignment indicated above under the National Youth Opportunities Towards Advancement (NYOTA) Project.

The NYOTA Project aims to increase employment and earnings and promote savings for targeted youth at national scale. The Project is expected to reach 820,000 vulnerable youth across all 47 counties of Kenya, including refugees in Garissa and Turkana counties. The Project beneficiaries are youth aged 18-29 years, and up to 35 years for persons with disabilities, with little or no education, who are unemployed or in vulnerable employment.

The consulting services (“the Services”) will be responsible for the delivery and design of Socio-emotional Skills Development (SESD) to 5,000 refugee youth. As SESD precedes OJE, the NGO / Service Provider selected for this consultancy should customize the approved NYOTA SESD curriculum that enables refugee youth and hostcommunity to integrate smoothly and maintain consistent participation, thereby strengthening readiness for and retention in OJE. In addition, the consultancy shall be responsible for delivery of On-The-Job Experience for five months and transitioning of the 5,000 refugee beneficiaries into paid employment for at least 6 months post OJE.

The initial contract period shall be twelve (12) months. The contract may be renewed in twelve-month periods, subject to satisfactory performance against agreed deliverables, continued need for the services, availability of funds, and compliance with quality and timeliness requirements. The contract shall not extend beyond the Project closing date of 31st December 2028, unless that date is formally extended and the Contract is amended in accordance with the applicable procurement and contract provisions.

Interested firms should provide information and proof demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be downloaded from https://nyotaproject.go.ke/tenders and https://youth.go.ke/tenders-and-awards/

The shortlisting criteria:

  1. Minimum of 8 years’ relevant experience and technical capacity to provide Socio-emotional Skills Development, apprenticeship and job placement interventions in refugee settings.
  2. Knowledge of RPL certification processes.
  3. Undertaken a minimum of two assignments of similar or comparable nature in the past five years including at least one in Kenya (2021 to present) in refugee settings.
  4. The NGO / service provider must exhibit the necessary resources, experience, and staff to complete this assignment in the refugee-hosting counties.
  5. Have a digital platform or ability to use NYOTA system where youth attendance and participation can be tracked
  6. Have the following Key Experts for SESD and OJE;
  1. Team Leader
  2. Human Resource Expert
  3. Quality Assurance Manager
  4. Social Emotional Skills Development Expert
  5. Technical lead – On-the-Job experience and Recognition of Prior Learning
  6. Lead Trainer – Socio-Emotional Skills Development
  7. Key Trainer (K1)–Soft skills
  8. Key Trainer (K2)– Core Business and Basic Digital Skills

 

Note: Key experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The attention of interested consulting firms is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank's "Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers" dated July 2016 and revised in September 2025 (6th Edition) ("Procurement Regulations"), setting forth the World Bank's policy on conflict of interest. In addition, consulting firms shall not be hired for any assignment that would be in conflict with their prior or current obligations to other clients, or that may place them in a position of being unable to carry out the assignment in the best interests of the Borrower.

Consultants may submit their REOI as an individual firm or in association in the form of a joint venture or sub-consultancy. All the members of the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire assignment. However, the experience of sub-consultant will not be considered while short-listing.

A Consultant/firm will be selected in accordance with Fixed Budget Selection (FBS) method set out in the World Bank Regulations.

Interested firms may obtain further information from the Project Supply Chain Management Office at NYOTA offices, Bruce House, Standard Street, 3rd Floor Northern Wing Room No. 321 during official working hours (8.00 a.m-5.00 p.m.) and days.

Detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) are available at:

www.nyotaproject.go.ke/tenders | www.youth.go.ke/tenders-and-awards

Complete EOI document (paginated and stamped/signed on each page) and enclosed in plain sealed envelope marked with the Tender Reference Number should be submitted in a sealed envelop on or before 10th November, 2026, at 10.00 hours

The REOIs will be closed/opened immediately thereafter at the NYOTA Boardroom, Bruce House, 3rd Floor Standard Street Nairobi.

notices.title: Public Financial Management Specialist for Hirshabelle State
notices.description:
Hirshabelle State of Somalia

Ministry of Interior and Local Government.

BULSHO PROJECT - Strengthening Community Institutions for Social Cohesion, Inclusion and Resilience.

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (REOI)

 

Individual Selection of Consultant

Country: Federal Government of Somalia

Project ID No. P508408

Name of the Project: Bulsho Project - Strengthening Community Institutions for Social Cohesion, Inclusion and Resilience

Consulting Service: PIU Bulsho PFM Specialist   

Individual/Firm: Individual

Ref No: SO-MOIFAR-571563-CS-INDV

Duty Station: Jowhar, Hirshabelle Somalia (with potential travel to the target Districts and Cities of Bulsho Project)

 

Deadline: 7th November, 2026

 

BACKGROUND OF THE PROJECT

 

The Bulsho Project – Strengthening Community Institutions for Social Cohesion, Inclusion and Resilience (P508408) is under the lead of the Ministry of Interior, Federal Affairs and Reconciliation – MoIFAR of the Federal Government of Somalia and responsible for the national program called Bulsho, the Somali word for society. The Bulsho Program puts citizens and communities at the center of the government’s action.  The Bulsho Program is a Somali government-led initiative designed to strengthen community and local institutions, fostering social cohesion, inclusion, and resilience. As Somalia continues its recovery from two decades of civil war, the program places a strong emphasis on enhancing service delivery, rebuilding the social contract, and promoting community-centered governance. This uniquely Somali-owned and -driven initiative underscores government ownership and leadership at federal, member state, and district levels, ensuring institutional sustainability and the realization of key policy outcomes.

The Ministry of Interior and Local Government of Hirshabelle State of Somalia have established Project Implementation Units - PIUs, headed a State Project Managers, which have the responsibility for the activities that take place in Hirshabelle State.

The PIUs are responsible for managing project activities at state-level and to liaise with districts. Specifically, the PIUs are responsible for: (i) Verifying eligibility of districts, appraising districts’ request to participate – this includes allocation of Bulsho packages and conducting lottery for each package and verifying the fulfilment of district commitments. (ii) Preparing state-level procurement plans. (iii) Preparing annual project work plans and budgets for state-level activities. (iv) Carrying out procurement for state-level activities. (v) Managing the contract with the logistic firm. (vi) Delivering capacity building activities and providing quality assurance and technical backstopping to districts - this includes trainings of district officials and staff. as well as community entities that play a role in the project. (vii) Preparing requisitions for funds to be transferred to districts, as per the project workplan, and in accordance with the grant agreement/sub-agreements and this POM and its annexes. (viii) Preparing quarterly narrative and financial reports for project activities taking place in their states. (ix) Verifying technical and E&S appraisal of local investments (Component 3) as well as other E&S actions as per the Environment and Social Management Plan. (x) Verifying the soundness of sustainability plans for the local investment prepared by the districts, including Operations & Maintenance (O&M) plans and the Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs) for the management of local infrastructures; and (xi) Preparing security management plans and applying security protocols in partnership with the security firm.

The Ministry of Interior of Hirshabelle State of Somalia is seeking to use a portion of the Bulsho Project to finance the recruitment of a Public Financial Management – PFM Specialist to support the Hirshabelle Project Implementation Unit - PIU.

Responsibilities: For the Bulsho Project activities, the PFM Specialist will work in closely with the PCU Financial Management and Procurement Specialists for oversight, guidance, quality assurance and also to ensure harmonization of procedures, and compliance with fiduciary requirements. The role will also provide technical support and capacity building to cities and district counterparts. The PFM Specialist in collaboration with the Hirshabelle State External Assistance Fiduciary Section (EAFS), prepare Unaudited Quarterly Financial Reports (IFRs) and Annual Financial Statements, ensuring adherence to international reporting standards.

The PFM Specialist is to ensure that Bulsho Financial Management and Procurement are done in line with the applicable Somalia Government and World Bank procedures and second is to support build Public Financial Management (PFM) capacity at the FMS, Districts and Community levels. The PIU Public Financial Management (PFM) Specialist will be required to be an all-around PFM professional combining both financial management and procurement responsibilities.

The State PIU PFM Specialist will perform the following key areas: -

A. Financial Management

  1. Financial Reporting and Oversight: Prepare and submit periodic financial reports (monthly, quarterly, annually) in approved formats, ensuring compliance with the financing agreement and also ensure timely identification and reporting of material variances for financial oversight and strategic decision-making and also ensure internal audit is carried out by Ministry of Finance (MoF) on project activities.
  2. Budgeting and Financial Planning: Develop and review annual work plans for the PIU and consolidated Bulsho budget in collaboration with PIU and the District Focal Points (DFPs), ensuring alignment with the standard chart of accounts. The budget to be consolidated by the MoIFAR and approved by Parliament by December 31and also prepare, monitor, and interpret cash flow forecasts to support financial planning and ensure disbursements align with approved budgets, work plans, and financial agreements.
  3. Fund Disbursement and Payment Processing: Verify payments adhere to accounting practices and financing agreements, obtaining No Objection letters through PCU where applicable and also facilitate the district disbursement requests through the Hirshabelle State EAFS and the Hirshabelle MoF and disburses the funds to the District Approved Accounts (DAAs).
  4. Subledger Reconciliation and Documentation: Conduct monthly bank reconciliations for the project accounts and also prepare Statements of Expenditure (SoEs) to ensure accurate financial tracking and timely documentation in client connection and ensure timely and regular updates to the Fixed Assets Register, conducting physical verification of assets at least twice a year and ensure regular update the Contracts Disbursement Register, ensuring proper reconciliation of new contracts and supplier payments.
  5. Audit Coordination and Risk Management: Work with auditors to facilitate timely annual financial audit and address queries and ensure compliance with internal control systems, EAFS manual, POM, COAPM, and other regulatory procedures and identify emerging fiduciary risks that inform revisions of the EAFS manual and POM, including Matching Grants Manual (MGM).
  6. Regulatory Compliance and Updates: Keep abreast of changes in financial regulations and ensure accounting staff remain updated and ensure no project category or component is overspent without proper World Bank authorization.

B. Procurement

1. Procurement Planning: Under the guidance of the PIU Project Manager, in consultation with the other PIU specialists, and in and close collaboration with the PCU Procurement Specialist, prepare the annual procurement plans for Hirshabelle State Bulsho activities and update the overall procurement plan for the state, in line with the consolidated national procurement plan and budget for Bulsho and track the implementation of the Hirshabelle State Procurement Plan, by updating progress against the Procurement Plan’s milestones, providing details on challenges and remaining actions, and indicating when procurement activities have been completed.

2. Tender Processing: Prepare inputs such as Terms of Reference, Schedules of Requirements, Specifications, Prequalification Documents (PQDs), Bidding Documents (BDs), and Requests for Proposals (RFPs), in line with World Bank regulations, the Bulsho POM and the project procurement plan and manage all procurement processes, including preparation and issuance of invitations, receipt of proposals and bids, opening of EOIs, proposals, and bids, evaluation of submissions, and preparation of evaluation reports in line with World Bank regulations and the Bulsho POM.

3. Contract Management: Under the direct guidance of the Project Manager, manage all contracts awarded under the project, including monitoring execution, tracking deliverables, and ensuring timely delivery of goods, services, and consultant reports in full compliance with contractual provisions and under the direct guidance of the Project Manager, address procurement-related queries, disputes, and complaints, and ensure issues are resolved in accordance with World Bank regulations, the Bulsho POM and applicable procedures.

4.  Compliance and Reporting: Ensure that all procurement activities comply with applicable World Bank regulations, the Bulsho POM and Government procedures, and submit reports to the PIU Project Manager and PCU Procurement Specialist for oversight and also together with the technical specialists, carry out direct verification of all purchased goods, services and works, by verifying that purchased goods, services and works are timely delivered and meet the specifications indicated in the purchase orders or contracts.

C. Capacity Building

  1. Conduct financial management and procurement training needs assessments and prepare structured capacity-building plans for the PIU, district finance officers and community committees implementing Bulsho-funded local investments, in coordination with the Local Government Institute (LGI).
  2. Provide tailored, hands-on mentoring and on-the-job support to district governments and community committees in procurement and contract management, focusing on the practical application of Bulsho project rules and procedures.
  3. Support districts and community committees in carrying out their procurement functions, including preparation of tender documents, evaluation of bids, contract award and management, and oversight of the procurement cycle, in compliance with the Bulsho POM and World Bank regulations.
  4. Participate in joint reviews, training sessions, and learning events organized by the PCU, and cascade knowledge to PIU and district staff.

D. Monitoring, Evaluation, and Reporting:

  1. The PFM Specialist shall collaborate with the PIU M&E Specialist to ensure that financial and procurement data are integrated into the project’s results framework.
  2. Track progress against fiduciary indicators (e.g., disbursement rate, audit c

MINISTÈRE DE L’AMÉNAGEMENT DU TERRITOIRE

ET DES SERVICES FONCIERS

---------------------

PROJET DE DÉVELOPPEMENT URBAIN INTÉGRÉ ET RÉSILIENT POUR L’EMPLOI (PRODUIRE)

SOLLICITATION DE MANIFESTATION D’INTÉRÊT POUR LE RECRUTEMENT D’UN RESPONSABLE ADMINISTRATIF ET FINANCIER DE L'UNITE DE GESTION A ANTANANARIVO DU PROJET DE DEVELOPPEMENT URBAIN INTEGRE ET RESILIENT POUR L’EMPLOI (PRODUIRE)

 

 

Pays : MADAGASCAR

AMI N : 010-2026/MATSF/PRODUIRE

Projet : Projet de Développement Urbain Intégré ET RESILIENT POUR L’EMPLOI

Crédit : IDA 8089 MG

Date de lancement : 23 octobre 2026

1. Le Gouvernement de la République de Madagascar a reçu un financement de 225 millions USD de l’Association Internationale de Développement (IDA) au profit du Projet de Développement Urbain Intégré et Résilient pour l’Emploi (PRODUIRE) et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie de ce crédit pour financer le contrat de services d’un Responsable Administratif et Financier de l’Unité de Gestion de Projet à Antananarivo.

L’Objectif de Développement du Projet (ODP) est de renforcer la résilience climatique des communautés urbaines, d'améliorer l'administration foncière et de soutenir l'emploi dans certaines villes.

2. Les services du consultant (« les Services ») consistent à assurer la gestion administrative et financière du Projet pour une meilleure utilisation des fonds.

3. Le mandat fera l’objet d’un contrat de soixante (60) mois assorti d’une tranche ferme de douze (12) mois et de quatre (04) tranches conditionnelles de douze (12) mois dont la condition d’affermissement sera l’évaluation positive de la performance du consultant. Une période d’essai de six (06) mois est prévue dans la tranche ferme. Le lieu de travail est au siège du projet à Antananarivo.

4. Le Responsable Administratif et Financier doit :

  • Etre titulaire d’un diplôme de Master (bacc +5) en finances et comptabilité délivré par une université ou un établissement d’enseignement supérieur parmi la liste des diplômes habilités par l’OECFM, ou dans un domaine apparenté,
  • Sur les dix (10) dernières années, ayant eu un ou des expérience(s) réussie(s) d’au moins sept (7) années dans la gestion administrative et financière de projets financés par les bailleurs de fonds (dont le financement moyen annuel géré s’élève à au moins 10 millions USD) ou dans une entité ayant un chiffre d’affaires moyen annuel de 1millionUSD,
  • Maîtrise des logiciels courants de comptabilité,
  • Maîtrise des outils informatiques de bureautique et de messagerie électronique
  • Maîtrise de la langue française et bonne connaissance de l’Anglais,
  • Grande capacité d’analyse de données, de synthèse et de rédaction,
  • Capacité à travailler de manière autonome et en équipe,
  • Méthodique, rigoureux, intègre,
  • Disponible et apte pour des déplacements dans les zones d’intervention du projet.

 

5. De plus amples informations peuvent être obtenues à l’adresse ci-dessous de 08 heures à 16 heures pendant les jours ouvrables.

6. Le MATSF invite les consultants individuels qualifiés à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les services décrits ci-dessus. Les consultants intéressés doivent fournir les informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications requises et une expérience pertinente pour l’exécution des services. Son dossier de candidature comprendra entre autres :

  1. Lettre de motivation
  2. Curriculum vitae avec coordonnées (adresse, téléphone, e-mail)
  3. Copie des diplômes, attestation de formations
  4. Certificat/ attestation de prestations similaires
  5. Trois références professionnelles

En cas d’envoi de manifestation par e-mail, le Candidat fournira toutes les pièces en un seul fichier PDF.

7. Il est porté à l’attention des Consultants que les dispositions des paragraphes 3.16 et 3.17 du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement (FPI) » septième édition septembre 2025, relatives aux règles de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflits d’intérêts sont applicables.

8. Un consultant sera sélectionné selon la méthode Sélection de Consultant Individuel telle que décrite dans le Règlement. Les candidats présélectionnés à l’issue de l’examen des dossiers seront convoqués à un entretien.

9. Les consultants Individuels intéressés sont invités à demander par courriel la version électronique des termes de référence de la mission à l’adresse ci-dessous. Le nom, le contact ainsi que l’adresse physique et électronique du consultant individuel devront être spécifiés dans la demande.

10. Les manifestations d’intérêt doivent être déposées et/ou envoyées par courriel, au plus tard  le 9 novembre 2026 à 16 heures à l’adresse ci-dessous, en mentionnant la référence :

SOLLICITATION DE MANIFESTATION D’INTERET

AMI N°010- 2026/MATSF/PRODUIRE

Recrutement d’un Responsable administratif et financier

11. L’adresse à laquelle il est fait référence ci-dessus est :

notices.description:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

 

Country: Republic of Tajikistan

Project: Strengthening Resilience Agricultural Sector Project

Grant No.: E1450-TJ 

Assignment Title: Consulting Services for Practical Training on Agricultural Drone Operations, Multispectral Data Acquisition and Processing for the Agriculture Technical Team (ATT)

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): SRASP-CS-RFP-2026-01

  1. The Republic of Tajikistan has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the “Strengthening Resilience of the Agriculture Sector Project” additional financing and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. 

The State Institute “Agriculture Entrepreneurship Development” now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

 

2. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website:

https://ehukumat.tj/uploads/2026/10/20/6d930c69cd233bb8346fd4277b38f10f_original.244861.pdf

3. The State Institute “Agriculture Entrepreneurship Development” now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The criteria for selecting the Consultant are:

4. The Training provider shall be a firm with proven experience in similar assignments including (but not limited to) Expertise in the following:   

  • documented experience operating professional UAV systems
  • practical experience with agricultural or multispectral UAV surveys
  • experience in RGB and multispectral image processing
  • knowledge of photogrammetry
  • experience with vegetation indices such as NDVI and NDRE
  • experience with GIS software
  • knowledge of RTK/GNSS positioning
  • experience delivering practical UAV training
  • capacity to conduct field-based training in the Republic of Tajikistan.

Experience with DJI Mavic 3 Multispectral, DJI Terra, precision agriculture, Sentinel-2 imagery or agricultural remote sensing shall be considered an advantage.

 

The above experience shall be demonstrated through a list of similar projects/contracts, including, at a minimum: description of services provided, contract amount, name of the contractor/client, project location/country, duration, assignment budget, and percentage of completion.

Where applicable, the submission shall also specify the Consultant’s role in joint ventures or sub consultancy arrangements, as well as the Consultant’s core business activities.

In addition, the above information shall be supported by certificates of completion or other documentary evidence confirming satisfactory performance, duly verified by the respective counterparties to the contracts concerned.

5. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraph 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (July 2016, revised in September 2023) Procurement in Investment Project Financing Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services (“the Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

6. The selection of consultants will be conducted using the Consultant Qualification Selection (CQS) method, in accordance with the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (July 2016, revised in September 2023) Procurement in Investment Project Financing Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services.

7. Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours from 08:00 to 17:00.

notices.description:
Request for Proposals (RFP)

Project                  Inclusive Connectivity and Development Project (ICDP)

Contract title:      Procurement of Design, Supply, and Installation of Land Acquisition Information Management System (LAIMS) for the Road Development Authority of Sri Lanka

Country                Sri Lanka

Loan No.              9290-LK

Contract No         LK-RDA-572729-GO-RFP

Issued on              October 22, 2026

1.        The Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka has received a loan from the financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Inclusive Connectivity and Development Project (ICDP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under the contract Procurement of Design, Supply, and Installation of Land Acquisition Information Management System (LAIMS) for the Road Development Authority of Sri Lanka

2.        The Chairperson, Project Procurement Committee on behalf of Inclusive Connectivity and Development Project now invites sealed Proposals from eligible Proposers for Procurement of Design, Supply, and Installation of Land Acquisition Information Management System (LAIMS) for the Road Development Authority of Sri Lanka.

3.        The procurement process will be conducted through national competitive procurement using Request for Proposals (RFP) as specified in the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” Seventh Edition September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), and is open to all eligible Proposers as defined in the Procurement Regulations.

  1. General Experience: Bidder should have general experience in Information Technology Contracts in the role of contractor, subcontractor or management contractor at least Eight (8) years prior to the bid submission deadline
  2. Specific Experience: Participation as a prime supplier, management contractor, JV member, sub-contractor, in at least one (01) ICT contract within the last ten (10) years, each with a value of at least LKR 30 million, that have been successfully completed. The bidder shall be certified in ISO 9001:2015 and ISO 27001
  3. Average Annual Turnover: Minimum required average annual turnover of the successful Proposer in the last five (05) years shall be LKR 300 million.
  4. Financial Resources: Minimum amount of liquid assets and/or credit facilities, net of other contractual commitments, of the successful Proposer shall be LKR 50 million.

4.        Proposal will be evaluated in accordance with the evaluation process set out in the Request for Proposals (RFP). The following weightings shall apply for Rated Criteria (including technical and non-price factors): 60 %. and for Proposal cost: 40 %.

5.        Interested eligible Proposers may obtain further information from Project Director, Inclusive Connectivity and Development Project (e-mail: wbicdpbid@gmail.com) and inspect the request for proposals document during office hours from 0900 to 1600 hours at the address given below or may be downloaded and reviewed from https://promise.lk/  and https://rda.gov.lk/ websites only for reference purpose.

6.        The request for proposals document in English may be purchased by interested eligible Proposers upon the submission of a written application to the address below and upon payment of a non-refundable fee of LKR 35,400.00 (With VAT) or an equivalent amount in a freely convertible currency in Sri Lanka from 22nd October 2026 between 9.00 am to 3.00 pm on any working day. The method of payment will be Cash or Bank Transfer. The document will be sent by email or could be collected by hand.

7.        Proposals must be delivered to the address below on or before 25th November 2026 at 2.00 p.m. electronic procurement will not be permitted. Late Proposals will be rejected. The outer Proposal envelopes marked “ORIGINAL PROPOSAL”, and the inner envelopes marked “TECHNICAL PART” will be publicly opened in the presence of the Proposers’ designated representatives and anyone who chooses to attend, at the address below on 25th November 2026 at 2.00 p.m. All envelopes marked “FINANCIAL PART” shall remain unopened and will be held in safe custody of the Purchaser until the second public Proposals opening.

8.        All Proposals must be accompanied by a Proposal Security in the form of Bank Guarantee.

9.        A Pre-Proposal Meeting will be arranged at 10:30 a.m. on 10th November 2026 in the Conference Room at the address given below.

10.    Attention is drawn to the Procurement Regulations requiring the Borrower to disclose information on the successful Proposer’s beneficial ownership, as part of the Contract Award Notice, using the Beneficial Ownership Disclosure Form as included in the request for proposal document.

11.    The address referred to above is Inclusive Connectivity and Development Project, 3rd floor, “Sethsiripaya - Stage I”, Battaramulla, Sri Lanka.

Inclusive Connectivity and Development Project,
