notices.description:
TheGovernmentofBotswana(GoB) is undertaking the Promoting Participation and Enhancing Learning (PROPEL) (P513800) project supported by the World Bank (WB).  

The Project Development Objective (PDO) is to increase participation in preprimary and senior secondary education and improve learning conditions in supported schools, particularly at the junior secondary level. The Project consists of the following four components: 

  • Component 1: Increasing participation in education 
  • Component 2: Enhancing the learning environment 
  • Component 3: Strengthening system capacity for quality education service delivery 
  • Component 4: Project management and implementation support 

 

The Ministry of Child Welfare and Basic Education (MCWBE) is the implementing entity for the Project. AProject Delivery Unit (PDU)(or Program Coordinating Unit) is being  establishedwithin MCWBE to support the effective implementation of project activities, including procurement and contract administration; monitoring, evaluation and reporting of progress under the project; fiduciary management; and environmental and social safeguards management. Specifically, the PDU will be responsible for preparing the Project Operations Manual (POM) to guide the implementation of the project. The MCWBE seeks to engage an Individual Consultant to support the preparation of the POM.

 

The objective of this assignment is to support the PDU in the development and finalization of the POM to clearly describe how the project will be implemented to achieve the expected development objectives and outcomes.

 

The POM is expected to be the key document which describes the structure of the project and the many stakeholders that are going to be involved in its implementation, including defining the roles and responsibilities of the various stakeholders under each component and sub-component and clarifying the implementation arrangements for all the components and sub-components.

 

The POM should include (i) detailed description of Project activities; (ii) the specific roles and responsibilities of the Project Steering Committee (PSC), PDU, and other entities participating in the implementation of the project and the arrangements for ensuring coordination among them; (iii) arrangements on fiduciary matters, including financial management, audit, and procurement; (iv) institutional administration coordination and day to day execution of project activities; (v) selection criteria and modalities for technical assistance in project supported activities; (vi) monitoring and evaluation; (vii) reporting arrangements; (viii) social and environmental safeguards requirements and procedures; and (ix) other technical and organizational arrangements and procedures as shall be required for the Project.

 

The POM will be organized or structured as follows:

 

  • Section 1 will describe the Project Context. This will include a brief background to the development of the project; state the Project Development Objective (PDO) and the indicators that will be used to measure progress towards the achievement of the objective; clarify the project target beneficiaries; and define the scope of the project.
  • Section 2 will discuss implementation arrangements by components, sub-components and activities of the project. It will include detailed implementation plan (IP) for each activity under the sub-components with clear selection criteria for specific activities. This will also include a detailed section on implementation modalities for activities related to civil-works and community driven development.
  • Section 3 will describe the institutional administrative and implementation arrangements of the project by entity-roles, attributions and responsibilities.
  • Section 4 will discuss the Monitoring and Evaluation Framework and the data collection arrangements to effectively measure project results and communicate them to the project stakeholders.
  • Section 5 will clarify the roles and responsibilities related to the financial management arrangements of the project, including the fiduciary responsibilities, reporting requirements, disbursement arrangements and financial controls and auditing of the project.
  • Section 6 will expand on the procurement management and guiding principles. This will also include updating the procurement plan and preparation of Annual Work Plans and Budget (AWPB).
  • Section 7 will discuss social and environmental safeguards requirements and procedures.
  • Section 8 will discuss Grievance Redress Mechanisms, (GRM), Citizen’s Engagement, Gender and Climate actions. 
  • Section 9 will discuss the communication plan for the project.
  • Section 10 will discuss training and capacity building plan under the project.
  • Section 11 will discuss other provisions.

 

The Consultant shall deliver the following products:

 

  • Outline of the Project Operations Manual.
  • Draft version of the POM
  • Final version of the POM

 

The assignment is planned for up to 3 months between November 2026 and January 2027 and the expected level of efforts is 35 working days. The initial two (2) weeks will be earmarked for the outline of the POM, six (6) weeks for the draft version of the POM and the last four (4) weeks for the final version of the POM.

 

The consultant will report to the Project Coordinator at the Ministry of Child Welfare and Basic Education, Gaborone. The Consultant will work in close coordination with PDU and MCWBE staff and liaise with the World Bank task team, as required.

The Ministry of Child Welfare and Basic Education now invites eligible individual consultants to indicate their interest in providing the services. Interested consultants must provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services.

The Consultant shall have: 

  • At least a master’s degree in economics, social sciences, law, business administration, management or a related field. Background in engineering/architecture will be an added advantage.
  • At least 8 years of experience in Project Management and monitoring.
  • At least 3 years of direct relevant experience in preparing similar POMs, particularly in projects implemented in sub-Saharan Africa.
  • Knowledge and experience of World Bank procedures and familiarity with World Bank financed projects.
  • Knowledge of Botswana’s education system.

notices.description:
Government of Somaliland

    Hargeisa Local Government

  Somali Urban Resilience Project (SURP II)

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST(REOI)

(INDIVIDUAL CONSULTING SERVICES)

PIU Monitoring and Evaluation Specialist

 

Country: Government of Somaliland

Project ID No: P170922

Project: Somali Urban Resilience Project (SURP-II)

Consultant Service: PIU Monitoring and Evaluation Specialist

Individual/Firm: Individual

Duty Station: Hargeisa

Deadline: November 05, 2026

Ref: SO-HM-574039-CS-INDV

 

  1. Background of the Project

 

The Hargeisa Local Government is implementing the SURP II Project (Nagaad Project) financed by the World Bank. The Project Development Objective (PDO) of the Nagaad Project is to strengthen the public service delivery capacity of local governments, expand access to climate-resilient urban infrastructure and services, and enable an immediate and effective response to eligible crises or emergencies in targeted areas.

 

Hargeisa Municipality is responsible for managing and supervising all project activities within the municipality, including timely implementation of civil work, procurement of goods and services, application of environmental and social safeguards, and continuous community engagement. It oversees contractors and supervision consultants to ensure quality, manages financial accounts in coordination with the EAFD, ensures timely payments, and prepares periodic plans, budgets, and reports.

Hargeisa Municipality is seeking to use of the SURP II project to finance the recruitment of PIU M&E Specialist.

 

  1. Responsibilities

 

  • The PIU Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) Specialist will be responsible for designing, implementing, and overseeing the monitoring and evaluation framework of the SURP-II project at the city level. The specialist will ensure the collection, analysis, and reporting of high-quality data to support decision-making, track project progress, and assess impact in line with World Bank and Government requirements.
  • Provide substantive support in collecting and transcribing relevant information from community members and municipal authorities during field visits and consultations.
  • Keep the Project Coordinator continuously informed about any local issues or social dynamics that may impact project implementation or community relations.

 

All specific duties and responsibilities are detailed in the Terms of Reference (TOR), available on the Hargeisa Municipality website at https://hargeisamunicipality.com or upon request via in-person submission or email.

 

 

 

  1. Selection Criteria

 

The selection shall be based on qualifications, experience and skills of the candidate and followed by an interview. The qualifications, experience and competencies include:

 

  • A master’s degree in a relevant field such as Project Management, Economics, Statistics, Data Science, Management Information Systems, Development Studies, Social Sciences, or related disciplines, with a focus on monitoring and evaluation, statistics, or research methods.
  • Minimum of seven (7) years of progressive professional experience in monitoring and evaluation, of which at least four (4) years in a lead or specialist M&E role on development projects.
  • At least three (3) years of demonstrated experience in designing and implementing M&E systems for urban infrastructure or urban development projects. This includes results frameworks, indicator definitions, data collection tools, MIS/databases and progress reporting.
  • At least two (2) years of experience on World Bank-financed projects or similar donor-funded urban infrastructure programmes (e.g., AfDB, EU, UN agencies) is highly desirable. Familiarity with World Bank results frameworks and Implementation Status and Results (ISR) reporting is an added advantage.
  • Expertise in survey design, field-testing tools, and use of mobile data collection applications (e.g., ODK, KoboToolbox, ONA) and use of computerized database systems or Monitoring Information Systems (MIS).

 

    1. REPORTING

 

The M&E Specialist will report directly to the PIU Project Coordinator and work under the overall guidance of the World Bank Task Team Leader(s) for the SURP II Project.

  1. TIMING Duration of Assignment:

The M&E Specialist shall be contracted for an initial period of one-year, renewable subject to satisfactory performance evaluation by the Municipality and approval by the World Bank, as well as the availability of project funds.

 

Hargeisa Local Government now invites eligible Individual Consultants to indicate their interest in providing the above-mentioned services. Interested consultants must provide the following (i) Curriculum Vitae (CV) with 3 reference people; (ii) copies of certificates of academic qualifications; and (iii) cover letter indicating that they are qualified to perform the services, and (iv) ID or Copy of passport.

 

  1. SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to section III, para 3.14,3.16 & 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers: Procurement in Investment Projects Financing Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services, July 2016, revised November 2017, August 2018, November 2020, and September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

notices.description:
Avis d'appel à candidature pour le recrutement d'un (e) Assistant (e) comptable pour le PGRPEC

                            N° Prêt : 8098-CI / P513144

Contexte et justification

La Côte d'Ivoire mène d'importantes réformes des finances publiques pour mieux mobiliser ses recettes intérieures et gérer ses dépenses publiques. Parmi les avancées clés : la Stratégie de mobilisation des recettes à moyen terme (2024-2028), le Schéma Directeur de Réforme des Finances Publiques (SDRFP), et la digitalisation de l'administration fiscale et douanière (dont la plateforme SIGOMAP pour les marchés publics).
Malgré ces progrès, plusieurs marges de progression demeurent : rationaliser les dépenses fiscales, améliorer l'efficacité de la TVA (actuellement 3,3 % du PIB, ratio d'efficacité de 0,18 %), renforcer la productivité de l'impôt sur les sociétés (7-8 %), et consolider la capacité des institutions de contrôle.

D’un montant de 100 millions de dollars US et exécuté selon le mécanisme Programme pour les résultats (PforR), l'objectif de développement du programme (ODP) du Programme de Gestion des ressources publiques pour l’emploi et la croissance en Côte d'Ivoire (PGRPEC) est d'accroître les recettes intérieures et d'améliorer l'efficacité de la gestion des dépenses publiques en Côte d'Ivoire.                                                                                                        

Dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre de ses activités le PGRPEC souhaite par le présent avis d’appel à candidatures recruter pour son Secrétariat Technique :

-Un (1) Assistant Comptable                                                                             Profil du candidat : qualifications et expériences requises                          

  • Un (e) Assistant Comptable
  • Un diplôme Bac + 2 en comptabilité, finance, contrôle de gestion ou audit ou domaine connexe.
  • Expérience professionnelle cumulée d’au moins trois (3) ans dans les domaines de la comptabilité, les finances, contrôle de gestion ou audits acquises en entreprises (privées ou publiques), en cabinet d’audit et d’expertise comptable, dans les projets de développement ou dans une institution internationale de développement ;
  • Au moins deux (2) ans à un poste d’assistant(e) Comptable sur un projet en développement financé par les bailleurs de fonds ;
  • Maîtrise des logiciels comptables ;

notices.title: The selection of Digital Transformation Senior Coordinator
notices.description:
Ministry of Education and Human Resources Development

Modernizing Education, Skills, and Administrative Reforms (MASAR) Program

Terms of Reference for:  Digital Transformation Senior Coordinator

Reference No.:  JO-MOE-566807-CS-INDV

Program Background:

The Modernizing Education, Skills, and Administrative Reforms (MASAR) Program for Results (PforR) is a transformative, system-wide reform initiative anchored in Jordan’s Economic Modernization Vision (EMV). The MASAR Operation is designed to support the Ministry of Education and Human Resources Development in addressing foundational bottlenecks in access, quality, and relevance of education, with a dual emphasis on equity and efficiency. The operation aims to strengthen institutional capacity while enabling measurable improvements in learning outcomes and employability, particularly through early childhood education and labor market-aligned technical and vocational education and training (TVET), and digital transformation in education.

The program became effective in 2024, with a total financing envelope of USD 400 million, supported by the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD). It comprises two core components:

  1. Program-for-Results (PforR): the principal financing instrument that disburses against verified achievement of results tied to government reform priorities.
  2. Investment Project Financing (IPF): a complementary technical assistance (TA) component aimed at supporting the implementation of system-strengthening activities and accelerating the achievement of Disbursement Linked Indicators (DLIs).

MASAR is structured around four interlinked Results Areas (RAs) that are strategically aligned with key education-sector transition points and cross-cutting governance reforms:

  • RA1: Home to School – Expanding Access to Foundational Learning. This includes (i) increasing equitable access to KG2, particularly in under-served districts and refugee-hosting communities; (ii) enhancing the quality of early childhood education through a revised KG1-KG2 curriculum and quality assurance mechanisms; and (iii) improving foundational literacy skills for Grades 1–3 through targeted pedagogical interventions and a comprehensive implementation plan.
  • RA2: School to Work – Increasing Access to Labor Market-Relevant TVET. MASAR seeks to improve the alignment of TVET with private sector needs by institutionalizing public-private partnerships, scaling apprenticeships, and expanding career guidance and employment pathways. This is complemented by the operationalization of an equivalency system that supports the portability and recognition of TVET qualifications, and enhanced use of learner trajectory data to inform student support services.
  • RA3: Strengthening Sector Governance and Efficiency. The program supports the operationalization of a restructured governance model for the education sector and introduces reforms to human resource management, with a particular focus on teacher recruitment, deployment, and professional development policies.
  • RA4: Digital Transformation in Education, to be introduced through the MASAR Additional Financing (AF), supporting digital and AI-enabled learning for students in Grades 4-12 and strengthening the institutional infrastructure needed for national-scale technology integration in education.

In addition to its core education objectives, MASAR embeds environmental and social sustainability principles across its implementation.

Ultimately, MASAR is designed to deliver measurable, inclusive, and sustainable improvements in Jordan’s education system. It expands access to early learning, strengthens foundational skills, improves graduate employability, strengthens digital skills, technology-enabled learning, and future-ready competencies, and reinforces institutional coherence through evidence-based policymaking. By supporting inclusive education and strengthening school-to-work transitions, the program directly contributes to Jordan’s long-term economic resilience and human capital development agenda.

Objectives of the Assignment:

The objective of this assignment is to provide strategic and operational support for the implementation of MASAR Result Area 4 (Digital Transformation in Education) and the coordination of MoE's digital education transformation portfolio, ensuring achievement of RA4 DLRs, alignment with national reform priorities, effective inter-institutional and donor coordination, and timely delivery of evidence required for programme verification and disbursement.

The Senior Coordinator will support operational follow-up, troubleshoot bottlenecks, monitor implementation against annual work plans, coordinate GFPP-financed preparatory activities, and contribute to institutionalizing sustainable digital education governance, EdTech implementation capacity, child-safe and inclusive digital learning standards, and cross-government coordination mechanisms within MoE systems.

Specifically, the Senior Coordinator will:

  • Lead MASAR RA4 preparation and implementation, driving progress against DLR 8.1-8.5 milestones and ensuring that technical assistance, procurement, capacity building, and institutional arrangements are sequenced to deliver required results on time.
  • Serve as the coordination focal point responsible for tracking, consolidating, and supporting delivery of RA4-related DLRs and associated verification evidence.
  • Coordinate GFPP-financed preparation activities so that technical assessments, pilots, PIU establishment, EdTech and AI Hub readiness, knowledge exchange, and capacity building directly inform the MASAR AF design and first-year implementation readiness.
  • Coordinate the digital education donor and partner portfolio, to ensure strategic alignment with the Education Strategic Plan, the National Education Sector Strategy, the EMV, and MASAR AF priorities while preventing duplication across programmes.
  • Produce regular, analytically rigorous RA4 and digital education portfolio progress reporting for DCU leadership, MASAR operational program manager, and relevant government counterparts.
  • Identify unresourced digital transformation priority areas and support resource mobilization and partner alignment.

Scope of Work

  1. MASAR RA4 Planning and Implementation
  • Develop, update, and closely monitor annual action plans for RA4, ensuring alignment with MASAR’s overall results framework, DLR timelines, and MoE priorities.
  • Break activities into operational tasks with clear milestones, dependencies, and responsible units.
  • Support the preparation and review of annual work plans, budgets, and implementation schedules to ensure timely delivery of programme results.
  • Conduct periodic implementation reviews and recommend adjustments to activities, sequencing, resource allocation, and technical assistance arrangements to maintain progress toward DLR achievement.
  • Provide regular progress reports against implementation for result area 4 workplan under MASAR, including the preparation of MASAR's bi-annual progress reports.
  • Support the preparation and quality review of ToRs for RA4 consultancies and contracts, including connectivity assessments, device pilots, EdTech technical assistance, AI governance, digital content development, cybersecurity, data privacy, and M&E assignments.

Digital Education Portfolio Coordination and Partner Alignment

  • Maintain and analyse a Digital Education Projects Matrix as a strategic portfolio management tool, identifying gaps, duplication risks, sequencing challenges, and opportunities for synergies across interventions.
  • Advise DCU and MASAR leadership on the prioritisation, alignment, endorsement, modification, and coordination of Digital Transformation initiatives to support implementation of the Education Strategic Plan (ESP) and national reform priorities.
  • Screen new digital education, EdTech, AI, connectivity, content, teacher training, and device-related proposals for alignment with RA4 DLRs, existing interventions, MoE standards, and donor investments.
  • Facilitate division-of-labour arrangements among development partners and stakeholders, ensuring clarity of roles, responsibilities, expected results, and implementation timelines.
  • Identify un-resourced Digital Education priority areas and support resource mobilisation efforts through engagement with development partners and relevant stakeholders.
  • Maintain cluster meeting records and action trackers; ensure follow-through on agreed actions between meetings.
  • Serve as the focal point for the Google Chromebook project.
  1. Stakeholder Coordination and Representation
  • Serve as the primary coordination focal point for digital transformation reforms, ensuring effective collaboration among Ministry directorates, development partners, implementing agencies, and other stakeholders.
  • Coordinate regularly with relevant MoE directorates and external stakeholders to ensure clarity of roles, timelines, and expected contributions.
  • Participate in technical committees, working groups, task teams, and workshops, providing inputs and ensuring follow-up on agreed actions.
  • Attend all MASAR supervision missions as the RA4 technical focal point.
  • Represent DCU’s coordination mandate at all Digital Transformation technical working groups and maintain proactive, technically substantive relationships with implementing agencies including UN agencies, development partners, private sector technology firms, telecom providers, universities, and others, as needed.
  1. Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification
  • Track all RA4-relevant MASAR DLRs and maintain a real-time DLR risk register; flag at-risk DLRs to the Program Manager and DCU Leadership with sufficient lead time for corrective action.
  • Monitor implementation progress across the broader digital transformation portfolio, maintaining oversight of milestones, deliverables, risks, dependencies, and corrective actions
  • Coordinate the preparation, consolidation, and quality assurance of DLR verification evidence, ensuring compliance with agreed verification protocols and readiness for independent verification reviews.
  • Review Verification reports submitted by the verification agency for the DLRs under result area 4.
  • Support monitoring, evaluation, reporting, verification, and learning requirements across digital transformation-related donor-funded programmes, ensuring timely provision of data, performance information, and evidence in accordance with donor requirements.
  • Support supervision missions, evaluations, audits, verification exercises, and technical assessments by ensuring data readiness and facilitating access to relevant information and stakeholders.
  1. Risk Management and Troubleshooting
  • Identify implementation risks, bottlenecks, and systemic constraints affecting RA4 and the broader digital transformation portfolio.
  • Provide timely solutions or mitigation measures and engage relevant directorates to resolve issues.
  • Escalate critical challenges to the Program Manager and DCU Deputy Director with clear problem statements and recommended actions.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REOI)

(SELECTION OF AN NGO)

Country: Bangladesh

Name of Project: ISO Component 05: Socio-economic Development of the Host Community and FDMN through Capacity Enhancement Project, (Credit No: IDA-7546-BD & E326-BD)

Assignment Title: Selection of an NGO for Monitoring, Evaluation and Operational Review (Spot Checks) for both Host Community and FDMN activities.

Reference No.: SD-16

The Government of Bangladesh is implementing the Inclusive Services and Opportunities for Host Communities and Displaced Rohingya Population (ISO) Project with World Bank financing. The Project Development Objective is to improve access to human capital services for vulnerable host communities and displaced Rohingya populations. Component 3, implemented by the Department of Social Services (DSS) under the Ministry of Social Welfare (MoSW), supports social care, child protection, and economic empowerment interventions for the Host Communities and Forcibly Displaced Myanmar Nationals (FDMN) in Chattogram Division. Under this assignment, DSS intends to conduct independent Monitoring, Evaluation, and Operational Reviews (Spot Checks) to assess whether child protection and economic empowerment interventions under the ISO Project are being implemented in accordance with approved guidelines / procedures and agreed protocols. The assignment will verify operational performance, beneficiary targeting, service delivery quality, use of systems among others and assess progress toward intended outputs and outcomes.

Purpose

The Monitoring, Evaluation and Operational Review (Spot Checks) will be conducted in a representative sample of locations where ISO Project interventions are being implemented for both Host Community (Chattogram Division) and FDMN populations (Camps in Cox’s Bazar and Bhasan Char). The assignment will cover both Child Protection and Economic Empowerment interventions. The NGO will be responsible for conducting independent monitoring, evaluation and operational reviews to assess operational performance, beneficiary targeting, use of digital systems, adequacy and capacity of human resources, quality of service delivery Relevant indicators will be drawn from the ISO Project Results Framework, as applicable. The assignment will be implemented over Eighteen (18) months.

Objectives

The objective of this assignment is to conduct independent Monitoring, Evaluation, and Operational Reviews (Spot Checks) to assess whether child protection and economic empowerment interventions under the ISO Project are being implemented in accordance with approved guidelines / procedures and agreed protocols. The assignment will verify operational performance, beneficiary targeting, service delivery quality, use of systems among others and assess progress toward intended outputs and outcomes.

 

The assignment will also involve an outcome evaluation of the social care and economic empowerment interventions in terms of beneficiary households’ progress across a set of relevant socio-economic / welfare indicators. Findings from the operational reviews and outcome evaluation would also need to be analyzed from a gender and social inclusion perspective, identifying any differential experiences or gaps affecting women and vulnerable groups, and will provide practical recommendations to support corrective actions and continuous improvement.

The shortlisting criteria are:

The NGO shall meet the following minimum qualification and experience requirements:

  • At least 10 years of relevant experience in monitoring, evaluation, operational reviews, or spot checks of large-scale development programs, preferably in Bangladesh or the region.
  • Experience in applying participatory and verification-based approaches to beneficiary targeting and service delivery assessment.
  • Strong understanding of social protection, livelihoods, poverty reduction, and community-based programs in Bangladesh and similar socio-economic contexts, including experience with government led programs and demonstrated experience with World Bank- or development partner-financed projects.
  • Proven experience in designing and implementing digitally enabled quantitative and qualitative data collection (using CAPI devices configured with KOBO Toolbox, Survey CTO and other similar platforms etc.), including household surveys, focus group discussions, key informant interviews, and field observations.
  • Demonstrated capacity to configure and deploy Bangla-language digital instruments using CAPI / mobile platforms, offline data capture in low-connectivity locations, and routine data quality checks such as back-checks and spot re-interviews.
  • Capacity to maintain a secure database for storing, managing and analyzing all data collected under the assignment, with respondent-level unique identifiers and appropriate access, backup and confidentiality controls.
  • Strong analytical, conceptual, and reporting capacity, with demonstrated ability to produce clear, evidence based, and actionable reports.
  • Demonstrated capacity to analyze quantitative and qualitative data using standard analysis software (i.e., Stata, R, SPSS, Python etc.)
  • Adequate organizational capacity to manage multi location field operations and deploy digitally equipped field teams across multiple districts and camps.
  • Demonstrated experience in monitoring or evaluating child protection, social service workforce, case management, or gender-based violence prevention and response programs.
  • Demonstrated experience of field data collection in humanitarian or fragility, conflict and violence settings, preferably in the Rohingya camps in Cox's Bazar and Bhasan Char or similar refugee contexts.
  • Demonstrated commitment to safeguarding, with an established Code of Conduct and experience of implementing / adopting Sexual Exploitation and Abuse and Sexual Harassment (SEA/SH) prevention and response protocols in field-based programs.
  • The NGO shall also have documented data protection and confidentiality policies for personally identifiable and case-related data, including data relating to children and survivors.

NGOs should submit:

  1. NGOs should provide sufficient information demonstrating their qualifications and relevant experience, including a brief description of similar assignments, clients, implementation periods, contract values, and the NGO's role. Copies of contracts, completion certificates, and other supporting documents are required at this stage.  CVs of individual experts are not required and will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.; and
  2. The JV agreement or letter of intent to form a JV, if applicable.

NGOs may associate with other NGOs to enhance their qualifications and capacity and shall clearly indicate whether the association is in the form of a joint venture or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all members shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. The qualifications and experience of the joint venture members will be assessed collectively, taking into account their respective roles. The qualifications and experience of proposed subconsultants will not be considered in the evaluation of expressions of interest for shortlisting.

notices.title: The Selection of Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) Senior Coordinator
notices.description:
Ministry of Education and Human Resources Development

Modernizing Education, Skills, and Administrative Reforms (MASAR) Program

Terms of Reference for:  Technical and Vocational Education and Training - TVET - Senior Coordinator

Reference No.:  JO-MOE-566808-CS-INDV

Program Background:

The Modernizing Education, Skills, and Administrative Reforms (MASAR) Program for Results (PforR) is a transformative, system-wide reform initiative anchored in Jordan’s Economic Modernization Vision (EMV). The MASAR Operation is designed to support the Ministry of Education and Human Resources Development in addressing foundational bottlenecks in access, quality, and relevance of education, with a dual emphasis on equity and efficiency. The operation aims to strengthen institutional capacity while enabling measurable improvements in learning outcomes and employability, particularly through early childhood education and labor market-aligned technical and vocational education and training (TVET), and digital transformation in education.

The program became effective in 2024, with a total financing envelope of USD 400 million, supported by the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD). It comprises two core components:

  1. Program-for-Results (PforR): the principal financing instrument that disburses against verified achievement of results tied to government reform priorities.
  2. Investment Project Financing (IPF): a complementary technical assistance (TA) component aimed at supporting the implementation of system-strengthening activities and accelerating the achievement of Disbursement Linked Indicators (DLIs).

MASAR is structured around four interlinked Results Areas (RAs) that are strategically aligned with key education-sector transition points and cross-cutting governance reforms:

  • RA1: Home to School – Expanding Access to Foundational Learning. This includes (i) increasing equitable access to KG2, particularly in under-served districts and refugee-hosting communities; (ii) enhancing the quality of early childhood education through a revised KG1-KG2 curriculum and quality assurance mechanisms; and (iii) improving foundational literacy skills for Grades 1–3 through targeted pedagogical interventions and a comprehensive implementation plan.
  • RA2: School to Work – Increasing Access to Labor Market-Relevant TVET. MASAR seeks to improve the alignment of TVET with private sector needs by institutionalizing public-private partnerships, scaling apprenticeships, and expanding career guidance and employment pathways. This is complemented by the operationalization of an equivalency system that supports the portability and recognition of TVET qualifications, and enhanced use of learner trajectory data to inform student support services.
  • RA3: Strengthening Sector Governance and Efficiency. The program supports the operationalization of a restructured governance model for the education sector and introduces reforms to human resource management, with a particular focus on teacher recruitment, deployment, and professional development policies.
  • RA4: Digital Transformation in Education, to be introduced through the MASAR Additional Financing (AF), supporting digital and AI-enabled learning for students in Grades 4-12 and strengthening the institutional infrastructure needed for national-scale technology integration in education.

In addition to its core education objectives, MASAR embeds environmental and social sustainability principles across its implementation.

Ultimately, MASAR is designed to deliver measurable, inclusive, and sustainable improvements in Jordan’s education system. It expands access to early learning, strengthens foundational skills, improves graduate employability, strengthens digital skills, technology-enabled learning, and future-ready competencies, and reinforces institutional coherence through evidence-based policymaking. By supporting inclusive education and strengthening school-to-work transitions, the program directly contributes to Jordan’s long-term economic resilience and human capital development agenda.

Objectives of the Assignment:

The objective of this assignment is to provide strategic and operational support for the implementation of MASAR Result Area 2 and the coordination of the implementation of other projects supporting the Ministry of Education and Human Resource Development’s TVET development portfolio, ensuring achievement of Disbursement Linked Results (DLRs), alignment with national reform priorities, effective donor coordination, and timely delivery of evidence required for programme verification and disbursement.

The Senior Coordinator will support operational follow-up, troubleshoot bottlenecks, monitor implementation against the Annual Work Plan, and contribute to institutionalizing sustainable TVET governance, labour market alignment, and donor coordination mechanisms within MoE systems.

Specifically, the Senior Coordinator will:

  • Lead MASAR RA2 implementation, driving progress against all DLR milestones and ensuring that TA inputs are sequenced to deliver required results on time.
  • Serve as the coordination focal point responsible for tracking, consolidating, and supporting delivery of all RA2-related DLRs and associated verification evidence.
  • Support the timely achievement of MASAR DLRs by facilitating coordination and sequencing across relevant donor-supported programmes, ensuring that required inputs are aligned with DLR timelines.
  • Coordinate the DCU’s full TVET donor portfolio, ensuring strategic alignment with the ESP 2026–2030 and preventing duplication across programmes, to prevent misalignment between parallel donor interventions through structured division-of-labour processes.
  • Produce regular, analytically rigorous TVET portfolio and RA2 progress reporting for DCU leadership and MASAR operational program management
  • Identify portfolio gaps for unresourced TVET priority areas.

Scope of Work

  1. MASAR RA2 Planning and Implementation
  • Develop, update, and closely monitor annual action plans for RA2, ensuring alignment with MASAR’s overall results framework, DLR timelines, and MoE priorities.
  • Break activities into operational tasks with clear milestones, dependencies, and responsible units.
  • Support the preparation and review of annual work plans, budgets, and implementation schedules to ensure timely delivery of programme results.
  • Conduct periodic implementation reviews and recommend adjustments to activities, sequencing, resource allocation, and technical assistance arrangements to maintain progress toward DLR achievement.
  • Provide regular progress reports against implementation for result area 2 workplan under MASAR, including the preparation of MASAR's bi-annual progress reports.
  • Supports the Managing Director of TVET at MoE in the preparation of TORs for activities identified in the workplan
  1. TVET Portfolio Coordination and Donor Alignment
  • Maintain and analyse the TVET Projects Matrix as a strategic portfolio management tool, identifying gaps, duplication risks, sequencing challenges, and opportunities for synergies across interventions.
  • Advise DCU leadership on the prioritisation, alignment, endorsement, modification, and coordination of TVET initiatives to support implementation of the Education Strategic Plan (ESP) and national reform priorities.
  • Screen new TVET programme proposals and assess their alignment with sector priorities, existing interventions, and donor investments.
  • Facilitate division-of-labour arrangements among development partners and stakeholders, ensuring clarity of roles, responsibilities, expected results, and implementation timelines.
  • Identify un-resourced TVET priority areas and support resource mobilisation efforts through engagement with development partners and relevant stakeholders.
  • Provide regular progress reports against implementation of the DCU’s full TVET donor portfolio.
  • Maintain cluster meeting records and action trackers; ensure follow-through on agreed actions between meetings.
  1. Stakeholder Coordination and Representation
  • Serve as the primary coordination focal point for TVET-related reforms, ensuring effective collaboration among Ministry directorates, development partners, implementing agencies, and other stakeholders.
  • Coordinate regularly with relevant MoE directorates and external stakeholders to ensure clarity of roles, timelines, and expected contributions.
  • Participate in technical committees, working groups, task teams, and workshops, providing inputs and ensuring follow-up on agreed actions.
  • Attend all MASAR supervision missions as the DCU TVET/RA2 technical focal point.
  • Represent DCU’s coordination mandate at all TVET technical working groups and maintain proactive, technically substantive relationships with implementing agencies including UNESCO, ILO, GIZ, and others.
  1. Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification
  • Track all TVET-relevant MASAR DLRs and maintain a real-time DLR risk register; flag at-risk DLRs to the Program Manager and DCU Leadership with sufficient lead time for corrective action.
  • Monitor implementation progress across the broader TVET portfolio, maintaining oversight of milestones, deliverables, risks, dependencies, and corrective actions
  • Coordinate the preparation, consolidation, and quality assurance of DLR verification evidence, ensuring compliance with agreed verification protocols and readiness for independent verification reviews.
  • Review Verification reports submitted by the verification agency for the DLRs under result area 2.
  • Support monitoring, evaluation, reporting, verification, and learning requirements across TVET-related donor-funded programmes, ensuring timely provision of data, performance information, and evidence in accordance with donor requirements.
  • Support supervision missions, evaluations, audits, verification exercises, and technical assessments by ensuring data readiness and facilitating access to relevant information and stakeholders.
  1. Risk Management and Troubleshooting
  • Identify implementation risks, bottlenecks, and systemic constraints affecting RA2 and the broader TVET portfolio.
  • Provide timely solutions or mitigation measures and engage relevant directorates to resolve issues.
  • Escalate critical challenges to the Operational Program Manager and DCU Deputy Director with clear problem statements and recommended actions.
  1. Knowledge Management and Institutional Strengthening
  • Facilitate knowledge exchange across MoE directorates and donor partners, ensuring that lessons learned, technical guidance, and best practices are captured and shared.
  • Support capacity-building efforts related to TVET programme delivery, labour market alignment, and TVET qualification equivalency systems.
  • Promote institutionalization of MASAR RA2 processes and DCU TVET coordination mechanisms within MoE systems to strengthen long-term sustainability.

AVIS D’APPEL A CANDIDATURE POUR LE RECRUTEMENT D’UN COMPTABLE POUR LE PROGRAMME DE GESTION DES RESSOURCES PUBLIQUES POUR L’EMPLOI ET LA CROISSANCE                                       N° Prêt : 8098-CI / P513144   

Contexte et justification

La Côte d'Ivoire mène d'importantes réformes des finances publiques pour mieux mobiliser ses recettes intérieures et gérer ses dépenses publiques. Parmi les avancées clés : la Stratégie de mobilisation des recettes à moyen terme (2024-2028), le Schéma Directeur de Réforme des Finances Publiques (SDRFP), et la digitalisation de l'administration fiscale et douanière (dont la plateforme SIGOMAP pour les marchés publics).
Malgré ces progrès, plusieurs marges de progression demeurent : rationaliser les dépenses fiscales, améliorer l'efficacité de la TVA (actuellement 3,3 % du PIB, ratio d'efficacité de 0,18 %), renforcer la productivité de l'impôt sur les sociétés (7-8 %), et consolider la capacité des institutions de contrôle.

D’un montant de 100 millions de dollars US et exécuté selon le mécanisme Programme pour les résultats (PforR), l'objectif de développement du programme (ODP) du Programme de Gestion des ressources publiques pour l’emploi et la croissance en Côte d'Ivoire (PGRPEC) est d'accroître les recettes intérieures et d'améliorer l'efficacité de la gestion des dépenses publiques en Côte d'Ivoire

Dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre de ses activités le PGRPEC souhaite par le présent avis d’appel à candidatures recruter pour son Secrétariat Technique un (1) Comptable.                                                                                                              

Profil du candidat : qualifications et expériences requises

  •    Un (e) Comptable
  • Être titulaire d’un diplôme de niveau BAC + 4 au minimum en gestion comptable et financière ;
  • Avoir une expérience professionnelle générale de cinq (05) ans au moins dans le domaine de la comptabilité, de la gestion financière et de la comptabilité analytique de projets de développement financés par les partenaires au développement ;
  • Avoir des expériences à un poste similaire dans des projets financés par la Banque Mondiale serait un atout ;
  • Avoir une connaissance des procédures de gestion financières et comptables des partenaires techniques et financiers notamment de la Banque mondiale ; connaissance des procédures de gestion des finances publiques serait un avantage ;
  • Avoir la maîtrise de logiciels comptables usuels et de systèmes informatisés de gestion adaptés aux projets de développement financés par les PTF ;
  • Avoir la maitrise de logiciel de gestion comptable généralement utilisé sur les projets financés par la Banque Mondiale.                                                     Responsabilités du Spécialiste en Sauvegarde Environnementale et Sociale                                                                                                     L’ensemble de toutes leurs tâches est précisé dans les Termes de Référence. Les candidat(e)s intéressé (e)s devront à cet effet solliciter les Termes de Référence par courriel aux adresses ci-dessous.                             Constitution et dépôt des candidatures                                                      

    Les candidat(e)s intéressé(e)s aux différents postes devront soumettre un dossier de candidature comprenant :

  • Une lettre de motivation ;
  • Un Curriculum vitae détaillé, récent et certifié sincère par le candidat ;
  • Une copie du ou des diplômes requis et attestations ou tout autre document attestant les qualifications et expériences acquises par les candidats ;
  • Les références d’au moins 2 emplois antérieurs et les coordonnées accessibles des employeurs.                                                                              
  • Procédure de recrutement

  • La procédure de recrutement des candidats sera conduite conformément au Règlement de Passation des Marches de la Banque mondiale en vigueur (Edition Septembre 2025) et plus précisément de la clause 7.36 « Sélection de Consultants Individuels par mise en concurrence ouverte ».

    Le recrutement s’effectuera par appel à candidature et comportera deux (2) phases :

    •     Une phase de présélection des candidats par l’établissement d’une liste restreinte des candidats les plus qualifiés pour le poste au regard de l’analyse de leur CV ;

1. Forward Digital Mena has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Digital Skilling for Employment (DSE) Project (P506407), and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under the contract for Design, Development and Deployment of an AI-Enabled Digital Skills and Employment Platform (nammiskills V2). For this contract, the Borrower shall process the payments using the Direct Payment disbursement method, as defined in the World Bank's Disbursement Guidelines for Investment Project Financing, except for those payments which the contract provides to be made through letter of credit.

2. Forward Digital Mena now invites sealed Proposals from eligible Proposers for Design, Development, Deployment, Integration, Testing, Commissioning, and Support of an AI-enabled Digital Skills and Employment Platform (nammiskills V2) in Lebanon.

The assignment includes the enhancement and further development of the existing nammiskills platform, including its Learner, Employer and Administrator spaces, AI-enabled functionalities, Customer Relationship Management (CRM) setup and configuration and the provision of the required CRM subscriptions, third-party integrations, data and system migration, cloud deployment, security and data protection requirements, training, documentation, warranty and post-deployment support.

The Information System (IS) is expected to be implemented over a period of 27 weeks. The contract shall also cover the provision of CRM subscriptions, maintenance, technical support and related follow-up services, as specified in the RFP, through 31 December 2027, which constitutes the contractual completion date.

3. The procurement process will be conducted through international competitive procurement using Request for Proposals (RFP) as specified in the World Bank's Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, September 2025 ("Procurement Regulations"), and is open to all eligible Proposers as defined in the Procurement Regulations.

4. Proposals will be evaluated in accordance with the evaluation process set out in the RFP document. The following weightings shall apply: Rated Criteria (including technical and non-price factors): 70%; Proposal cost: 30%.

5. Interested eligible Proposers may obtain further information from Forward Digital Mena, Attention: Michelle Boustany, Procurement Specialist, at procurement@forwardmena.org. The Request for Proposals document will be available electronically as specified below.

6. The Request for Proposals document in English will be provided free of charge to interested eligible Proposers upon submission of a written request by email to procurement@forwardmena.org. The Request for Proposals document will be sent electronically by email.

7. Proposals must be submitted physically to the address indicated below or electronically by email to procurement@forwardmena.org on or before 30 November 2026 at 12:00 noon (Beirut local time). Electronic submission will be permitted. Late Proposals will be rejected.

For electronic submission, Proposals shall be submitted in two separate parts: (i) the Technical Part and (ii) the Financial Part. Both parts shall be submitted as separate encrypted, password-protected electronic files. Passwords shall not be included in the submission email.

The password for the Technical Part shall be provided during the scheduled Technical Proposal opening, following the Purchaser's instructions. The password for the Financial Part shall not be provided at the time of Proposal submission or during the Technical Proposal opening.

The Technical Parts will be opened on 30 November 2026 at 12:30 PM (Beirut local time), in the presence of Proposers' designated representatives who choose to attend, either physically or virtually. Virtual connection details will be communicated to Proposers in advance.

The Financial Parts shall remain unopened and inaccessible to the Purchaser during the technical evaluation. Following completion of the technical evaluation, only Proposers whose Technical Parts qualify for progression to the financial evaluation will be invited to provide the passwords for their Financial Parts for the subsequent Financial Proposal opening. The location, date and time of the Financial Proposal opening will be communicated to those Proposers in accordance with the RFP.

1.  The Republic of North Macedonia has received a grant from the World Bank, acting as trustee of the Grant Facility for Project Preparation (GFPP), for the preparation of the above-mentioned project and intends to apply part of the proceeds towards payments under the contract for the procurement of a professional unmanned aircraft system.

2.  The Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Water Economy, through the Project Implementation Unit (the “Purchaser”), invites eligible and qualified bidders to submit a quotation for the procurement, delivery and commissioning of one (1) complete professional unmanned aircraft system (UAS) for mapping, photogrammetry and visual inspection, with RTK and/or PPK functionality, associated equipment, software and training for at least two representatives of the Purchaser/User. The procurement is a single indivisible package; partial quotations will not be considered.

Participation is open to all eligible and qualified bidders from any country, in accordance with these Regulations and the conditions set out in the RFQ.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REOI) 

(INDIVIDUAL CONSULTING SERVICES) 

 

Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI) 

Digital RMI Project 

P171517 

 

Assignment Title:  

Reference No.: MH-DIDA- Digital Unit: Government Technical Support Specialist/s 

(Majuro based position) 

 

The Government of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (the Government) is undertaking a major investment program supported by the World Bank under the proposed Digital RMI Project (Project).  The proposed development objective includes establishing the critical foundations for digital government services and the digital economy. 

 

To support the development of digital government services and a digital economy the Government, with World Bank funding support, has established a Digital Unit reporting into the Office of the Chief Secretary.  

 

The Director of the Digital Unit is now seeking to recruit up to 2 technical support specialist staff members who will help progress the Digital Unit work program and support the rollout of the Microsoft platform, and applications as approved in the RMI Future State Roadmap Report.  The role involves working closely with relevant Ministry(s) to provide technical support for the implementation of and migration to the Microsoft platform and associated applications. 

 

 A description of the Digital Unit’s functions is set out in the position description in terms of reference, and a copy of the Future State Roadmap Report can be provided on request. 

 

The roles are based in Majuro.  This is a full-time position and is for a 2-year contracted period (with the possibility of an extension), with a 3-month probationary period. The remuneration will reflect the fact that this is a contracted role and not a permanent public sector role. 

 

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the can be found at the following link:https://digitalrmi.com/opportunities/ or supplied on request to the Project Officer galbert.robert@rmigov.mh. 

 

Division of International Development Assistance (DIDA) now invites eligible Individuals (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services.  Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services (attach curriculum vitae with description of experience in similar assignments, similar conditions, etc.). The criteria for selecting the Consultant are: 

 

Mandatory Requirements (pass /fail) 

The successful candidate shall:  

 

  1. Qualification (associate degree or equivalent, or higher) experience in Information Technology, Computer Science, or a related field ora minimum of 2 years of experience in technical support roles, preferably in a similar organizational context. 

 

  1. Proven expertise in administering networks, hardware, software, and operating systems 

 

  1. Advanced troubleshooting skills with a track record of effectively diagnosing and resolving complex technical issues. 

 

Additional Desirable Requirements: 

 

  1. Experience in implementing and supporting Microsoft Products (Microsoft 365 and Azure) 

 

  1. Supporting Cloud infrastructure – an understanding of cloud architecture and operating principles 

 

  1. Demonstrated experience in coordinating software procurement and managing licensing tracking systems. 

 

  1. Strong communication and interpersonal abilities, with a knack for conveying technical concepts clearly. 

 

  1. Previous experience in conducting training sessions and facilitating knowledge transfer among team members. 

 

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraph 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers dated November 2020 (“the Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.  

 

Expressions of interest must be delivered in written form to the address below (in person, or by e-mail) by no later than 5pm July 10th, 2026 (RMI time). 

 

Siddarth Pimpale 

Project Manager 

Digital RMI

notices.title: Recruitment of Project Engineer No:2
notices.description:
NATIONAL LOCAL GOVERNMENT FINANCE COMMITTEE

                      Governance to Enable Service Delivery (GESD) Project – GESD 2.0

                                                  Agreement No:  IDA-E6540

Individual Consultant- Project Engineer (2)

No: MW-NLGFC-563895-CS-INDIV/ MW-NLGFC-563897-CS-INDIV

                     

                                          Date of Issue: 20th August ,2026

  1. Background

 

The Government of Malawi (GoM) through the National Local Government Finance Committee (NLGFC) has received financing towards the cost of Governance to Enable Service Delivery (GESD) Project. The NLGFC intends to apply part of the proceeds of this financing to eligible payments under the contract for hiring two Project Engineer on a three - year contract renewable annually based on performance and availability of financial resources or mutually agreed by both parties.    

 

NLGFC therefore invites applications from suitably qualified and interested candidates to fill the position of two (2) Project Engineer tenable at the NLGFC Offices. The terms of Reference (TORs) for two (2) Project Engineer) are as follows:

 

2. The Objectives of the Assignment

The Project Engineer (Specialist) shall lead, coordinate and support local authorities and all relevant ministries, departments and agencies in the design and implementation of the project. The Project Engineer (Specialist) will lead and have approving authority for preparing and/or interpreting designs, bill of quantities (BoQs), tendering and engineering cost estimates prepared. The Project Engineer (Specialist) will work closely with relevant district authorities, including district engineers, other officers and specialists in the PIT, including safeguards, Project Coordinator, NLGFC, MoLGRD and other relevant stakeholders, including but not limited to supervision consultants. The Project Engineer (Specialist) will support monitoring of the sub-projects and will address and manage technical engineering questions in local investment projects implemented by the local authorities that are financed by GESD 2.0. 

 

  1. Duties and Responsibilities of the Project Engineer (Consultant)

 

The Project Engineers (Consultants) will be responsible for providing technical leadership and engineering oversight to ensure that project activities are planned, designed, implemented, monitored, and completed in accordance with approved specifications, quality standards, budget, schedule, and applicable regulations.

 

Specific tasks will include the following:

 

  1. Coordinate and support all engineering functions and activities related to infrastructure construction and rehabilitation in the local authorities, namely Department of Planning and Development and Department of Public Works;
  2. Support data collection for all proposed sub-project sites to aid development and customisation of architectural designs, production of BoQs and engineering estimates, tendering processes and ensuring that designs are in conformity with results of site-specific resilience and risk related investigations and analysis;
  3. Ensure timely and correct submission of information into the Public Management Information System (PMIS) by local authorities;
  4. Provide technical support to the Local Authorities in project selection, reviewing annual investment plans, works designs, BoQs, costs estimate, tendering, supervision and monitoring;
  5. Coordinate topographic surveys for the design of infrastructure to be developed under the Project;
  6. Support local authorities in conducting initial site investigation;
  7. Facilitate the production of location maps and sketches if necessary for all engineering sites that need maintenance and repair (selected as subprojects under GESD 2.0);
  8. Support and if necessary lead the review and approval of submissions by design engineers, including ensuring timely submission of the same;
  9. Support and if necessary lead design options stakeholder consultations with communities and relevant departments so that their inputs are incorporated in the designs to ensure acceptance and ownership of solutions to be developed;
  10. Conduct technical supervision of all construction works ensuring that the works are implemented to the required standards, within the assigned cost and time;
  11. Check Supervision Consultant’s work so as to conduct verification of contractors’ payment claims for works done;
  12. Manage changes to engineering constructions works ensuring that any changes have no adverse effect on the project and they are undertaken following project works change protocols, including documentation;
  13. Facilitate preparation of work plans and budgets for local investment projects to ensure relevance to outputs and outcomes of local investment project;
  14. Support the preparation of schedule of works and materials for project activities in collaboration with relevant stakeholders;
  15. Review and assess contractors’ and consultants’ payment certificates for engineering works
  16. Prepare and conduct training programs for Local Authority technical staff involved in contract and procurement management; and other related activities as directed by the PIT;
  17. Ensure compliance with all statutory and regulatory requirements;
  18. Liaise with other project specialists and officers, including safeguards, occupational health & safety, procurement, and advise the PIT on all construction Engineering technical related matters;
  19. Collect projects’ progress reports from the LAs, liaise with the monitoring & evaluation officer in the PIT in producing reports for project activities, consolidate them and submit them to PIT/PC, Executive Director and World Bank Task Team;
  20. Preparation and timely submission of monthly, quarterly and annual engineering project progress reports and other reports to the Project Coordinator, Executive Director and the World Bank Task Team.
  21. Facilitating the review of Annual Investment Plans (AIPs) for Local authorities and provide guidance on cost and time estimates.

 

  1. Deliverables

 

Deliverables for the assignment correspond to the duties and responsibilities above. Specifically, they will comprise:

 

  1. Timely review of AIPs submitted by local authorities, including review of cost and time estimates;
  2. Reviewed and approved engineering designs and drawings.
  3. Technical specifications and BoQs.
  4. Engineering project progress reports and other reports timely compiled
  5. Site inspection reports.
  6. Quality assurance and quality control (QA/QC) reports.
  7. Defects and corrective action reports.
  8. Monthly and quarterly progress reports, aligned with PMIS information.
  9. Physical progress monitoring reports.
  10. Work completion certificates.

 

  1. Performance Criteria

 

The following performance criteria will be used to assess the performance of the Project Engineer annually and based upon these assessments the contract with the project (GESD 2.0) may be continued or terminated:

  • 100% of required technical reports submitted on time.
  • At least 95% compliance with approved engineering specifications and quality standards.
  • Site inspections conducted according to approved supervision schedules.
  • 100% of contractor payment certificates reviewed and processed within agreed timelines.
  • All identified defects and non-compliance issues addressed within specified corrective action periods.
  • Minimal cost and schedule overruns attributable to technical deficiencies.
  • No major engineering failures or quality-related incidents.
  • Timely completion and handover of project infrastructure.
  • PMIS utilization by local authorities.

 

  1. Qualifications, Skills and Expertise

 

The candidate should meet the following minimum qualifications:

 

  1. Bachelor’s Degree in Civil Engineering/Architecture/Quantity Surveying
  2. Master’s Degree in Construction/Engineering related field and ;
  3. Registration with an approved professional body, such as Malawi Engineering Institution/Board of Architects and Quantity Surveyors
  4. A minimum of 8 years of relevant working experience;
  5. Excellent communications, writing/reporting skills;
  6. Proficiency in computer aided design packages (AutoCAD, ArchCAD, GIS etc)
  7. Proficient in the use of Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Microsoft Project etc.);
  8. Strong organizational, self-starting and communications skills;
  9. Experience working with government institutions and organizations; working experience with local authorities in Malawi is considered an advantage;
  10. Highly motivated and enthusiastic person with excellent planning, analytical, communications and interpersonal skills as well as a high level of diplomacy; and
  11. Excellent oral and written communication skills in English, as well as team participation and management skills

 

  1. Reporting Arrangements

 

The Project Engineer (Specialist) will primarily report to the Project Coordinator with a technical reporting line to the Director of Social and Economic Services at NLGFC for all technical matters, and will support local authorities’ in implementation of GESD 2.0 project.

 

  1. Location of Assignment

 

The Project Engineer (Specialist) will be based at the NLGFC offices in Lilongwe. The Project Engineer (Consultant) will occasionally be required to travel to local government authorities in Malawi where the Project is implementing its activities to engage with district officials to guide and improve project implementation.

 

  1. Duration of Assignment

 

The assignment is expected to span a total period of up to three (3) years, with annual performance reviews and contract extensions subject to satisfactory performance.

.

notices.buyer: Ministry of Water, Energy and Minerals
notices.description:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES - INDIVIDUAL SELECTION)

 

UNITED REPUBLIC OF TANZANIA

SUSTAINABLE RURAL WATER SUPPLY AND SANITATION PROGRAM (SRWSSP) PHASE II

 

Assignment Title: Consultancy Service for Engagement of an Individual Consultant to Provide Technical Expert Services in Water Resources Management

 

Reference No. TZ-MOWEM-576846-CS-INDV

 

The Revolutionary Government of Zanzibar (RGoZ), through the United Republic of Tanzania, has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of Sustainable Rural Water Supply and Sanitation Program (SRWSSP) Phase II and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

 

Objective of the Assignment

The overall objective of this assignment is to provide sustained technical support to the Ministry of Water, Energy and Minerals in strengthening water resources management systems in Zanzibar.

 

Specifically, the assignment aims to:

  • Improve understanding of water resources availability and utilization
  • Strengthen monitoring, data management, and decision-making systems
  • Promote sustainable and equitable allocation of water resources
  • Enhance climate resilience and environmental protection
  • Strengthen institutional capacity for effective water governance

The outputs of this assignment will be used to inform

  1. Future water resources and WASH investments in Zanzibar;
  2. strengthening of regulatory and abstraction control mechanisms;
  3. climate and drought preparedness planning; and
  4. coordination with development partners and the private sector, including utilities and major water users.

Success of the assignment will be measured by improved availability of water resources information; informed and enhanced decisionmaking on water resources allocation, planning, abstraction and protection; strengthened institutional capacity and well-aligned practices; and increased readiness to manage climate and drought risks in water resources management.

 

Specific Tasks of the Consultant

The Consultant will act as a Technical Advisor and Lead Expert, strengthening the institutional capacity of the Division of Water Resources Management by supporting analysis, providing technical guidance, undertaking capacity development endeavours and coordination, while implementation and daytoday data collection remain the responsibility of relevant institutions. The Technical Advisor shall support the Division of Water Resources Management through undertaking the following tasks:

  • Undertake capacity appraisal for the division and identify strategic areas of support
  • Conduct a comprehensive assessment of water resources, including groundwater and surface water systems.
  • Review existing policies, laws, and strategies related to water resources management.
  • Assess current water abstraction, usage patterns, and demand projections.
  • Evaluate the status of aquifers, recharge areas, and catchment zones.
  • Identify risks related to climate change, pollution, and over-extraction.
  • Develop strategies for sustainable water resources management, including conservation and protection measures.
  • Conduct consultations (physical and virtual) with experts and stakeholders at national, regional (Eastern & Southern Africa), and international levels to identify and promote best IWRM practices applicable to Zanzibar.
  • Propose mechanisms for improving water resources monitoring, data collection, and information systems.
  • Support development of regulatory and institutional frameworks for effective water governance.
  • Support Technical Assistance on drafting of new Water and Sanitation Act.
  • Prepare and present technical reports and recommendations to the Ministry.

 

The Ministry of Water, Energy and Minerals now invites eligible expert to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

 

  • At least Master’s Degree in Water Resources Engineering, Hydrology, Environmental Engineering, or related field.
  • At least 12 years of experience in undertaking Water Resources Management projects.
  • Proven experience with international donor-funded programs (World Bank, AfDB, etc.).
  • Demonstrated completion of at least three (3) comparable assignments as an individual consultant or team leader.
  • Experience in national-level assignments. Must have participated in at least 1 assignment of a similar nature in Tanzania (mainland or Zanzibar)
  • Competency in water resource management analytics (especially groundwater), capacity development, team building, policy analysis, reporting, and stakeholder engagement.
  • Registered by the relevant registration and professional boards.
  • Fluency in written and spoken English; working experience in Water Sector in Zanzibar and knowledge of Kiswahili is a strong advantage.

 

The attention of interested consulting firms is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers”, Seventh Edition, September 2025, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. Consulting firms intending to submit an Expression of Interest shall not have any conflict of interest or unfair competitive advantage and must comply with the provisions of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations.

 

The Consultant will be selected in accordance with the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, Seventh Edition, September 2025, using the Individual Consultant Selection method through an open national competitive process.

notices.description:
REPUBLIC OF ANGOLA

MINISTRY OF PLANNING

ACCELERATING ECONOMIC DIVERSIFICATION AND JOB CREATION PROJECT

Loan No.: IBRD-95270

Project ID: P178035

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

Assignment Title: CONSULTING SERVICES FOR THE DIAGNOSIS OF LABORATORIES THAT ANALYZE AND TEST GOODS, AND FOR SIMPLIFYING LABORATORY CONTROL PROCEDURES IN INTERNATIONAL TRADE.

Reference No. 102CS1/MINPLAN/26

 

The Government of Angola has received financing from the World Bank Group's International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) toward the cost of the Accelerating Economic Diversification and Job Creation Project (Diversifica Mais) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services for the Diagnosis of Laboratories that Analyze and Test Goods, and for Simplifying Laboratory Control Procedures in International Trade.

Consulting Services (“the Services”) aim to diagnose national laboratory capacity relevant to international trade, analyze and simplify laboratory control procedures for imports and exports, define functional requirements for future technological integration, and prepare a prioritized action plan to strengthen the national laboratory infrastructure. The consulting firm shall, inter alia:

  1. Map and characterize public and private laboratories authorized to perform analyses and tests on goods for export or subject to import controls, including their authorization status, sectoral scope and geographic coverage;
  2. Assess the installed technical, technological and human capacity of laboratories, including equipment, testing methods, staff qualifications, accreditation status and operational performance indicators;
  3. Analyze the legal, institutional and regulatory framework, as well as laboratory control procedures applicable to imports and exports, identifying redundancies, constraints and opportunities for simplification;
  4. Benchmark relevant international experience and formulate recommendations for strengthening the laboratory infrastructure and simplifying laboratory control regimes for international trade;
  5. Define functional, technical, data, security and interoperability requirements for the future adaptation of relevant automated systems, including JUCE, excluding any software development, acquisition, configuration or implementation;
  6. Prepare practical guidance for economic operators; deliver capacity-building and awareness-raising activities for laboratory agencies, the private sector and customs administration; and validate findings with stakeholders.

The expected duration of the consultancy contract will be five (5) months.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained at the address given below.

The Accelerating Economic Diversification and Job Creation Project (Diversifica Mais) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

  • A minimum of seven (7) years of proven experience in conducting studies, diagnoses or audits in quality infrastructure, metrology, accreditation or international trade;
  • Demonstrated technical and logistical capacity to conduct fieldwork in sub-Saharan African countries—at a national scale—will be an advantage.;
  • A regular legal, tax and financial status, demonstrated by the applicable legal documentation;
  • Demonstrated knowledge of the national legal and institutional framework related to quality, standardization and foreign trade.

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” revised in September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours 0800 to 1600 hours.
