MINISTÈRE DE L’AMÉNAGEMENT DU TERRITOIRE

ET DES SERVICES FONCIERS

---------------------

PROJET DE DÉVELOPPEMENT URBAIN INTÉGRÉ ET RÉSILIENT POUR L’EMPLOI (PRODUIRE)

---------------------

 

SOLLICITATION DE MANIFESTATION D’INTÉRÊT POUR LE RECRUTEMENT DE DEUX COMPTABLES  DE L'UNITE DE GESTION D'ANTANANARIVO DU PROJET DE DEVELOPPEMENT URBAIN INTEGRE ET RESILIENT POUR L’EMPLOI (PRODUIRE)

Pays : MADAGASCAR

AMI N : 09-2026/MATSF/PRODUIRE

Projet : Projet de Développement Urbain Intégré ET RESILIENT POUR L’EMPLOI

Crédit : IDA 8089 MG

Date de lancement : 5 octobre 2026

1. Le Gouvernement de la République de Madagascar a reçu un financement de 225 millions USD de l’Association Internationale de Développement (IDA) au profit du Projet de Développement Urbain Intégré et Résilient pour l’Emploi (PRODUIRE) et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie de ce crédit pour financer le contrat de services de deux (02) comptables de l’Unité de Gestion de Projet à Antananarivo. 

L’Objectif de Développement du Projet (ODP) est de renforcer la résilience climatique des communautés urbaines, d'améliorer l'administration foncière et de soutenir l'emploi dans certaines villes.

2. Les services des consultants  consistent à assurer l’exécution correcte, complète et diligente des travaux comptables quotidiens du Projet, y compris l’enregistrement des opérations, la préparation des dossiers de dépenses et de paiement, la tenue des livres de caisse et de banque, ainsi que le classement et l’archivage des pièces justificatives..

3. Le mandat fera l’objet d’un contrat de soixante (60) mois assorti d’une tranche ferme de douze (12) mois et de quatre (04) tranches conditionnelles de douze (12) mois dont la condition d’affermissement sera l’évaluation positive de la performance du consultant. Une période d’essai de six (06) mois est prévue dans la tranche ferme. Le lieu de travail est au siège du projet à Antananarivo.

4. Le Comptable doit :

  • être titulaire d’un diplôme de niveau Licence en comptabilité, finance, gestion ou discipline équivalente ;
  • disposer d’une expérience professionnelle pertinente d’au moins trois (03) années en comptabilité ou gestion financière au cours des cinq (05) dernières années;
  • une expérience au sein d’un projet financé par des partenaires techniques et financiers internationaux constitue un atout ;
  • avoir une bonne connaissance des principes comptables, de la gestion des pièces justificatives et des opérations de caisse et de banque
  • maîtriser les logiciels comptables ainsi que les outils bureautiques, notamment les tableurs
  • faire preuve de rigueur, d’intégrité, d’organisation, de discrétion et de capacité à travailler dans le respect des délais;
  • avoir une bonne maîtrise du français écrit et oral ; la connaissance de l’anglais constitue un atout
  • être disponible pour des déplacements ponctuels dans les zones d’intervention du Projet, si necessaire.

 

5. De plus amples informations peuvent être obtenues à l’adresse ci-dessous de 08 heures à 16 heures pendant les jours ouvrables.

6. Le MATSF invite les consultants individuels qualifiés à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les services décrits ci-dessus. Les consultants intéressés doivent fournir les informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications requises et une expérience pertinente pour l’exécution des services. Son dossier de candidature comprendra entre autres :

a. Lettre de motivation

b. Curriculum vitae avec coordonnées (adresse, téléphone, e-mail)

c. Copie des diplômes, attestation de formations

d. Certificat/ attestation de prestations similaires

e.Trois références professionnelles

En cas d’envoi de manifestation par e-mail, le Candidat fournira toutes les pièces en un seul fichier PDF.

7. Il est porté à l’attention des Consultants que les dispositions des paragraphes 3.16 et 3.17 du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement (FPI) » septième édition septembre 2025, relatives aux règles de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflits d’intérêts sont applicables.

8. Un consultant sera sélectionné selon la méthode Sélection de Consultant Individuel telle que décrite dans le Règlement. Les candidats présélectionnés à l’issue de l’examen des dossiers seront convoqués à un entretien.

9. Les consultants Individuels intéressés sont invités à demander par courriel la version électronique des termes de référence de la mission à l’adresse ci-dessous. Le nom, le contact ainsi que l’adresse physique et électronique du consultant individuel devront être spécifiés dans la demande.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST

(Consulting Services – Individual Selection)

Finance Officer (Accountant) to support the Program Management Unit (PMU) at the Ethiopia Digital ID for Inclusion and Services Project

Country

Ethiopia

Project

Ethiopia Digital ID for Inclusion and Services Project

Project ID

P179040

Assignment Title

Finance Officer (Accountant)

Reference No.

ET-NIDP-576621-CS-INDV

The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia, Ministry of Finance (MoF), has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Ethiopia Digital ID for Inclusion and Services Project. The National ID Program (NIDP), the ultimate project implementer, intends to apply part of the proceeds for selecting an individual consultant.

The National ID Program is looking for a Finance Officer (Accountant) to support the Program Management Unit (PMU) in the financial management and accounting of the Project. The position will support the PMU in ensuring that project funds are used for their intended purposes with due attention to economy, efficiency, effectiveness, transparency, and accountability, and in compliance with Government of Ethiopia requirements, the Financing Agreement, Project Implementation Manual (PIM), and World Bank financial management and disbursement requirements.

Key Responsibilities

  • Execute the overall financial management activities for the Project consistent with applicable agreements, manuals, and project documents.
  • Work closely with the Financial Management Specialist on budgeting, accounting, internal controls, fund flows, financial reporting, and audit matters.
  • Support annual planning and budgeting and the process of incorporating the project budget into the Government budget.
  • Maintain budget discipline and report budget variances and the reasons for such variances to the Financial Management Specialist.
  • Support the preparation and submission of budgets and ensure that relevant development-partner requirements are appropriately captured.
  • Implement and maintain adequate financial management systems and procedures and ensure that books of accounts and accounting records are complete, current, and properly documented.
  • Support periodic financial reporting for development partners and the Government in accordance with applicable reporting requirements and formats.
  • Prepare quarterly Interim Financial Reports (IFRs) and annual project financial statements in accordance with World Bank and Government requirements and ensure timely submission.
  • Participate in mitigating financial risks and implement applicable development-partner disbursement procedures in accordance with the financing agreements and requirements.
  • Collect bank advice and bank statements and prepare timely bank reconciliations.
  • Support preparation and submission of Withdrawal Applications, monitor Designated Account balances, and reconcile project expenditures with Client Connection records and disbursement reports.
  • Apply internal controls for petty cash and bank management and participate in safeguarding project assets, fixed assets, and inventories.
  • Process monthly employee salary payments and support management of income tax and pension contributions.
  • Ensure timely settlement of advances, prepayments, and payables and timely reporting to tax authorities and other relevant government organizations.
  • Verify the completeness, accuracy, and adequacy of supporting documents before processing payments and ensure compliance with applicable procedures, financing agreements, and project manuals.
  • Support internal and external audits, ensure documents are available to auditors, and coordinate implementation of audit recommendations through an appropriate tracking mechanism.
  • Carry out other related duties as assigned by NIDP/PMU.

Minimum Qualifications and Experience

  • Minimum of a Bachelor’s Degree in Finance, Accounting, or a related field; a Master’s Degree is preferred.
  • At least four (4) years of relevant professional experience for Bachelor’s Degree holders, or at least two (2) years for Master’s Degree holders, with progressively responsible experience in a major company, government institution, or non-government organization.
  • At least three (3) years of prior experience in implementing projects/programs or in project financial management.
  • Relevant experience in Government of Ethiopia or donor-financed projects is required; experience in a World Bank-financed project is an advantage.
  • Ability to use accounting and financial management software, including IFMIS, Peachtree/accounting software, spreadsheets, and databases.
  • Knowledge and practical experience with World Bank financial management, disbursement, reporting, and Client Connection procedures is an advantage.
  • Excellent communication and reporting skills, including the ability to present financial information and analysis to management.
  • Fluency in English and Amharic.
  • High level of personal integrity and a transparent, systematic, and accountable working style.
  • Ability to work under pressure, meet deadlines, and undertake additional assignments as required by NIDP/PMU.

Duration and Location

The consultant will be engaged on a full-time basis for an initial period of twelve (12) months, with the possibility of extension subject to satisfactory performance and availability of budget. The position will be based in Addis Ababa.

Selection Method

The selection method is based on paragraphs 7.36 and 7.37 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations. The attention of interested individuals is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers,” July 2016, as revised, including February 2025, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

An individual will be selected in accordance with the Selection of Individual Consultant (Section V) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The Expression of Interest should include a CV, formal application/cover letter, and documentary evidence supporting the stated qualifications and experience, including descriptions of relevant assignments and experience in similar conditions.

Dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre du Projet d’Appui à l’Amélioration des Compétences et de l’Employabilité des Femmes et des Jeunes (PACEJ), le Gouvernement de la République du Burundi a obtenu un financement de l’Association Internationale de Développement (IDA). Les Termes de Référence (TDR) détaillés de la mission peuvent être obtenus à l’adresse ci-dessous :

pacej@pacej.bi, avec copie à nirsanctus@gmail.com, muhindo.kiana@pacej.bi, et hatungimanapatrick@gmail.com en envoyant une demande écrite précisant le numéro et l'intitulé du marché (AMI n° BI-PACEJ-571364-CS-INDV).

Le PACEJ invite par la présente les consultants éligibles (« Consultants ») à manifester leur intérêt pour la prestation des services décrits ci-dessus. Les Consultants intéressés doivent fournir les informations démontrant qu'ils possèdent les qualifications requises et l'expérience pertinente pour exécuter la mission.

 

QUALIFICATION DU CONSULTANT

Pour assurer cette mission le consultant devra avoir les qualifications suivantes :

  1. Être titulaire d’un diplôme de niveau minimum BAC+4 en ingénierie de la formation, sciences de l’éducation, économie, gestion, ressources humaines, ou tout autre diplôme équivalent ;
  2. Avoir au moins dix (10) ans d’expérience professionnelle dans le domaine de la formation professionnelle et de la formation par apprentissage.
  3. Avoir au moins une expérience avérée en tant que consultant ou responsable au sein d’une structure de mise en œuvre dans la gestion de projets d’apprentissage dual dans des pays en développement selon un modèle analogue à celui exécuté par le PACEJ ;
  4. Avoir une parfaite maîtrise de la langue française (écrit et oral) ;
  5. Avoir une bonne maîtrise de l’outil informatique, des logiciels bureautiques courants (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) et de l’internet ;
  6. Avoir une bonne aptitude à travailler en équipe ;
  7. Avoir un esprit d’initiative et le sens de l’anticipation.

L'attention des Consultants intéressés est attirée sur la Section III, paragraphes 3.14, 3.16 et 3.17 du Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement (FPI) de la Banque mondiale (édition, novembre 2020), relatif aux règles de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflit d'intérêts.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST
(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

 

Country: Republic of Uzbekistan
Credit No.: IDA 7787-UZ
Project: Geospatial Infrastructure for Sustainable Territorial Development Project (GISTDP)
Assignment Title: Audit of the Project Financial Statements
Reference No.: GISTDP/C4/LCS/01

 

1. Background

The Republic of Uzbekistan has received financing from the International Development Association (IDA) toward the cost of the Geospatial Infrastructure for Sustainable Territorial Development Project (GISTDP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds to consulting services for the audit of the Project Financial Statements.

The Project is implemented by the Cadastre Agency under the National Committee for Sustainable Development of Urbanization and Housing Market of the Republic of Uzbekistan (“the Client”). Its objective is to improve the availability and accessibility of geospatial data in Uzbekistan through the development of the National Spatial Data Infrastructure, modernization of surveying and mapping infrastructure, enhancement of geospatial information systems, and institutional capacity building.

2. Objective and Duration of the Assignment

The objective of the assignment is to enable an independent auditor to express a professional opinion on the Project Financial Statements, including the Project’s financial position and its income and expenditure for the respective reporting periods, in accordance with the Financing Agreement and the Terms of Reference.

The assignment covers the following five reporting periods:

No.

Reporting period

Deadline for submission of the Final Audit Report and Management Letter to the World Bank

1

September 23, 2025 (effectiveness date) to December 31, 2026

30 June 2027

2

Fiscal year ending December 31, 2027

30 June 2028

3

Fiscal year ending December 31, 2028

30 June 2029

4

Fiscal year ending December 31, 2029

30 June 2030

5

January 1, 2030 to October 31, 2030 (application deadline date)

December 31, 2030, or another date agreed between the Recipient and the World Bank

 

The services shall be performed periodically for the respective reporting periods and shall continue through completion of the final audit and submission of the required deliverables.

3. Scope of Services

The audits shall be conducted in accordance with International Standards on Auditing (ISA). The consulting services include, but are not limited to:

- Auditing the Project Financial Statements and expressing an independent audit opinion for each reporting period;

- Reviewing whether the financial statements have been prepared in accordance with the financial reporting framework specified in the Terms of Reference;

- Examining the use of IDA financing and Government counterpart funds for compliance with the Financing Agreement and the purposes for which the funds were provided;

- Reviewing compliance of project procurement with the applicable provisions of the Financing Agreement and World Bank procurement requirements;

- Reviewing accounting records, supporting documentation and internal controls, including relevant records maintained in the 1C accounting system and FundsChain;

- Auditing Statements of Expenditure and Interim Unaudited Financial Reports submitted in support of withdrawal applications, including the eligibility of reported expenditures and reconciliation with the underlying accounting records;

- Reviewing the operation and reconciliation of the Project’s Designated Accounts;

- Verifying project assets and inventory, as required by the Terms of Reference;

- Preparing a Management Letter identifying internal control deficiencies, instances of noncompliance, ineligible expenditures and other significant findings, together with recommendations and management responses; and

- Following up on the implementation of recommendations from previous audit periods.

For each reporting period, the Draft Audit Report and Draft Management Letter shall be submitted within two weeks from notification of commencement of the respective audit. The Final Audit Report and Management Letter shall be submitted within two weeks from approval of the Draft Audit Report, subject to the reporting deadlines specified above.

All reports shall be prepared in English, Uzbek and Russian and submitted in the number of copies specified in the Terms of Reference.

The detailed Terms of Reference may be obtained from the Client at the address indicated below.

 

4. Invitation and Eligibility of Audit Firms

The Client now invites eligible audit firms (“Consultants”) to express their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants shall provide information demonstrating their relevant qualifications, experience, and technical and managerial capacity to undertake the assignment.

The auditor shall be selected from the six (6) audit firms included in the applicable World Bank – ECA – List of Eligible Audit Firms for Uzbekistan. Inclusion in that list is a mandatory requirement for consideration under this assignment. Interested Consultants shall provide evidence of their inclusion, identifying the firm’s exact legal name and the applicable list entry.

Consultants wishing to express interest as a joint venture shall identify the proposed association and its members in their Expression of Interest. Each member shall satisfy the applicable audit-firm eligibility requirement. All joint venture members shall be jointly and severally liable for performance of the entire Contract, if awarded.

Participation by sub-consultants is not permitted. Any proposed joint venture shall be identified at the Expression of Interest stage; shortlisted Consultants will not be permitted to form new associations with other shortlisted or non-shortlisted firms at the proposal stage.

O Governo de São Tomé e Príncipe (GoSTP) recebeu uma subvenção do Donativo da Associação Internacional para o Desenvolvimento (IDA) para cobrir o custo do Projeto de Oportunidades de Emprego para Jovens de São Tomé e Príncipe (POEJ) e pretende aplicar uma parte dessa subvenção em serviços de consultoria para Contratação de um(a) Consultor(a) Assistente de Tecnologia de Informação e Dados para apoiar a Unidade de Implementação do Projeto. 

 

Os objetivos gerais desta consultoria são:

notices.description:
Lao People's Democratic Republic

                                    Peace, Independent Democracy, Unity, Prosperity

                                     Job Title:                   

Department:

Impact Assessment International Consultant

(Part-time, Lump Sum Contract)

(01 Position)

Ministry of Education and Sports

Department Technical and Vocational Education and Training (DTVET)

Lao PDR: Priority Skills for Growth Project (Lao-PSG)

Project ID: P172774 Project Coordinator Unit (PCU-DTVET)

Location:

            Commence date

Vientiane Capital

15 January 2027

JOB PURPOSE

The Lao People's Democratic Republic (Lao PDR) faces a significant skills gap, particularly in key economic sectors such as agriculture, logistics, and information and communication technology (ICT). At the same time, labor market intermediation services remain underdeveloped, making it difficult for job seekers, even those with relevant skills, to find suitable employment. Women, migrants, and disadvantaged populations face even greater challenges in accessing opportunities for skills development and employment. For Lao PDR to realize its economic growth potential and ensure inclusive development, strategic investments in skills supply and employment services are critical.

Recognizing these challenges, the World Bank has been supporting the Government of Lao PDR through technical assistance and financial loan support to implement the Priority Skills for Growth Project from July 2022 to June 2027. This project is led by the Ministry of Education and Sports (MOES) and the Ministry of Labor and Social Welfare (MOLSW) and aims to enhance access, quality, and relevance of skills development and employment services for youth and other vulnerable groups in the three priority sectors: agriculture, logistics, and ICT. Over five years, the project aims to catalyze system-level reforms, ensuring that skills training programs are more aligned with labor market needs.

As part of evidence-based reporting, Lao-PSG will send consultants to assess the impact of the Priority Skills for Growth Project (Lao-PSG). The Project Impact Assessment will cover the assessment of Lao-PSG inputs and deliverables based on the Project Design Monitoring Framework (DMF), specifically but not limited to the following:

The study will be carried out on behalf of the Ministry of Education and Sports' Department of Technical Vocational Education and Training (DTVET) and the Ministry of Labor and Social Welfare. The evaluation results will be used in evidence-based reporting to influence the technical and vocational education, job centers, and skill development centers (SDCs) subsector, as well as future projects.

The consultant will conduct a project impact assessment for Loan No. Credit No. 7042-LA, Lao PSG. Based on the PIM, including the DMF, Covenants/Safeguards, and others, the impact assessment will provide (i) an overall assessment of project results by outputs focused on achievement, constraints including capacity, financial support, ownership and commitment at all levels, and legal framework or policy; (ii) analysis of findings and recommendations; and (iii) detailed information and analysis in terms of capacity, financing, and ownership. The findings and recommendations can be used and mentioned in the project's final report. It will examine and revise the DMF, ESF, and other covenants.

To support this endeavor, the project is looking to an international consultant to conduct a joint impact evaluation of the Lao-PSG and make strategic recommendations to increase its role in skills development and workforce planning. The nation consultant will work closely with both ministries, MOES and MoLSW.

SCOPE OF WORK

Scope of Work

At the overall project level, covering the components and activities implemented by both MOES and MOLSW, the study will address the following objectives:

  1. Assess implementation progress and the delivery of project activities, outputs, and outcomes across the components implemented by MOES and MOLSW, including achievement of targets under the Results Monitoring Framework (RMF).
  2. Assess the project’s relevance and alignment with government priorities, labour market needs, and the needs of target beneficiaries.
  3. Assess the project’s effectiveness and the positive and negative effects of its interventions on access to, quality of, and relevance of skills development, technical and vocational education and training, employment services, and self-employment support.
  4. Assess the project’s efficiency, including the use of financial, human, and institutional resources, implementation arrangements, coordination between the two ministries, monitoring mechanisms, and delivery timelines.
  5. Assess institutional capacity development, ownership, and commitment at central and subnational levels across MOES and MOLSW, including supported institutions and service providers.
  6. Assess the sustainability of project results, systems, services, and institutional capacities beyond project completion, and identify associated risks and practical mitigation measures.
  7. Identify cross-cutting and component-specific implementation gaps, lessons learned, and good practices, and recommend practical measures for the remaining implementation period and future skills development and employment projects.
  8. Provide clear quantitative and qualitative evidence to substantiate all assessment findings and ratings, with analysis disaggregated by ministry, component, institution, location, and beneficiary group where relevant.
  9. .

Detailed Tasks and/or Expected Output

The international consultant will work with the national consultant in carrying out the following project impact assessment stages and will help ensure timely completion of the report. The consultant will also both with PMUs, and relevant stakeholders under MOES and MOLSW to complete following project impact assessment stages and ensure the timely submission of all required report.

First Stage Implementation

  1. Develop a sound understanding of the project.
  2. Identify key project activities, outputs, and outcomes.
  3. Identify the most critical indicators of progress and results.
  4. Review the project’s RMF and apply it to the assessment.

 

Second Stage Implementation

  1. Prepare survey tools and instruments
  2. Pilot and refine the tools and instruments

Third Stage Implementation

  1. Review secondary data.

2. Collect field data

Fourth Stage Implementation

  1.  Analyze the data and prepare the report.
  2. Validate the report.

Finalize and complete the reportData will be gathered from; (i) fieldwork supported by the national consultant; (ii) secondary sources; (iii) meetings with key stakeholders, and beneficiaries across the MOES-; MOLSW-implemented components; (iv) relevant project and government information systems, including the TVET Education Management Information System (TVET-MIS) and Labour Market Information System (, LMIS);; and (v) other relevant sources. Both  PMUs  will provide available data, facilitate access to relevant institutions and stakeholders, and support the consultants’ fieldwork.

The consultants may use field survey questionnaires and group discussions to generate quantitative and qualitative evidence for the assessment and analysis.

The study will be completed within five months. The first three months will be devoted to field visits and data collection, and the remaining two months to data consolidation, analysis, reporting, and report validation.

APPEL A CANDIDATURES

UN(E) RESPONSABLE EN GESTION DES RISQUES ENVIRONNEMENTAUX DU PROJET RIZ PLUS

Référence : CON-065/MG-RIZPLUS/2026

Date de lancement : 14 octobre 2026

1. Le Gouvernement de la République de Madagascar a reçu un financement de la Banque mondiale pour financer la mise en œuvre du Projet de Productivité et de Résilience des Moyens de Subsistance Ruraux (RIZPLUS), et a l'intention d’utiliser une partie de ce financement pour effectuer les paiements au titre du contrat de consultant individuel objet du présent appel à candidatures.

Ce contrat sera financé conjointement par l’Agence Française de Développement (AFD). La passation du Marché sera conforme aux règles de passation des marchés de la Banque mondiale.

2. Sous la supervision directe du Coordonnateur du Projet, le/la Responsable en Gestion des Risques Environnementaux a pour mission principale d'assurer l'intégration effective de la gestion des risques et impacts environnementaux dans la préparation, la passation des marchés, la mise en œuvre et le suivi des activités et investissements du Projet Riz Plus.

Le lieu d’affectation est à Antananarivo, Madagascar (siège de l'UGP RIZPLUS). La durée du contrat est fixée jusqu’au 29 décembre 2028, sous réserve d’une évaluation annuelle satisfaisante des performances du consultant.

3. Les Termes de Référence détaillés pour la mission peuvent être obtenus à l’adresse électronique indiquée ci-dessous. Les candidats devront clairement préciser la référence de l’Appel à candidatures avec leurs coordonnées dans leur demande.

4. L’Unité de Gestion du Projet RIZPLUS invite les candidat(e)s intéressé(e)s à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les services cidessus. Un Consultant sera sélectionné conformément à la méthode de sélection des Consultants Individuels prévues dans le « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement (FPI) pour les fournitures, travaux, services autres que les services de consultants » 7ème édition, Septembre 2025. Les candidats les mieux classés à l’issue de l’évaluation des dossiers seront invités à un entretien.

5. Le consultant recherché doit répondre aux qualifications minimales suivantes :

  • Être titulaire au minimum d'un diplôme de niveau Bac+4 en agronomie, sciences environnementales, génie de l'environnement, gestion des ressources naturelles, écologie ou toute autre discipline pertinente en rapport avec la gestion des risques environnementaux ;
  • Justifier d'au moins dix (10) années d'expérience professionnelle pertinente dans la gestion des risques environnementaux, l'évaluation environnementale ou la gestion des impacts environnementaux dans le cadre de projets de développement ou au sein d'institutions ou organisations pertinentes ;
  • Justifier d'au moins deux (02) expériences pertinentes et réussies au cours des dix (10) dernières années dans le domaine de la gestion des risques environnementaux ou de la gestion environnementale de projets
  • Disposer d'une expérience pratique dans l'identification, l'évaluation et le suivi des risques et impacts environnementaux ;
  • Justifier d'une expérience dans la préparation, la revue ou le suivi de la mise en œuvre d'instruments environnementaux, notamment les EIES, PGES, plans ou mesures de gestion environnementale ;
  • Avoir une bonne connaissance du cadre juridique et réglementaire malagasy applicable à la protection de l'environnement et à l'évaluation environnementale ;
  • Avoir une expérience pertinente dans le suivi environnemental d'activités de développement, d'infrastructures, d'agriculture, de gestion des ressources naturelles ou de secteurs similaires ;
  • Avoir de bonnes capacités d'analyse, de synthèse et de rédaction ;
  • Maîtriser les outils informatiques courants, notamment les logiciels de traitement de texte, de tableur, de présentation, de messagerie électronique et les outils de cartographie ;
  • Avoir une excellente capacité de communication en français et en malagasy ;
  • Être disponible pour effectuer des déplacements fréquents, y compris dans les zones rurales ou reculées.

Seront considérés comme des atouts :

  • Une expérience au sein d'un projet financé par la Banque mondiale ;
  • Une expérience pratique de l'application du Cadre Environnemental et Social de la Banque mondiale, des Normes Environnementales et Sociales pertinentes et des Directives EHS applicables ;
  • Une connaissance du contexte de développement rural et des enjeux environnementaux dans les zones d'intervention du Projet ;
  • La connaissance des pratiques culturelles et des dialectes des régions d'Alaotra Mangoro et de Sofia ;
  • La maîtrise de l'anglais.

6. Les candidat(e)s intéressé(e)s doivent envoyer exclusivement par mail leur dossier de candidature, sous format PDF, composé d’une lettre de motivation, d’un CV détaillé avec références professionnelles, les copies certifiées conformes des diplômes ainsi que les attestations de travail au plus tard le 28 octobre 2026 à minuit à l’adresse : cn.rizplus@gmail.com ; copie à : rizplus-pm@googlegroups.com .

7. L’objet du mail d’envoi doit porter obligatoirement la mention suivante « CON-065/MG-RIZPLUS/2026 : RESPONSABLE EN GESTION DES RISQUES ENVIRONNEMENTAUX ».

 

Antananarivo, le 14 octobre 2026

L’Unité de Gestion du Projet RIZPLUS

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

FEDERAL DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF ETHIOPIA

LOWLANDS LIVELIHOOD RESILIENCE PROJECT – PHASE II (LLRP-II)

Credit No.: 7519-ET

Assignment Title: Consultancy Services for Route Selection and Survey, Feasibility Study, Detailed Engineering Design, ESIA and Tender Document Preparation of Two (2) Gravel Roads: Gereni – Dubti Woreda and Abida – Gelealu Woreda Gravel Road Projects, Afar Region

Reference No.: ET-AFR-RPCU-569662-CS-QCBS

The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Lowlands Livelihood Resilience Project – Phase II (LLRP-II), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include route selection and survey, feasibility study, detailed engineering design, Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) and preparation of tender documents for two (2) gravel roads in Afar Region: (i) Gereni – Dubti Woreda Gravel Road, approximately 85 km, in Zones 01 and 06; and (ii) Abida – Gelealu Woreda Gravel Road, approximately 30 km, in Zone 03.

The Services will be carried out in two phases, following the latest Ethiopian Roads Administration (ERA) design manuals and quality manual, the LLRP-II environmental and social instruments and the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF):

 

(a)  Phase I – Route Selection and Survey, and Feasibility Study: identification and multi-criteria comparison of at least three alternative routes; site reconnaissance and investigation; stakeholder consultation; traffic counts and axle load surveys; full topographic survey and Digital Terrain Model; preliminary design; ESIA of the selected route; preliminary cost estimates; economic evaluation; and climate and natural hazard vulnerability assessment.

(b) Phase II – Detailed Engineering Design, ESIA and Preparation of Bidding Documents: materials and site investigation; geometric, drainage, pavement, geotechnical and bridge/structural design, including an independent bridge design check; road safety design and audit; utilities and private accesses; estimate of the construction contract period; final ESIA and Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP); and preparation of bidding documents based on the World Bank Standard Procurement Documents, including technical specifications, drawings, bills of quantities and the Engineer’s cost estimate.

The implementation period is three (3) months from the date of commencement, and the assignment is expected to start in December 2026.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained at the address given below.

The Afar National Regional State, Office of the President, Lowlands Livelihood Resilience Project (LLRP-II) Regional Project Coordination Unit now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

(a)  Core business and years in business: the firm’s core business shall be in road/highway engineering consultancy services. Provide the company profile, certificate of registration and number of years in business.

(b) General experience: experience in civil engineering consultancy services (studies, design and/or construction supervision of roads, bridges or other civil infrastructure) during the last ten (10) years.

(c)  Specific experience: experience in assignments of similar nature and complexity, i.e. feasibility studies and detailed engineering design of roads (new construction, rehabilitation or upgrading, including gravel/low-volume roads), covering route selection, topographic surveys, drainage and bridge structures, ESIA and preparation of bidding documents, preferably in arid, semi-arid or lowland areas and under projects financed by the World Bank or other international development partners. For each assignment, indicate the client, location, road length, contract value, duration, scope of services and the firm’s role, supported by contract or completion certificates.

 

(d) Technical and managerial capability of the firm: organizational structure, survey equipment (e.g. GPS and total stations), access to soil and materials testing laboratories, road design and economic evaluation software, quality assurance systems, and capacity to mobilize multidisciplinary field teams to remote areas of Afar Region.

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

FEDERAL DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF ETHIOPIA

LOWLANDS LIVELIHOOD RESILIENCE PROJECT – PHASE II (LLRP-II)

 

Credit No.: 7519-ET

 

Assignment Title: Consultancy Services for Hydrogeological and Geophysical Investigation for Groundwater Development in Seven Woredas (Kori, Gereni, Elidaar, Erebti, Dalol, Yalo and Telalak) of Afar Region

 

Reference No.: ET-AFR-RPCU-569659-CS-QCBS

 

The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Lowlands Livelihood Resilience Project – Phase II (LLRP-II), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

 

The consulting services (“the Services”) include hydrogeological and geophysical investigations to identify, assess and recommend technically feasible, sustainable, climate-resilient, environmentally sound and socially acceptable groundwater drilling sites for potable water supply and irrigation development at seven (7) locations in Afar Region, one in each of the following woredas (kebeles): Kori (Musle), Gereni (Gewili) and Elidaar (Dishoto) in Zone One; Erebti (Fiayito) and Dalol (Deriru) in Zone Two; Yalo (Gubidora) in Zone Four; and Telalak (Wayiduleli) in Zone Five.

 

The Services comprise: review of existing information and preparation of an Inception Report; reconnaissance survey, baseline assessment and stakeholder consultation with pastoral and agro-pastoral communities, women and vulnerable groups; hydrogeological mapping; geophysical surveys and their interpretation; water sampling and laboratory analysis for drinking and irrigation suitability; environmental and social screening and assessment in accordance with the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF), including preparation of Environmental and Social Management Plans (ESMPs); groundwater development planning; establishment of a GIS database and maps; capacity building of Client staff; estimation of the drilling contract period; and preparation of preliminary engineering recommendations, draft bidding documents (technical specifications, drawings and bills of quantities) and the Engineer’s cost estimate for the subsequent borehole drilling works.

 

The implementation period is three (3) calendar months from the date of commencement, and the assignment is expected to start in December 2026.

 

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained at the address given below.

 

The Afar National Regional State, Office of the President, Lowlands Livelihood Resilience Project (LLRP-II) Regional Project Coordination Unit now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

 

(a)  Core business and years in business: the firm’s core business shall be in groundwater/hydrogeological investigation and water resources consultancy services. Provide the company profile, certificate of registration and number of years in business.

 

(b) General experience: experience in consultancy services for water supply, irrigation and/or water resources development during the last ten (10) years.

The Government of The Federated States of Micronesia (FSM) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Strengthening Public Financial Management II (PFM II) Project (P181237) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

 

The consulting services (“the Services”) involve providing full-time technical advisory and capacity-building support under Component 2 – Expand Core Financial Management Information System (FMIS), Subcomponent 2.1 – Continued Rollout of Core Public Finance System of the PFM II Project.

 

The Finance Consultant for Chuuk State will support the Chuuk State Finance Department in the continued rollout, operationalization, and stabilization of the FreeBalance FMIS. The assignment will focus on validating financial transactions and data migrated from FundWare to FreeBalance, reconciling FY26 opening balances, strengthening accounting and financial reporting processes, improving internal controls related to FMIS operations, and building the capacity of State Finance staff to use the system effectively and sustainably.

 

The key responsibilities will include, but not be limited to:

  • Reviewing and validating financial transactions, account balances, and data migrated from FundWare to FreeBalance, including the reconciliation and validation of FY26 opening balances.
  • Supporting FreeBalance stabilization by identifying, documenting, prioritizing, escalating, and following up on accounting, data migration, transaction-processing, reporting, and system-related issues.
  • Supporting monthly financial reporting, bank reconciliations, accounting entries, and month-end and year-end accounting processes in accordance with applicable GASB, GAAP, and FSM accounting requirements.
  • Reviewing and strengthening internal controls, accounting procedures, and compliance-monitoring practices relevant to FMIS operations.
  • Providing hands-on coaching and on-the-job training to Chuuk State Finance staff in government accounting, FreeBalance operations, reconciliations, financial reporting, data validation, and issue resolution.
  • Coordinating with the FSM Department of Finance and Administration at the National Government level, the PFM II Project Management Unit, the FMIS Adviser, ICT personnel, and FreeBalance specialists to resolve accounting and system issues and support sustainable FMIS operations.

 

The assignment will be based in Weno, Chuuk State, Federated States of Micronesia, with coordination with the FSM Department of Finance and Administration at the National Government level. The consultancy is expected to be full-time for twelve (12) months, with an anticipated start date as soon as possible, subject to completion of the selection and contracting process.

 

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the Department of Finance and Administration website: https://dofa.gov.fm, as part of this REOI, or can be obtained at the address given below.

 

The Department of Finance and Administration now invites eligible individuals (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. Consultants should submit a Curriculum Vitae (CV) describing their qualifications, professional experience, experience in similar assignments and relevant experience in similar institutional or country contexts together with a cover letter outlining their interest in the assignment and suitability for the position.

 

The criteria for selecting the Consultant are:

Mandatory Requirements:

The Consultant shall possess:

  1. Education: A Master's degree in Accounting. Candidates holding a CPA qualification together with a degree in Finance, Information Systems, Public Administration, or an equivalent related field are also encouraged to apply.
  2. Professional Experience: At least ten (10) years of progressive experience in public sector accounting, financial management, and Public Financial Management (PFM) reforms.
  3. Technical Expertise: Demonstrated expertise in applying Governmental Accounting Standards Board (GASB) pronouncements and Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP), extensive experience with FMIS implementation, operationalization, stabilization, transaction processing, financial reporting, reconciliation and/or data migration, and demonstrated ability to identify, analyze, and resolve accounting, financial data, and system-related issues in an FMIS environment.

Desirable:

  1. Software Proficiency: Experience with FundWare and/or FreeBalance, particularly in FMIS stabilization, troubleshooting, issue escalation, and coordination with system vendors and national-level technical teams.
  2. Capacity Building and Communication: Proven ability to train and mentor government staff in financial reporting, PFM principles, and new software systems, supported by excellent analytical, communication, and report-writing skills.
  3. Governmental Accounting Knowledge: Thorough knowledge of governmental fund financial statements and government-wide financial reporting, including the Statement of Net Position, the three categories of Net Position, program and general revenues, Transfers and Internal Balances, the five categories of Fund Balance, and the distinction between Revenues and Other Financing Sources and Expenditures and Other Financing Uses.
  4. Geographic Experience: Prior experience working with island nations or small governments.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, Seventh Edition, September 2025 (“the Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Le Gouvernement de la République de Madagascar a reçu un financement de la Banque mondiale pour financer la mise en œuvre du Projet de Productivité et de Résilience des Moyens de Subsistance Ruraux (RIZPLUS), et a l'intention d’utiliser une partie de ce financement pour effectuer les paiements au titre du contrat de consultant individuel objet du présent appel à candidatures.

Ce contrat sera financé conjointement par l’Agence Française de Développement (AFD). La passation du Marché sera conforme aux règles de passation des marchés de la Banque mondiale.

2. Sous la supervision hiérarchique du Coordonnateur Régional et la supervision fonctionnelle du Responsable Administratif et Financier (RAF) de l'UGP nationale, le RAFR assure la gestion administrative, budgétaire, comptable et financière de l'UGPR. Il veille à une utilisation efficiente et conforme des ressources allouées par l'IDA et l'AFD, dans le respect de l'Accord de financement, de la Convention de crédit AFD, de la Lettre de décaissement et d'information financière, et du Manuel de procédures administratives, financières et comptables du Projet.

Un Consultant sera sélectionné conformément à la méthode de sélection des Consultants Individuels prévue dans le « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement (FPI) pour les fournitures, travaux, services autres que les services de consultants » 7ème édition, Septembre 2025. Les candidats les mieux classés à l’issue de l’évaluation des dossiers seront invités à un entretien.

5. Le consultant recherché doit répondre aux qualifications minimales suivantes :

  • Être titulaire d'un diplôme de Master (niveau Bac+5) au minimum en finances et comptabilité ou en gestion, option finances et comptabilité ;
  • Justifier d'au moins sept (7) années d'expériences professionnelles réussies en administration et finances dont au moins cinq (5) années réussies dans un poste similaire, sur les dix (10) dernières années, au sein de projets financés par des bailleurs de fonds internationaux ou d'organisations de grande envergure ;
  • Maîtrise des logiciels comptables et de gestion financière de projet ;
  • Maîtrise de la comptabilité générale et analytique de projet, du PCG 2005, ainsi que de la législation fiscale et sociale malagasy ;
  • Maîtrise des outils informatiques usuels, notamment des tableurs, pour le suivi des réalisations et des tableaux de bord ;
  • Capacités rédactionnelles et facilité de communication ;
  • Maîtrise du français et du malagasy.

Seront considérés comme des atouts :

  • La connaissance de l'anglais ;
  • Expérience réussie dans un projet financé par la Banque mondiale ;
  • Expérience en gestion financière au sein d'une unité régionale ou décentralisée de projet ;
  • Expérience professionnelle dans la région Alaotra Mangoro.

6. Les candidat(e)s intéressé(e)s doivent envoyer exclusivement par mail, sous format PDF, leur dossier de candidature, comprenant une lettre de motivation, un CV détaillé avec références professionnelles, des copies certifiées conformes des diplômes ainsi que les attestations de travail au plus tard le 28 octobre 2026 à minuit à l’adresse : cn.rizplus@gmail.com ; copie à : rizplus-pm@googlegroups.com .

7. L’objet du mail d’envoi doit porter obligatoirement la mention suivante « CON-078/MG-RIZPLUS/2026 : RESPONSABLE ADMINISTRATIF ET FINANCIER REGIONAL ».

 

Antananarivo, le 14 octobre 2026

The Government of Albania has received a loan in the amount of 51.6 million EUR financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Building Resilient Bridges Project (BRBP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for individual consulting services under this Request for Expressions of Interest (REoI).  

The Albanian Road Authority (ARA), as the implementing agency of the Project, now invites eligible individual consultants to indicate their interest in providing the services described below.

The consulting services include the provision of services as an Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) Specialist as an integral member of the Project Implementation Team (PIT) established within the ARA for implementation of the BRBP. The OHS Specialist will provide specialized technical expertise and support to the PIT in the planning, implementation, monitoring and reporting of occupational health and safety requirements associated with the rehabilitation and reconstruction of bridges and associated infrastructure under the Project. The Consultant will be responsible for monitoring and assessing occupational health and safety risks and hazards at Project sites and ensuring that Project activities are implemented in compliance with applicable Albanian legislation and regulations, relevant World Bank requirements, Environmental, Health and Safety Guidelines, good international industry practice, and applicable Project environmental and social instruments and contractual requirements.

The assignment is expected to be carried out on a full-time basis, with the Consultant based at the ARA/PIT office in Tirana and undertaking frequent visits to Project construction sites as required. The initial duration of the assignment is twelve (12) months from contract signing and/or entry into force of the contract, subject to a three (3)-month probation period. Subject to satisfactory performance, the contract may be renewed for the duration of the Program or for such other period as may subsequently be agreed in writing by the parties. 

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website https://www.arrsh.gov.al/njoftime-brbp

  • Working knowledge of local and international health and safety standards and risk management;

  • Reliable, independent, and dynamic worker with high social competency and good team spirit
  • Excellent knowledge in presentation, communication and writing of English and Albanian language (in speaking and writing).

Applicants who meet the minimum qualification requirements will be evaluated based on the following criteria:

  1. General Qualifications – 30 points

The Government of The Federated States of Micronesia (FSM) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Strengthening Public Financial Management II Project (P181237) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

 

The consulting services (“the Services”) involve providing full-time technical advisory and capacity-building support under Component 1 – Improved PFM Practices and Controls, Subcomponent 1.1 – Strengthening Budgeting and Reporting Practices of the PFM II Project.

 

The Senior US GASB Financial Reporting and Capacity Building Advisor will support the Government in strengthening accounting policies, financial reporting procedures, the Government Chart of Accounts, and institutional capacity to prepare financial statements in accordance with applicable United States Governmental Accounting Standards Board (US GASB) requirements. The assignment will focus on improving the consistency and quality of financial reporting across the National Government and the four State Governments, strengthening in-house capacity to prepare financial statements, and progressively establishing the foundations for consolidated Whole-of-Government financial reporting.

 

The key responsibilities will include, but not be limited to:

  • Review and strengthen government accounting policies, procedures, and financial reporting frameworks to support compliance with applicable US GASB requirements.
  • Develop standardized financial reporting manuals, year-end procedures, financial statement templates, working papers, disclosure templates, and supporting schedules.
  • Review the Government Chart of Accounts and recommend improvements to account classifications and alignment between FMIS outputs and financial reporting requirements.
  • Provide technical advice, mentoring, coaching, and training to National and State Government accounting personnel to strengthen in-house preparation of financial statements.
  • Support implementation of financial statement review recommendations and progress toward the PFM II Results Framework indicators for National Government and consolidated financial statements.
  • Assess consolidation arrangements and develop a roadmap for progressive implementation of consolidated Whole-of-Government financial reporting.
  • Develop capacity-building and knowledge-transfer arrangements to strengthen institutional sustainability and reduce long-term reliance on external technical assistance.

 

The assignment will be based in Palikir, Pohnpei, Federated States of Micronesia, with travel to the four State Governments as required. The assignment is expected to be full-time for twenty-four (24) months, with an anticipated start date as soon as possible, subject to completion of the selection and contracting process.

 

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the Department of Finance and Administration website: https://dofa.gov.fm, as part of this REOI, or can be obtained at the address given below.

Consultants should submit a Curriculum Vitae (CV) describing their qualifications, professional experience, experience in similar assignments and relevant experience in similar institutional or country contexts together with a cover letter outlining their interest in the assignment and suitability for the position.

 

The criteria for selecting the Consultant are:

Mandatory Requirements:

The Consultant shall possess:

  1. Academic and Professional Qualifications: A Master's degree in Accounting, Finance, Public Financial Management, Economics, or a related field from a recognized university, and a professional accounting qualification such as CPA, CA, ACCA, or equivalent.
  2. Public Sector Financial Reporting Experience: A minimum of fifteen (15) years of experience in public sector financial reporting, including demonstrated experience in applying US GASB standards and supporting the preparation of government financial statements.
  3. Technical and Capacity-Building Experience: Demonstrated experience in developing accounting policies, procedures, and financial reporting frameworks, and designing and delivering capacity-building programs for government accounting personnel.

Desirable:

  1. Government-Wide Financial Reporting Reforms: Experience supporting government-wide financial reporting reforms.
  2. FMIS-Enabled Financial Reporting: Experience supporting implementation of FMIS-enabled financial reporting.
  3. Consolidated Government Financial Reporting: Experience supporting the preparation of consolidated government financial statements and the development of Whole-of-Government financial reporting arrangements.
  4. Small Island Developing States (SIDS): Experience working with Small Island Developing States (SIDS).

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, Seventh Edition, September 2025 (“the Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

NB : l’absence de l’offre témoin entraîne l’irrecevabilité de l’offre du candidat concerné, dès l’ouverture des plis par la Commission de Passation des Marchés.

La période de validité des offres est de quatre-vingt-dix (90) jours à compter de la date d’ouverture des plis.

NB : Les originaux de la caution et du récépissé CDEC seront remis à la CSPM en salle, lors du dépouillement.

notices.title: Finance Consultant State of Yap 2
notices.description:
FEDERATED STATES OF MICRONESIA

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

Country

Federated States of Micronesia

Project

Project for Strengthening Public Financial Management II (P181237)

Project Implementing Agency / Client

Department of Finance and Administration (DOFA)

Assignment Title

Finance Consultant for Yap State

Selection Method

Open International

Contract Type

Time Based 

Reference No.

FM-DOFA-574066-CS-INDV

Credit/Grant No.

IDA-E4120

Date of Advertisement

October 16, 2026

Deadline for Submission

October 31, 2026

 

The Government of The Federated States of Micronesia (FSM) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Strengthening Public Financial Management II (PFM II) Project (P181237) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

 

The consulting services (“the Services”) involve providing full-time technical advisory and capacity-building support under Component 2 – Expand Core Financial Management Information System (FMIS), Subcomponent 2.1 – Continued Rollout of Core Public Finance System of the PFM II Project.

 

The Finance Consultant for Yap State will support the Yap State Finance Department in the continued rollout, operationalization, and stabilization of the FreeBalance FMIS. The assignment will focus on validating financial transactions and data migrated from FundWare to FreeBalance, reconciling FY26 opening balances, strengthening accounting and financial reporting processes, improving internal controls related to FMIS operations, and building the capacity of State Finance staff to use the system effectively and sustainably.

 

The key responsibilities will include, but not be limited to:

  • Reviewing and validating financial transactions, account balances, and data migrated from FundWare to FreeBalance, including the reconciliation and validation of FY26 opening balances.
  • Supporting FreeBalance stabilization by identifying, documenting, prioritizing, escalating, and following up on accounting, data migration, transaction-processing, reporting, and system-related issues.
  • Supporting monthly financial reporting, bank reconciliations, accounting entries, and month-end and year-end accounting processes in accordance with applicable GASB, GAAP, and FSM accounting requirements.
  • Reviewing and strengthening internal controls, accounting procedures, and compliance-monitoring practices relevant to FMIS operations.
  • Providing hands-on coaching and on-the-job training to Yap State Finance staff in government accounting, FreeBalance operations, reconciliations, financial reporting, data validation, and issue resolution.
  • Coordinating with the FSM Department of Finance and Administration at the National Government level, the PFM II Project Management Unit, the FMIS Adviser, ICT personnel, and FreeBalance specialists to resolve accounting and system issues and support sustainable FMIS operations.

 

The assignment will be based in Colonia, Yap State, Federated States of Micronesia, with coordination with the FSM Department of Finance and Administration at the National Government level. The consultancy is expected to be full-time for twelve (12) months, with an anticipated start date as soon as possible, subject to completion of the selection and contracting process.

 

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the Department of Finance and Administration website: https://dofa.gov.fm, as part of this REOI, or can be obtained at the address given below.

 

The Department of Finance and Administration now invites eligible individuals (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. Consultants should submit a Curriculum Vitae (CV) describing their qualifications, professional experience, experience in similar assignments and relevant experience in similar institutional or country contexts together with a cover letter outlining their interest in the assignment and suitability for the position.

 

The criteria for selecting the Consultant are:

Mandatory Requirements:

The Consultant shall possess:

  1. Education: A Master's degree in Accounting. Candidates holding a CPA qualification together with a degree in Finance, Information Systems, Public Administration, or an equivalent related field are also encouraged to apply.
  2. Professional Experience: At least ten (10) years of progressive experience in public sector accounting, financial management, and Public Financial Management (PFM) reforms.
  3. Technical Expertise: Demonstrated expertise in applying Governmental Accounting Standards Board (GASB) pronouncements and Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP), extensive experience with FMIS implementation, operationalization, stabilization, transaction processing, financial reporting, reconciliation and/or data migration, and demonstrated ability to identify, analyze, and resolve accounting, financial data, and system-related issues in an FMIS environment.

Desirable:

  1. Software Proficiency: Experience with FundWare and/or FreeBalance, particularly in FMIS stabilization, troubleshooting, issue escalation, and coordination with system vendors and national-level technical teams.
  2. Capacity Building and Communication: Proven ability to train and mentor government staff in financial reporting, PFM principles, and new software systems, supported by excellent analytical, communication, and report-writing skills.
  3. Governmental Accounting Knowledge: Thorough knowledge of governmental fund financial statements and government-wide financial reporting, including the Statement of Net Position, the three categories of Net Position, program and general revenues, Transfers and Internal Balances, the five categories of Fund Balance, and the distinction between Revenues and Other Financing Sources and Expenditures and Other Financing Uses.
  4. Geographic Experience: Prior experience working with island nations or small governments.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, Seventh Edition, September 2025 (“the Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

 

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours 08:00 to 17:00 hours, Pohnpei Time.

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below by e-mail only preferably by 5pm Pohnpei Time, October 31, 2026. Expressions of Interest must be submitted by email only to the following addresses:

 

Attn: Osbert Atusaasiire
Project Manager PFM II

Department of Finance and Administration

Palikir, Federated States of Micronesia

Email: osbert.atusaasiire@dofa.gov.fm

And cc to: arrio.abello@dofa.gov.fm
