notices.description:
PROJET DE DÉVELOPPEMENT URBAIN INTÉGRÉ ET RÉSILIENT POUR L’EMPLOI (PRODUIRE)

 

APPEL À MANIFESTATION D’INTÉRÊT POUR LE RECRUTEMENT

D’UN(E) RESPONSABLE SUIVI-EVALUATION DE L’UNITE DE GESTION DU PROJET PRODUIRE TOAMASINA

 

 

Pays : MADAGASCAR

AMI N : 04 -2026/MATSF-UCR/PRODUIRE

Projet : Projet de Développement Urbain Intégré ET RESILIENT POUR L’EMPLOI (PRODUIRE)

Crédit : IDA 80890

Date de lancement :  05 OCTOBRE 2026

 

1 - Le Gouvernement de la République de Madagascar a reçu un financement de 225 millions USD de l’Association Internationale de Développement (IDA) au profit du Projet de Développement Urbain Integré et Résilient pour l’Emploi (PRODUIRE) et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie de ce crédit pour financer le contrat de services d’un Responsible Suivi-évaluation  de Projet  de l’Unité de Gestion de Projet à Toamasina.

L’Objectif de Développement du Projet (ODP) est de renforcer la résilience climatique des communautés urbaines, d'améliorer l'administration foncière et de soutenir l'emploi dans certaines villes.

2 - Les services du consultant (« les services ») consistent à

  • Concevoir, mettre en œuvre et animer le Système de Suivi-Évaluation (SSE) du projet PRODUIRE pour L’unité de gestion de Toamasina (UGT) Toamasina.
  • Assurer le suivi systématique des indicateurs de performance, de réalisation et d'impact du projet (Cadre de Résultats), ainsi que la collecte, le traitement, la qualité et la restitution des données relatives aux interventions post-Gezani. 
  • Opérationnaliser le Manuel de Suivi-Évaluation du projet adapté aux interventions post-Gezani à Toamasina.
  • Établir et mettre à jour le Cadre de Résultats du projet (indicateurs ODP, indicateurs d'intermédiaires, valeurs cibles, valeurs de référence/baseline).
  • Concevoir et déployer les outils de collecte de données (fiches de suivi, questionnaires, outils digitaux de collecte sur le terrain).
  • Assurer l'intégration des données de suivi dans les systèmes d'information de la Banque Mondiale (ex. STEP, GRS, etc., le cas échéant).
  • Organiser et superviser la collecte régulière des données auprès des entreprises exécutantes, des bureaux d'études, des autorités locales et des communautés bénéficiaires.
  • Mettre en place un système de contrôle et de vérification de la qualité des données pour garantir leur exactitude, fiabilité et exhaustivité.
  • Alimenter et maintenir à jour la base de données centrale du projet à Toamasina.
  • Assurer l'intégration et l'exploitation des données géographiques et spatiales nécessaires au suivi des investissements et indicateurs territoriaux du projet.
  • Documenter la chronologie d'exécution du projet et assurer le suivi de la fidélité de mise en œuvre, en enregistrant tout changement ou retard dans les activités planifiées afin de faciliter la préparation du rapport d'achèvement du projet (ICR).
  • En collaboration avec le Responsable administratif et financer, le Responsable en passation des marchés, établir l’esquisse du PTBA (Plan de travail et budget annuel) pour chaque composante en fonction des activités identifiées avec le budget prévu ;
  • Assister les responsables des activités et des composantes dans la planification de leurs activités ;
  • Elaborer et mettre en forme le POA (Plan opérationnel d’activités) par actualisation et consolidation des données en provenance des composantes ;
  • Contrôler la conformité du PTBA/POA par rapport au cadre logique des activités et composantes ;
  • Effectuer la présentation technique du POA à la réunion de coordination ;
  • Finaliser le POA et transmettre au Coordonnateur de projet pour la procédure d’approbation ;
  • Contribuer à l’éligibilité technique des demandes de déblocage de fonds (requêtes) ;
  • Participer à la validation des aspects techniques des dossiers de passation de marchés ;
  • Elaborer le Plan de Suivi Evaluation ;
  • Mettre en place et actualiser le cadre logique des projets ;
  • Assurer la fiabilité et la qualité des données programmatiques en mettant en place des indicateurs SMART (spécifiques, mesurables, atteignables, réalistes et temporellement défini) sur la base des lignes directrices claires définissant les indicateurs, les sources de données, les méthodes de collecte de données, la fréquence et les responsables concernés ;
  • Elaborer le plan de supervision des projets.
  • Consolider et analyser les données de performance physique et financière des activités.
  • Assurer le suivi des indicateurs du Cadre de Résultats du projet et analyser périodiquement les écarts entre les prévisions et les réalisations. 
  • Rédiger les rapports de suivi périodiques (mensuels, trimestriels, semestriels et annuels) conformément aux formats et exigences de la Banque Mondiale et du Gouvernement.
  • Élaborer et actualiser les tableaux de bord de suivi technico-financier permettant le pilotage des activités du projet. 
  • Assurer le suivi, la consolidation et le reporting des indicateurs environnementaux et sociaux du projet conformément au Cadre Environnemental et Social (CES/ESF) de la Banque mondiale.
  • Assurer le suivi des indicateurs liés au mécanisme de gestion des plaintes, aux activités de Violence Basée sur le Genre (VBG), aux Plans d'Action de Réinstallation (PAR) et aux autres engagements environnementaux et sociaux du projet.
  • Préparer les données et documents de suivi requis pour les missions d'appui à la mise en œuvre (Supervision Missions) de la Banque Mondiale.
  • Appuyer le Coordonnateur dans le suivi de la mise en œuvre des recommandations issues des missions de supervision, des audits et des revues de performance. 
  • Documenter les bonnes pratiques, les leçons apprises et les études de cas liées à la reconstruction post-Gezani.
  • Préparer les TDR et suivre les études d'évaluation, incluant les études de base (baselines), les enquêtes finales (endlines), les évaluations à mi-parcours, les évaluations d'impact et l'évaluation finale de clôture.
  • Élaborer les termes de référence et superviser la collecte de données, la diffusion et les activités d'apprentissage pour l'évaluation d'impact pré-post des activités foncières, en coordination avec le/la Spécialiste en Suivi-Évaluation d'Antananarivo, en vue de déterminer le potentiel de passage à l'échelle nationale de ces activités.
  • Collaborer avec les consultants externes chargés des audits techniques ou socio-économiques.
  • Participer à la capitalisation des acquis du projet et à la documentation des bonnes pratiques, innovations, leçons apprises et impacts observés.
  • Superviser et coordonner la contractualisation et la conduite de la revue à mi-parcours du projet ainsi que de l'évaluation finale de clôture.

Un période d’essai de 6 mois est prévue dans la tranche ferme. Le lieu de travail est au siège du projet à Toamasina.

4 - Le responsible Suivi-évaluation  de l’unité de gestion de projet devra justifier de :

  • niveau Bac+5 (Master 2, DEA ou équivalent) en Statistique, Économie, Démographie, Gestion de Projet, Sciences Sociales ou domaine connexe.
  • Au moins cinq (05) ans d'expérience professionnelle probante à un poste de Responsable ou Spécialiste en Suivi-Évaluation au sein d'un projet de développement d'envergure.
  • Au moins trois (03) ans d'expérience dans des projets financés par la Banque Mondiale ou d'autres bailleurs de fonds internationaux (BAD, PNUD, AFD, etc.).
  • Expérience avérée dans le suivi de projets d'infrastructures urbaines, de gestion des risques de catastrophes ou de réponse d'urgence post-catastrophe. Une expérience en suivi-évaluation dans les domaines fonciers et/ou habitat est également un atout.
  • Expérience démontrée dans la collecte et l'analyse de données issues de sources variées : enquêtes ménages, entretiens avec des informateurs clés (KII), groupes de discussion (FGD), et données administratives ou institutionnelles.

  • Maîtrise avérée des concepts, méthodologies et outils modernes de suivi-évaluation (Cadre logique, Théorie du changement, Gestion Axée sur les Résultats - GAR).
  • La maîtrise des logiciels d'analyse statistique (SPSS, Stata, R, etc.) et des outils de collecte de données mobiles (KoboToolbox, ODK, CommCare, etc.) est un atout significatif.

notices.title: Provision of Consultancy Services for the Development of the Organization and Design of Museum and Cultural Spaces at the Dvin and Dashtadem Sites
notices.description:
TRIP-CQS-02

                                                                                                                    TERMS OF REFERENCE

Provision of Consulting Services for the Planning and Design Development of the Dvin and Dashtadem Museum and Cultural Sites under the Implementation of TRIP-DP-01 and TRIP-DP-02 Subprojects in the Republic of Armenia

  1. BACKGROUND

The Tourism and Regional Infrastructure Program (TRIP) aims to promote Armenia’s tourism potential through targeted infrastructure and non-infrastructure investments in a number of regions. The Program will support seven out of the twenty identified tourism clusters, focusing on wine, wellness, adventure, cultural, educational, and ecotourism in the regions of Ararat, Vayots Dzor, Shirak, Tavush, and Syunik. Within the framework of the Program, access to the identified clusters will be improved, and infrastructure at tourism destinations will be developed. The Program also seeks to leverage Armenia’s natural resources and human potential by developing the entrepreneurial and professional skills of residents of neighboring communities, with the aim of maximizing employment opportunities. In addition, the TRIP Program is aligned with the World Bank’s approach to attracting private investment to these tourism clusters.

The infrastructure investment component of the TRIP Program includes the construction of new public buildings, including museum buildings; the restoration and preservation of historical and cultural monuments; the revitalization of the urban environment of historic towns and villages, including the restoration of building façades, public spaces, museums, and roads; as well as the improvement of cultural and natural heritage sites, including ensuring their accessibility and appropriate presentation.

Under the World Bank’s Local Economy and Infrastructure Development (LEID) Project, which preceded the Tourism and Regional Infrastructure (TRIP) Program, designs for the museum buildings at the Dvin archaeological site and Dashtadem Fortress were developed and approved in 2024. Based on these designs, construction works will be implemented under the TRIP Program.

Under the TRIP Program, in parallel with the work of the museum specialist, the design documentation will be updated, the cost estimate will be recalculated based on current prices, and the accompanying documentation will be updated, including the Architectural Planning Assignment (APA), technical specifications, expert examination conclusions, approvals, and other relevant documents. The revision of the design will be carried out through the conclusion of a direct contract with the original design author.

At present, within the framework of the TRIP Program, it is necessary to develop conceptual approaches for the organization of the museum environment and exhibitions for the museums at the Dvin and Dashtadem archaeological sites, including exhibition design, taking into consideration their respective missions, visions, and objectives.

 

  1. OBJECTIVE OF THE ASSIGNMENT

Objective of the Assignment

The objective of the assignment is to:

  • Dvin: Present the archaeological museum of Dvin and the preserved monuments of the archaeological site of the “Capital of Dvin” to tourists by creating a culturally rich and, at the same time, scientific and educational environment that is historically grounded while incorporating modern amenities and design, archaeological exhibits, and historical reconstructions.
    Proposed museum type: Archaeological Museum.
  • Dashtadem: Determine the type and content of the Dashtadem Museum; develop and collect exhibits; plan interactive activities and festivals; recreate historical events using the entire area of the large fortress; and incorporate all structures of the restored fortress into programs featuring reenactments of historical episodes and military-sport games.
    Proposed museum type: Military-Historical Museum, though a broader historical scope could also be suggested (subject to further discussion).

Expected Results of the Assignment

The expected result of the assignment is the establishment of operational archaeological and military-historical museums at Dvin and Dashtadem, respectively, featuring:

  • Exhibitions developed on a sound scientific basis;
  • Modern lighting and design;
  • Information delivered through multimedia tools;
  • A management system compliant with modern museum standards, including digitized databases and appropriate conditions for the preservation, conservation/restoration, and display of exhibits;
  • Increased tourist visitation and increased tourism-generated revenues.

 

  1. SCOPE OF SERVICES

The scope of consulting services is divided into three phases:

Phase 1. Preliminary Study, Collection Assessment and Documentation, and Development of the Exhibition Concept and Layout Plans

This phase shall include a preliminary study of the sites and museums, assessment and documentation of the existing collections, and development of the conceptual approach to the organization of the exhibitions and the relevant layout plans.

Phase 2. Development of Museum Content, Exhibition Planning, and Development of Exhibition Design and Lighting Schemes

This phase shall include the development of the museums’ content, exhibition planning, and the development of exhibition design and lighting schemes for both interior and exterior spaces, in accordance with the requirements applicable to the “Design Developement” stage.

Phase 3. Integration of the Approved Solutions into the Museum Design Documentation, Capacity Building, Support for the Development of Management Policies, and Final Reporting

This phase shall include:

  • Integration of the solutions approved under Phase 2 into the design documentation of the museums;
  • Capacity building for museum staff;
  • Support for the development of museum management policies; and
  • Preparation and submission of the final report.

The interim and final deliverables shall be submitted to the Armenian Territorial Development Fund (ATDF) (the Client) for review and comments.

Key Stakeholders

The key stakeholders of the assignment are:

  • The Ministry of Economy of the Republic of Armenia, Tourism Committee (MoE Tourism Committee);
  • The Ministry of Education, Science, Culture and Sports of the Republic of Armenia (MoESCS);
  • The World Bank;
  • The “Service for the Protection of Historical Environment and Cultural Museum-Reservations” State Non-Commercial Organization; and
  • Relevant local self-government and state administration bodies.

 

PHASE 1. PRELIMINARY STUDY, COLLECTION ASSESSMENT AND DOCUMENTATION, AND DEVELOPMENT OF THE EXHIBITION CONCEPT AND LAYOUT PLANS

Task 1. Preliminary Study

  • Study the key objectives and priorities of the Program, as well as the principles governing the organization and development of similar museums.
  • Review the existing collections and exhibits; review and update the collection inventory; and assess the physical condition of the collections, the level of documentation, the potential for expanding the exhibitions, and opportunities for the application of modern technologies and best practices.
  • Update or create object records/passports for the collection items in the Collection Management System (CMS) or other appropriate information platforms.
  • Review the design documentation for the Dvin and Dashtadem museums and assess all spaces suitable for exhibition purposes.
  • Conduct inception meetings with the museum (and archaeological site) management and relevant departments to discuss existing challenges and perspectives, with the participation of all relevant stakeholders. The Client (ATDF) shall be notified in advance of the scheduled meetings.
  • Prepare and submit to the Client a brief report summarizing the work carried out, meetings held, and recommendations and proposals received from stakeholders.

 

Task 2. Collection Assessment and Documentation

For Dvin:

  • Classify the exhibits and archaeological finds into two lists: items intended for display and items to be placed in storage for further study and/or conservation/restoration.
  • For the items intended for display, identify their proposed display locations, such as exhibition halls, entrance/lobby areas, outdoor platforms, excavated pits protected by glass covers or shelters, and other appropriate locations.
  • Assess the informational signage and other small-scale architectural elements included in the design, and provide recommendations on whether they should be retained or modified.
  • Prepare preliminary classified lists of exhibits and archaeological finds according to their proposed display locations (e.g., exhibition hall, entrance/lobby, outdoor areas, archaeological site recreation/rest area, etc.).

 

For Dashtadem:

  • Identify, collect information on, and inventory all potential exhibits and archaeological finds, including their current locations and the organizations holding them. Classify them into two lists: items intended for display and items to be placed in storage for further study and/or conservation/restoration, indicating the current location of each exhibit and the arrangements made for obtaining/accessing it.
  • Propose a list of exhibits to be reconstructed and/or reproduced, together with sketches or photographs of relevant examples.
  • Assess the informational signage and other small-scale architectural elements included in the design, and provide recommendations on whether they should be retained or modified.
  • Prepare preliminary classified lists of exhibits and archaeological finds according to their proposed display locations (e.g., exhibition hall, entrance/lobby, outdoor areas, archaeological site recreation/rest area, etc.).

Task 3. Development of the Exhibition Concept and Layout Plans

For Dvin and Dashtadem:

  • Develop the exhibition concept, including proposed display locations, visitor circulation routes, descriptions, justification of the selected exhibition schemes, principles for organizing the interior spaces, the proposed design and lighting style, the placement of information panels and exhibit labels, and other relevant elements.
  • Develop exhibition layout plans and/or wall elevations, assigning identification numbers to the displayed items. Prepare a numbered list of exhibits, indicating for each exhibit its name, historica

  1. The Republic of Moldova has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Small and Medium-Sized Enterprise Competitiveness Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under the contract for Procurement of a Dedicated Hosting Infrastructure (Equipment to enhance governmental digital infrastructure).

2.         The Project Implementation Unit of the World Bank MSME Competitiveness Project now invites sealed Bids from eligible Bidders for the delivery and installation of a dedicated, high-availability hosting infrastructure - comprising compute, storage, network, and cybersecurity components (including Privileged Access Management, Security Information and Event Management, and vulnerability management systems) to support the Qualified Trust Services of the Government Certification Authority (PKI) of the Republic of Moldova, together with associated implementation, training, warranty, and technical support services, to be delivered and implemented across two geographically distinct data centers (a Primary Data Center and a Disaster Recovery Data Center) operated by the Information Technology and Cyber Security Service (STISC) in Chisinau, Republic of Moldova. No margin of domestic preference applies to this procurement.

3.         Bidding will be conducted through international competitive procurement using a Request for Bids (RFB)  as specified in the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” dated November 2020 (“Procurement Regulations”), and is open to all eligible Bidders as defined in the Procurement Regulations that meet the following minimum qualification criteria:

  1. Financial Capability: The Bidder shall submit audited financial statements or, if not required by the law of the Bidder's country, other financial statements acceptable to the Purchaser, for the last three (3) years prior to the Bid submission deadline (i.e., 2023, 2024, and 2025), demonstrating the current soundness of the Bidder's financial position. For a joint venture, this requirement shall be met by each member.

Minimum average annual turnover: The Bidder shall demonstrate a minimum average annual turnover, calculated as the total certified payments received for contracts in progress or completed, within the last three (3) years (2023, 2024, and 2025), of at least EUR 3,000,000.00 or equivalent.

For a joint venture, the sum of all Partners' average turnover amounts may be used to meet this requirement. In such case, the Partner in charge (leader) must have had an average annual turnover equivalent to at least seventy-five percent (75%) of the amount required for the most recent three (3) years, whereas the other Partner(s) shall have not less than twenty-five percent (25%) of the total requirement.

  1. Specific Experience: The Bidder shall demonstrate that it has successfully completed at least two (2) contracts within the last five (5) years prior to the Bid submission deadline, each with a value of at least EUR 800,000.00 or equivalent, that have been successfully and substantially completed and that are similar in nature and complexity to the Goods and Related Services under the Contract (i.e., supply and installation of hyper-converged/virtualized infrastructure with integrated cybersecurity components such as PAM and/or SIEM, SOAR).

For a joint venture, this requirement may be met by all members combined.

  1. Staff experience: qualification requirements for the personnel proposed by the Bidder, including education, certifications and professional experience for each position, are fully specified in Section VII, Schedule of Requirements, Technical Specifications and are assessed as mandatory minimum requirements.

For each proposed position the Bidder shall submit (i) a CV signed by the individual, stating the role performed, the responsibilities, and the start and the completion dates of the assignment; (ii) copies of the university diplomas of the proposed project team (iii) copies of the certifications relied upon; and (iv) a written declaration by the Bidder confirming that information.

  • Project Manager: higher-education graduate holding a bachelor's degree; project-management competencies as specified in the Bidding document; at least 5 years' professional experience.
  • Architect: bachelor's degree in computer science or IT engineering; the active certifications specified in the Bidding document, including CISSP and an internationally recognized trainer diploma, the active certifications specified in the Bidding document; at least 10 years' professional experience.
  • Infrastructure and Automation Engineer: bachelor's degree in computer science or IT engineering; the active certifications specified in the Bidding document; at least 5 years' professional experience.
  • Security Testing Expert: bachelor's degree in computer science or IT engineering; CEH, CISSP or CompTIA Security+ certification; at least 5 years' professional experience.
  • Auditor: bachelor's degree in IT engineering, a technical field or economics; the active certifications specified in the Bidding document, including CISA, CISM, CRISC and CISSP; at least 5 years' professional experience and at least 5 system-audit projects.
  • Cybersecurity Trainer (Instructor): bachelor's degree; active cybersecurity and trainer certifications (equivalent to or higher than CISSP, CISM, or GIAC GSLC, NSE7); at least 5 years' professional experience in cybersecurity and at least two references confirming delivery of similar courses; able to deliver the training in Romanian.

 

  1. Manufacturing Experience and Technical Capacity: if the Bidder itself manufactures any of the items offered under the Contract (e.g., the HCI compute servers, network/security appliances), the Bidder shall furnish documentary evidence to demonstrate that:
  1. it has manufactured goods of similar nature and complexity for at least three years, prior to the bid submission deadline; and
  2. its annual production capacity of goods of similar nature and complexity for each of the last three years prior to the bid submission deadline, is at least 2 times the quantities specified under the contract.

Where the Bidder is not the manufacturer of an item, sub-paragraph (f) below apply instead.

  1. Cyber Security Experience: Given the cybersecurity-sensitive nature of this Contract (PKI/trust services infrastructure, PAM, SIEM, and vulnerability management components), the Bidder shall demonstrate:
  1. successful completion of at least two (2) projects within the last five (5) years involving the design, supply, and/or implementation of Privileged Access Management (PAM), Security Information and Event Management (SIEM), or comparable cybersecurity infrastructure (SOAR, etc.), of similar scope and complexity to the Related Services under this Contract; and
  2. that the Bidder (or the subcontractor/partner responsible for the cybersecurity components, if applicable) holds a valid ISO/IEC 27001 certification (Information Security Management System), or equivalent, current as of the Bid submission deadline.
  1. Manufacturer's Authorization: A Bidder who does not manufacture an item/s where manufacturer authorization is required in accordance with BDS ITB 17.2(a), shall provide evidence of being duly authorized by a manufacturer (Manufacturer's Authorization Form, Section IV, Bidding Forms), meeting the criteria in (d) above, to supply the Goods.
  2. State Security Investment Screening: The Goods and Related Services under this Contract fall within the domains referred to in Article 4, letters (a), (b), and (j) of Law No. 174/2021 of the Republic of Moldova on the mechanism for examining investments of importance for State security, namely the operation of data processing or storage infrastructure, the operation of information technologies within cyber security infrastructure, and the security of public networks and information systems.

Accordingly, the Bidder shall obtain the prior approval of CEIISS for its planned investment/participation in this Contract, in accordance with Law No. 174/2021, before signature of the Contract (https://www.asp.gov.md/ro/informatii-utile/consiliul-pentru-examinarea-investitiilor-de-importanta-pentru-securitatea).

Where the Bidder is a joint venture, this approval shall be obtained by, and shall be required for, each member of the joint venture.

The Bidder (and, where applicable, each member of the joint venture) shall state whether it already holds such approval, attaching a copy if so, or shall submit confirmation that it has requested prior approval of the investment from CEIISS.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL CONSULTING SERVICES)

 

Country:                                                           Independent State of Samoa

 

Name of Project:                                      Samoa Finance Sector Resilience and Development Project (SFSRDP) 2025 – 2029 (World Bank Financed Project P181456)

 

Loan No./Credit No./Grant No.:     IDA – E3780

 

Assignment Title:                                      Diagnostic assessment for a core banking solution (CBS)

 

Reference No.:                                            CBS/ICS/010

 

 

1. The Government of Samoa has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the SFSRDP P181456 and intends to apply part of the proceeds to consulting services for the procurement of a Consultant to carry out a diagnostic assessment for a core banking solution for the Central Bank of Samoa.

 

2. The primary objective of the assignment is to conduct a comprehensive diagnostic assessment of the Central Bank’s current operational environment, identify capability gaps, define future-state requirements, and provide a strategic recommendation and roadmap for introducing a Core Banking Solution that aligns with international good practices and future needs of the Central Bank.

 

3. The estimated assignment duration is for 8 weeks. The consulting firm is expected to begin work by January  2027.

 

4. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website: www.cbs.gov.ws and www.mof.gov.ws or can be obtained at the address given below:

 

Central Bank of Samoa

Financial System Development Department

Level 1, Central Bank of Samoa Building

2 Apia City Boulevard

Email: lanna.lome@cbs.gov.ws.

 

5. The Bank now invites eligible all Individual (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing services. All interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualification and relevant experience to perform the Services (attach curriculum vitae with the description of experience in similar assignments, similar conditions, responsiveness to the TOR etc.). Firms; staff may express interest through the employing firm for the assignment and, under such situation, only the experience and qualifications of individuals shall be considered in the selection process.

 

 

6. The evaluation criteria are:

Mandatory

  • A Master’s degree in Information Systems, Computer Science, Finance, Banking, Business Administration, or a related field.
  • A minimum of 10 years of professional experience in financial sector IT strategy and enterprise architecture.
  • Central Banking Domain Expertise, including but not limited to:
    • Core Functions: Proven experience working with or consulting for central banks, specifically regarding monetary policy execution, currency management (vault/mint operations), and government banking.
    • Treasury & Settlement: Deep understanding of Treasury Single Account (TSA) management, Real-Time Gross Settlement (RTGS) system integrations, and Automated Clearing House (ACH) frameworks.
    • Accounting Standards: Familiarity with central bank financial reporting, statutory accounting rules, and international frameworks (e.g., IFRS).

 

  • Enterprise Architecture & Diagnostic Capability, including but not limited to:
    • System Diagnostics: Demonstrated track record of conducting IT gap analyses, legacy system audits, and business process re-engineering (BPR) for complex financial institutions.
    • Core Banking Systems: Strong technical knowledge of modern Core Banking Solutions (CBS), modular service-oriented architectures (SOA), cloud vs. on-premise trade-offs, and data migration complexities.
    • Security & Resilience: Knowledge of financial sector cybersecurity frameworks, business continuity planning (BCP), and disaster recovery (DR) protocols.

 

  • Strategy, Procurement & Roadmap Design, including but not limited to:
    • Strategic Planning: Experience drafting high-level IT roadmaps, cost-benefit analyses, and Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) models for large-scale software implementations.
    • Procurement Knowledge: Experience writing technical specifications, Functional/Technical Requirements documents, and Terms of Reference (TOR) or Requests for Proposals (RFP) for international vendor bidding.

 

  • Communication & Stakeholder Management, including but not limited to:
    • Executive Advisory: Proven capability to interview, advise, and present strategic technical assessments to high-level executives
    • Reporting Skills: Portfolio of high-quality, clear, and structured technical diagnostic reports written in English

 

Desirable

  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.
  • Excellent speaking, writing and interpersonal skills

 

 

7. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14,3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2023, setting forth the World Bank’s Policy on conflict of interest.

FEDERAL REPUBLIC OF SOMALIA

MINISTRY OF PUBLIC WORKS, RECONSTRUCTION AND HOUSING

SOMALIA INFRASTRUCTURE DEVELOPMENT FOR ACCESS AND JOBS, PHASE 1 (P513127)

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REOI)

CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION

Country:                              Somalia

Name of the Project:            Somalia Infrastructure Development for Access and Jobs, Phase 1 (P513127)

Credit/Grant No.                           IDA-E6630

Assignment Title:                 Consultancy Services for the Preparation of Detailed Design and Environmental and Social (E&S) Assessments for a New MoPWRH Headquarters Building in Mogadishu

Ref No.:                               SO-MPWRH-568985-CS-CQS

1. The Federal Government of Somalia has received financing from the World Bank (International Development Association) towards the cost of the Somalia Infrastructure Development for Access and Jobs, Phase 1 (P513127) – the first phase of a Multiphase Programmatic Approach (MPA) – and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

2. The consulting services (“the Services”) comprise the preparation of a complete, construction-ready detailed design package (architectural, structural, civil, and mechanical/electrical/plumbing) and a World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF)-compliant set of environmental and social instruments (including an Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA), an Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP), and any resettlement, labor, stakeholder engagement, and health-and-safety instruments triggered by the proposed works) for a new MoPWRH headquarters building, on an identified plot of approximately 120 m x 50 m (approximately 6,000 m²) in the Shangani District, Mogadishu. The assignment also includes preparation of a detailed cost estimate, Bill of Quantities (BoQ), and complete tender/bidding documents suitable for competitive procurement of construction works under a future MPA phase. The Consultant will undertake all the specific tasks detailed in the Terms of Reference. The duration of the assignment is six (6) months, and the estimated professional staff-months is 36.

3. The Detailed Terms of Reference for this assignment, with the scope of the assignment, can be found on the Ministry of Public Works, Reconstruction and Housing’s website: www.mpwr.gov.so, or it can be provided upon submission of the application by e-mail to the e-mail address provided below.

4. The Ministry of Public Works, Reconstruction and Housing of the Federal Government of Somalia (“Client”) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The shortlisting criteria are as follows:

  • Core business and years in business: The firm shall be registered/incorporated as a consulting firm with core business in any of the following areas: (i) Architectural and Building Engineering Design Services; (ii) Civil/Structural Engineering Consulting Services; (iii) Environmental and Social Consulting Services; or (iv) Urban and Infrastructure Planning Services, for a period of at least ten (10) years.
  • Relevant experience: The firm shall demonstrate experience in: (i) detailed design (architectural, structural, and mechanical/electrical/plumbing) of multi-story public or institutional buildings; and (ii) preparation of environmental and social safeguards instruments under the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) or an equivalent multilateral development bank (MDB) safeguards system (such as the former OP/BP 4.01 or IFC Performance Standards); as well as experience in any two of the following: (i) geotechnical investigation and structural design in seismic and/or coastal environments; (ii) cost estimation, Bill of Quantities preparation, and tender/bidding documentation for public works procured under World Bank or comparable MDB procurement procedures; (iii) stakeholder engagement and consultation for infrastructure or building projects; and (iv) work in fragile and conflict-affected settings (FCV), particularly in Somalia or comparable Horn of Africa/East Africa contexts. Additionally, the firm should demonstrate successful execution and completion of at least two (2) assignments of a similar nature and in a similar operating environment in the last ten (10) years. Details of similar assignments – name and address of the client, scope, value, and period – should be included in the Expression of Interest (EOI).
  • Technical and managerial capability of the firm: The firm(s) shall demonstrate as having the requisite technical capability, which shall entail a description of relevant personnel, equipment, software, etc., and managerial capacity to undertake the assignment. Key experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The maximum page limit for the EOI, including any annexes, is 20 pages. This limit applies for single entities as well as firms in associations.

5. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, First Published July 2016 and Revised in September 2023 (5th Edition) (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

6. Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

7. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Selection based on Consultants’ Qualifications (CQS) method set out in the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers.

8. Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours from 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Mogadishu time (excluding public holidays).

9. Expressions of Interest (EOI) must be delivered only by e-mail to the address below on or before 17th October, 2026 at 16:00 Hours (Mogadishu Time).

10.       The subject line of the email should clearly indicate: SO-MPWRH-568985-CS-CQS: CONSULTANCY SERVICES FOR THE PREPARATION OF DETAILED DESIGN AND ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL (E&S) ASSESSMENTS FOR A NEW MOPWRH HEADQUARTERS BUILDING IN MOGADISHU.

notices.title: Consultoría para aplicar control de calidad de vuelos fotogramétricos, MDS y MDT y ortoimágenes
notices.description:
SOLICITUD DE EXPRESIONES DE INTERÉS

SERVICIOS DE CONSULTORÍA

República Dominicana

Proyecto de Respuesta a Emergencias y Resiliencia de la República Dominicana

Préstamo No.: 9473-DO

Título del Trabajo:  Consultoría para aplicar control de calidad de vuelos fotogramétricos, MDS y MDT y ortoimágenes.

No. de Referencia: DO-MEPyD-470659-CS-QCBS

El Gobierno de la República Dominicana ha recibido financiamiento del Banco Mundial para cubrir el costo del Proyecto de Respuesta a Emergencias y Resiliencia de la República Dominicana a través del Ministerio de la Presidencia y tiene la intención de aplicar parte de los fondos a la contratación de servicios de consultoría.

Los servicios de consultoría ("los Servicios") comprenden la supervisión, verificación progresiva, control de calidad externo y validación técnica de los productos cartográficos básicos generados por el contrato de producción cartográfica del Proyecto. La firma consultora deberá revisar la correcta aplicación del aseguramiento de calidad del Proveedor del Servicio de producción y realizar las comprobaciones independientes adicionales que resulten necesarias, en gabinete y, cuando corresponda, en campo, para verificar la conformidad de los insumos, procesos, productos intermedios y productos finales con las especificaciones técnicas, estándares y criterios de aceptación aplicables.

El alcance comprende, principalmente, los vuelos fotogramétricos con captura de imágenes aéreas y datos LiDAR; puntos de fotocontrol y comprobación; orientación de imágenes y aerotriangulación; ajuste, filtrado y clasificación de nubes de puntos LiDAR; Modelos Digitales de Superficie (MDS) y Modelos Digitales del Terreno (MDT); y mosaicos de ortoimágenes digitales verdaderas (true-orthos), así como la documentación técnica, metadatos, formatos, certificados de calidad y demás respaldos asociados. La producción objeto de supervisión cubre aproximadamente 48,196.00 km² del territorio nacional, diferenciados en zona urbana (2,896.70 km²) y zona rural (45,299.30 km²). Los Servicios tendrán una duración de doce (12) meses calendario, conforme al alcance y condiciones establecidos en los Términos de Referencia (TDR). Esta descripción es de carácter general; el detalle de los alcances y especificaciones técnicas se encuentra en los TDR.

El Ministerio de la Presidencia ahora invita a las firmas consultoras elegibles ("Consultores") a indicar su interés en proporcionar los Servicios. Los Consultores interesados deben proporcionar información que demuestre que tienen las calificaciones requeridas y la experiencia relevante para prestar los Servicios. Los criterios de preselección son:

  • Actividad principal, experiencia y trayectoria de la firma. La firma consultora deberá acreditar trayectoria institucional en servicios relacionados con información geoespacial, cartografía, geodesia, fotogrametría aérea, teledetección, LiDAR, modelos digitales de elevaciones, ortoimágenes, control de calidad cartográfica, supervisión técnica o validación de productos geoespaciales. Deberá demostrar una experiencia general mínima de ocho (8) años y haber ejecutado satisfactoriamente al menos cinco (5) contratos relacionados con estos servicios durante los últimos ocho (8) años.
  • Experiencia específica y comparabilidad de proyectos. La firma deberá acreditar al menos tres (3) contratos de naturaleza comparable ejecutados satisfactoriamente durante los últimos ocho (8) años. En conjunto, dichas experiencias deberán incluir: (i) al menos dos (2) contratos con actividades de supervisión, auditoría técnica, QA/QC, validación o aceptación de productos fotogramétricos y/o LiDAR; (ii) al menos un (1) proyecto de cobertura nacional, subnacional extensa, regional o territorialmente continua; y (iii) al menos un (1) proyecto que haya comprendido productos LiDAR y modelos digitales de elevaciones, además de ortoimágenes u ortofotos. Un mismo contrato podrá acreditar más de una condición cuando su alcance lo demuestre de manera verificable. La experiencia en producción cartográfica será considerada únicamente cuando evidencie funciones sustantivas de aseguramiento o control de calidad sobre los productos generados.
  • Capacidad técnica, organizativa y operativa. La firma deberá demostrar capacidad para ejecutar revisiones concurrentes y especializadas por bloques, productos o frentes de trabajo; aplicar procedimientos de QA/QC; gestionar grandes volúmenes de imágenes aéreas, nubes de puntos LiDAR, MDS, MDT y ortoimágenes; y mantener trazabilidad documental, control de versiones y seguimiento de observaciones y subsanaciones. Deberá acreditar disponibilidad de recursos computacionales, software, licencias, infraestructura de procesamiento y almacenamiento, herramientas especializadas y mecanismos seguros de intercambio y respaldo de información, así como capacidad organizativa para iniciar oportunamente la consultoría y cumplir los tiempos de revisión previstos.
  • Correspondencia con el alcance de la consultoría. La correspondencia será valorada mediante el análisis integrado de la experiencia y las capacidades institucionales acreditadas frente a la escala y complejidad de los Servicios. Se considerará especialmente la experiencia en revisión y validación de planes de vuelo, cobertura y GSD, GNSS/IMU, control terrestre, aerotriangulación, ajuste y clasificación LiDAR, MDS/MDT, ortorrectificación, ortoimágenes verdaderas, exactitud posicional, completitud, consistencia radiométrica, formatos, metadatos y trazabilidad documental, así como la capacidad para coordinar técnicamente con el Contratante y el Proveedor del Servicio de producción preservando la independencia del control de calidad externo.

La firma consultora deberá actuar con independencia técnica respecto del Proveedor del Servicio de producción y declarar cualquier vínculo contractual, societario, comercial, técnico o profesional que pueda comprometer la objetividad de la supervisión. Los Servicios se prestarán en idioma español, en modalidad combinada de gabinete y, cuando corresponda, actividades presenciales o verificaciones de campo. La firma adjudicataria deberá disponer o establecer una oficina local en Santo Domingo durante la ejecución de la consultoría.

Nota: Los Expertos Clave no serán evaluados en la etapa de preselección y no deberán presentarse CV en esta etapa.

Para estos fines la firma consultora deberá remitir la documentación de forma clara, estructurada, verificable y directamente vinculada con los criterios de preselección establecidos en la presente Solicitud de Expresiones de Interés (SEI). El documento principal no deberá exceder de cuarenta (40) páginas. Los documentos legales y los soportes documentales presentados para acreditar la experiencia y capacidad declaradas no se computarán dentro de este límite y deberán incorporarse como anexos debidamente identificados, paginados y referenciados. La documentación técnica de soporte no deberá exceder de ciento cincuenta (150) páginas para una firma consultora individual. En caso de APCA, consorcio, joint venture o asociación equivalente, el límite será de ciento cincuenta (150) páginas por cada integrante que acredite experiencia o capacidad técnica, organizativa u operativa relevante para los criterios de preselección. El registro mercantil, la nómina de accionistas y los documentos legales equivalentes no se computarán dentro de estos límites de páginas.

La documentación requerida es la siguiente:

  • Carta de expresión de interés, con datos generales de la firma consultora (firmada y sellada).
  • Detalle de experiencia directa de la firma consultora donde se evidencie: actividad principal y años en el negocio, experiencia general y específica, capacidad técnica y de gestión de acuerdo con los criterios indicados. Para cada experiencia declarada deberá indicarse, como mínimo, el nombre del contrato o proyecto, cliente y país, fechas de ejecución, monto contractual, alcance, rol desempeñado por la firma o integrante de la APCA, productos o actividades efectivamente ejecutados, superficie o cobertura territorial, componentes fotogramétricos y/o LiDAR comprendidos, funciones de QA/QC, supervisión o validación realizadas, criterios o estándares de calidad aplicados, criterio o criterios de preselección que acredita y referencia exacta del soporte documental presentado. Para acreditar las experiencias no será necesario presentar el contrato completo; podrán aportarse únicamente las páginas pertinentes del contrato, certificaciones, actas de recepción, constancias de conformidad, informes finales aprobados u otra documentación equivalente emitida o validada por el cliente o contratante que permita verificar la experiencia declarada.
  • Estructura organizativa general de la Firma Consultora o APCA, con una breve descripción de sus áreas técnicas, capacidades institucionales, recursos permanentes, infraestructura computacional, software y mecanismos de gestión y control de calidad relevantes para la consultoría. En esta etapa no deberán presentarse CV ni se evaluarán las calificaciones de expertos individuales.
  • Declaración de independencia técnica y ausencia de conflictos de interés que puedan afectar la objetividad de la consultoría, con el compromiso de informar al Contratante cualquier posible conflicto que se identifique durante el proceso de selección o la ejecución del contrato.
  • Registro mercantil actualizado o equivalente en su país de origen.
  • Nómina de accionistas o documento equivalente en su país de origen.

Nota: Toda la documentación que se presente deberá estar en idioma español.

La lista corta estará integrada por un mínimo de cinco (5) y un máximo de ocho (8) firmas consultoras.

Se llama la atención de los Consultores interesados sobre la Sección III, párrafos 3.14, 3.16 y 3.17 de las “Regulaciones de Adquisiciones para Prestatarios en Proyectos de Inversión del Banco Mundial”, actualizadas a noviembre de 2020 (“Regulaciones de Adquisiciones”), en las que se establece la política del Banco Mundial sobre conflictos de intereses.

notices.description:
REPUBLIC OF MALAWI
MINISTRY OF ENERGY
 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRM SELECTION)

Country

Malawi

Project Name

ASCENT Malawi Project

Project Number

P502464

Assignment Title

Consultancy for Provision of Fund Management Services for the Ngwee Ngwee Ngwee Fund

Reference No.

MW-MOE.-574017-CS-QCBS

EOI Issue Date

28th September 2026

This request for expression of interest follows the General Procurement Notice for this Project that appeared in the United Nations Development Business (UNDB) on 31st January 2025.

The Government of the Republic of Malawi through the Ministry of Energy (MoE) has received financing from the International Development Association (IDA) and the Energy Sector Management Assistance Program (ESMAP) towards the cost of implementing the Accelerating Sustainable and Clean Energy Access Transformation in Malawi (ASCENT Malawi) Project. It is intended that part of the proceeds of the financing will be used to cover eligible payments under the contract for these consultancy services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) are intended to engage a qualified consulting firm or consortium to provide Fund Management Services for the Ngwee Ngwee Ngwee Fund (NNNF). The Fund Manager will support the Ministry of Energy in delivering ASCENT Malawi Project Components 2, 3 and 4; managing legacy Malawi Electricity Access Project (MEAP) loan collections and residual obligations; and supporting the transition and institutionalisation of the NNNF as a sustainable standalone revolving fund.

The assignment is expected to be implemented over forty-eight (48) Calendar months, from 1st January 2027 to 31st December 2030, subject to contract signature and availability of financing.

The objective of the assignment is to provide specialised fund management services that enable timely, compliant and well-secured financing to eligible Participating Organisations; ensure sound portfolio, fiduciary, safeguards, data and risk management; protect the Fund’s creditor rights; support achievement of ASCENT energy-access and market-development results; and strengthen systems, national capacity and arrangements for the long-term sustainability of the NNNF.

The scope of work under this assignment shall include, but not be limited to:

a) Inception, portfolio takeover, reconciliation and structured handover of existing NNNF facilities, commitments, systems, records and outstanding actions;

b) Cross-cutting fund administration, including drawdown and payment review, portfolio monitoring, forecasting, records management, risk management and reporting;

c) Administration of Component 2 debt and Results-Based Financing (RBF) facilities for off-grid solar companies, including disbursements, repayments, verification interfaces, portfolio quality and recovery actions;

d) Administration of Component 3 financing and performance-linked payments for electrification of public schools and health facilities, in coordination with the ASCENT PIU technical team;

e) Administration of Component 4 clean cooking financing, including loans, repayments, security, portfolio monitoring and carbon-finance interfaces;

f) Management of loan collateral, security perfection, covenant monitoring, enforcement and recoveries, subject to Ministry approvals;

g) Management and collection of the legacy MEAP loan portfolio, including arrears, restructuring, recoveries and close-out actions;

h) Data management, monitoring, dashboards, financial and operational reconciliation, fraud and corruption controls, cybersecurity and data protection;

i) Implementation and monitoring of environmental and social requirements in accordance with the NNNF ESMS, applicable Malawi law and World Bank requirements;

j) Coordination with the Independent Verification Agent, Legal Advisor, Carbon Consultant, technical specialists and other consultants engaged by the Ministry; and

k) Support to institutionalisation of the NNNF, including governance arrangements, capitalisation options, sustainable business model, capacity development, systems transfer and final handover.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TORs) for the assignment can be found at the following websites: Ministry of Energy (https://energy.gov.mw/resources/), Ngwee Ngwee Ngwee Fund (https://www.nnnf.energy.gov.mw/resources/) and ASCENT Malawi Project (https://www.ascent.mw/resources/), or upon request through amopiha@ascent.mw copied to info@ascent.mw and austin.theu@energy.gov.mw. All requests for clarification should be sent through the above email addresses.

The MoE now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are as follows:

1. Core business of the firm(s) and years in business of not less than 5 years organizational capability and relevant experience in fund management, investment, lending, RBF/grant facilities or comparable financing programmes.

2. Relevant similar experience, which should specifically include the below:

a) Off-grid solar and clean cooking sector expertise: experience in, and understanding of, the off-grid solar and clean cooking market in Sub-Saharan Africa, including Energy-as-a-Service and PAYGo solar business models (minimum of five years), together with specific experience in, and understanding of, the Malawi off-grid solar and clean cooking market and the success factors of for-profit businesses in this sector;

b) Results-Based Financing (RBF) and grant facility management: a minimum of three years track record of structuring and managing RBF grant facilities aimed at market stimulation, ideally facilities funded by multilateral development banks, development finance institutions and/or bilateral development assistance agencies;

c) Debt and consumer financing track record: a minimum of three years track record of providing debt financing to off-grid solar and clean cooking distribution businesses and/or consumer finance businesses, including microfinance institutions;

d) Malawi presence and government/development-partner engagement: an established or committed local footprint in Malawi sufficient to manage relationships and reporting with the Government of Malawi and with RBF Grant Window and Debt Window applicants and investees and experience managing reporting relationships with government stakeholders and large development finance organisations;

e) Integration & Institutional Capability: Capacity to integrate sector expertise, financing mechanisms, and local presence, with into a coherent delivery model, supported by evidence of technical and managerial systems for coordinating RBF, debt financing, and stakeholder reporting, and scalable energy-access ability to sustain and scale operations in Malawi’s energy access sector.

3. Technical and managerial capability of the firm (provide only the structure of the organization, general qualifications, and number of key staff. Do not provide CVs of the staff. Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

This Request for Expressions of Interest is open to all eligible firms as defined in the World Bank's Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (July 2016, as revised November 2017, August 2018, September 2023 and February 2025). Firms declared ineligible by the World Bank Group in accordance with the Bank's guidelines on Preventing and Combating Fraud and Corruption in Projects Financed by IBRD Loans and IDA Credits and Grants are not eligible to participate.

Consultants may associate with other firms in the form of a Joint Venture (JV) or sub-consultancy to enhance their qualifications. In the case of a JV, the firms should clearly identify the lead firm and the nature of the association. All partners in a joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality- and Cost-Based (QCBS) Selection method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers.

Interested firms are requested to submit an Expression of Interest containing the following information:

  • Firm Profile: organisation name, legal status, country of registration, year of establishment, core business and contact details.
  • Relevant Experience: description of similar assignments, including client, assignment title, duration, contract value, scope and role of the firm; reference contacts should be provided.
  • Approach Statement: a brief statement responding to the shortlisting criteria outlined above. 
  • Statement of Availability and Commitment: Signed declaration of the firm's availability and commitment to execute the assignment.
  • Joint Venture Agreement (if applicable): A Letter of Intent to form a JV or sub-consultancy, signed by all parties

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours from 8:00 to 12:00 and 13:00 to 16:00 hours local time, Monday to Friday, except National Holidays.

notices.title: Consultancy Services to Support, Enhance, and Implement the Local Government Revenue Collection System (MUTM)
notices.description:
REVOLUTIONARY GOVERNMENT OF ZANZIBAR

 

MINISTRY OF FINANCE AND PLANNING

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

 

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRM SELECTION)

 

COUNTRY:                    UNITED REPUBLIC OF TANZANIA

 

NAME OF PROJECT: BOOSTING INCLUSIVE GROWTH FOR ZANZIBAR (BIG-Z)

 

Loan No:                         IDA - 69140 –TZ

 

Assignment Title:          Consultancy Services to Support, Enhance, and Implement the Local Government Revenue Collection System (MUTM)

 

Reference No:                TZ-POFP-573107-CS-QCBS.

 

This request for expression of interest follows the General Procurement Notice for the Boosting of Inclusive Growth for Zanzibar Project (BIG-Z) that appeared in the UN Development Business online No. WB-P811333-8 of 27-08-2021.

 

The United Republic of Tanzania has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Boosting Inclusive Growth for Zanzibar Project (BIG-Z), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

 

The Consultancy Services (“the Services”) include: conducting a comprehensive assessment of the existing Local Government Revenue Collection System (MUTM), including its functional capabilities, architecture, source code, database, data quality, security posture, performance and scalability; identifying technical, operational, legal and policy gaps and interoperability constraints; developing at least two technically feasible and costed upgrade options and a detailed implementation roadmap; and implementing the approved upgrade. The Services further include GIS enablement aligned with ZanSDI; interoperability with ZanMalipo, Zanzibar Revenue Authority systems, Ministry of Finance and Planning systems, eGAZ requirements and LARIS, as applicable; data cleansing and migration; software development and configuration; testing, User Acceptance Testing (UAT), deployment to all 12 Local Government Authorities; capacity building and Training-of-Trainers (ToT); preparation of manuals and SOPs; knowledge transfer; and post-deployment support/hypercare.

 

The duration of the services for conducting this assignment is expected to be thirty-six (36) weeks (approximately nine (9) months) from contract commencement, comprising Phase 1 (Weeks 1–16) and Phase 2 (Weeks 17–36).

 

The detailed Terms of Reference (ToR) for the assignment can be found upon request to the following email: bigzpmt@gmail.com

 

The Principal Secretary, Ministry of Finance and Planning now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services. The shortlisting criteria are:

 

A: Core business and at least ten (10) years of experience in ICT, software development, and IT system assessment.

 

B: Relevant similar experience as specified below

 

The firm must have carried out at least one (1) assignment of a similar nature and scope involving the assessment and design of a public financial management system or municipal revenue system in a developing country.

 

The firm should demonstrate proven experience in the assessment, design, development/configuration and implementation of large-scale public-sector ICT systems, preferably financial management, municipal revenue, taxation, billing, payment, or related government information systems.

 

The consultant should demonstrate experience in system architecture, database design and administration, software development lifecycle management, performance/scalability assessment, information security, testing, User Acceptance Testing (UAT), deployment, operational handover and post-deployment support.

 

The consultant should demonstrate experience in GIS/SDI-enabled systems and geospatial interoperability, including integration of GIS workflows with enterprise applications and, where feasible, use of open-source technologies such as PostgreSQL/PostGIS, GeoServer and QGIS or equivalent technologies.

The consultant should demonstrate experience in systems interoperability and API/data exchange integration with government platforms such as e-payment gateways, revenue/tax systems, land administration systems, digital government platforms or other comparable public systems, including data migration, cleansing, reconciliation, logging and auditability.

 

Experience in capacity building and Training-of-Trainers (ToT), including development of user/admin manuals and institutional knowledge transfer, is desirable. Proven experience in Sub-Saharan Africa will be considered a significant advantage, and experience on donor-funded projects or assignments financed by international development partners will be a strong advantage.

 

C: Technical and managerial capability of the firm (Provide only the structure of the organization, general qualifications, and number of key staff). Do not provide CV of the key staff. Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

 

The attention of interested consultants is drawn to section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” Sixth Edition, February 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s Policy on conflict of interest.

 

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. Therefore, each member of JV shall independently meet the requirements of the evaluation criteria.

 

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations

 

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours i.e. 07.30 am to 03.30 pm EAT excluding public holidays.

 

Expressions of Interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person or by mail) by 20th October 2026. The firms that will submit their REOI via e-mail must get confirmation of the receipt of their documents from the Project Coordinator, BIG-Z Project. In case the firm does not receive an acknowledgement within two days after sending the documents via email they should call +255 777 429269 for follow-up.

 

The address referred above is:

Ministry of Finance and Planning

Attn: Project Coordinator, BIG -Z Project

P.O. BOX 1154

First Floor, Sea View-Wing, Vuga Street

Zanzibar – Tanzania

Email: bigzpmt@gmail.com

 

The Principal Secretary, Ministry of Finance and Planning

Request for Expressions of Interest

(Consulting Services – Firms Selection)

Country             : Bangladesh

Project Name     :   Host and Rohingya Enhancement of Lives Project (HELP)

Credit/Grant No.:   7545-BD/E325-BD

Assignment Title: Consultancy Service for Review & Update of existing ICT-based Monitoring and billing software of DPHE including O&M and related ICT equipment

Reference No.    :   Contract Package Number SD-19

  1. The People's Republic of Bangladesh has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Host and Rohingya Enhancement of Lives Project (HELP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services for Review and Update of existing ICT-based Monitoring and billing software of DPHE including O&M and related ICT equipment.
  2. The broad scope of consulting services (“the Services”) includes: provide all professional services, software, licenses (where applicable), source code, configuration, interfaces, data migration, infrastructure support, installation, security hardening, testing, training, documentation, domain/cloud, web-based storage, warranty, support and knowledge transfer required to establish Integrated Digital Management and Information System (IDMIS) as a production enterprise platform. The scope covers discovery and process assessment, solution architecture, iterative configuration and development, integration, data migration, phased rollout, and transition to DPHE operations.
  3. The objectives of the consultancy services are to: review, update, integration, and operationalization of DPHE’s existing ICT-based systems and establishment of an Integrated Digital Management and Information System (IDMIS). The assignment will include assessment and gap analysis of existing systems; integration of approximately 30–40 DPHE information systems through APIs/middleware; establishment of centralized identity and access management, data warehouse, dashboards and business intelligence; strengthening of project monitoring, procurement, billing, accounts, O&M, GIS-based asset management, field data collection, reporting, audit and citizen services; interoperability with relevant Government platforms; data migration and legacy archiving; introduction of appropriate AI-assisted analytics and decision-support tools; and ensuring cybersecurity, privacy, scalability and business continuity. The assignment will also include necessary training, knowledge transfer, technical documentation, source-code handover, and post-implementation maintenance and technical support for sustainable operation of the IDMIS.
  4. The detailed Terms of Reference (ToR) can be found at the following website: www.dphe.gov.bd. The ToR or any further information can be obtained at the address of the undersigned given below, during office hours from 9:00 am to 4:00 pm Bangladesh Standard Time (BST).
  5. Department of Public Health Engineering (DPHE) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services.  The shortlisting criteria are: a) At least ten (10) years of general experience in providing ICT/software development, or other relevant consultancy services. In the case of a Joint Venture (JV), each JV member shall individually meet the minimum requirement of ten (10) years of general experience.b) Completed at least two (2) assignments of a similar nature within the last five (5) years for Government/public-sector institutions or under development partner-funded projects or programs. Such assignments shall involve the development, upgrading, integration, and/or implementation of enterprise-level MIS, ERP, web-based monitoring and dashboard systems, e-Governance platforms, or other comparable large-scale ICT systems. c) An average annual turnover of at least BDT 4.00 crore from consultancy/ICT-related services during any three (3) of the last five (5) financial years, supported by audited financial statements/reports. d) Demonstrate relevant experience in implementing similar ICT consultancy assignments for development partner-funded projects or programs. e) Demonstrate adequate managerial, organizational, and technical capacity to undertake the assignment, including an appropriate organizational structure, relevant technical resources, facilities, equipment and logistics, and applicable professional/institutional accreditations or certifications. Consultants are requested to submit, but not limited to, the following supporting documents as evidence of their qualifications and relevant experience against the above-mentioned criteria: (i) valid incorporation/registration documents of the Firm issued by the competent authority in its country of registration; (ii) Firm’s brochure/profile; (iii) details of similar consultancy assignments, including scope of services, contract value, client name, contract period, and country/location, supported by relevant contracts and/or completion certificates. For assignments undertaken as a Joint Venture (JV), the Firm’s role and share of responsibilities shall also be specified. (iv) valid membership/registration certificates from relevant professional or statutory bodies and (v) audited financial statements/reports.
  6. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to the Section III, Para 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.
  7. Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but shall indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture (i.e. all members of the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable) and/or a sub-consultancy (i.e. the Consultant will be responsible, including for the services of the sub-consultant). In case of an association, the Consultant must explain in the EoI submission (a) the rationale/ justification for the proposed inclusion of the JV members and/or sub-consultants; and (b) the anticipated role and relevant qualifications of each member of the Joint Venture and/or of each sub-consultant for carrying out the assignment. Failure to provide the above explanation in the EoI may risk the association not being shortlisted for the assignment. However, the qualifications/experience of sub-consultants will not be considered and CV of Key Experts not evaluated by the Client in the evaluation of Expressions of Interest for Shortlisting purposes.
  8. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Fixed Budget (FBS) method; Market Approach-Open National set out in the Procurement Regulations.
  9. Expected date for commencement of the services is February 2027.
  10. Expressions of Interest (EOIs) must be delivered in writing to the address indicated below, either (i) in person or by courier, together with a soft copy in Microsoft Word format on a USB drive; or (ii) by e-mail, with the EOI attached in both PDF and Microsoft Word formats. The EOI must be received no later than 15:00 hours (BST, GMT+6) on October 15, 2026.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REOI)

(SELECTION OF CONSULTANT FIRM/NGO)

Country: Bangladesh

Name of Project: ISO Component 05: Socio-economic Development of the Host Community and FDMN through Capacity Enhancement Project, (Credit No: IDA-7546-BD & E326-BD)

Assignment Title: Selection of Consulting Firm/NGO for Capacity Strengthening of Social workers on Elderly Care & support and Special Needs and disability Management.

Reference No.: SD-18

The Government of Bangladesh is implementing the Inclusive Services and Opportunities for Host Communities and Displaced Rohingya Population (ISO) Project with World Bank financing. The Project Development Objective is to improve access to human capital services for vulnerable host communities and displaced Rohingya populations. Component 3, implemented by the Department of Social Services (DSS) under the Ministry of Social Welfare (MoSW), supports social care, child protection, and economic empowerment interventions for the Host Communities and Forcibly Displaced Myanmar Nationals (FDMN) in Chattogram Division. Under this assignment, DSS intends to strengthen the professional capacity of its social workers to provide inclusive, rights-based and person-centred services to older persons and persons with disabilities, including assessment, care planning, case management, referral, safeguarding and community-based support.

Purpose

To strengthen the knowledge, practical competencies and professional skills of DSS social workers in delivering quality, inclusive, rights-based and person-centered services for elderly persons and persons with disabilities (PWDs). The assignment will be implemented over Fourteen (14) months.

Objectives

The consultancy/training assignment shall:

  • Enhance technical knowledge on ageing, elderly care and disability management.
  • Build skills / competencies on: (i) case management and counselling skills, (ii) assessment of functional ability and care needs, (iii) disability-inclusive social protection.
  • Enhance referral and coordination with health, rehabilitation and community services.
  • Strengthen safeguarding, protection and ethical practice.
  • Promote family and community-based care approaches.
  • Improve reporting, documentation and digital case management.
  • Build Training of Trainers (ToT) capacity within DSS.

The Department of Social Services now invites eligible consulting firms/NGOs (‘Consultants’) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The shortlisting criteria are:

  1. Core business and years in business, including at least 10 years of experience in social development and/or institutional capacity strengthening;
  2. Experience in successfully completed or substantially completed assignments of similar nature, size and complexity, particularly assignments involving training-needs assessment, competency-based curriculum development, Training of Trainers and large-scale training related to elderly care, disability inclusion, rehabilitation, social work, case management, safeguarding or community-based support;
  3. Experience in providing capacity-development services to government or public-sector institutions in Bangladesh or comparable country contexts;
  4. Experience in competency-based curriculum development
  5. Experience in developing and conducting post training evaluation
  6. Technical and managerial capability of the firm, including its organizational structure, permanent professional capacity, quality-assurance arrangements and capacity to manage large-scale training. Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

Consultants should submit:

  1. Proof of legal establishment or registration in their country of origin;
  2. a brief firm/NGO profile, including its organizational and permanent professional capacity;
  3. Details of relevant assignments, including assignment name, client, country, implementation period, completion status, contract value, the Consultant’s role and a brief description of the services performed;
  4. Client references or evidence of satisfactory completion, where available; and
  5. The JV agreement or letter of intent to form a JV, if applicable. Detailed CVs of proposed experts are not required, as Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s ‘Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers’, Fifth Edition, September 2023 (‘Procurement Regulations’), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications and capability and should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all members of the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. Consultants should briefly describe the respective roles of the JV members and/or subconsultants in carrying out the assignment. The qualifications and experience of subconsultants will not be considered in the evaluation of Expressions of Interest for shortlisting purposes.

A Firm will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours, i.e. 0900 to 1600 hours. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be downloaded from https://iso.dss.gov.bd website or can be obtained upon request from the address below either by e-mail or in person during the office hours (Local Time: 09:00 to 16:00 hours).

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, or by mail, or by e-mail- procurement.iso.dss.msw@gmail.com) by 19 October 2026 up to 1400 hours (UTC+ 6 hours).

The Procuring Entity (PE) reserves the right to accept or reject any or all EOIs without assigning any reason whatsoever.

 

 

(Golam Mostofa)

Project Director

ISO Component 05: Socio-economic Development of the Host

Community and FDMN through Capacity Enhancement Project

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST
