Assignment Title:

:

Commercial Compliance and Documentation Assurance Consultancy Firm

Reference No.

:

ID-COMP 4 IHSS-550312-CS-QCBS

 

  1. The Ministry of Health (MoH) of the Republic of Indonesia has received loan financing from the World Bank to support the implementation of the Indonesia Health System Strengthening (IHSS) Project, with total funding amounting to EUR 3.7 billion. The IHSS Project operates at an unprecedented scale, serving over 10,000 health facilities across Indonesia's 6,500 inhabited islands, involving high-volume and complex procurement of medical and laboratory equipment. Given this complexity, MoH requires additional capacity to strengthen its commercial documentation, compliance arrangements, and governance processes. To address this, MoH intends to engage a suitably qualified consulting firm to provide concurrent commercial compliance advisory and review support. The selected firm will work in close coordination with the Inspectorate General (IG), the probity auditor, and the World Bank to ensure alignment and avoid duplication of efforts.
  2. The consulting services ("the Services") consist of concurrent commercial compliance audit and advisory support to MoH for the implementation of the IHSS Project, with a focus on transactions, engagements, and communications with vendors, suppliers, and other private sector actors across the SOPHI, SIHREN, InPULS, and project management components. The scope of services will include, but not be limited to, the following: (1) commercial compliance reviews of vendor engagements and procurement transactions; (2) design and implementation of a commercial documentation and indexing framework; (3) risk identification and mitigation in commercial practices; (4) preparation of a Commercial Compliance Whitepaper; and (5) capacity building and training for MoH staff.  
  3. The assignment is expected to require approximately 120 professional staff-months over the implementation period. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website: https://s.kemkes.go.id/CCDAConsultancyFirm 
  4. The Services for Commercial Compliance and Documentation Assurance Consultancy Firm is expected to commence in November 2026 and conclude by April 2028.
  5. The Ministry of Health (MoH) now invites eligible firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide sufficient information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services (including the name and location/country of the Client, type and scope of services provided, period of contract, contract amount, role of the firm, starting and completion dates, key output delivered and experts involved in the assignment). The shortlisting criteria are:
  • Legal Status and Registration: The firm must be a legally registered entity with a valid business license, and possess national and/or international accreditations/registrations (e.g., ISO 37001, ISO 9001, or equivalent certification).
  • Core Business and Years in Business: Minimum ten (10) years of proven experience in any of the following core business areas: commercial auditing, compliance review, and probity assurance. Other line of business such as strategic advisory related to procurement, contracting, and risk management will be considered as an advantage.
  • Relevant Project Experience:
    • Successfully implemented at least three (3) similar assignments within the last seven (7) years, demonstrating experience in any of the following areas:
      • commercial compliance audits or reviews in the public sector or health services; 
      • development of compliance frameworks or governance-oriented whitepapers; 
      • strategic advisory support in procurement and contracting processes; 
      • relevant project experience should be similar in nature, complexity, and scale to the current assignment, including key components such as commercial compliance review, procurement advisory, and risk assessment. 
      •  
      • Similar experience in any of the above areas under projects financed by Multilateral Development Banks (MDBs) such as the World Bank, ADB, AIIB, and IsDB, is an advantage.
    • Experience in establishing knowledge management systems, databases, and tested methodologies to support the implementation of nationwide projects is an advantage.
  • Technical and Managerial Capability of the Firm: Availability of a qualified team of multidisciplinary experts with demonstrated competencies in law, auditing, risk management, documentation, and information systems. 
  1. The qualifications and experience of Key Experts shall not be included in the shortlisting criteria. Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage. The MoH will evaluate the Expressions of Interest (EOI) and develop a shortlist of qualified firms. Shortlisted firms will subsequently be invited to submit full technical and financial proposals in accordance with the World Bank's “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” Fifth Edition September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”).
  2. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” Fifth Edition September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.
  3. The Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but shall clearly indicate in EOI whether the association is in the form of a Joint Venture (JV) and/or a sub-consultancy arrangement. In the case of JV, the EOI shall clearly identify the lead member authorized to represent the JV, and all JV members shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire assignment if selected. For the purpose of EOI evaluation and shortlisting, only the qualifications and experience of the JV members shall be considered in assessing compliance with the shortlisting criteria. The qualification and experience of sub-consultants shall not be taken into account for the evaluation of the EOI.
  4. A consultant awarded the contract for either the Consultancy Services for Project Management Consultant (PMC) or the Legal Compliance and Documentation assignment shall not be eligible for award of the Consultancy Services for the Commercial Compliance and Documentation Assurance. Intitule de la mission : Spécialiste en Micro, Petites et Moyennes Entreprises (MPME) du PRETE

Numéro de référence (selon le Plan de Passation des marchés) : BI-ADB-571156-CS-INDV

La République du Burundi a obtenu un financement de la Banque mondiale pour couvrir le coût du Projet pour l’Emploi et la Transformation Economique (PRETE), et a l'intention d’utiliser une partie du montant de ce don pour effectuer les paiements au titre du contrat suivant : « Spécialiste en Micro, Petites et Moyennes Entreprises (MPME) du PRETE ».

Les services de consultants (« les services ») consistent à appuyer techniquement l’UGP du PRETE dans la préparation, la coordination, le suivi et la qualité de la mise en œuvre de la Composante 1 « Accès des MPME aux marchés et développement des chaînes de valeur ». Le/la Spécialiste en Micro, Petites et Moyennes Entreprises (MPME) du PRETE veillera à la cohérence et à la qualité technique des activités conduites au titre des sous-composantes 1.1, 1.2 et 1.3 et à leur contribution à l’atteinte des résultats du projet.

La durée des prestations s’étend jusqu’à la date de clôture du Projet (29/12/2028) à partir de la notification du contrat.

Les termes de référence détaillés (TdR) pour la mission peuvent être obtenus à l'adresse indiquée ci-dessous ou par mail.

L’Unité de gestion du PRETE invite maintenant les candidats éligibles (« Consultants individuels ») à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les Services. Les candidats intéressés doivent fournir toutes les informations nécessaires démontrant qu'ils possèdent les qualifications requises et l'expérience pertinente pour exécuter les services. Le Consultant devra répondre aux critères suivants :

  • Être titulaire au minimum d’un Master en sciences économiques, gestion, administration des affaires, entrepreneuriat, sciences du développement, sciences sociales ou dans une autre discipline pertinente ;
  • Avoir au moins cinq (5) années d’expérience professionnelle pertinente dans le développement, l’accompagnement ou l’appui aux Micro, Petites et Moyennes Entreprises (MPME), dont une expérience significative au Burundi ;
  • Justifier d’une expérience avérée dans la conception, la préparation, la coordination, la mise en œuvre et/ou le suivi de programmes en faveur des MPME, notamment dans les domaines de l’accès aux marchés, des chaînes de valeur, du développement des fournisseurs, de l’accompagnement entrepreneurial, du renforcement des capacités et de l’adoption des technologies ;
  • Avoir une expérience pratique en matière d’accès des MPME aux infrastructures productives, d’amélioration de la productivité et de la compétitivité, de certification et de qualité, de développement de partenariats et de mise en relation commerciale ;
  • Avoir une bonne connaissance de l’écosystème du secteur privé et des MPME au Burundi, notamment des institutions publiques, chambres de commerce, organisations professionnelles, institutions financières, entreprises principales, prestataires de services et structures d’appui aux entreprises ;
  • Posséder une bonne compréhension des principales contraintes auxquelles sont confrontées les MPME burundaises, notamment en matière d’accès aux marchés, d’intégration dans les chaînes de valeur, d’infrastructures productives, de financement, de technologies et transformation numérique, de compétences managériales et techniques, de normes et certification, ainsi que de résilience au changement climatique ;
  • Avoir une expérience de collaboration avec des institutions publiques, des organisations du secteur privé, des chambres de commerce, des associations professionnelles, des partenaires techniques et financiers et/ou des programmes de développement ;
  • Une expérience dans la préparation de PTBA, de termes de référence, de dossiers techniques et dans la collaboration avec des projets financés par la Banque mondiale ou d’autres partenaires au développement constitue un atout ;
  • Avoir une bonne capacité d’organisation du travail, de planification, d’analyse, de rédaction de rapports et de préparation de documents techniques ;
  • Être capable d’effectuer des missions sur le terrain et de travailler avec des équipes, partenaires et bénéficiaires dans différents contextes ;
  • Avoir une bonne maîtrise des logiciels informatiques standards, notamment Word, Excel, PowerPoint et des outils usuels de communication et de collaboration en ligne ;
  • Avoir une intégrité professionnelle, un sens élevé des responsabilités et de bonnes aptitudes à travailler en équipe ;
  • Avoir de bonnes aptitudes en communication écrite et orale et un bon sens des relations humaines ;
  • Avoir une bonne connaissance du français écrit et parlé et une bonne maîtrise de l’anglais.

L'attention des Consultants intéressés est attirée sur la Section III, paragraphes 3.14, 3.16 et 3.17 du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement FPI » de septembre 2023 (« Règlement »), énonçant la politique de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflits d'intérêts.

Un consultant sera sélectionné conformément à la méthode de Sélection des Consultants Individuels avec approche ouverte nationale, énoncée dans le Règlement de passation des marchés de la Banque mondiale pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le (FPI), Edition de septembre 2023 et conformément aux critères exigés par les termes de référence.

notices.title: Consulting Firm for ITAS preparation: tax business process re-engineering, legal and regulatory review, and preparation of the ITAS procurement package
notices.description:
LEBANESE REPUBLIC

MINISTRY OF FINANCE

Lebanon Fiscal Management Project - Project Coordination Unit

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES - FIRMS SELECTION)

Country

Lebanese Republic

Project

Lebanon Fiscal Management Project (FMP) (P181155)

Loan No.

IBRD-96440

Assignment Title

Consulting Firm for ITAS Preparation: Business Process, Legal Review and Procurement Support

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan)

LB-MOF-568490-CS-QCBS

Market Approach

Open - International

Deadline for Submission of Expressions of Interest

30 September 2026 at 15:00, Beirut local time

 

1. Financing

The Lebanese Republic has received financing from the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) toward the cost of the Lebanon Fiscal Management Project (FMP), and intends to apply part of the proceeds of this financing to eligible payments under the contract for the consulting services described below.

The consulting services (“the Services”) will be provided to the Ministry of Finance of the Lebanese Republic (“the Client”), which is the implementing agency for the Project.

2. Objective and scope of the Services

The Ministry of Finance intends to deploy a modern Integrated Tax Administration System (ITAS) to replace its current legacy tax administration environment, which comprises SIGTAS for income tax and VAT, together with separate applications for Built Property Tax, Inheritance Tax, Stamp Duty and Collection. The ITAS will support core tax administration functions across the Revenue Directorate and the VAT Directorate, and must be designed to interoperate with Lebanon’s customs system (ASYCUDA), the Treasury single account system, the civil registry, the land registry, and the e-invoicing platform currently under development at the Ministry of Finance.

The Ministry of Finance seeks to engage a single consulting firm with multidisciplinary capacity to deliver two interdependent and sequenced streams of preparatory work under one integrated assignment:

Stream 1 - Business Process and Legal Review: current state assessment and gap analysis of tax administration business processes, laws, regulations, procedures and institutional arrangements across the Revenue Directorate and the VAT Directorate; business process re-engineering and definition of future “To-Be” processes; a Legal Reform Matrix identifying the legislative and regulatory amendments required to enable electronic filing and payment, electronic taxpayer notification, legal validity of digital records, data privacy and taxpayer rights in a digital environment; institutional readiness and change management assessment; and update of the relevant sections of the Ministry’s administrative procedures manual.

Stream 2 - ITAS Procurement Preparation: preparation of the complete technical and functional documentation required for the procurement of the ITAS solution, including the Functional Requirements Specification, the Technical Requirements Specification and Architecture Note, the SIGTAS-to-ITAS data migration plan, service level agreements, training and capacity building plan, change management strategy, phased implementation and rollout strategy, testing and user acceptance testing framework, the technical evaluation methodology and scoring matrix, and the complete, ready-to-issue Request for Proposals with all technical annexes.

The assignment comprises five deliverables: an Inception Report; a Diagnostic Report; a Reform and Readiness Report; a Draft ITAS Specifications and Procurement Package; and a Final Report and Complete RFP Package. All deliverables shall be submitted in English.

3. Duration, place of performance, and contract type

The assignment is expected to commence in the second quarter of 2027 and to be completed within approximately one hundred (100) working days from the date of contract signature, exclusive of Lebanese public holidays. The Services will be delivered through a combination of remote work and in-person engagements at the premises of the Ministry of Finance in Beirut, Lebanon.

The contract will be a lump-sum contract. The contract price shall be inclusive of all professional fees and all costs required to perform the assignment, including in-country missions, international and local travel, accommodation, subsistence, local transportation, communications, insurance, taxes and other incidental expenses.

4. Terms of Reference

The detailed Terms of Reference for the assignment are attached to this Request for Expressions of Interest. They may also be obtained at the address given in paragraph 12 below, or requested by email.

5. Invitation

The Ministry of Finance now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consulting firms should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

Expressions of interest shall be structured so as to address each of the shortlisting criteria set out in paragraph 6 below, in the order in which they appear. Submissions that do not address these criteria may not be considered.

6. Shortlisting criteria

Consultant will be shortlisted on the basis of the following criteria. Only the qualifications and experience of the firm - and, where an association is proposed, of its joint venture partners - will be assessed at this stage.

  1. Core business and years in business. The Consultant’s core business shall lie in one or more of the following fields: IT and business advisory services, tax administration reform, public financial management, revenue authority modernization, and the design, specification and procurement of government revenue information system. The consultant shall have a minimum of ten (10) years of relevant experience in business process engineering for the purpose of tax administration reform including the design, implementation or modernization of related information technology systems.  
  2. Relevant experience in ITAS or comparable revenue management systems. The firm shall demonstrate having successfully executed and completed at least two (2) assignments within the last ten (10) years involving the tax administration modernization, business process re-engineering within a revenue administration, or tax legal and regulatory reform, procurement preparation, functional and technical specification, or implementation of an Integrated Tax Administration System or a comparable integrated revenue management system.
  3. Combined legal and information systems capability. notices.title: Recruitment of Procurement Assistant
notices.description:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REOI)

CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT SELECTION
 

Country: – Republic of Mauritius

Project: Rodrigues Airport Project, New Runway and Associated Facilities Project (P180266)

Loan No.: IBRD-95910

Assignment Title: Procurement Assistant

Reference No.: MU-AML-567481-CS-INDV


1. BACKGROUND

The Ministry of Finance has received financing from the World Bank and a grant from the European Union toward the cost of the Construction of a New Runway and Other facilities for Plaine Corail Airport, Rodrigues and intends to apply part of the proceeds towards recruitment of Individual Consultancy for Procurement Assistant.

2. OBJECTIVE OF THE ASSIGNMENT 

The Procurement Assistant is to support all activities and procedures related to the procurement of goods, works, consulting services and non-consulting services under the specified threshold and act as an understudy to the Procurement Specialists and Sr. Procurement Specialist, providing support in procurement operations, ensuring compliance with policies and timely delivery of procurement activities. The Assistant will progressively assume more responsibility under supervision to support the project’s procurement needs

3.0       BRIEF SCOPE OF THE ASSIGNMENT

  • The Procurement Assistant will handle procurement activities under supervision, of the Procurement Specialist.
  • The Assistant will support and assist the Procurement Specialist with procurement activities and procedures as described in the Project Operations Manual (POM) and the World Bank Procurement Regulations.
  • Assist in the preparation and publication of procurement notices, bidding documents, evaluation reports, and contract documentation under supervision.
  • Prepare and update the Project’s Annual Procurement Plan using STEP.
  • Assist with organizing bid opening sessions, evaluation meetings, and negotiation documentation.
  • Prepare the minutes of the Evaluation Committee meetings.
  • Maintain updated procurement records, databases, and filing systems according to project and donor requirements.
  • Assist in updating the STEP system with procurement activities and contract management information.
  • Maintain and organize procurement documentation and ensure records are complete and audit ready.
  • Help ensure procurement activities comply with World Bank, Airports of Mauritius Co. Ltd and Government of Mauritius policies and regulations.

4. INVITATION FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

The Airports of Mauritius Co. Ltd now invites eligible candidates (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

5.0       QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE                                 

The consultant should have the following minimum qualifications and experience:

Qualifications

  • A bachelor’s degree (or higher) in Business Administration, Public Administration, Procurement, supply chain management, Project Management, Engineering, Economics, Law, or a related field would be considered an asset.
  • A diploma or certificate in Procurement or Contract Management is an asset.

Experience

  • At least 2 (two) years of experience in procurement as a Procurement Assistant.
  • Familiarity with World Bank or other international financial institution procurement policies and procedures is preferred.
  • Experience with e-procurement systems, such as the World Bank’s STEP platform, will be an advantage.
  • Work experience in similar projects financed by international multilateral institutions in a similar position, will be a definite advantage.
  • Experience in the procurement for building/civil projects, including bid documents, opening and evaluating bidders' proposals, negotiating and managing contracts

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained at the following link: https://aml.mru.aero/index.php/business/rap

The attention of interested individual Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” dated July 2016, revised November 2017, August 2018, November, 2020, and September, 2023, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

6.0 CONFLICT OF INTEREST

Please refer to paragraph 3.17 of the Procurement Regulations on conflict of interest related to this assignment which is available on the Bank’s website athttp://projects-beta.worldbank.org/en/projects- operations/products-and-services/brief/procurement-new-framework.    

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant Selection Method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours 8:00 am to 5:00 pm on Mondays to Fridays.

7.0       DURATION OF THE ASSIGNMENT                                                                              

The contract will be for an initial period of 24 months with the possibility of renewal based on satisfactory performance and project continuation. Annual performance assessment will be conducted for this position to review the performance level of the Procurement Assistant. The contract can be renewed subject to satisfactory performance and availability of funds.

8.0       SUBMISSION OF EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below by e-mail by 09th October 2026 at 15.00hrs on the following email address rap.recruitment@aml.aero   including the following documents:

•   A signed Expression of Interest / application letter;

•   A Curriculum Vitae (CV) in the World Bank format or other acceptable professional CV format;

•   Copies of diplomas, certificates, and other documents demonstrating qualifications;

•   Documents demonstrating relevant experience in procurement, project administration, contract administration, or similar assignments

Request for Expressions of Interest

(Consulting Services – Selection of Firms)

People’s Republic of China

World Bank Loan Hainan Project for Prevention, Preparedness and Response to Emerging Infectious Diseases (Global One Health Hainan Demonstration Project)

Loan No.: 9084-CN

Procurement No.: 0733-26094168

Assignment Name: Establishment and Promotion of Community Pilot Sites for Sustainable Vector Control in Tropical Areas Based on the One Health Approach

Contract No.: HN-FC-84

The Government of the People’s Republic of China has received a loan from the World Bank toward the cost of the World Bank Loan Hainan Project for Prevention, Preparedness and Response to Emerging Infectious Diseases (Global One Health Hainan Demonstration Project), and intends to apply part of the proceeds of this loan to payments for consulting services.

The consulting services (hereinafter referred to as the “Services”) mainly include the following: The consulting service period is 12 months after the contract is signed and becomes effective, and the expected commencement date of the consulting services is December 2026. The Services consist of, but are not limited to, the following 13 tasks:

  1. Preparation of the implementation plan;
  2. Selection and pre-assessment of community pilot sites;
  3. Conducting training activities;
  4. Routine mosquito prevention and control;
  5. Health education;
  6. Mosquito monitoring;
  7. Preparation of training reference materials and technical manuals;
  8. Development and maintenance of the data platform;
  9. Establishment and improvement of a multi-sectoral joint prevention and control mechanism at the community level;
  10. Development of evaluation indicators and management standards;
  11. Final evaluation of sustainable vector control communities and awarding ceremony;
  12. Provision of policy recommendations and suggestions;
  13. Data analysis and summary.

The Terms of Reference (TOR) for this consulting service are attached to this Request for Expressions of Interest.

Hainan Provincial Disease Control Bureau (hereinafter referred to as the “Client”) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to express their interest in providing the consulting services. Interested Consultants shall provide relevant supporting documents in accordance with the following requirements. The Expression of Interest (i.e., the proposal document) shall include, at a minimum, the following:

  1. A brief introduction of the consulting firm, including its organizational structure, staffing information, etc.
  2. The Letter of Authorization, identification documents of the legal representative and the authorized representative; if the Consultant is a joint venture, the joint venture agreement shall also be provided (format to be prepared by the Consultant).
  3. The Consultant shall provide a copy of its relevant business license or Certificate of Legal Person of Public Institution.
  4. If the Consultant is a state-owned enterprise or public institution, it shall provide its Articles of Association or the approval document for its establishment, as well as the audited financial audit report and financial statements for the year 2025 (including, at a minimum, the balance sheet, cash flow statement, and income statement/profit and loss statement), or the “internal financial statements of the entity” for 2025, or the final account report approved by the competent authority, or other equivalent supporting documents. (If the Consultant is a newly established entity and is unable to provide the above-mentioned documents for 2025, it shall provide financial statements and other relevant documents since its establishment.)
  5. The Consultant shall have a good track record and reputation and shall provide a “Commitment Letter on Good Track Record and Reputation” (in a self-prepared format) affixed with the official seal of the entity.
  6. The Consultant shall have successfully completed at least two similar projects during the past five years (from January 1, 2021 to the deadline for submission of documents). Similar projects refer to consulting assignments in areas including, but not limited to, infectious disease prevention and control, public health risk assessment, establishment of various pilot programs, tropical disease research, or disease surveillance and early warning. The contract amount of each project shall be no less than RMB 1 million. The Consultant shall submit supporting documents for relevant experience, including:
    Copies of key pages of the contracts, which shall at least demonstrate key information such as the contract date, contract amount, scope of services, and signatures/seals of both parties;
    Acceptance documents demonstrating that the projects have passed evaluation and acceptance; and
    Supporting documents proving that payments have been received by the Consultant.
  7. Other documents that the Consultant considers necessary to provide (if any).

Key experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

Interested Consultants should pay attention to the provisions regarding the World Bank’s conflict of interest policy set forth in paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (November 2020 edition).

Consulting firms may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications; however, they shall clearly indicate whether such association is in the form of a joint venture and/or subcontracting arrangement. If a joint venture arrangement is selected, all members of the joint venture shall meet the “Consultant Qualification Requirements” specified in this Request for Expressions of Interest. If the joint venture Consultant is selected, all parties of the joint venture, as well as any subcontracted Consultants, shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract.

The Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality- and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method specified in the Procurement Regulations.

Further information may be obtained during working hours from 9:00 to 17:00 on business days by contacting CITIC International Tendering Co., Ltd.

Expressions of Interest must be delivered in writing (by hand delivery, mail, or email) to Room 1817, 18/F, No. 59 Dongsanhuan Middle Road, Chaoyang District, Beijing, before 17:00 on October 22, 2026 (the deadline for submission of Expressions of Interest).

Consultants are recommended to submit hard-copy Expression of Interest documents. If submitting hard copies (sealed and bound), the submission shall include one (1) original copy and four (4) copies, together with a USB flash drive containing a scanned PDF version of the signed and stamped original Expression of Interest and an editable Word version (the content of which shall be consistent with the scanned original copy). In case of any discrepancy between the electronic version and the hard-copy version, the hard-copy version shall prevail.

If submitting by email, please send the scanned PDF version of the signed and stamped original Expression of Interest and the editable Word version (the content of which shall be consistent with the scanned original copy).
